Aeliana’s silver eyes widened in shock as the squishy artillery-based gravity mage suddenly appeared directly inside the perimeter of her Aegis shield.
Rowenna didn’t cast a spell.
She rotated her hips, planted her bare foot into the freezing mud beneath the snow, and delivered a devastating and fully committed roundhouse kick directly across Aeliana’s pristine face.
THWACK!
The sickening sound of physical impact echoed over the blizzard and the force of the blow made the Elf shoot backward like a cannonball.

Aeliana skidded violently across the frozen slate courtyard, her boot digging deeply into the icy ground in a desperate attempt to arrest her momentum leaving a massive trench of snow piling up behind her heel as her face was tossed viciously to the side.
The freezing wind ripped across the dark slate courtyard, howling through the stone arches of the territory.
Aeliana skidded backward through the thick slush, her pristine white spider-silk boots digging deep trenches into the accumulating snow to arrest her violent momentum.
Her head was snapped to the side from the concussive force of the roundhouse kick.
For a single agonizing second, everyone was dead silent.
The seventy-one women standing in the massive circle around them completely stopped breathing.
The only sound was the howling of the Umbral Basin blizzard.
Slowly, the Starlight Arcanist turned her head back to the center of the ring.
Her silver hair was wild, plastered against her cheek by the wet snow as she raised a delicate pale hand and touched her upper lip.
When she pulled her fingers away, they were smeared with bright, crimson blood.
Aeliana stared at the blood on her fingertips.
Her green eyes, normally pools of calm composure, suddenly narrowed into razor-sharp luminous slits.
The elegant high-society woman completely vanished, replaced in a fraction of a second by a true warrior.
She lowered her hand, letting the blood drip from her chin onto the snow.
"You will regret that..." Aeliana promised.
Her voice wasn’t a yell like one would expect, it was a cold level whisper that somehow cut through the roaring wind with clarity.
Thirty feet away, Rowenna’s feet hit the snow.
The blue-haired Runic Arcanist stumbled slightly, her chest heaving violently as she gasped for freezing air.
The golden aura that had coated her body completely evaporated, fizzling out into useless sparks.
Her newly integrated Fast! spell had deactivated.
Rowenna gritted her teeth, feeling a burning ache deep inside her B-Rank mana core.
She was new to the spell.
Because it was a support buff that forcefully bypassed her standard biological limits to artificially spike her physical velocity, the mana drain was quite volatile.
She could only use it in short explosive bursts, and the physical recoil on her unconditioned muscles was staggering.
Her right leg throbbed from the impact of kicking the Elf’s jaw.
Before Rowenna could even suck in a second breath of air, the snow in front of Aeliana exploded.
The Elf just moved.
Utilizing her Elven Swiftness passive, Aeliana caught the currents of the howling blizzard, using the wind shear to completely eliminate her own air resistance.
She blurred across the courtyard, moving with a terrifying liquid grace that completely defied human biology.
Rowenna’s eyes widened in panic.
The artillery mage instinctively raised her arms, throwing up a desperate cross-armed guard to protect her head.
Aeliana crashed into her.
The Elf didn’t throw a magical projectile... she threw a devastating, picture-perfect left hook.
The punch bypassed the center of Rowenna’s guard entirely, slamming into the blue-haired girl’s right forearm with the force of a swinging iron mallet.
CRACK!
"Agh!"
Rowenna hissed in pain, the density of the A-Rank Epic Elf jarring her bones.
She successfully blocked the hook, leaning her weight forward to brace against the snow, but Aeliana was already moving.

Using the momentum of the blocked left hook, Aeliana pivoted flawlessly on her lead foot, sinking her weight into the slush, and unleashed a lightning-fast brutal right straight directly through the tiny gap in Rowenna’s forearms.
The knuckles bypassed the block and buried themselves directly into the center of Rowenna’s face.
THWACK!
Rowenna’s head snapped violently backward with her vision flashed blindingly white.
A choked wet cough tore from her throat as she stumbled backward, her boots sliding uselessly on the black ice beneath the snow.
She turned her head, spitting a thick glob of blood and saliva onto the pristine white snowdrift beside her.
"Is this a joke?!" Thora bellowed from the sidelines, leaning over the shoulders of the infantry girls.
The dwarven blacksmith waved her empty ale mug furiously in the air.
"They’re mages!
Why are they throwing hands like tavern drunks?!
Use the glowing lights, you squishy cowards!"
"Shut up, dwarf!" Morwenna roared right back, pumping her fist in the air.
She was quite thrilled by the raw violence taking place here.
"This is a real fight!
Break her nose, pointy-ears!"
Silas stood on the edge of the circle with his golden-ringed eyes tracking every micro-movement.

’Aeliana has quite a lot of Vitality...’ Silas analyzed with a sigh, running the numbers in his head. ’Rowenna has vitality too so technically, Rowenna can take physical punishment but Aeliana’s baseline elven agility gives her a massive rotational advantage in close-quarters combat...
Rowena needs to find a way to break through this.’
In the center of the ring, Rowenna tasted copper.
The coppery tang of her own blood flooded her mouth.
Her vision swam, but the loyalty she had for her Lord was still burning in her chest and refused to let her stay down.
Silas was watching.
The Lord was standing right there.
She would rather die in the snow than look weak in front of him.
"Haaaa!" Rowenna let out a furious scream.
She bypassed her aching core, aggressively channeling a dense surge of raw mana directly down her right arm.
The golden aura of the Fast! spell violently flared to life around her fist and forearm, vibrating with unstable energy.

She didn’t try to cast a rune with the newfound speed, instead she stepped into the pocket, planted her back foot, and launched an accelerated right cross aimed directly at the center of the Elf’s chest, intent on caving Aeliana’s ribs in even if it meant breaking her hand.
The punch generated a shockwave however...
Aeliana was already gone.

chapters.title: Chapter 155: Aeliana Vs. Rowena [II / Bonus Chapter]
paragraphs: With her Elven Swiftness enhancing her reaction time, Aeliana simply slipped her head a fraction of an inch to the left.
The glowing accelerated fist grazed her pristine white collar, ripping the silk fabric but completely missing her flesh.
Rowenna’s momentum carried her awkwardly forward with her balance completely overextended.
Seeing the miss, Aeliana’s green eyes flashed.
The Elf fluidly brought her right hand up, bending her elbow in a wide sloppy arc, as if she was attempting to deliver a clumsy sweeping backhand to Rowenna’s exposed neck.
Rowenna, operating on pure adrenaline, saw the sweeping right hand coming.
She immediately shifted her weight, bringing her left arm up in a rigid desperate block to catch the incoming blow and protect her neck but the blow never landed.
Aeliana’s sweeping right hand completely stopped mid-air.
It was a fake! A flawless high-speed feint...
Rowenna’s eyes widened as she realized her left arm was now raised high in the air, completely exposing the entire left side of her torso.
Before the Runic Arcanist could even attempt to pull her arm back down, Aeliana stepped deeply into the pocket, completely closing the distance.

The Elf dropped her center of gravity, loaded her hips like a coiled spring, and unleashed her real attack... a devastating, perfectly executed left hook that buried itself wrist-deep into Rowenna’s exposed floating ribs.
CRUNCH!
The sickening sound of cartilage fracturing echoed over the howling wind.
All the air violently exploded out of Rowenna’s lungs in a choked breathless gasp.
Her eyes bulged with her knees instantly buckling as the agonizing pain of the liver-shot shut down her nervous system.
The girls on the sidelines winced collectively.
Brida sucked in a sharp breath through her teeth, instinctively rubbing her own ribs.
"That’s a powerful strike," Vala muttered in shock, staring at the elegant Elf. "She fights exactly like Lord Graves."
Rowenna folded forward, gagging for breath with her hands dropping uselessly toward the snow.
As her vision grayed out, a deep suppressed memory violently surfaced in the back of her mind.
’F-fuck...’
It was a memory from the Sovereign Realm but before she met her Lord and before the Blessed Land was even established.
It was a memory of a stuffy, brightly lit combat-theory classroom back at the Academy that she attended before being summoned here.
’You are a mage, Rowenna...’ the gruff scarred voice of her old combat instructor echoed clearly in her head.
The memory immediately made her wince harder than when she was hit. Out of everybody she remembered, why was it him?

’Mages die in the field because they think their spells make them gods but you are not a god... You are a squishy bag of blood holding a loaded gun. If a swordsman gets inside your guard, you bleed exactly like anyone else so what do you do when the enemy breaches the pocket?’
Rowenna sighed, the answer was quite simple... It was to—
’I create space.’

’Exactly,’ the instructor’s voice barked. ’Do not look at their hands as their hands lie. Look at their shoulders, control your breathing and create space like I taught you... The goal is to survive.’
Rowenna gritted her bloody teeth.
She forced her eyes open, fighting through the blinding pain of her bruised ribs but she didn’t look at Aeliana’s hands.
She locked her blurry blue eyes directly onto the Elf’s pristine, white-silk shoulders.
She saw Aeliana’s right shoulder twitch, dropping slightly.
’An uppercut...’ Rowenna read the telegraph perfectly. She was grateful that she had taken Combat classes.
Using every ounce of willpower she possessed, Rowenna threw her head violently backward, completely abandoning her stance just as Aeliana launched a brutal right uppercut aimed at her chin.
The Elf’s knuckles grazed the tip of Rowenna’s nose, missing the knockout blow by a fraction of an inch.
Rowenna desperately tried to scramble backward, her bare feet kicking up slush as she tried to put distance between herself and the melee monster.
’Create space... Create space...’
But the theory nor practice at the Academy didn’t account for the terrifying reality of an Epic-Rank combatant in the Sovereign Realm.
Aeliana didn’t let her retreat.
The Elf simply flowed forward like water, sticking to Rowenna like a shadow, completely dictating the pacing of the engagement.
Rowenna tried to throw a desperate sloppy jab to keep her away, but Aeliana casually parried the strike away with her left hand, completely opening up the Runic Arcanist’s center line again.
What followed was a brutal and perfectly executed disassembly.
Aeliana stepped in.
THWACK!
A lightning-fast straight right caught Rowenna flush on the cheekbone, snapping her head to the left and sending a spray of blood into the falling snow.
THUD!
Aeliana immediately followed up with a crushing left hook to the exact same bruised ribs she had hit seconds ago.
Rowenna screamed with her body folding in half.
CRACK.
Before Rowenna could collapse, Aeliana grabbed the back of her blue hair with her left hand, hauled her head downward, and drove her right knee violently upward.
The knee collided directly with Rowenna’s sternum with the force of a battering ram.
’I don’t hate you but I want to be the woman that my Lord brings around...’ Aeliana thought,
Rowenna’s eyes rolled back in her head.
Her arms fell completely limp at her sides. She was practically unconscious on her feet, held up entirely by the Elf’s grip on her hair.
"Holy shit," Tasmin whispered on the sidelines with her eyes wide. "She’s butchering her."
Silas watched without blinking.
He didn’t intervene just yet.
’Rowenna needs to learn more... she has a lot of potential after all.’ Silas thought.
In the Sovereign Realm, you learned by bleeding. If Rowenna wanted to survive the Secret Realm, she had to figure out how to survive an opponent who completely out-statted her in close quarters.
Aeliana released her grip on Rowenna’s hair, letting the battered, bloody girl begin to drop toward the slush however the Elf didn’t stop there.
Aeliana pivoted on her left foot, spinning her entire body with flawless dancer-like grace.

She dropped her center of gravity, planting both of her hands flat against the freezing, snow-covered slate tiles, and launched her right leg upward in a devastating capoeira-style spinning hook kick.
The heel of Aeliana’s pristine white boot caught Rowenna perfectly, squarely in the center of her chest.
BOOM!
The force of the kick lifted the Runic Arcanist completely off her feet.
Rowenna was launched backward like a discarded ragdoll.
She flew through the air, crossing fifteen feet of open space before slamming violently into the ground.

Rowenna tumbled head-over-heels through the freezing slush, her limp body skipping across the slate tiles like a skipped stone until she finally rolled to a complete, devastating halt near the edge of the circle.
She lay there in the snow, completely motionless.
The courtyard was dead silent as the only sound was the howling of the blizzard.
"Match over!" Brida yelled out, taking a step forward to go check on the B-Rank mage. "The runic girl is out cold! Lady Eluned, please heal her!"
Reina, the referee, raised her hand, taking a deep breath to officially call the fight and declare the Starlight Arcanist the victor.
Aeliana slowly stood up from her crouch. The Elf brushed a speck of snow off her white silk robes with her chest heaving slightly.
She looked across the courtyard at the crumpled form of her rival with a look of genuine pity crossing her elegant features.
"She fought bravely..." Aeliana murmured, turning her head to look back at Silas for his approval.
Silas didn’t look at Aeliana.
His golden-ringed eyes were locked with focus on Rowenna’s crumpled body.
’Look at her feet,’ Silas thought.

While Rowenna had been getting her face boxed in, while she was getting brutally dismantled by the combo, and while she was tumbling helplessly through the freezing slush... Silas had seen something completely unnatural.
Her bare toes had been dragging through the snow.
As she rolled across the slate tiles, her toes had carved deep and perfectly straight, geometric lines into the mud beneath the frost.
At the edge of the ring, Rowenna lay face down in the snow.
Slowly, agonizingly, her right hand twitched.
She didn’t push herself up.
She simply slapped her bloody, bruised palm flat against the wet slate tiles, pressing her hand directly into the center of the geometric lines she had carved with her feet.
Rowenna coughed, a thick mouthful of blood spilling onto the ice.
She weakly turned her head, looking through the blizzard directly at Aeliana.
Her left eye was completely swollen shut, her lip was split, and her ribs were screaming but the unyielding grin that broke across her bloody face was quite terrifying.
"Checkmate... you pointy-eared bitch," Rowenna croaked.
The moment her hand touched the snow, the ambient mana in the courtyard violently inverted.
FZZZZZZZZT!
A blinding dense flash of deep violet light erupted from the ground directly beneath Aeliana’s boots.
The lines Rowenna had carved during her beating connected perfectly.
The entire section of the courtyard beneath the Elf flared with the unmistakable geometry of a crafted magical array.
Runic Gravity Well (10x).
Aeliana’s silver eyes widened in horror.
Before the Elf could even attempt to cast her Aegis shield, the spell activated.
The gravity within a twenty-foot radius of the violet circle instantly, violently multiplied by a factor of ten.
CRACK!
The thick slate tiles beneath Aeliana’s feet immediately buckled and shattered under the sheer atmospheric pressure.
Aeliana didn’t just fall; she was physically slammed down into the ground by an invisible crushing skyscraper of gravity.
She hit the floorboards on her hands and knees with a sickening thud with the breath exploding from her lungs.
The snow around her was instantly compressed into solid, flat sheets of black ice from the downforce.
"Augh!"
The Elf let out a choked scream of agony, her pristine white robes pressing flat against her skin as her bones groaned under the weight of her own body mass being multiplied tenfold.
The girls erupted into chaos.
"YES!" Morwenna roared at the top of her lungs, throwing her hands in the air. "DIRTY PIRATE TACTICS! SHE SET A TRAP WHILE SHE WAS GETTING HER TEETH KICKED IN! THAT’S MY KIND OF MAGE!"
Eluned narrowed her glowing green eyes, genuinely impressed by the masochistic dedication it took to maintain a complex runic casting sequence while actively suffering a concussion.

"She weaponized her own defeat," Eluned murmured, looking at the bloody B-Rank mage with newfound respect. "She deliberately baited Aeliana into a false sense of security... That’s quite outstanding, and Aeliana isn’t doing so bad either."
Silas crossed his arms with a grin breaking across his face.
’That’s my girl,’ Silas thought proudly. ’Both of them... now Aeli, I want to see how you break past this.’
In the center of the violet circle, Aeliana was completely pinned to the shattering slate.
She couldn’t lift her arms and she couldn’t stand up.
The gravity was so intense it felt like her internal organs were being slowly dragged out of her back.
The physical superiority she possessed as an A-Rank Elf was neutralized; muscles meant absolutely nothing when the planet itself was trying to swallow you whole.
Rowenna slowly, painfully pushed herself up onto her knees outside the perimeter of the gravity well.
She wiped the blood from her chin with her blue eyes full of triumph.
She raised her right hand, channeling her remaining mana reserves, preparing to drop a massive Ignis Rune directly onto the pinned Elf and end the match with a pillar of superheated fire.
’I have her,’ Rowenna thought with her heart pounding. ’I did it.’
Inside the crushing violet well, Aeliana forced her head up, her eyes locking onto the glowing crimson rune forming in Rowenna’s hand.
Aeliana bared her teeth in a furious snarl.
"I am not... done!" Aeliana ground out through clenched teeth.
She couldn’t move her body, so she abandoned physical movement entirely.
Aeliana closed her eyes, entirely bypassing the crushing physical gravity, and aggressively tapped directly into her A-Rank mana core.

The air around her pinned body began to hum with a high-pitched vibrating sound as brilliant blinding particles of blue-white starlight began to bleed directly out of her skin, swirling wildly in the heavy air.
Silas’s eyes widened. "She’s bending the space?"
Rowenna saw the starlight gathering.
She panicked, accelerating her casting speed.
The crimson Ignis Rune finalized in her palm and she thrust her hand forward, unleashing a massive roaring torrent of superheated fire directly at the pinned Elf.
The fire crossed the courtyard, melting the snow instantly into a cloud of thick, blinding steam but a microsecond before the flames engulfed her, Aeliana screamed.
’Spatial Teleportation!’
BOOM!
The space inside the gravity well violently warped as the air displaced with the sound of a thunderclap.
The fire washed over the slate tiles, completely incinerating the spot where Aeliana had just been kneeling but the Elf wasn’t there.
Rowenna’s head snapped upward, her eyes frantically searching the blizzard.
Thirty feet straight up in the freezing air, hovering completely unaffected by the 10x gravity field anchored to the ground below, Aeliana materialized out of a flash of blue-white starlight.
The Elf was floating in the sky with her white robes fluttering wildly in the howling blizzard.
She was panting heavily, her mana core screaming from the sheer cost of forcing a spatial teleportation while under the crushing influence of a gravity well but she was free.
’And now... I have the high ground.’

The air around her pinned body began to hum with a high-pitched vibrating sound as brilliant blinding particles of blue-white starlight began to bleed directly out of her skin, swirling wildly in the heavy air.
Silas’s eyes widened.
"She’s bending the space?"
Rowenna saw the starlight gathering.
She panicked, accelerating her casting speed.
The crimson Ignis Rune finalized in her palm and she thrust her hand forward, unleashing a massive roaring torrent of superheated fire directly at the pinned Elf.
The fire crossed the courtyard, melting the snow instantly into a cloud of thick, blinding steam but a microsecond before the flames engulfed her, Aeliana screamed.
’Spatial Teleportation!’
BOOM!
The space inside the gravity well violently warped as the air displaced with the sound of a thunderclap.
The fire washed over the slate tiles, completely incinerating the spot where Aeliana had just been kneeling but the Elf wasn’t there.
Rowenna’s head snapped upward, her eyes frantically searching the blizzard.
Thirty feet straight up in the freezing air, hovering completely unaffected by the 10x gravity field anchored to the ground below, Aeliana materialized out of a flash of blue-white starlight.
The Elf was floating in the sky with her white robes fluttering wildly in the howling blizzard.
She was panting heavily, her mana core screaming from the sheer cost of forcing a spatial teleportation while under the crushing influence of a gravity well but she was free.
’And now...
I have the high ground.’

chapters.title: Chapter 156: Aeliana Vs. Rowenna [III / Bonus Chapter]
paragraphs: Aeliana raised both of her hands high above her head.
The sky above the Keep literally darkened as the ambient starlight mana in the atmosphere violently converged upon her location.
"Burn," Aeliana commanded coldly. "Starfall Barrage."
Ten volatile orbs of pure compressed starlight materialized in the air around her floating form.
They pulsed with destructive arcane energy, humming like miniature suns.
With a vicious downward sweep of her arms, Aeliana launched the barrage.
The starlight orbs rained down from the sky like an orbital artillery strike, seeking Rowenna with guided precision.
The crowd of girls screamed, frantically scrambling backward to get out of the blast radius.
"Hold the line!" Silas roared.
He didn’t pull his sword.
Silas stepped forward, instantly projecting his golden aura in a massive invisible dome over the spectators, creating a buffer to ensure none of his recruits caught a stray magical attack.
Rowenna looked up at the incoming orbital strike.
She didn’t have time to run and she didn’t have the physical speed to dodge.
Rowenna slammed both of her hands into the snow, screaming as she burned her rapidly depleting mana reserves.
Kinetic Repulsion Field!
A violent translucent dome of reversed gravity exploded outward from Rowenna’s body just as the first starlight orb made impact.
KA-BOOM!
The explosion was apocalyptic.
The starlight orb detonated against the repulsion field with a blinding flash of blue-white energy.
The shockwave ripped across the courtyard, instantly vaporizing the surrounding snowdrifts into a massive, choking cloud of hot white steam.
KA-BOOM! KA-BOOM! KA-BOOM!
Three more starlight orbs slammed into the barrier in rapid succession.
The shockwaves overlapped, shaking the very foundations of the library.
Inside the repulsion dome, Rowenna dropped to one knee with blood pouring from her nose.
The strain of holding a kinetic shield against an A-Rank Epic bombardment was physically tearing her apart.
The dome cracked, splintering like fragile glass.
’I can’t hold it,’ Rowenna realized desperately with her B-Rank core flashing a dangerous hollow red in her mind. ’She’s going to crack the shield... I have to go on the offensive!’
Rowenna dropped the repulsion field entirely.
She didn’t wait for the steam to clear, Rowena relied on her instinct.
Rowenna swept her hands across the frozen ground, rapidly etching two distinct complex runic circles into the ice simultaneously.
Glacial Rune! Fulgur Rune!
The ambient temperature in the courtyard plummeted even further.

A massive array of freezing sapphire light erupted from the ground as dozens of razor-sharp, six-foot-tall spikes of solid glacial ice shot upward through the thick steam, seeking the floating Elf in the sky.
But the ice wasn’t just physical damage...
Wrapped tightly around the rising glacial spikes was a violent seeking web of high-voltage golden lightning.
The Fulgur Rune chained perfectly with the ice, turning the physical projectiles into electrically charged surface-to-air missiles.
High above, Aeliana saw the golden lightning cutting through the steam.
Because she had burned so much mana on the teleportation and the barrage, she couldn’t afford to cast another Aegis shield in mid-air so she had to rely on agility.
Using her Elven Swiftness, Aeliana literally surfed the shockwaves of her own explosions.
She kicked off a pocket of dense air, twisting her body with acrobatic grace.
Three electrified ice spikes tore through the space where her torso had just been, grazing her ribs and singing the fabric of her white robes with the smell of sharp ozone.
As she flipped through the air, completely inverted, Aeliana extended her right index finger, pointing it directly down through the steam at Rowenna’s blurry silhouette.
’Arcane Piercer.’
A hyper-compressed beam of destructive blue starlight lanced from her fingertip, shooting downward with the speed of a laser.
Rowenna saw the blue flash and she slammed her palm into the dirt.
Terra Rune!
A massive six-inch-thick slab of razor-sharp obsidian erupted from the bedrock, forming a crude barricade directly in front of her.
The Arcane Piercer slammed into the obsidian.
The high-tier starlight laser punched directly through the solid rock as if it were wet tissue paper, melting the edges of the hole into glowing slag.
The beam didn’t hit Rowenna center-mass but it grazed her left shoulder.
"Ahhhh!"
Rowenna screamed as the intense compressed heat of the laser instantly cauterized the flesh, sending her spinning into the snow.
Aeliana hit the ground, landing in a graceful three-point crouch on the edge of the courtyard.
The blizzard howled around them.
The steam from the melted snow slowly began to clear, revealing the unmitigated destruction they had unleashed upon the courtyard.
The slate tiles were shattered, cratered with scorch marks, covered in jagged ice spikes, and littered with chunks of obsidian.
The two mages stood thirty feet apart, staring at each other through the swirling white flakes.
Both of them were completely running on fumes and Silas looked at their statuses again.

’Rowenna’s mana is at eighty,’ Silas noted, his eyes narrowing. ’Aeliana is sitting at roughly one hundred and fifty... Neither of them has enough juice in the tank to cast a wide-area spell or a high-tier barrier so they’re quite dry.’
Rowenna was swaying on her feet. Her left eye was completely swollen shut, blood was pouring down her chin, and her left arm hung limply at her side from the laser graze.
Her chest heaved, her breath coming in ragged, painful gasps.
Aeliana didn’t look much better. The pristine, elegant Elf was covered in dirt and soot.
Her expensive white spider-silk robes were torn, scorched by lightning, and soaked in freezing slush.
Her silver hair was a tangled, wild mess, and her green eyes were slightly unfocused from the severe mana drain.
They locked eyes through the storm.
There were no more tricks, no more traps and no more wide-area bombardments. It was going to end in one final brutal clash.
’Fuck it...’ Rowena thought as she channeled every last, agonizing drop of her eighty remaining mana directly into her right fist.
She didn’t etch a rune on the floor.
She etched the glowing crimson geometry of an Ignis Rune directly onto her own bleeding knuckles and her fist erupted into a ball of superheated roaring flame.
Aeliana didn’t back down.
The Elf pulled the last dregs of starlight from her core, wrapping the blue-white energy tightly around her right forearm, forming a crude condensed Arcane Aegis gauntlet over her fist.
They charged.

They ran directly across the shattered freezing courtyard, screaming at the top of their lungs, ignoring the blizzard, ignoring the pain and ignoring the terrified cheers of the seventy women watching them.
They met in the dead center of the ring and they simply threw everything they had left into one final devastating strike.
Rowenna’s flaming rune-etched right cross smashed directly into Aeliana’s jaw.
Aeliana’s starlight-coated armor-piercing right straight buried itself sickeningly deep into the center of Rowenna’s bruised ribs.
BOOM!
The simultaneous impact was deafening.
A massive, circular shockwave of concussive force, mixed with explosive crimson fire and blinding blue starlight, erupted outward from the point of impact.
The shockwave completely blew the falling snow away, clearing a fifty-foot radius of perfectly dry air in the middle of the blizzard.
A thick cloud of gray smoke and white steam engulfed the center of the ring, completely obscuring the two combatants from sight.
The courtyard was dead silent.
Nobody cheered and nobody moved. Silas slowly lowered his arm with the barrier dissipating as the energy faded.
The freezing wind howled, slowly dragging the thick smoke away. As the steam cleared, the silhouettes of the two mages slowly became visible.
They were both standing.
They were standing inches apart, staring directly into each other’s eyes with their fists still pressed against each other’s bodies.
Rowenna stared at the Elf.
Her thoughts were completely silent for a long moment then, a dull hum filled her ears.
’F-fuck...’
She couldn’t feel her legs anymore. They felt like they were made of water.
The fire on her knuckles had completely died out, leaving behind nothing but cold bruised flesh.
She looked at Aeliana.
The Elf’s jaw was bruised a dark angry purple from the flaming punch. Aeliana was swaying violently in the wind, her green eyes looking unfocused while staring blankly ahead.
But Aeliana was still standing. Her Epic-Rank biology was keeping her upright through stubborn pride.
Rowenna on the other hand felt the darkness creeping into the edges of her vision as the world began to tilt sideways.
’I lose,’ Rowenna realized with a crushing sense of failure washing over her numb brain. ’I gave her everything... and she’s still standing.’
She felt her knees buckle as the freezing wind felt strangely warm.
’If only...’ Rowenna thought, her vision turning completely black as she began to fall backward toward the slush. ’If only... If only I was a little bit stronge—’
Rowenna’s eyes rolled back.
She collapsed completely, falling backward and hitting the snow-covered slate with a soft, final thud.
Rowena fainted.
Reina, standing frozen on the edge of the blast radius, raised her spear high into the air.
"The match is over!" Reina announced, her voice echoing over the blizzard. "The winner is Aeliana!"
The girls erupted.
The cheers were deafening, a massive roaring wave of respect for the two mages who had just turned a snowy courtyard into a apocalypse.
Morwenna whistled loudly, while Brida immediately sprinted forward with three glowing green healing potions in her hands that Eluned made.
In the center of the ring, Aeliana stood perfectly still.
She heard the cheers and she heard Reina announce her name.
A slow and incredibly genuine smile broke across her battered, soot-stained face.
She slowly turned her head, her unfocused green eyes searching the crowd until they locked onto the tall broad-shouldered silhouette of Silas standing there.
She held his gaze for exactly one second then, Aeliana’s eyes rolled back in her head.
Her knees completely gave out beneath her.
The Starlight Arcanist folded like a marionette with its strings cut, falling face-first straight down into the freezing snow, utterly and completely unconscious.
But as the darkness took her, a single incredibly happy thought echoed through her exhausted mind.
’I did it... My Lord...’
Rowenna woke up with a sharp gasp with her blue eyes snapping open as a dull, throbbing ache radiated directly outward from the center of her ribcage.
"Haah... Haah..."
She was lying on her back.
The air around her smelled of crushed herbs and damp linen, rather than the snow she had been in.
She blinked, her vision slowly clearing, and realized she was staring up at the familiar beams of the Barracks.
She felt something damp and cool resting across her forehead.
Rowenna reached up with a weak hand, pulling a cold wet towel off her brow. She slowly turned her head.
Silas was sitting right beside her cot.
The Lord had pulled up a heavy wooden chair, his broad shoulders hunched forward slightly with his forearms resting on his knees as he watched her wake up.
He had taken off his dark trench coat, wearing only his fitted black shirt.
The moment she saw him, the adrenaline and pride that had fueled her through the blizzard completely evaporated.
The reality of the match... the memory of her knees buckling in the snow and Aeliana’s eyes staring down at her crashed into her mind.
"I lost," Rowenna whispered with her voice cracking slightly.
She didn’t try to sit up; she just stared at the ceiling, her chest tightening with crushing failure.
"I’m sorry, Lord Graves. I’m so sorry. I really wanted to embark on that whole journey to the Secret Realm with you."
She swallowed hard, her fingers digging tightly into the rough fabric of her wool blanket. "If I was just stronger... if I had just managed to hold the repulsion field a second longer..."
Silas let out a slow sigh.
He didn’t lecture her.
Silas leaned forward. He reached out with his large right hand, resting his palm gently on the crown of her messy, sweat-dampened blue hair.
He patted her head slowly, running his fingers through the blue strands with a reassuring warmth.
Rowenna froze. She slowly turned her head back to look at him, her blue eyes wide and shining with unshed tears.

"You fought an A-Rank Epic Hero in close quarters, Rowenna and no offense but you’re just a troop." Silas told her, she couldn’t hear any bit of disappointment in his voice. "So naturally a Hero is superior..."
He looked her directly in the face with his golden-ringed eyes locking onto hers.

"You weaponized your own defeat. You baited her into a trap while you were actively getting your ribs broken, and you forced her to burn her entire mana core just to survive. You didn’t lose because you were weak but you lost because you ran out of juice."
He offered her a small smirk. "Next time, you’ll pin her to the floor before she can even blink. You just need more reps."
’I already told Aeli her own motivational words... I have to keep the two of them active yunno.’

chapters.title: Chapter 157: Preparations For Valoria Academy [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Rowenna stared at him.
The unshakeable confidence he had in her potential... the certainty that she would win the rematch made her breath catch in her throat.

"Thank you, my Lord," Rowenna whispered fervently with her loyalty spiking into the stratosphere as she grabbed the edge of the blanket. "I promise you. I will grow stronger... For your sake. I won’t ever fall in the snow again."
"I know you won’t," Silas replied, giving her hair one last pat. "I’ll be waiting."
Rowenna’s face instantly flushed a brilliant hot shade of crimson.
’Lord Graves...’
Silas chuckled, standing up from the wooden chair.
He left the Runic Arcanist to rest and walked out of the cramped sleeping quarters.
The barracks were relatively quiet.

The seventy-three soldiers were currently split across the Keep; half of them were still browsing the new Tier 3 Library, while the other half were gathered in the lower communal floor of the barracks, warming up by the massive stone hearth.
As Silas descended the wooden stairs to the lower floor, he heard a loud overlapping chorus of voices echoing near the hearth.
He reached the bottom step and saw a bizarre concentrated briefing taking place.
Aeliana was sitting on a sturdy wooden bench near the fire.
The Starlight Arcanist had changed out of her ruined, scorched white robes and was now wearing a simple, clean linen tunic.
Eluned had healed her bruised purple jaw from Rowenna’s flaming punch and now she looked completely focused.
Surrounding her in a tight semi-circle were Eluned, Morwenna, Brida, and Thora.

The two divine beings and the other women were aggressively advising the Elf on what to do when she accompanied their Lord into the Secret Realm, specifically regarding her interactions with the other Lords on Earth.

"If another Lord looks at the Warlord for longer than three seconds," Morwenna instructed loudly, slamming her fist into her palm, "you drop her... You don’t ask questions and you don’t negotiate. You just break her knees and throw her into the nearest ditch."
"Do not be barbaric, pirate," Eluned corrected her smoothly, adjusting her green silk dress.
The Goddess of Nature leaned closer to Aeliana as her green eyes flashed with malice.

"Aeliana, you must employ psychological dominance... If this woman attempts to assert authority over our Lord, you simply remind her that she is a transient weed, and you are the apex flora. You show them exactly what their place is beneath the Blessed Land."
"And if she tries to get handsy with the Warlord," Thora chimed in, holding her alcohol mug high, "you remind her that he prefers women with actual big breasts! Tell her to go eat a loaf of bread!"

Aeliana was blushing a brilliant shade of pink, completely overwhelmed by the territoriality of her peers but she nodded firmly, her silver eyes burning with serious commitment to the mission parameters.
Then, Aeliana looked past the crowd and saw Silas standing at the bottom of the stairs.
She immediately stood up from the bench, brushing past the commanders, and stopped directly in front of him.
"I have won, Lord Graves," Aeliana stated, her voice carrying a soft fierce pride.
She bowed her head slightly. "I will enjoy being your weapon in the dark."
Silas smiled, reaching out and placing a heavy, reassuring hand on her slender shoulder.

"I’ll be glad to have you watching my back, Aeli," Silas told her honestly. "The raid is in three days and I don’t have the exact coordinates yet. I’ll get more information when I’m back on Earth tomorrow morning."
The entire room went dead silent.
Eluned blinked, her delicate brow furrowing in deep divine confusion. She took a step forward, looking at him as if he had just spoken in ancient dwarven.
"My Lord..." Eluned started slowly. "You just got back. You ascended mere hours ago and you have to go back again tomorrow?"
"Yeah," Silas nodded, letting his hand drop from Aeliana’s shoulder.
He looked around at the disappointed faces of his women. "Yes, Elu. I have to put my sister in school."
All women present on the lower floor of the barracks stopped completely still.
They looked at him like he was talking absolute, unfiltered gibberish.
Eluned blinked rapidly, her flawless face completely blank.
"S-sister?" Eluned repeated with her voice pitching up slightly.
The Lord... their Lord... had a sister? A little sister? That he was taking to school?
[The Next morning.]
The early sunlight of Valoria City filtered through the expensive, reinforced glass windows of the Silverleaf apartment.
Downstairs in the modern kitchen, Lia was practically skipping across the hardwood floor.
The eleven-year-old girl was wearing her brand-new tailored denim pants and a soft dark blue breathable shirt.
She was currently standing on her stool by the marble island, making tea while humming a bright, off-key tune about going to school.
"Hmmm~ Books and pens to write and write~"
She poured the boiling water into two ceramic mugs, letting the expensive tea bags steep.
Silas stepped downstairs a few minutes later.

He was wearing clean comfortable civilian clothes... a fitted dark gray henley and sturdy black trousers and currently he was rubbing the back of his neck, having just gotten off a lengthy encrypted phone call upstairs.
He walked into the kitchen and sat down at the island.
Lia immediately slid one of the steaming ceramic mugs across the marble counter toward him, offering him a bright incredibly eager smile.
"Good morning Big brother... have a drink."
Silas looked down at the dark aromatic liquid. He raised an eyebrow, looking back up at the eleven-year-old former pickpocket.
"Is this spiked?" Silas joked deadpan, picking up the mug.
"Big Bro!" Lia gasped with her cheeks puffing out in cheeky offense. "I am trying to be a refined student! I wouldn’t poison your tea! I didn’t even steal the tea bags... you bought them last night!"
Silas chuckled, taking a slow sip of the hot tea. It was actually perfectly brewed.

"I just got off the phone," Silas told her, setting the mug down. "I spoke with the Principal’s secretary at the Valoria City Academy. I booked a direct meeting with the man for this morning so we’re going in to get you registered and tested for placement."
Lia’s eyes widened.
She grabbed her own mug, her hands shaking slightly with pure excitement.

"That’s good," Lia said, her voice dropping into a soft, deeply sincere whisper. She looked at him over the rim of her cup. "My Big brother is working so hard for me so I should be a good little sister and work hard for him too."
Silas smiled warmly. He reached across the marble island and patted the crown of her hair, ruffling the messy brown strands.
They finished their tea quickly and they moved to the front door.
Silas placed his hand on the metal panel, temporarily disengaging the heavy glowing Spirit Lock to let them pass.

Once they stepped out into the hallway, he pressed his palm against the exterior scanner, re-engaging the dense mana ward to ensure the apartment remained completely impenetrable while they were gone.
CLICK!
Both of them were outside now and the rain from the previous night had completely cleared, leaving the cobblestone streets clean and shining in the morning sun.
Silas walked down the sidewalk, stopping near the edge of the immaculate, gated community.

He looked at his own completely empty driveway slot then, he glanced across the street. His next-door neighbor... a wealthy corporate executive had a sleek glowing silver anti-grav sedan parked elegantly in his designated spot.
Silas crossed his arms, looking down at Lia.

"You know," Silas joked dryly, tilting his head toward the empty driveway. "I have enough liquid capital right now. I should probably buy a supercar like the midnight-blue one Elora used to pick us up yesterday. It would make the commute easier."
Lia instantly spazzed out.
Her financial trauma flared back to life with a vengeance as she grabbed his arm, violently shaking her head back and forth.

"No!" Lia shrieked, completely horrified by the prospect of him spending more money. "No supercars! I don’t want to ride in an extra expensive car! It’s a terrible investment! If we go broke again and want to sell it, it wouldn’t even go for half the price! The depreciation rate on those models is awful! Big Brother, please don’t buy a car!"
Silas sighed, rubbing the bridge of his nose.
Money was not an issue anymore.
He could generate another two million credits tonight just by dumping more Star-Iron on Peter’s appraisal table but looking at her panicked face, he knew she wasn’t wrong about the depreciation rate.
And honestly, driving in Valoria City traffic sounded like a nightmare compared to just taking a cab.
’Besides I have to go get a driver’s license too...’ Silas thought.
"Fine. No supercar," Silas conceded.
He pulled his phone out of his pocket, opened the local transit app, and pinged a commercial cab.
Two minutes later, a standard yellow mag-cab pulled up to the curb, hovering silently on its repulsors.
Silas opened the back door, ushering his sister inside before sliding in next to her.
"Take us to Valoria City Academy..." Silas instructed the driver. "I’ll pay once we get there."
"You got it, boss," the driver replied, engaging the thrusters.
The mag-cab pulled smoothly away from the curb, accelerating down the cobblestone street and merging into the heavy morning traffic, leaving the Silverleaf district entirely behind.
As the yellow cab disappeared around a distant, sweeping curve in the road, the quiet residential street fell still.
Directly across from Silas’s apartment complex, sitting casually on a pristine white wrought-iron bench beneath a manicured oak tree, a figure moved.
Harper reached up and slowly took off her wide-brimmed sun hat.
The purple-haired girl stared down the empty street.
"He has a younger sister too, huh?" Harper muttered to herself with her voice becoming a low intrigued purr.
It was true.
After her rejection encounter at the Solstice Cafe, she had immediately run his name through the deep-dive Valoria City registry.

The algorithm had flagged his file, showing that Silas Graves had officially registered a dependent named Lia when he had been thirteen years old but the file noted she had been missing for two years.
Harper hadn’t expected them to be reunited and living together so soon.
A smile appeared on Harper’s lips.
"Well, that works for me," Harper murmured, tapping her manicured nails against the wooden slats of the bench.
She had been stalking him since dawn.
She hadn’t even bothered to actively hide her physical presence or mask her mana signature.
She knew Silas was capable of seeing through baseline stealth spells anyway. She was simply sitting in plain sight, observing his movement patterns.

’Not only is he going to the Secret Realm too...’ Harper thought, mentally reviewing the intel she had purchased from her father’s guild contacts last night, ’but he’s also taking his sister to the Academy... What a busy day for the Lord hehe~’
She leaned back against the bench.

While he was inside the Secret Realm, dealing with whatever ancient boss monster was guarding the vault, Harper already had a meticulous multi-step checklist of things she was going to do to ensure they grew significantly closer during the expedition.
She had already planned out the endgame. The raid was going to end with Silas taking her virginity.
’Oh my...’
Her cheeks turned a dusky pink.
It wasn’t because she was genuinely flustered or embarrassed by the prospect of intimacy.
It was the thrill of the entrapment itself.

’We won’t carry any condoms in our combat gear...’ Harper strategized. ’He’ll ravage me in the heat of the moment after the boss fight. He’ll finish inside and once he does... I already have the high-tier fertility pills.’
She was most certainly going to get pregnant!
And once she was carrying his child, the Lord of the Blessed Land wouldn’t have a choice.
She would use the pregnancy as unshakeable leverage for them to get married, permanently locking his unprecedented power and territorial assets into her father’s guild.
It was the ultimate acquisition but to execute the plan flawlessly, she needed a distraction.
’I need someone to establish a friendship with his sister...’
Harper reached into her designer jacket and brought out her encrypted gold-plated phone.
She dialed a highly secure number.
The phone rang twice then, a person on the other side answered the call.
"Hello?" the voice of a young girl echoed through the receiver, sounding bored and slightly annoyed.
Harper smiled.
"Hello, bitch," Harper greeted her cheerfully. "Would you like to go to Valoria Academy?"
There was a long pause on the other end of the line. The young girl clearly wasn’t expecting the offer.
"No," the girl replied bluntly.
Harper let out a long exasperated sigh. She raised her free hand, running her fingers through her sleek purple hair, completely unfazed by the rejection.
"Tsk, tsk, tsk..." Harper tutted softly into the receiver. "This simply won’t do."

"I promise you.
I will grow stronger...
For your sake.
I won’t ever fall in the snow again."
"I know you won’t," Silas replied, giving her hair one last pat.
"I’ll be waiting."
Rowenna’s face instantly flushed a brilliant hot shade of crimson.
’Lord Graves...’
Silas chuckled, standing up from the wooden chair.
He left the Runic Arcanist to rest and walked out of the cramped sleeping quarters.

The seventy-three soldiers were currently split across the Keep; half of them were still browsing the new Tier 3 Library, while the other half were gathered in the lower communal floor of the barracks, warming up by the massive stone hearth.

He reached the bottom step and saw a bizarre concentrated briefing taking place.
Aeliana was sitting on a sturdy wooden bench near the fire.
The Starlight Arcanist had changed out of her ruined, scorched white robes and was now wearing a simple, clean linen tunic.
Eluned had healed her bruised purple jaw from Rowenna’s flaming punch and now she looked completely focused.
Surrounding her in a tight semi-circle were Eluned, Morwenna, Brida, and Thora.

The two divine beings and the other women were aggressively advising the Elf on what to do when she accompanied their Lord into the Secret Realm, specifically regarding her interactions with the other Lords on Earth.
"If another Lord looks at the Warlord for longer than three seconds," Morwenna instructed loudly, slamming her fist into her palm, "you drop her...
You don’t ask questions and you don’t negotiate.
You just break her knees and throw her into the nearest ditch."
"Do not be barbaric, pirate," Eluned corrected her smoothly, adjusting her green silk dress.
The Goddess of Nature leaned closer to Aeliana as her green eyes flashed with malice.
"Aeliana, you must employ psychological dominance...
If this woman attempts to assert authority over our Lord, you simply remind her that she is a transient weed, and you are the apex flora.
You show them exactly what their place is beneath the Blessed Land."
"And if she tries to get handsy with the Warlord," Thora chimed in, holding her alcohol mug high, "you remind her that he prefers women with actual big breasts!
Tell her to go eat a loaf of bread!"

Aeliana was blushing a brilliant shade of pink, completely overwhelmed by the territoriality of her peers but she nodded firmly, her silver eyes burning with serious commitment to the mission parameters.
Then, Aeliana looked past the crowd and saw Silas standing at the bottom of the stairs.
She immediately stood up from the bench, brushing past the commanders, and stopped directly in front of him.
"I have won, Lord Graves," Aeliana stated, her voice carrying a soft fierce pride.
She bowed her head slightly.
"I will enjoy being your weapon in the dark."
Silas smiled, reaching out and placing a heavy, reassuring hand on her slender shoulder.
"I’ll be glad to have you watching my back, Aeli," Silas told her honestly.
"The raid is in three days and I don’t have the exact coordinates yet.
I’ll get more information when I’m back on Earth tomorrow morning."
The entire room went dead silent.
Eluned blinked, her delicate brow furrowing in deep divine confusion.
She took a step forward, looking at him as if he had just spoken in ancient dwarven.
"My Lord..." Eluned started slowly.
"You just got back.
You ascended mere hours ago and you have to go back again tomorrow?"
"Yeah," Silas nodded, letting his hand drop from Aeliana’s shoulder.
He looked around at the disappointed faces of his women.
"Yes, Elu.
I have to put my sister in school."
All women present on the lower floor of the barracks stopped completely still.
They looked at him like he was talking absolute, unfiltered gibberish.
Eluned blinked rapidly, her flawless face completely blank.
"S-sister?" Eluned repeated with her voice pitching up slightly.
The Lord... their Lord... had a sister?
A little sister?
That he was taking to school?

chapters.title: Chapter 158: Arrival At Valoria Academy
paragraphs: HUMM...
The hum of the yellow mag-cab’s repulsors changed into a whining decrescendo as the vehicle banked smoothly off the primary commercial thoroughfare of the Silverleaf district.
Silas sat in the back of the cab with his broad shoulders resting against the cracked leather seat, watching the city blur past the rain-streaked window.
The towering neon-drenched skyscrapers of the corporate zones were entirely gone now.
In their place, the architecture became more modern and the air practically smelled of elitism.
They were approaching the Valoria City Academy.
Even from six blocks away, the massive educational fortress dominated the skyline.
It wasn’t just a school... It was an architectural monument to the terrestrial awakened hierarchy.
’Well all big cities have their own Academies.’ Silas thought.

Massive spired towers constructed from polished white marble pierced the gray morning clouds. High stone walls, etched with glowing blue defensive runes, wrapped around an estate that looked large enough to house a small country’s standing army.
Sitting right next to him, Lia had her small hands pressed flat against the glass of the window with her breath fogging up the pane.
Her brown eyes were wide as dinner plates.
She was practically vibrating with a mixture of hype and deep terror.

"Big brother..." Lia whispered with her voice barely audible over the hum of the cab. "It’s... it’s huge. It looks like a castle. Are you sure I’m supposed to go here? This doesn’t look like a place for people from the outer wards."

"It’s the Academy," Silas replied smoothly, leaning forward and resting his forearms on his knees. "And you aren’t from the outer wards anymore, Lia... You’re a resident of the Silverleaf district. You belong here just as much as any of the brats walking those halls."
He reached over and gently tapped his index finger against the glass, pointing toward the massive central spire of the campus.

"Besides," Silas explained. "The system here is very standard. Since you’re eleven years old, you’re exactly at the baseline age for the primary student intake. You’ll be placed in the foundational sector with the other kids your age. You learn mathematics, terrestrial history, basic mana theory, and core biology."
Lia pulled her face away from the glass, looking up at him with wide eyes.
"How long do I have to stay?"
"Until you’re eighteen," Silas told her flatly.
Lia blinked. "Eighteen? That’s seven years of school!"

"That’s until Awakening Day," Silas corrected her, his golden-ringed eyes narrowing slightly at the memory of his own brutal, grinding experience inside those walls. "The Academy isn’t just about reading books, Lia... It’s like a pressure cooker. They feed you nutrients, they teach you how the Sovereign Realm works, and they push your limits... When you turn eighteen, you undergo the Awakening Ceremony. If you possess a latent spark, your core ignites. You become a Lord and you could get drafted by a guild though you won’t need to, you have your big bro after all."
He leaned back against the leather seat.

"If you don’t awaken... you graduate with a standard corporate degree and you get a comfortable high-paying desk job in the inner city. Either way, you never have to sleep in a damp alleyway ever again."
The weight of that promise completely overrode Lia’s anxiety.
The idea of seven years of guaranteed safety and an actual future made her chest tighten.
She didn’t look terrified anymore.
A fierce brilliant spark of excitement ignited in her dark eyes as she puffed out her chest, adjusting the collar of her brand-new dark blue shirt.
"I’m going to be the smartest kid in the whole building," Lia declared with her confidence returning in full force. "I’m going to learn everything."
"Don’t get cocky. Just pass the entrance interview first," Silas chuckled.
The mag-cab pulled to a smooth hovering halt directly in front of the colossal wrought-iron front gates of the Valoria City Academy.
"Here we are, boss," the driver announced through the partition. "Valoria Academy, main entrance."
Silas pulled his Association-issued phone from his pocket, tapping the digital meter on the back of the driver’s headrest.
The screen chimed, instantly transferring the required Spirit Credits plus a generous twenty percent tip directly to the driver’s account.
"Thanks," Silas said, pushing the heavy passenger door open.
He stepped out onto the pristine swept cobblestones.
Lia scrambled out right behind him, instantly grabbing the edge of his dark trench coat as the intimidating scale of the front gates loomed over them.
The cab hummed with its repulsors flaring as it pulled away from the curb and drove off down the street, leaving them standing alone in front of the massive entrance.
Silas looked up at the gates.
Standing directly in the center of the walkway, positioned beneath a towering stone archway, was an armored Academy security guard.
The man looked incredibly tired.

He had dark circles under his eyes with his posture was slightly slumped, and he was holding a high-tier corporate-issued mana rifle loosely across his chest, looking like a bored worker counting down the minutes until his shift ended.
’Tired, my ass,’ Silas thought with his golden-ringed eyes lazily scanning the shadows cast by the high stone walls.
His Gold Core passively heightened his sensory perception, picking up the subtle suppressed magical frequencies bleeding into the morning air.
He felt them.
Thirty feet to the left, perched on a recessed stone gargoyle, was a stealthed archer.
Forty feet to the right, hidden behind an optical illusion barrier near the guardhouse, was a high-tier elemental mage.
Directly above the archway, concealed in the iron latticework, was an sniper with a kinetic suppression rifle aimed directly at the back of Silas’s skull.

’It’s a prestigious Academy after all...’ Silas thought with a sigh, keeping his hands perfectly visible. ’It housed Elora Verinda, the City Lord’s daughter, and half the heirs to the major Valoria guilds. Of course they aren’t relying on one bored guy with a flashlight. They need to be prepared for corporate espionage, rival guild assassinations, and terror attacks... The bored guy at the gate is just the bait to make intruders lower their guard.’
Silas didn’t react to the snipers,he had long since knew that they existed since he was a student here before.
He simply walked forward with his boots clicking against the stone and Lia trailing nervously in his shadow.
As they approached the gate, the tired-looking guard raised his free hand, holding up his palm to halt their progress.

"Hold it right there, citizen," the guard commanded, his bored tone perfectly rehearsed. "This is a restricted academic zone... I need to see proper identification and an authorized visit ticket before you take another step."
Silas didn’t argue.
He didn’t flex his aura or try to intimidate the man as he simply reached into the inner pocket of his dark trench coat, pulled out his metallic Lord ID card, and handed it directly to the guard.
The guard took the card with a lazy sigh, glancing down at the polished metal surface.
The microsecond the guard’s eyes registered the engraved name and the glowing blue core verification stamp on the corner of the card, his entire demeanor shattered immediately.
The man’s jaw literally dropped.
His eyes bugged out of his skull, darting frantically from the heavy metallic card up to the towering ridiculously broad-shouldered man standing in front of him.
He knew that name... Of course he did.
Silas Graves.
He was a really good student who came to school using the Mag-Train from the slums but... when did Silas Graves become this beautiful?
The guard stared at Silas’s handsome face, the messy dark hair, and the terrifying physique he had stretching the fabric of his dark shirt.

’This hunk of a man in front of me is Silas Graves?!’ the guard thought with his mind completely short-circuiting. ’Is this really someone who used to be from the slums?! He looks like he eats bears for breakfast!’
"L-Lord Graves!" the guard stuttered violently with his tired facade evaporating into panic.
His hands were shaking so hard he almost dropped the heavy ID card.
He frantically thrust the card back toward Silas, bowing so deeply he nearly snapped his own spine in half.
"I-I apologize! Congratulations on your successful awakening! Congratulations on becoming a Lord!"
"Thanks," Silas replied smoothly, plucking the card from the trembling man’s fingers and sliding it back into his coat pocket.
He gestured casually toward the sprawling campus behind the gates. "I’m going to see the Principal. I booked a meeting this morning."
The guard swallowed incredibly hard, sweat beading on his forehead.
On normal grounds, standard procedure dictated that even mid-tier corporate parents needed an authorized digitally verified visitation ticket signed in triplicate just to get past the courtyard.
But Silas Graves was a Lord...

And he wasn’t just a normal, bottom-feeding entry-level Lord either. The glowing stamp on his ID officially designated him as a Blue Core Lord... a tier that placed him quite high up in the terrestrial societal ladder.
You didn’t ask a Blue Core Lord for a piece of paper. You opened the gates and prayed he didn’t decide to obliterate your guardhouse for being mildly annoying.

"O-of course, Lord Graves! No ticket required for a Lord of your standing!" the guard babbled quickly, stepping hastily to the side and aggressively tapping the glowing green release rune on the control pedestal.
The massive wrought-iron gates groaned, smoothly swinging inward to grant them access.

"You will need to head directly toward the central administrative spire," the guard instructed, pointing a shaking finger down the main pristine walkway. "Just follow the cobblestones past the fountain. You’ll have to enter campu—"
Before the guard could even finish his sentence, the mahogany front doors of the administrative building located just inside the gates clicked and swung open.
A woman stepped outside.
She was the Principal’s secretary.

She was a tall and incredibly stunning woman in her mid-twenties. The woman had sleek and perfectly straightened black hair that cascaded down her back, piercing gray eyes, and a flawlessly beautiful manicured face.
She was wearing a tight, tailored gray pencil skirt and a crisp white blouse, holding a digital corporate clipboard against her chest.
She stopped at the top of the marble steps, her gray eyes locking onto Silas instantly.
"Lord Graves," the Secretary called out, her voice was a smooth alluring purr that carried easily across the courtyard.
She offered a deep respectful bow hiking up her skirt a bit in the process.
"Welcome back to Valoria Academy and welcome to your little sister as well. The Principal is waiting for you in his office. I will guide you there personally."
As she straightened up, her gray eyes swept over Silas’s towering muscled frame.
A visible flush of pink spread across her high cheekbones as she bit her lower lip slightly with her professional demeanor cracking as she actively checked him out from head to toe.
Silas looked at the flushed beautiful Secretary but he didn’t blush back.
He just reached down, firmly grasped Lia’s small hand to ensure she didn’t wander off, and looked at the woman with exhausted eyes.
Silas had not been here for even an hour yet and he already wanted to go home.
"Alright," Silas said flatly. "Let’s follow her."
He walked through the open iron gates, stepping onto the pristine Academy grounds.
As they followed the swaying hips of the Secretary down the wide manicured cobblestone path, Silas let out a long bitter internal sigh.
’I’m still trying to understand,’ Silas thought, staring at the back of the Secretary’s head. ’Of all the girls in this Academy, why her?’
He remembered her perfectly.

Back when he was an exhausted student at this exact Academy, busting his ass on four hours of sleep just to maintain his baseline grades, he had actually harbored a massive unrequited crush on this exact woman.
She had been a senior administrative assistant at the time. She was beautiful, unattainable, and always smelled like expensive perfume but the illusion had shattered violently during his third year.
He hadn’t learned the truth through some dramatic confrontation.
He had just been emptying the trash bins near the faculty parking garage late one night to earn extra meal credits when he accidentally overheard a conversation.
He had learned the beautiful Secretary was nothing more than one of the many, easily replaceable side pieces belonging to Elora Verinda’s older cousin.
She didn’t care about hard work, and she certainly didn’t care about scrawny slum kids with good grades.

’And Elora’s cousin is an irredeemable piece of garbage,’ Silas thought with a shake of his head. ’I really do not want to meet that guy in the Secret Realm expedition in some days... If I see his smug face in the dark, I might accidentally let Aeliana kill that fucker and blame it on the boss monster.’
And it wasn’t even about the crush, that fucker wasn’t even in this school and had disrespected him on multiple occasions.
’If I do see him, I’ll get him back for all of that.’

sentences.text: HUMM...
The hum of the yellow mag-cab’s repulsors changed into a whining decrescendo as the vehicle banked smoothly off the primary commercial thoroughfare of the Silverleaf district.
Silas sat in the back of the cab with his broad shoulders resting against the cracked leather seat, watching the city blur past the rain-streaked window.
The towering neon-drenched skyscrapers of the corporate zones were entirely gone now.
In their place, the architecture became more modern and the air practically smelled of elitism.
They were approaching the Valoria City Academy.
Even from six blocks away, the massive educational fortress dominated the skyline.
It wasn’t just a school...
It was an architectural monument to the terrestrial awakened hierarchy.
’Well all big cities have their own Academies.’ Silas thought.
Massive spired towers constructed from polished white marble pierced the gray morning clouds.
High stone walls, etched with glowing blue defensive runes, wrapped around an estate that looked large enough to house a small country’s standing army.
Sitting right next to him, Lia had her small hands pressed flat against the glass of the window with her breath fogging up the pane.
Her brown eyes were wide as dinner plates.
She was practically vibrating with a mixture of hype and deep terror.
"Big brother..." Lia whispered with her voice barely audible over the hum of the cab.
"It’s... it’s huge.
It looks like a castle.
Are you sure I’m supposed to go here?
This doesn’t look like a place for people from the outer wards."
"It’s the Academy," Silas replied smoothly, leaning forward and resting his forearms on his knees.
"And you aren’t from the outer wards anymore, Lia...
You’re a resident of the Silverleaf district.
You belong here just as much as any of the brats walking those halls."
He reached over and gently tapped his index finger against the glass, pointing toward the massive central spire of the campus.
"Besides," Silas explained.
"The system here is very standard.
Since you’re eleven years old, you’re exactly at the baseline age for the primary student intake.
You’ll be placed in the foundational sector with the other kids your age.
You learn mathematics, terrestrial history, basic mana theory, and core biology."
Lia pulled her face away from the glass, looking up at him with wide eyes.
"How long do I have to stay?"
"Until you’re eighteen," Silas told her flatly.
Lia blinked.
"Eighteen?
That’s seven years of school!"
"That’s until Awakening Day," Silas corrected her, his golden-ringed eyes narrowing slightly at the memory of his own brutal, grinding experience inside those walls.
"The Academy isn’t just about reading books, Lia...
It’s like a pressure cooker.
They feed you nutrients, they teach you how the Sovereign Realm works, and they push your limits...
When you turn eighteen, you undergo the Awakening Ceremony.
If you possess a latent spark, your core ignites.
You become a Lord and you could get drafted by a guild though you won’t need to, you have your big bro after all."
He leaned back against the leather seat.
"If you don’t awaken... you graduate with a standard corporate degree and you get a comfortable high-paying desk job in the inner city.
Either way, you never have to sleep in a damp alleyway ever again."
The weight of that promise completely overrode Lia’s anxiety.
The idea of seven years of guaranteed safety and an actual future made her chest tighten.
She didn’t look terrified anymore.
A fierce brilliant spark of excitement ignited in her dark eyes as she puffed out her chest, adjusting the collar of her brand-new dark blue shirt.
"I’m going to be the smartest kid in the whole building," Lia declared with her confidence returning in full force.
"I’m going to learn everything."
"Don’t get cocky.
Just pass the entrance interview first," Silas chuckled.
The mag-cab pulled to a smooth hovering halt directly in front of the colossal wrought-iron front gates of the Valoria City Academy.
"Here we are, boss," the driver announced through the partition.
"Valoria Academy, main entrance."
Silas pulled his Association-issued phone from his pocket, tapping the digital meter on the back of the driver’s headrest.
The screen chimed, instantly transferring the required Spirit Credits plus a generous twenty percent tip directly to the driver’s account.
"Thanks," Silas said, pushing the heavy passenger door open.
He stepped out onto the pristine swept cobblestones.
Lia scrambled out right behind him, instantly grabbing the edge of his dark trench coat as the intimidating scale of the front gates loomed over them.
The cab hummed with its repulsors flaring as it pulled away from the curb and drove off down the street, leaving them standing alone in front of the massive entrance.
Silas looked up at the gates.
Standing directly in the center of the walkway, positioned beneath a towering stone archway, was an armored Academy security guard.
The man looked incredibly tired.

He had dark circles under his eyes with his posture was slightly slumped, and he was holding a high-tier corporate-issued mana rifle loosely across his chest, looking like a bored worker counting down the minutes until his shift ended.
’Tired, my ass,’ Silas thought with his golden-ringed eyes lazily scanning the shadows cast by the high stone walls.
His Gold Core passively heightened his sensory perception, picking up the subtle suppressed magical frequencies bleeding into the morning air.
He felt them.
Thirty feet to the left, perched on a recessed stone gargoyle, was a stealthed archer.
Forty feet to the right, hidden behind an optical illusion barrier near the guardhouse, was a high-tier elemental mage.
Directly above the archway, concealed in the iron latticework, was an sniper with a kinetic suppression rifle aimed directly at the back of Silas’s skull.

’It’s a prestigious Academy after all...’ Silas thought with a sigh, keeping his hands perfectly visible. ’It housed Elora Verinda, the City Lord’s daughter, and half the heirs to the major Valoria guilds.
Of course they aren’t relying on one bored guy with a flashlight.
They need to be prepared for corporate espionage, rival guild assassinations, and terror attacks...
The bored guy at the gate is just the bait to make intruders lower their guard.’
Silas didn’t react to the snipers,he had long since knew that they existed since he was a student here before.
He simply walked forward with his boots clicking against the stone and Lia trailing nervously in his shadow.
As they approached the gate, the tired-looking guard raised his free hand, holding up his palm to halt their progress.
"Hold it right there, citizen," the guard commanded, his bored tone perfectly rehearsed.
"This is a restricted academic zone...
I need to see proper identification and an authorized visit ticket before you take another step."
Silas didn’t argue.
He didn’t flex his aura or try to intimidate the man as he simply reached into the inner pocket of his dark trench coat, pulled out his metallic Lord ID card, and handed it directly to the guard.
The guard took the card with a lazy sigh, glancing down at the polished metal surface.
The microsecond the guard’s eyes registered the engraved name and the glowing blue core verification stamp on the corner of the card, his entire demeanor shattered immediately.
The man’s jaw literally dropped.
His eyes bugged out of his skull, darting frantically from the heavy metallic card up to the towering ridiculously broad-shouldered man standing in front of him.
He knew that name...
Of course he did.
Silas Graves.
He was a really good student who came to school using the Mag-Train from the slums but... when did Silas Graves become this beautiful?
The guard stared at Silas’s handsome face, the messy dark hair, and the terrifying physique he had stretching the fabric of his dark shirt.
’This hunk of a man in front of me is Silas Graves?!’ the guard thought with his mind completely short-circuiting. ’Is this really someone who used to be from the slums?!
He looks like he eats bears for breakfast!’
"L-Lord Graves!" the guard stuttered violently with his tired facade evaporating into panic.
His hands were shaking so hard he almost dropped the heavy ID card.
He frantically thrust the card back toward Silas, bowing so deeply he nearly snapped his own spine in half.
"I-I apologize!
Congratulations on your successful awakening!
Congratulations on becoming a Lord!"
"Thanks," Silas replied smoothly, plucking the card from the trembling man’s fingers and sliding it back into his coat pocket.
He gestured casually toward the sprawling campus behind the gates.
"I’m going to see the Principal.
I booked a meeting this morning."
The guard swallowed incredibly hard, sweat beading on his forehead.
On normal grounds, standard procedure dictated that even mid-tier corporate parents needed an authorized digitally verified visitation ticket signed in triplicate just to get past the courtyard.
But Silas Graves was a Lord...
And he wasn’t just a normal, bottom-feeding entry-level Lord either.
The glowing stamp on his ID officially designated him as a Blue Core Lord... a tier that placed him quite high up in the terrestrial societal ladder.
You didn’t ask a Blue Core Lord for a piece of paper.
You opened the gates and prayed he didn’t decide to obliterate your guardhouse for being mildly annoying.
"O-of course, Lord Graves!
No ticket required for a Lord of your standing!" the guard babbled quickly, stepping hastily to the side and aggressively tapping the glowing green release rune on the control pedestal.
The massive wrought-iron gates groaned, smoothly swinging inward to grant them access.
"You will need to head directly toward the central administrative spire," the guard instructed, pointing a shaking finger down the main pristine walkway.
"Just follow the cobblestones past the fountain.
You’ll have to enter campu—"
Before the guard could even finish his sentence, the mahogany front doors of the administrative building located just inside the gates clicked and swung open.
A woman stepped outside.
She was the Principal’s secretary.
She was a tall and incredibly stunning woman in her mid-twenties.
The woman had sleek and perfectly straightened black hair that cascaded down her back, piercing gray eyes, and a flawlessly beautiful manicured face.
She was wearing a tight, tailored gray pencil skirt and a crisp white blouse, holding a digital corporate clipboard against her chest.
She stopped at the top of the marble steps, her gray eyes locking onto Silas instantly.
"Lord Graves," the Secretary called out, her voice was a smooth alluring purr that carried easily across the courtyard.
She offered a deep respectful bow hiking up her skirt a bit in the process.
"Welcome back to Valoria Academy and welcome to your little sister as well.
The Principal is waiting for you in his office.
I will guide you there personally."
As she straightened up, her gray eyes swept over Silas’s towering muscled frame.
A visible flush of pink spread across her high cheekbones as she bit her lower lip slightly with her professional demeanor cracking as she actively checked him out from head to toe.
Silas looked at the flushed beautiful Secretary but he didn’t blush back.
He just reached down, firmly grasped Lia’s small hand to ensure she didn’t wander off, and looked at the woman with exhausted eyes.
Silas had not been here for even an hour yet and he already wanted to go home.
"Alright," Silas said flatly.
"Let’s follow her."
He walked through the open iron gates, stepping onto the pristine Academy grounds.
As they followed the swaying hips of the Secretary down the wide manicured cobblestone path, Silas let out a long bitter internal sigh.
’I’m still trying to understand,’ Silas thought, staring at the back of the Secretary’s head. ’Of all the girls in this Academy, why her?’
He remembered her perfectly.
