chapters.title: Chapter 159: Registering Lia
paragraphs: The Secretary led them across the sprawling campus.
The morning bells had just rung, and the wide courtyards were currently flooded with hundreds of students transitioning between the early weekend remedial classes and the combat-theory halls.
’Right... Classes are on Saturday too.’ Silas thought, he was thankful he was doing with this whole thing.
As Silas walked down the center of the path, the entire campus practically ground to a halt.
The students stopped dead in their tracks and they looked at him.
They weren’t just looking; they were outright staring.
The transformation from the invisible young man they used to ignore in the hallways to the ridiculously handsome broad-shouldered beast of a man walking past them now was completely irreconcilable.
They didn’t even know they were staring at Silas and the whispers erupted like a tidal wave across the courtyards.
Groups of girls clustered together, their faces flushing brilliant red as they practically swooned over his sharp jawline and massive shoulders, whispering frantically behind their textbooks.
Even the arrogant high-tier male students took one look at his cold expression and immediately stepped backward off the cobblestones, instinctively yielding the right of way to a predator.
Lia, holding his hand, looked around at the hundreds of wealthy and infatuated students parting like the Red Sea for them.
She looked up at her brother and her chest puffed out with pride.
Her Big Brother was the coolest person on the planet!
They finally reached the towering central administrative spire.
The Secretary led them inside with her heels clicking against the polished marble floors.
They took an elevator up to the top floor, stepping out into a quiet, opulent hallway lined with expensive ancient terrestrial artwork and plush velvet carpets.
The Secretary stopped directly outside the heavy, dark oak doors of the Principal’s office.
She turned around to face Silas.
The professional facade she had maintained across the courtyard completely dropped as she took a half-step closer to him, completely invading his personal space.
Her gray eyes looked up at him through her dark lashes and they looked quite infatuated.

"I have to say, Silas," the Secretary murmured with her voice turning into an intimate whisper as she deliberately used his first name. "I am really proud of how much you have grown. You used to be so quiet in the halls but looking at you now... you’re absolutely breathtaking."
She reached out, her manicured fingers gently brushing against the lapel of his dark trench coat.

"If you perhaps wanted to meet up later," the Secretary offered, biting her lip suggestively. "Maybe get a drink in the upper wards to celebrate your successful awakening... I am more than down for it."
She smoothly slipped a small, folded piece of thick expensive cardstock paper directly into his hand.
It was her private comm-slate number.
Silas looked down at the piece of paper in his palm as he looked back at her beautiful flushed face.
"Thanks," Silas said flatly.
He took the paper.
The Secretary offered him a final suggestive smile, completely convinced she had just secured a date with a Blue core Lord.
She turned gracefully on her heel and walked back down the plush hallway toward the elevator banks with her hips swaying deliberately.
’It’s just disappointing to see some girl you actually loved for their personality turn out like this.’ Silas thought as he watched her turn the corner.
The exact microsecond she was out of sight, Silas didn’t even hesitate.
He turned his head, spotted a polished brass dustbin resting against the hallway wall, and casually tossed the slip of paper directly into the trash.
Swish!
Lia, who had watched the entire interaction with narrowed eyes, let out a loud approving snort.
Silas let out a heavy, exhausted sigh, rubbing the bridge of his nose.

’Ah, for fuck’s sake,’ Silas groaned internally. ’All these women... It’s exactly like those trashy novels. They either love me solely for the fact that I’m a Lord with a Blue core who probably has an excellent territory, or they want to jump my bones because of this physique. Are there literally any women left in this miserable city who want anything else from me at least? Is genuine human connection completely extinct?’
He shook the bitter thought away. He didn’t have time to psychoanalyze the gold-digging habits of the Valoria elite as he had a sister to enroll.
Silas raised his hand and knocked firmly on the heavy oak door.
"Come in!" a warm authoritative voice called out from inside.
Silas pushed the door open, leading Lia inside.
The Principal’s office was massive, impeccable, and incredibly well-organized.
The walls were lined with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves filled with magical theory tomes and framed glowing certifications.
A massive mahogany desk dominated the center of the room, lacking any form of paper as it only had a single runic terminal resting on the polished wood.
Sitting behind the desk was the Principal.
He was an older man with distinguished graying temples, wearing a dark three-piece suit.
’I’m sure the Principal is a Lord who lost his territory.’ Silas thought, when one was a Lord and lost their territory land...

They could still enter the Sovereign Realm though they would never be able to form territories again. These people were Adventurers... a Lord that lost his or her territory and was only destined to Adventure..
The Principal immediately stood up from his leather chair as they entered.
He didn’t scowl at Silas’s casual trench coat, and he didn’t look down at Lia’s small frame.
He offered a wide genuine smile, waving them forward.

"Lord Graves!" the Principal greeted warmly, gesturing toward the two plush leather guest chairs positioned in front of his desk. "Please, take a seat! It is an honor to welcome one of our own alumni back into these halls, especially under such... unprecedented circumstances."
"Thank you, Principal," Silas replied smoothly, taking the right chair and gesturing for Lia to sit in the left.
The old man settled back into his seat, folding his hands over his desk.

"I was thrilled to receive your call this morning," the Principal began. "You mentioned you wished to enroll your sister into the Academy’s primary foundational sector. Given your status as a registered Blue Core Lord, we are more than happy to bypass the standard six-month waiting lists and lotteries..."

"I appreciate it," Silas nodded. "Lia is eleven. I need her placed in a curriculum that fits her age, focusing on terrestrial history, mathematics, and baseline mana theory with no advanced combat-theory yet though Basic isn’t bad."
The Principal nodded in firm agreement.

"A very sensible approach, Lord Graves. At eleven years old, she will be placed in the Second Year Foundational Cohort... The classes are rigorous, but they provide the bedrock in case of a successful awakening."
The Principal paused, reaching into his desk drawer. He pulled out a single sheet of printed parchment and a sleek silver runic ink-pen.

"However," the Principal added gently, sliding the paper and the pen across the mahogany desk toward Lia. "Before I can officially assign her to a specific classroom tier, I must administer a small baseline assessment... It is merely a formality to gauge her current educational retention. If she performs well, she will be placed in the advanced track. If she struggles, we will provide her with the necessary remedial tutors."
Lia stared at the piece of paper as she looked at the silver pen.
She didn’t move.
She just froze with her small hands gripping the armrests of the leather chair.
Silas felt a terrifying spike of dread hit his chest.

’Fuck,’ Silas thought with his eyes widening slightly as true panic set in. ’I should have made her study... I should have bought her a textbook last night instead of sugar cookies. She hasn’t been in a classroom in two years! She spent her time picking pockets and learning how to dodge gang enforcers in alleyways! She doesn’t know anything about standard mathematics!’
He watched in agonizing slow motion as Lia slowly reached out and picked up the silver pen.
She looked down at the first question.
There was a tortuous pause.
The silence in the office was deafening.
Silas practically held his breath, fully preparing himself to swallow his pride and ask the Principal for an intensive remedial tutor program to fix the massive gap in her education.
Then, Lia blinked.
She leaned forward, pressed the nib of the silver pen against the paper, and started writing.
She didn’t just write... she blazed through the paper as though she was a scholar!
Her hand flew across the page with shocking precision.
Lia didn’t hesitate on the arithmetic and she didn’t pause on the reading comprehension.
She practically attacked the test.
Silas stared at her, completely bewildered.
’Well, she did like reading a lot so maybe she stole some books? Regardless, I’m glad it turned out alright.
Less than three minutes later, Lia slammed the silver pen down onto the desk with a triumphant satisfying click.
She slid the paper back across the desk toward the Principal, crossing her arms over her chest with a smug confident smirk that looked exactly like Morwenna’s.
"Finished..." Lia declared.
The Principal raised an eyebrow, clearly surprised by her speed. He picked up the paper, pulling a pair of reading glasses from his breast pocket, and scanned the answers.
As he read, the Principal’s eyes widened. He looked from the paper to Lia, and then over to Silas, his smile growing into an expression of genuine, absolute delight.

"Astounding," the Principal praised her warmly, setting the paper down. "Flawless arithmetic, excellent reading comprehension, and surprisingly sharp spatial reasoning. Lord Graves, your sister is exceptionally bright... She passes this test with flying colors."
Silas let out a suppressed sigh of relief, silently thanking the criminal underworld for teaching his sister basic math.
"I’m glad to hear it," Silas replied smoothly, acting as if he hadn’t just been having an internal heart attack.

"Indeed," the Principal smiled, stamping the bottom of the paper with a glowing blue approval rune. "Since today is Saturday, we have ample time to process her registry. Lia, you will officially resume your studies here on Monday morning. You will be placed in the Advanced Foundational Cohort..."
Lia beamed, practically vibrating in her leather chair.
She was going to school! An actual prestigious school!
The Principal reached for the intercom crystal sitting on the corner of his desk.
"I will call the Secretary back up," the Principal announced. "She will escort you both down to the uniform reservoir on the ground floor to ensure Lia is properly outfitted before Monday."
He tapped the crystal. Before he could even speak the command, three sharp, aggressive knocks echoed against the heavy oak door.
"Oh?" the Principal muttered, glancing at the ancient grandfather clock ticking in the corner of his office. "They’re here already?"
He raised his voice.
"Come in!"
The heavy oak doors clicked and swung open.
Silas didn’t even need to turn around.
The exact microsecond the door opened, a familiar wave of perfume flooded into the room.
Harper stepped into the Principal’s office.

The purple-haired woman was dressed in an immaculately tailored dark corporate blazer and a high-end pencil skirt, wearing a pair of sleek wire-rimmed glasses that gave her the cold look of a ruthless CEO.
Standing right beside her, holding her hand, was a smaller, ten-year-old version of her.
It was her little sister, Penelope.
Penelope had the exact same vibrant purple hair as Harper, though hers was tied up in twin pigtails.
She was wearing an expensive ruffled designer dress that looked completely impractical for a school setting.
A crisp, white medical bandage was taped neatly over the right side of her cheek, hinting at some recent undisclosed attack? Silas couldn’t bring himself to care that much
The Principal immediately stood up from his leather chair, practically falling over himself in his eagerness to welcome the heirs of a major guild.
"Ah! Lady Harper!" the Principal greeted enthusiastically, bowing respectfully. "And little Miss Penelope! Welcome, welcome! Please, come in!"
Harper offered a cool smile, completely ignoring Silas sitting in the chair as she stepped fully into the room.
"Principal," Harper replied smoothly. "I am glad that we aren’t late. Penelope’s morning combat-tutor ran slightly over schedule today."
Silas remained seated, crossing his arms over his chest. He looked at Harper, then looked at the little sister with the bandage on her face.
’Fuck me... why am I even surprised? She’s stalking me.’

The classes are rigorous, but they provide the bedrock in case of a successful awakening."
The Principal paused, reaching into his desk drawer.
He pulled out a single sheet of printed parchment and a sleek silver runic ink-pen.
"However," the Principal added gently, sliding the paper and the pen across the mahogany desk toward Lia.
"Before I can officially assign her to a specific classroom tier, I must administer a small baseline assessment...
It is merely a formality to gauge her current educational retention.
If she performs well, she will be placed in the advanced track.
If she struggles, we will provide her with the necessary remedial tutors."
Lia stared at the piece of paper as she looked at the silver pen.
She didn’t move.
She just froze with her small hands gripping the armrests of the leather chair.
Silas felt a terrifying spike of dread hit his chest.
’Fuck,’ Silas thought with his eyes widening slightly as true panic set in. ’I should have made her study...
I should have bought her a textbook last night instead of sugar cookies.
She hasn’t been in a classroom in two years!
She spent her time picking pockets and learning how to dodge gang enforcers in alleyways!
She doesn’t know anything about standard mathematics!’
He watched in agonizing slow motion as Lia slowly reached out and picked up the silver pen.
She looked down at the first question.
There was a tortuous pause.
The silence in the office was deafening.
Silas practically held his breath, fully preparing himself to swallow his pride and ask the Principal for an intensive remedial tutor program to fix the massive gap in her education.
Then, Lia blinked.
She leaned forward, pressed the nib of the silver pen against the paper, and started writing.
She didn’t just write... she blazed through the paper as though she was a scholar!
Her hand flew across the page with shocking precision.
Lia didn’t hesitate on the arithmetic and she didn’t pause on the reading comprehension.
She practically attacked the test.
Silas stared at her, completely bewildered.
’Well, she did like reading a lot so maybe she stole some books?
Regardless, I’m glad it turned out alright.
Less than three minutes later, Lia slammed the silver pen down onto the desk with a triumphant satisfying click.
She slid the paper back across the desk toward the Principal, crossing her arms over her chest with a smug confident smirk that looked exactly like Morwenna’s.
"Finished..." Lia declared.
The Principal raised an eyebrow, clearly surprised by her speed.
He picked up the paper, pulling a pair of reading glasses from his breast pocket, and scanned the answers.
As he read, the Principal’s eyes widened.
He looked from the paper to Lia, and then over to Silas, his smile growing into an expression of genuine, absolute delight.
"Astounding," the Principal praised her warmly, setting the paper down.
"Flawless arithmetic, excellent reading comprehension, and surprisingly sharp spatial reasoning.
Lord Graves, your sister is exceptionally bright...
She passes this test with flying colors."
Silas let out a suppressed sigh of relief, silently thanking the criminal underworld for teaching his sister basic math.
"I’m glad to hear it," Silas replied smoothly, acting as if he hadn’t just been having an internal heart attack.
"Indeed," the Principal smiled, stamping the bottom of the paper with a glowing blue approval rune.
"Since today is Saturday, we have ample time to process her registry.
Lia, you will officially resume your studies here on Monday morning.
You will be placed in the Advanced Foundational Cohort..."
Lia beamed, practically vibrating in her leather chair.
She was going to school!
An actual prestigious school!
The Principal reached for the intercom crystal sitting on the corner of his desk.
"I will call the Secretary back up," the Principal announced.
"She will escort you both down to the uniform reservoir on the ground floor to ensure Lia is properly outfitted before Monday."
He tapped the crystal.
Before he could even speak the command, three sharp, aggressive knocks echoed against the heavy oak door.
"Oh?" the Principal muttered, glancing at the ancient grandfather clock ticking in the corner of his office.
"They’re here already?"
He raised his voice.
"Come in!"
The heavy oak doors clicked and swung open.
Silas didn’t even need to turn around.
The exact microsecond the door opened, a familiar wave of perfume flooded into the room.
Harper stepped into the Principal’s office.

The purple-haired woman was dressed in an immaculately tailored dark corporate blazer and a high-end pencil skirt, wearing a pair of sleek wire-rimmed glasses that gave her the cold look of a ruthless CEO.
Standing right beside her, holding her hand, was a smaller, ten-year-old version of her.
It was her little sister, Penelope.
Penelope had the exact same vibrant purple hair as Harper, though hers was tied up in twin pigtails.
She was wearing an expensive ruffled designer dress that looked completely impractical for a school setting.
A crisp, white medical bandage was taped neatly over the right side of her cheek, hinting at some recent undisclosed attack?
Silas couldn’t bring himself to care that much
The Principal immediately stood up from his leather chair, practically falling over himself in his eagerness to welcome the heirs of a major guild.
"Ah!
Lady Harper!" the Principal greeted enthusiastically, bowing respectfully.
"And little Miss Penelope!
Welcome, welcome!
Please, come in!"
Harper offered a cool smile, completely ignoring Silas sitting in the chair as she stepped fully into the room.
"Principal," Harper replied smoothly.
"I am glad that we aren’t late.
Penelope’s morning combat-tutor ran slightly over schedule today."
Silas remained seated, crossing his arms over his chest.
He looked at Harper, then looked at the little sister with the bandage on her face.
’Fuck me... why am I even surprised?
She’s stalking me.’

chapters.title: Chapter 160: Stalker Pro Max
paragraphs: Even a dumb person could have seen her from a mile away... It wasn’t like she was hiding it, she had been sitting opposite his House!

’Of course,’ Silas thought, a migraine-inducing throb pulsing behind his eyes. ’Of course she’s here... I can’t even register my sister for basic math without tripping over another generic anime-villain plot device. What are the odds that her little sister is the exact same age as Lia, enrolling on the exact same day? Zero... It seems like the universe is actively conspiring against me.’
The Principal quickly navigated the introductions.
"Lady Harper, this is Lord Silas Graves. He is also enrolling his sister, Lia, into the Second Year Cohort this morning. I was just about to send them down to the uniform reservoir."
Harper finally turned her head, looking down at Silas as if she had just noticed him sitting there.
She acted perfectly surprised.
"Lord Graves...? What an unexpected coincidence."
"Yeah. Thrilling," Silas muttered deadpan.

"Excellent!" the Principal clapped his hands together, completely oblivious to the tension that was suffocating the room. "Since you both require outfitting, the Secretary can take both girls down to the reservoir simultaneously... It will save us a tremendous amount of time!"
Within five minutes, they had relocated.
They left the plush mahogany-lined office and rode the elevator down to the sprawling, brightly lit uniform reservoir located on the ground floor of the administrative spire.
The reservoir was massive, looking more like a high-end commercial department store than a school supply closet.
Rows upon rows of perfectly pressed Valoria Academy uniforms hung on enchanted racks.
There were dark blazers with silver trim, pleated skirts, tailored trousers, and heavy winter cloaks adorned with the Academy’s glowing crest.
The Secretary was currently showing the two young girls around the racks, pulling different sizes and styles for them to try on.
Lia and Penelope were ushered into a massive mirrored fitting room at the back of the reservoir.
Silas didn’t follow them in.

He walked over to a polished wooden bench situated in the hallway directly outside the fitting room doors, intending to sit down in silence, stare at the wall, and mentally prepare himself for the Secret Realm raid that was happening later.
He sat down, resting his elbows on his knees.
The curtain of the fitting room was drawn shut, but he could clearly hear the interaction taking place inside.
"Ugh, this fabric is incredibly stiff," Penelope’s voice whined loudly from behind the curtain.
The obnoxious popping sound of bubblegum being aggressively chewed punctuated her complaint.
"It’s so tight around the shoulders. My private tailor at the estate uses imported silk for my daily wear. This feels like I’m wearing a burlap sack."
’Haah... I can’t relate to Nepo Babies at all.’ Silas thought.
Lia, who had literally spent the last two years wearing actual burlap sacks and stealing clothes from donation bins, let out a highly unamused sigh.
"It’s just a uniform," Lia replied flatly. "It’s not supposed to be silk... You just wear it so you don’t look like a slob."
"Excuse me?" Penelope snapped back with her chewing pausing. "Do you know who my sister is? We don’t wear cheap cotton. I’m Penelope. What’s your name?"

"Lia," his sister shot back immediately, completely unbothered by the aristocratic threat. "And I don’t care who your sister is. My brother kills monsters for a living so he could probably throw your sister over a building."
Silas closed his eyes, rubbing his temples.
’Well, she’s not wrong about that...’
The Secretary, clearly realizing the situation was devolving into a playground turf war, quickly excused herself.

"I will leave you girls to finish adjusting the hemlines!" the Secretary announced cheerfully, stepping out from behind the curtain and practically sprinting down the hallway to escape the hostile energy.
Silas was left sitting alone on the wooden bench in the quiet hallway.
He let out a long slow breath, closing his eyes and trying to cycle his mana to clear the impending headache.
’I just need to think... and calm down.’
However before Silas could even try to, he heard the rhythmic click of expensive heels walking down the polished floorboards.
The footsteps stopped directly in front of him.
The fabric of the bench compressed slightly as someone sat down right next to him, invading his personal space and Silas didn’t open his eyes.
He already knew who it was.
Harper leaned back against the wooden bench. She reached up with a manicured finger, slowly and deliberately pushing her wire-rimmed glasses up the bridge of her nose.
She turned her head, looking at his sharp profile with a smug smile.
"Silas-kun!" Harper chimed softly, her voice dripping with artificial, saccharine sweetness. "We meet again..."
He immediately rolled his eyes. "You’re not Yamatoan."
’Apparently that’s what they call Japanese people in this world...’ Silas thought, he could have come up with a much better name but hey, he wasn’t on the World Council.
Harper froze.
The bubbly smile faltered slightly on her lips as she blinked behind her expensive lenses with her expression cracking just a fraction.
"Yamatoan?" Harper repeated, her brow furrowing in genuine confusion.
She tilted her head. "Wait. What country did ’kun’ actually come from? I thought it was just a generic pre-cataclysm term of endearment."

"It’s from the Yamato Sector of the island archipelago outside..." Silas corrected her flatly, leaning his broad shoulders back against the wall. "And it sounds ridiculous coming from a Lord who tried to recruit me not too long ago."
Harper’s cheeks flushed a very dusky pink as she cleared her throat, quickly abandoning the poorly researched linguistic angle.
Silas didn’t let her recover her momentum.
He turned fully toward her with his golden-ringed eyes locking onto her purple ones.

"Let me ask you a question," Silas said. "Is it just a coincidence that your little sister happens to be enrolling in the exact same cohort as mine, on the exact same Saturday morning... right after you spent the last two hours sitting on a bench directly across the street from my Silverleaf apartment?"
Harper let out a slow quiet breath.
She knew he had seen her on the bench, of course.
He was a Lord with a high ranking Core; his sensory perception would have picked up her mana signature the second he walked out of the lobby.
She just hadn’t expected him to be so brutally direct about it.
The standard noble males she usually dealt with would have danced around the subject for an hour, playing political chess while Silas just took a sledgehammer to the board.

’Right,’ Harper thought rapidly, adjusting her strategy. ’The aggressive approach isn’t working. If I keep pushing the hostile takeover angle, he’s just going to drop a spell on my head and walk away.’
Harper needed to make herself sound a lot less forceful, lest she scare him away before the actual endgame could begin.
She visibly deflated.
The rigid posture of a ruthless CEO vanished as she slumped her shoulders slightly, shyly looking down at the wooden bench between them.
Harper reached out, gently twiddling her manicured thumbs in her lap, presenting the perfect image of a humbled and slightly embarrassed young woman.

"After you rejected my offer in front of Solstice Cafe," Harper murmured with her voice soft and surprisingly vulnerable. "I took some time to reflect. And... I apologize. I apologize for approaching you out of the blue like that, and for asking you like that when it’s obvious what your answer will be. My father puts a lot of pressure on me to secure talent for the guild. I just hoped... I hoped we could start over. I just hoped we could be friends, is all."
Silas stared at her.
He looked at the downcast eyes, he looked at the twiddling thumbs and he looked at the perfect picture of remorse that seemed to be in her eyes.
It was times like this that Silas wished he had Eluned’s ability to read intents.

’That doesn’t really excuse the stalking,’ Silas thought. ’You can’t just slap a cute bandage over the fact that you actively tracked my residential address and followed my eleven-year-old sister to school.’
He didn’t keep the thought to himself.
"That doesn’t really excuse the stalking, Harper," Silas told her bluntly, crossing his arms over his chest. "Following me to my house isn’t exactly ’friendly’ behavior."
Harper winced with her shy facade breaking too as she realized he was immune to standard manipulation tactics.
"Okay, yes. The bench was a bit much," Harper admitted, letting out a heavy sigh and completely dropping the shy-girl act.

She leaned back against the wall, crossing her own arms and finally acting like a normal human being. "I apologize again. Truly. I just needed to figure out what your daily routine was... You’re an anomaly, Silas. You don’t operate like any other Lord in this city. I just wanted to figure you out."
’Why is she speaking like she got this from ChatGPT? Anomaly? Don’t operate like any other Lord in this city?’ Silas thought. What bullshit was she on?
"I like quiet mornings and staying out of guild wars," Silas replied smoothly. "There. You figured me out."
Before Harper could attempt to dissect that statement, the velvet curtain of the fitting room was violently shoved aside.
The two girls stepped out into the hallway.
The transformation was immediate.
Lia was wearing the impeccably tailored uniform of the Valoria Academy Foundational Cohort.
She wore a dark, charcoal-gray blazer with silver trim along the lapels, a crisp white button-down shirt, a tasteful dark blue tie, and a pleated gray skirt over dark leggings.
The uniform fit her perfectly, erasing the last lingering traces of the street-rat she used to be. Lia looked intelligent and fiercely proud.
Penelope stepped out right beside her. The purple-haired noble was wearing the exact same uniform, though she had somehow managed to make it look slightly chaotic.
Her blazer was unbuttoned, her tie was loose, and she was still aggressively chewing her bubblegum, popping a small pink bubble as she looked at her older sister.
Silas and Harper immediately stood up from the bench.
"Look at you," Silas smiled genuinely, stepping forward and adjusting the collar of Lia’s blazer. "You look like you’re about to run the entire campus."
Lia beamed, her chest puffing out. "I told you! I’m going to be the smartest kid in the building!"
Harper walked over to Penelope, offering her little sister an equally approving nod. "The tailoring suits you, Pen. It hides the fact that you keep getting into fistfights with your combat tutors."
"The tutor was weak," Penelope mumbled around her gum. "He couldn’t even block a basic attack."
They took off their clothes shortly after that.
The Secretary hurried out from behind the curtain, looking incredibly relieved that the two children hadn’t actually murdered each other in the fitting room.
She was carrying two massive paper shopping bags bearing the gold-leaf crest of the Valoria Academy.
"The uniforms are a perfect fit!" the Secretary announced cheerfully, maintaining a safe distance from Silas after her earlier talk.
She held the bags out toward the two Lords. "You may keep the primary uniforms today. I have packaged their old clothing and the secondary uniform sets in these bags for you to carry."
Silas didn’t reach for the paper bag and Harper didn’t either.
Instead, Silas simply raised his right hand.
A brief pixelated flash of golden light illuminated the hallway, and the pile of folded clothes resting on the fitting room counter instantly vanished, pulled directly into his Lord Inventory.
Right next to him, Harper casually flicked her wrist. A spatial ripple opened in the air, swallowing Penelope’s belongings into her own Lord storage space.
The Secretary froze, her hands awkwardly holding out the empty paper bags.

She blinked, her cheeks flushing a bright, embarrassed red as she realized she had just offered baseline terrestrial carrying bags to two incredibly powerful awakened Lords who could store entire buildings in their pockets.
"Ah... r-right. Of course," the Secretary stammered, quickly pulling the paper bags back and hiding them behind her back.

She cleared her throat, forcing her professional smile back into place. "The two girls will officially resume their classes on Monday morning. The required cohort timetables, access credentials, and standardized textbooks will be delivered directly to your respective residential estates by courier tomorrow."
"Thank you," Silas nodded, resting his hand on Lia’s shoulder.
"We appreciate the efficiency," Harper added smoothly.
With the logistics officially concluded, they turned and walked together down the plush carpeted hallway, riding the runic elevator back down to the ground floor.
They left the administrative spire, crossing the bustling courtyards, and finally stepped back out through the massive wrought-iron front gates of the Academy.
The cool morning air hit them as they reached the cobblestone sidewalk.
It was time to split up.
Silas looked at the purple-haired noble.
Harper was really a character.
She was manipulative and invasive but she hadn’t actively tried to kill him yet.
Regardless, Silas didn’t want to talk to her much longer. She felt quite slimy, and he had girls to manage.
"Well, see you around," Silas said, offering a curt nod.
Harper stopped on the curb.
She turned to face him with the cool CEO look returning flawlessly to her features. She reached up, adjusting her wire-rimmed glasses, and offered him a slow smile.
"I can’t wait to see you in the Secret Realm tonight, Silas-kun," Harper waved at him.

chapters.title: Chapter 161: The Day
paragraphs: Silas froze.
’Wait. What?’ Silas thought, his eyes widening slightly. ’She’s going to the Secret Realm? Elora said other Lords would come but still... How the hell did Harper get an invite?’
Before he could even open his mouth to interrogate her about the raid parameters, a sleek armored midnight-black corporate anti-grav limousine pulled up silently to the curb right in front of them.
The rear door slid open automatically.
Harper didn’t wait for his questions. She ushered Penelope into the luxurious back seat, climbed in right behind her, and offered Silas one final wave through the tinted glass.
The door slid shut.
The limousine’s repulsors flared, and the massive vehicle accelerated down the street, driving off and leaving Silas and Lia standing alone outside the Academy gates.
Silas stared after the retreating car with a deep headache beginning to form directly behind his eyes.
’I didn’t want her to come... this will be more trouble in the Long run especially for me in this situation.’ Silas thought.
"Big brother?"
Lia’s voice pulled him out of his spiral.
He looked down. Lia was looking up at him, her dark eyes shining with overwhelming gratitude as she grabbed the fabric of his coat, hugging his arm tightly.
"Thank you," Lia told him. "I’m so excited to start. I’m going to make you proud."
Silas’s frustration completely melted away. He smiled warmly, ruffling her hair.
"I know you will," Silas replied.

He looked down the street toward the commercial sector. "Why don’t we get you a bit more prepared? The Academy is sending the basic textbooks, but I’ll purchase some advanced terrestrial history and mana theory textbooks on the way home. Give you a head start."
Lia instantly cheered, her face lighting up. "Yes! I love reading! I’ll read whatever you give me!"
They turned and began walking together down the cobblestones, heading toward the high-end commercial bookstores, completely leaving the politics of Valoria City behind for the afternoon.
[Two Days Later - Monday Morning]
Silas stood in front of the sleek modern mirror in his Silverleaf apartment bathroom, aggressively brushing his teeth.
He was wearing a thick white wool bathrobe tied loosely around his waist as he leaned over the porcelain sink, spitting out the minty foam, and splashed freezing cold water on his face.
He looked up at his reflection.
’Not bad buster...’
He had bruised dark circles under his golden-ringed eyes as he looked like he hadn’t slept in a month.
The exhaustion was entirely the courtesy of the seventy-three women currently living inside his territory.
Managing a rapidly expanding high-tier faction in the Sovereign Realm was a logistical nightmare.

Over the last forty-eight hours, he had supervised the construction of a Tier 3 armory, dealt with Rowena and Aeliana demanding destructive rematches in the training yard, stopped Morwenna from wrestling a dire-bear, and helped Eluned map out a new agricultural grid so that crops would not only be grown where they were meant to but many other places.
He was exhausted but staring at the Lord looking back at him in the mirror, he didn’t mind it at all.
He was building an empire and this expedition was going to make it stronger...
Suddenly, the bathroom door banged open.
Lia marched in. The eleven-year-old was completely dressed in her Academy uniform, her dark blue tie perfectly knotted with her blazer immaculate.
She was carrying a heavy leather satchel over her shoulder, and her cheeks were puffed out in judgmental annoyance.

"Are you serious?!" Lia reprimanded him loudly, tapping her foot against the tile floor. "Stop taking your time! Are you a woman?! I have to be at the cohort assembly in forty minutes, and you are standing around in a bathrobe staring at yourself!"
Silas grabbed a towel, drying his face with a dry chuckle. "Hold on, menace. The cab isn’t even here yet."
"I need to get my secondary notebooks!" Lia complained, spinning on her heel and running back out into the hallway. "Hurry up!"
Silas hung the towel on the rack, shaking his head. He was genuinely glad that she was happy about going to school, but she was being a bit too aggressively excited.
He tied the wool robe tighter and walked out of the bathroom into the wide, sunlit living room.
As he stepped out, a middle-aged woman approached him from the kitchen.
She was dressed in a simple immaculate black-and-white domestic uniform. Her graying hair was pulled back into a tight, neat bun, and she carried a steaming cup of dark coffee on a silver tray.
She stopped three feet away from him, keeping her posture perfectly straight, and bowed her head deeply.
"Master," the woman spoke with her voice sounding calm and respectful. "I have prepared your civilian clothes for the day. They are laid out on your bed."
Silas took the coffee mug from the tray. "Thank you, Martha."
He took a sip of the bitter brew, walking past her toward the master bedroom. He stopped in the doorway, looking back over his shoulder.
"While I’m gone for the next few days," Silas instructed her clearly. "You are the one in charge of handling Lia and the house. She goes to school, she comes straight back. There are no detours."
Martha, the cute petite middle-aged woman, immediately bowed her head lower, her hands folded neatly in front of her apron.
"Understood, Master. I swear my full loyalty to the cause. The young miss will be perfectly safe."
Silas had hired a maid. Or, as the upper-class citizens of Valoria City legally defined it, a Servant.

When Silas had realized the sheer scale of the danger surrounding his identity, he knew he couldn’t leave Lia alone in the apartment while he was conquering Secret Realms or expanding the Blessed Land.
He needed someone to watch her but he couldn’t just hire a random babysitter off the terrestrial net.
If a normal civilian saw him vanish into thin air during an ascension, or overheard him talking about SSS-rank goddesses, they would sell that information to the corporate tabloids in a heartbeat.
In this world, if you needed operational security, you bought it.
The Valoria City legal code allowed citizens to willingly become Servants.
If an individual fell into massive debt, or simply wanted a guaranteed roof over their head and protection from the outer wards, they could sign their life away.
If one did, and wanted to be sold, a corporate Arcanist would engrave a ’Slave Rune’ onto their flesh.
A Slave Rune was a regulated and magically binding contract.
It was a physical declaration that you had completely surrendered your future autonomy.
Once a buyer paid the exorbitant terrestrial fee to the guild holding the contract, the Arcanist would engrave the corresponding ’Master Rune’ onto the buyer’s biometric registry.
It ensured that the servant belonged to the Master alone. It bound their vocal cords and their physical actions.
As much as Silas deeply hated the idea of people submitting as slaves, the logic nside him recognized the necessity of the magic.
He had willed the Master Rune to explicitly mandate that Martha couldn’t mention whatever he did, whoever she saw, or whatever anomalies occurred inside this apartment to anyone.
With that rune active, she physically couldn’t spread information about him if he ever let it slip up by mistake.
Her throat would simply lock up. This was the only way he could fully trust someone in this ruthless world to watch his sister.
It wasn’t exactly full chattel slavery since the terrestrial laws mandated baseline living conditions but when you sold yourself completely, it was expected that you gave everything to the Master.
Luckily, Martha was incredibly chill about the entire arrangement. She was a widow from the lower industrial wards who had willingly taken the rune to pay off her late husband’s medical debts.
To offset his own crushing moral guilt about owning a human being, Silas treated her exactly like a high-end corporate employee.
He had explicitly told her on the first day that he would be paying her a massive monthly salary in Spirit Credits, far beyond the standard living stipend required by the rune laws.
The promise of actual financial independence had made her quite happy.
As long as she continued this hard work, maintained the apartment, and kept Lia safe, Silas was perfectly content to let her live a comfortable life under his protection.
Silas walked into his master bedroom.
His clothes were laid out perfectly on the mattress. A crisp white button-down shirt with a dark charcoal vest, heavy black trousers, and his dark trench coat.
Martha followed him into the room, stepping up quietly behind him.
Without a word, she reached out and helped him shrug off the heavy wool robe, taking the garment and carefully draping the crisp white shirt over his broad, heavily scarred shoulders.
Silas stood still, letting her button the cuffs.

’I can understand why millionaires get slaves too,’ Silas thought, staring at the wall as she expertly adjusted his collar. ’Having someone dress you is actually quite soothing... if you completely look past the incredibly embarrassing part of standing half-naked in front of a middle-aged woman.’
Once he was dressed, they moved back downstairs.
Breakfast was already laid out on the marble island. Thick fluffy pancakes, heavily smoked bacon, and fresh fruit.
Silas sat down, pouring syrup over his plate, and immediately pointed his fork at Martha.
"Sit down and eat," Silas urged her firmly. "I’m not having you stand in the corner while we eat. There’s plenty."
Martha smiled warmly with her initial conditioning slowly breaking down under his casual treatment.
She pulled up a stool and served herself a small plate, eating quietly as Lia practically inhaled her bacon.
Ten minutes later, they were standing outside the apartment complex in the crisp Monday morning air.
Silas looked down the street, waiting for the mag-cab he had pinged on his app to arrive.
He looked at the empty driveway again, shaking his head.
"I really should have just bought a car," Silas commented dryly, checking his watch. "Waiting for public transit is going to get old fast."
Martha, standing respectfully behind Lia, chimed in smoothly.
"Master, I actually possess a Class-A terrestrial driver’s license. I was a courier in the middle wards before I took the contract..."
Silas turned his head as his golden-ringed eyes widened in delight.
"Are you serious?" Silas praised her, a massive grin breaking across his face. "Martha, you are literally one of the most valuable assets in this entire apartment."
Martha blushed deeply, dipping her head at the high praise.
"Thank you, Master."
The yellow mag-cab finally pulled around the corner, hovering smoothly to a halt by the curb.
Silas opened the rear door. He looked at the maid. "Make sure she gets to the Academy gates, Martha. And be there at three o’clock to pick her up."
"I will not fail you, Master," Martha nodded, stepping toward the cab.

Before Lia climbed inside, the eleven-year-old dropped her heavy leather satchel, threw her arms around Silas’s waist, and squeezed him tightly. She looked up, pressing a quick affectionate kiss against his cheek.
"Bye, Big brother!" Lia beamed. "Wish me luck!"
"You don’t need luck, menace," Silas smiled, patting her back. "Go show them how it’s done."
He let her go. Lia climbed into the cab, followed closely by Martha.
Silas leaned into the front window, tapping his phone against the driver’s console to prepay for a massive, guaranteed round-trip fare.
He stepped back, watching the cab accelerate down the cobblestone street until it disappeared around the corner.
Silas let out a slow breath, turning his back on the apartment complex.
He began walking downward toward the primary commercial intersection.
’Once that Secret Realm is open...’ Silas calculated grimly with his hands buried deep in his trench coat pockets. ’The spatial threshold is going to lock so I’ll at least be gone for five days.’
That was another massive reason why he had gotten Martha.
He needed someone to watch over Lia, yes, but having the maid around also made the massive apartment feel more lively.
Lia wouldn’t be sitting in complete isolation for a week, wondering if her brother had been eaten by an ancient god.
As Silas approached the main intersection, a low expensive hum vibrated through the cobblestones.
A beautiful, sleek, midnight-blue supercar with heavily tinted windows and four luxurious seats pulled up directly in front of him, blocking the crosswalk.
The passenger-side window rolled down with a smooth mechanical hiss.
Elora Verinda was sitting behind the wheel.
The City Lord’s daughter looked immaculate, dressed in a form-fitting and high-end stealth suit designed for elite combat maneuvering.
"Get in," Elora told him, her voice tight with suppressed adrenaline.
Silas didn’t hesitate. He pulled the heavy door open and slid into the plush, leather-upholstered front passenger seat.
As he buckled his harness, he glanced in the rearview mirror.
Jaxon and Maya were sitting in the back seats.
"Morning, Graves," Jaxon grunted respectfully, offering a brief nod.
"Hey," Silas greeted them smoothly.

chapters.title: Chapter 162: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Maya smiled politely, but her internal thoughts were spinning with petty frustration.

’He completely ignored my calls not only that,’ Maya thought, glaring at the back of Silas’s dark hair. ’Silas didn’t even give me his real number last time. Is it that he doesn’t take me seriously....?’
She crossed her arms over her chest.
’Well, I’m going to prove him wrong today. Once he sees my activities in the field, he’ll realize exactly what he’s missing.’

She was confident that she could impress him, especially now that she had Government support... she managed to break into Top 100 in the Newbie Leaderboard and not only that but she had even gotten personal people to train her Summons.
Though she lost 90% of her full control as her and the City were sharing it, but compared to the others, she was quite a low ranking Lord... They wouldn’t want to use her people at all.
Elora didn’t waste time on pleasantries.
She engaged the thrusters, and the supercar launched forward, pinning them all back in their seats as she merged aggressively onto the Valoria City highway.

"Alright, listen up," Elora commanded, her voice cutting through the hum of the engine as she navigated the dense morning traffic. "We should be completely focused on the Secret Realm. Do any of you actually know about Secret Realms, aside from the general knowledge they feed you in the Academy? Or what I told you initially?"
Silas remained silent, staring out the window. Jaxon grunted, scratching his jaw while Maya looked away.
When she got absolutely no reply from her strike team, Elora let out a long exasperated sigh.

"Fine. I will brief you," Elora explained. "Secret Realms are not simple single open battlefields. Similar to dungeons, they are separated into distinct, descending layers of spatial reality. Each layer is heavily guarded by high-tier Guardian monsters that have absorbed ambient mana for a long time. You cannot advance to the next layer until the Guardian of the current floor is butchered."
She took a sharp turn, bypassing the commercial district entirely and heading toward the desolate abandoned industrial sector on the edge of the city.

"Furthermore," Elora continued with her eyes locked on the road. "These anomalies are highly volatile. After a certain amount of time after being activated... which, based on the spatial decay rate in this specific case, is an estimated five to six days, the Secret Realm will violently collapse its entry matrix. The realm will forcibly eject any surviving biological matter back into the terrestrial world."
"Wait," Jaxon frowned, leaning forward. "Eject us? Like, teleport us out?"

"Yes," Elora nodded grimly. "If we don’t clear the final vault and claim the core before the five-day timer expires, the realm spits us out. If we are in the middle of fighting the boss when the timer hits zero, we lose the loot."
"What happens if we die inside?" Maya asked nervously.
"Then the realm digests your mana core and uses your blood to keep the lights on for another century," Silas answered bluntly, not even looking back at her.
Elora offered a grim nod of confirmation. "Be silent. We are approaching the breach point."
She pulled the supercar off the main highway, navigating down a series of cracked overgrown asphalt roads until she pulled up directly outside a massive towering rusted industrial warehouse.
The building looked entirely abandoned but as the supercar approached, hidden runic scanners flashed blue from the rusted eaves.
The big corrugated metal doors of the warehouse suddenly groaned, opening automatically like a massive hangar hatch.
Elora drove the car smoothly into the cavernous, pitch-black interior of the building.
The heavy doors slammed shut behind them, cutting off the sunlight and plunging them into darkness.
But it wasn’t completely dark.
Suspended directly in the center of the empty warehouse, hovering three feet off the concrete floor, was a terrifying violent anomaly.
It was a massive crack in the very reality of space.
The edges of the tear bled with shifting chaotic colors... blinding gold, deep violet, and aggressive crimson.
It looked like a bleeding wound in the fabric of the universe, humming with a deafening vibration that rattled the teeth in their skulls.
"That," Elora said softly, the glow of the spatial tear reflecting in her eyes. "That will lead us to the Sovereign Realm."
Jaxon and Maya immediately began to reach for their seat belts, fully intending to remove them and step out of the vehicle to approach the anomaly on foot.
Silas reached for his buckle as well.
"Hold on," Elora commanded abruptly.
She didn’t hit the brakes.
Elora’s eyes widened with pure adrenaline-fueled madness as she slammed her foot directly down on the accelerator.
The supercar’s anti-grav thrusters roared with explosive force.
"Wait! What are you doing?!" Maya shrieked in absolute terror from the back seat.
Elora didn’t answer.
She drove the heavily armored car straight forward, accelerating to eighty miles an hour, and launched the vehicle right into the center of the bleeding spatial crack.
As soon as the front bumper touched the anomaly, the sound of the engine vanished.
The world shattered and the fundamental laws of physics violently ceased to exist.

Passing through the dimensional anomaly didn’t feel like driving through a tunnel... It felt like being forcefully shoved through a meat grinder constructed entirely out of static electricity and gravity wells.
Silas gripped the leather armrest of the passenger door, his jaw clenching as a wave of intense nauseating vertigo slammed into his brain.

He felt quite weird. His internal organs felt like they were briefly floating outside of his physical body, while his eardrums popped under a sudden crushing shift in atmospheric pressure though that was all in his head.
His Gold Core immediately flared to life, flooding his veins with dense stabilizing mana to combat the spatial sickness, forcefully grounding his body.
He glanced into the rearview mirror.
Jaxon and Maya were not handling the transition nearly as well.

They were both registered Lords... individuals who possessed their own territories, their own mana cores, and their own baseline authority within the Sovereign Realm but their cores were clearly several tiers below Silas’s.
Jaxon was gripping the edges of his seat with white knuckles, his face a sickly shade of pale green as he fought the urge to vomit all over the expensive upholstery.
Maya had her eyes squeezed tightly shut, letting out a high-pitched, pathetic whine of discomfort as the dimensional friction rattled her bones.
Elora, gripping the steering wheel with ice-cold focus, didn’t even flinch.
The suffocating, reality-bending transition only lasted for a few agonizing seconds.
Then, with a loud concussive pop that echoed like a breaking vacuum seal, the supercar violently burst out the other side.
The heavy tires slammed down onto solid ground, kicking up a massive, trailing cloud of dry abrasive dust.
Silas blinked against the sudden blinding shift in light.
The dark rusted interior of the abandoned Valoria City warehouse was completely gone.
In its place was a sprawling and blindingly bright sandy dune.
It looked as though they had just driven straight out of an industrial sector and directly into the heart of a sun-baked desert.
The sky above them wasn’t the neon-lit, cloudy gray of Earth.
It was a deep burning amber color, completely lacking a sun, yet radiating an oppressive suffocating heat that instantly began baking the armored chassis of the supercar.
Elora hit the brakes, bringing the vehicle to a smooth, hovering halt atop a high ridge of packed sand.
Silas looked out through the windshield.
Down in the shallow basin of the dunes up ahead, they weren’t alone.
Not only were there several other high-end modified luxury off-road vehicles parked erratically across the vicinity, but dominating the center of the desert depression was the primary objective.
It was a massive, glowing white portal.
Unlike the chaotic spatial tear they had just driven through on Earth, this portal was perfectly circular, contained within a ring of ancient weathered obsidian.
The ring itself was elevated by some massive intricately carved stone stand stuff... heavy pillars buried deep into the sand, completely covered in glowing runes that pulsed like a heartbeat.
Elora killed the engine. The silence of the desert instantly pressed in on them.
"We’ve arrived," Elora announced smoothly, unbuckling her harness.

She looked through the glass at the glowing white gateway. "This is the staging ground. That construct ahead is the entrance to the Secret Realm of Ititius... He was an ancient forgotten deity of the sand."
Silas didn’t bother asking for a history lesson on Ititius. He unbuckled his seatbelt, kicked his door open, and stepped out into the baking heat.
All four of them left the comfortable interior of the supercar.
Silas’s heavy combat boots sank an inch into the loose burning sand.
He stood at his full height, adjusting the collar of his dark trench coat, and took a slow look around the basin.
They were the last people to arrive, probably.
Silas did a quick headcount.
He could see that there were exactly twenty people scattered around the vicinity of the glowing portal.
They were divided into small heavily armed cliques, standing near their respective vehicles.
They didn’t look like scrawny Academy students or desperate lower-ward scavengers.
These people were wearing custom-forged armor, carrying high-tier elemental staves, and projecting dense auras of authority.
"Silas-kun!"
A loud enthusiastic voice echoed across the dunes.
Silas didn’t even turn his head.
From the corner of his eye, he saw Harper standing near the front bumper of a massive, six-wheeled transport rover.
The purple-haired woman was waving at him frantically with a smug expectant smile plastered across her face.
Silas deliberately chose to ignore her.
He turned his back to her completely, focusing his golden-ringed eyes on the massive white portal.
Elora stepped up beside him, her boots crunching in the sand. Jaxon and Maya flanked them, the two lesser Lords finally shaking off their spatial nausea and drawing their respective weapons.
Elora leaned in closer to Silas with her voice dropping into a tight secure whisper that only the four of them could hear over the dry wind.

"Do not underestimate the people standing in this basin," Elora warned them, her eyes sweeping over the crowd of twenty elites. "This is not a public raid. The coordinates to this specific spatial fracture were auctioned off exclusively through the High Council’s black market channels... Most of the people standing here right now are either Blue Core Lords or Purple Core Lords. There is no baseline trash."
Silas crossed his arms.
’Purple Cores, huh?’ He thought. ’Rich kids who bought enough high-tier beast cores to artificially inflate their cultivation before they even turned eighteen.’
Speaking of that, he needed to get some high tier Beast cores for Lia... He had the money, it was time to start acting like a true young rich man.
"Be especially wary," Elora continued softly, her gaze locking onto a specific group standing near the base of the portal. "There are three Unique Lords here today... Two are men, one is a woman."
She discreetly tilted her head toward a tall arrogantly postured man wearing gleaming, gold-trimmed mythril armor.

"That is Valerius. And the one to his left is Kalind... Like me, they are directly related to the City Lords in their own respective terrestrial cities. They have diplomatic immunity, and their combat training is strictly elite."
Elora then moved her gaze toward a striking woman with fiery red hair, dressed in sleek crimson-scaled leather armor, casually inspecting a curved dagger.
"And the woman," Elora murmured with caution bleeding into her voice, Silas hadn’t even known she was capable of saying stuff with so much emotion.

"That is Lady Seraphina. She is the direct daughter of one of the chief magistrates sitting on the World Council... Do not engage her unless she strikes first. If you kill her, her father will glass your residential district from orbit."
"Noted," Silas replied deadpan. "Don’t murder the World Council’s kid, good to know."
Before Elora could finish her breakdown of the rival factions, the sound of expensive boots crunching aggressively through the sand approached them from behind.
"Well, well, well. If it isn’t my dear, overly ambitious cousin..." a loud, obnoxiously arrogant voice sneered.
Silas slowly turned around.
Among the different Lords here, Elora’s cousin had decided to make his presence known.
The man walking toward them looked exactly like the kind of aristocratic nepotism-fueled parasite Silas despised.
He was in his early twenties, possessing the same sharp good-looking features as Elora, but his face was twisted into a perpetual punchable smirk of superiority.
He was wearing highly impractical, ridiculously ornate silver armor that looked like it had never seen a single drop of actual blood.
As soon as he saw them, he immediately came over and stopped three feet away, his nose practically in the air.
He looked at them and then the cousin let out a loud mocking laugh, roasting his cousin without hesitation.

"Elora, darling," the cousin sneered, gesturing dismissively at Silas and the others. "What is this? Is the Verinda estate running a charity outreach program now? I knew your faction was struggling to maintain its quotas, but dragging Commoners into a Tier-4 Secret Realm? You’re going to get these poor, unwashed peasants slaughtered."

sentences.text: Maya smiled politely, but her internal thoughts were spinning with petty frustration.

’Well, I’m going to prove him wrong today.

"We should be completely focused on the Secret Realm.

Or what I told you initially?"
Silas remained silent, staring out the window.
Jaxon grunted, scratching his jaw while Maya looked away.
When she got absolutely no reply from her strike team, Elora let out a long exasperated sigh.
"Fine.
I will brief you," Elora explained.
"Secret Realms are not simple single open battlefields.

Each layer is heavily guarded by high-tier Guardian monsters that have absorbed ambient mana for a long time.
You cannot advance to the next layer until the Guardian of the current floor is butchered."
She took a sharp turn, bypassing the commercial district entirely and heading toward the desolate abandoned industrial sector on the edge of the city.
"Furthermore," Elora continued with her eyes locked on the road.
"These anomalies are highly volatile.

After a certain amount of time after being activated... which, based on the spatial decay rate in this specific case, is an estimated five to six days, the Secret Realm will violently collapse its entry matrix.
The realm will forcibly eject any surviving biological matter back into the terrestrial world."
"Wait," Jaxon frowned, leaning forward.
"Eject us?
Like, teleport us out?"
"Yes," Elora nodded grimly.
"If we don’t clear the final vault and claim the core before the five-day timer expires, the realm spits us out.
If we are in the middle of fighting the boss when the timer hits zero, we lose the loot."
"What happens if we die inside?" Maya asked nervously.
"Then the realm digests your mana core and uses your blood to keep the lights on for another century," Silas answered bluntly, not even looking back at her.
Elora offered a grim nod of confirmation.
"Be silent.
We are approaching the breach point."
She pulled the supercar off the main highway, navigating down a series of cracked overgrown asphalt roads until she pulled up directly outside a massive towering rusted industrial warehouse.
The building looked entirely abandoned but as the supercar approached, hidden runic scanners flashed blue from the rusted eaves.
The big corrugated metal doors of the warehouse suddenly groaned, opening automatically like a massive hangar hatch.
Elora drove the car smoothly into the cavernous, pitch-black interior of the building.
The heavy doors slammed shut behind them, cutting off the sunlight and plunging them into darkness.
But it wasn’t completely dark.
Suspended directly in the center of the empty warehouse, hovering three feet off the concrete floor, was a terrifying violent anomaly.
It was a massive crack in the very reality of space.
The edges of the tear bled with shifting chaotic colors... blinding gold, deep violet, and aggressive crimson.
It looked like a bleeding wound in the fabric of the universe, humming with a deafening vibration that rattled the teeth in their skulls.
"That," Elora said softly, the glow of the spatial tear reflecting in her eyes.
"That will lead us to the Sovereign Realm."
Jaxon and Maya immediately began to reach for their seat belts, fully intending to remove them and step out of the vehicle to approach the anomaly on foot.
Silas reached for his buckle as well.
"Hold on," Elora commanded abruptly.
She didn’t hit the brakes.
Elora’s eyes widened with pure adrenaline-fueled madness as she slammed her foot directly down on the accelerator.
The supercar’s anti-grav thrusters roared with explosive force.
"Wait!
What are you doing?!" Maya shrieked in absolute terror from the back seat.
Elora didn’t answer.
She drove the heavily armored car straight forward, accelerating to eighty miles an hour, and launched the vehicle right into the center of the bleeding spatial crack.
As soon as the front bumper touched the anomaly, the sound of the engine vanished.
The world shattered and the fundamental laws of physics violently ceased to exist.
Passing through the dimensional anomaly didn’t feel like driving through a tunnel...
It felt like being forcefully shoved through a meat grinder constructed entirely out of static electricity and gravity wells.
Silas gripped the leather armrest of the passenger door, his jaw clenching as a wave of intense nauseating vertigo slammed into his brain.
He felt quite weird.
His internal organs felt like they were briefly floating outside of his physical body, while his eardrums popped under a sudden crushing shift in atmospheric pressure though that was all in his head.
His Gold Core immediately flared to life, flooding his veins with dense stabilizing mana to combat the spatial sickness, forcefully grounding his body.
He glanced into the rearview mirror.
Jaxon and Maya were not handling the transition nearly as well.

They were both registered Lords... individuals who possessed their own territories, their own mana cores, and their own baseline authority within the Sovereign Realm but their cores were clearly several tiers below Silas’s.
Jaxon was gripping the edges of his seat with white knuckles, his face a sickly shade of pale green as he fought the urge to vomit all over the expensive upholstery.
Maya had her eyes squeezed tightly shut, letting out a high-pitched, pathetic whine of discomfort as the dimensional friction rattled her bones.
Elora, gripping the steering wheel with ice-cold focus, didn’t even flinch.
The suffocating, reality-bending transition only lasted for a few agonizing seconds.
Then, with a loud concussive pop that echoed like a breaking vacuum seal, the supercar violently burst out the other side.
The heavy tires slammed down onto solid ground, kicking up a massive, trailing cloud of dry abrasive dust.
Silas blinked against the sudden blinding shift in light.

chapters.title: Chapter 163: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Jaxon stiffened with his knuckles turning white around the handle of his shield while Maya bit her lip, her cheeks flushing dark red with humiliation.
Silas didn’t react.
He just stared at the man with dead eyes.
The cousin, interpreting Silas’s silence as fearful submission, turned his smug gaze entirely onto the Lord.
He took a step forward, extending a gauntleted hand, attempting to put on a show of fake aristocracy.

"I am Julian Verinda," the cousin introduced himself, trying to be friendly with him in the most deeply insulting way possible. "Try to stay behind me in the dark, peasant. If you grovel nicely enough, I might let you carry my loot bags when we clear the vault."
Silas looked down at the extended hand.
He didn’t take the handshake.
All Silas could feel was a deep rising tide of disgust.
He looked at the pristine silver armor, and he remembered how much this guy had insulted him the last time. It seemed that Julian didn’t even recognize him.
Silas’s right hand twitched as his body muscles tightened.
’I could break his wrist,’ Silas thought. ’I could grab his hand, shatter the radius bone in three places, and kick his ribcage so hard his spine turns to powder before he even blinks.’
However, before the killing intent could elevate into actual physical violence, Elora stepped directly between them.
The City Lord’s daughter didn’t yell and she didn’t cause a scene.
"Julian," Elora spoke, her voice dropping into a tone so chillingly flat it made the temperature around them seem to drop. "Fuck off. Politely."
Julian’s smug smile faltered. His hand dropped to his side. "Excuse me?"

"You heard me," Elora stared him down with her eyes completely dead. "You are embarrassing the family name. Weren’t you meant to be serious here? Father only secured you a slot in this raid because your core progression has completely stagnated. If you don’t do well here, and you fail to secure a high-yield artifact from this vault... he is going to banish you to the outer wards."
Julian’s face instantly drained of color.

Then, the realization that she had just aired his deepest, most shameful familial secret in front of a group of "commoners" hit him. The cousin reddened, his face turning a brilliant furious shade of crimson.
"You manipulative bitch," Julian cursed her out, completely dropping the facade.
He pointed a shaking, armored finger at her. "You think you’re so untouchable because you scored high in the Novice Trial! We’ll see who makes it out of the sand alive!"
He spun on his heel, kicking up a spray of dirt, and walked off, storming back toward his own clique of armed sycophants.
Silas watched him go, letting out a slow breath. He looked down at Elora with a sliver of genuine respect for her ruthless family dynamics forming in his mind.
Before Silas could even talk or offer a comment about her cousin’s impending doom, the ground beneath their boots violently lurched.
RUMBLE!
The massive ancient stone gate vibrated, sending deep concussive tremors across the Earth.
The grains of sand around their boots began to literally dance and hover in the air from the sheer volume of ambient mana flooding the basin.
The heavy obsidian ring elevated on the stone stands began to glow with blinding searing white light.
The Secret Realm was opening.
Instantly, a familiar glowing blue digital tab appeared directly in front of the eyes of every single Lord in the vicinity of the Secret Realm.
Silas looked at the translucent screen floating in his vision.
[SECRET REALM OF ITITIUS IS OPENING.]
[SPATIAL CAPACITY LIMIT DETECTED.]
[COMMAND: SELECT ONE (1) ENTITY (HERO / TROOP / MOUNT) TO SUMMON FOR DEPLOYMENT.]
Below the command prompt was a comprehensive, scrolling list of everyone currently stationed in his Territory.
He didn’t need to scroll. Aeli’s name was sitting right at the very up top of the registry, glowing with the distinct golden border of an Epic-Rank Hero.
But before he summoned her, a series of bright flashing magical signatures erupted all across the sandy basin.
Flashes of light came from right beside him.
Jaxon, sweating heavily under his armor, tapped his screen. He summoned his own Hero first.
In a burst of generic white light, a man materialized on the sand next to the tank.
It was a middle-aged man that was entirely shirtless, showcasing a torso covered in faded scars.
He had two heavy iron sword hilts strapped to the side of his hips, and he was wearing nothing but a pair of loose, dark black trousers.
The man cracked his neck, spitting a wad of saliva into the sand. He looked and felt to be quite a seasoned swordsman, possessing the rugged heavy-handed aura of a veteran mercenary.
Silas looked the man up and down, instantly evaluating the summon’s physical density, center of gravity, and muscle distribution.

’He’s a brawler,’ Silas thought with a shake of his head. ’But he’s quite slow. I’m quite confident that he is not taking Brida in a fight. Brida would catch his blade on her shield and snap his femur in half within ten seconds.’
Comparing like this only made him realize how strong his girls were actually.
A second flash of light illuminated the dune.
Maya’s purple hair whooshed wildly in the dry wind as she tapped her screen and summoned her own Vanguard entity.
A tall and incredibly edgy-looking man appeared beside the Lord.
He was a one-handed guy, his left arm cleanly amputated at the elbow as he was wearing a fitted black shirt with the free, empty sleeve blowing dramatically in the wind.
Strapped across his back was quite a big, heavily recurved longbow, which he supposedly fired using his teeth or a prosthetic hook.
The archer immediately dropped to one knee in the sand, bowing his head. "I pledge my loyalty to you, Lady Maya. My arrows shall find your enemies."
’A one-armed archer?’ Silas sighed internally, rubbing his temples. ’She summoned a gimmick character, that’s fantastic.’
To his right, Elora stepped forward as she tapped her screen.
A blinding, freezing pulse of pale blue light erupted.
Elora summoned a woman that had flowing ice-blue hair tied back in a severe, highly disciplined braid.
She wore pristine, tailored scholar robes adorned heavily with her territory’s official corporate emblem.
The woman was holding a thick glowing magic spellbook bound in white leather and she didn’t grovel in the dirt like Maya’s archer.
The ice-mage simply stood tall, offered a crisp perfect military salute, and immediately bowed, pledging her loyalty to Elora.
"At your command, Lady Verinda," the mage spoke.
Silas looked at the three summons.
They were standard, mid-to-high tier entities. They were exactly the kind of competent, generic soldiers you expected a Lord to bring to a raid.
Silas then sighed, raised his hand, and summoned his own, tapping directly on Aeliana’s name on the glowing blue screen.
The energy in front of him didn’t just flash after that... It violently swirled.
A roaring vortex of blinding blue-white starlight mana erupted from the sand, tearing a temporary hole in the fabric of the desert.
The ambient temperature around Silas instantly plummeted as in a brilliant, pixelated flash of golden light, Aeliana appeared on the ground.
The Starlight Arcanist was wearing her pristine tailored white spider-silk robes.
Her silver hair cascaded down her back like spun moonlight, and her green eyes glowed with an ethereal presence that completely dwarfed the generic mercenaries standing nearby.
She immediately dropped into a graceful fluid bow with her white robes pooling elegantly on the sand.
"I have arrived, Lord Sy," Aeliana stated, her melodious voice carrying effortlessly over the dry wind then, the Summon stood up.
The reaction was instantaneous.
Harper, who was standing fifty feet away by her rover. Maya, who was clutching her staff and even Elora.

All three women turned their heads. They looked at Aeli, taking in the flawless, aristocratic bone structure, the glowing green eyes, the impossibly pristine skin, and the overwhelming high-fantasy beauty radiating from the Epic-Rank Elf.
A single frustrated insecure thought ran simultaneously through their minds.
’Why the hell does she look so pretty?’
Aeli stood up to her full height.
She was an elite fighter and her situational awareness was flawless.
She didn’t blatantly look around the basin, but she could physically feel the envious glares of the people staring at her intensely.
She could easily guess that it was the people interested in her Master.
Aeliana’s silver eyes narrowed slightly.
She remembered the loud but effective words that Morwenna the Pirate Queen had just told her back in the barracks mere hours ago.
’If there are women jealous of you, pointy-ears, then you need to make them more jealous. Mark your territory before they try to plant their own flags in the Lord’s deck.’
Aeliana didn’t hesitate. She completely abandoned her usual respectful distance.
So she stood up, took a deliberate half-step forward, and went directly to her Master’s side.
She didn’t just stand near him... she aggressively closed the gap, pressing her soft, considerable breasts firmly and deliberately against his muscular right bicep.
She looked up at Silas through her long silver eyelashes as her voice dripped with an overwhelming devotion.
"Thank you for giving me the opportunity to be here with you, my Lord," Aeliana purred softly, ensuring her voice carried just enough to be heard by the surrounding women.
Silas froze.
’What is she doing?’ Silas thought. ’Why is she touching me like this in public? She’s a fighter, not a succubus!’
Five feet away, Maya gritted her teeth instantly.
An audible grinding sound of pure jealousy escaped her lips as she glared at the gorgeous Elf clinging to Silas’s arm.
Elora simply sighed, pinching the bridge of her nose.
The City Lord’s daughter wasn’t prone to petty jealousy, but she recognized an overwhelming high-tier threat when she saw one.
This summon felt very strong... the starlight bleeding off her robes was suffocating but Elora was not too convinced.
’My summon over here has the same feeling... I need to see her in action.’
She needed to see her actual combat capabilities in the field before she considered Silas to be the true target.
Elora stepped forward, cutting through the romantic tension with ruthless efficiency.
"The Secret Realm will be opening shortly so listen closely," Elora commanded, reaching into a small leather pouch on her belt. "These are spatial tether bands."
She brought out a handful of glowing black metal bands.

"With this band, we can meet up together after being separated in the Secret Realm," Elora explained, handing them out. "Because upon entering a high-tier Secret Realm through a raw portal, the entry fractures. While you and the specific member of your territory will be tethered together and deposited in the same location, the same could not be said for others. Our strike team will be scattered across the first floor. Wear these, and we can track each other’s coordinates to regroup."
All four of the Lords took the bands and wore them, snapping the metal around their wrists. She even gave them to the summons, producing four more bands so all eight of them were wearing it.
Silas took Aeliana’s band.

Because she was currently holding a staff Thora had made in one hand and pressing herself against his arm, Silas had to physically reach out, grab her delicate wrist, and wear Aeli her own band, snapping it into place for her.
The Elf smiled up at him and before Maya could complain about the intimate display, a deafening roar shattered the silence of the desert.
BOOM!
The massive white portal rippled once again. The blinding light violently expanded, surging outward like a tidal wave.
The gravitational force came out of the gate, exerting massive pressure on the Lords and their summons as the sand beneath their feet was instantly stripped away, sucked into the swirling vortex.
WHOOSH!
It immediately sucked everybody into it and Silas didn’t fight the pull. He grabbed Aeliana’s hand, bracing his core.
The world went black.
Silas once again felt the agonizing nauseating teleportation thing.
His stomach flipped into his throat as his physical mass was forcefully shoved through the spatial sieve of the dead god’s vault.
It felt like falling down an endless and suffocatingly tight elevator shaft.
Then, reality slammed back into place.
THUD!
