The City Lord’s daughter didn’t yell and she didn’t cause a scene.
"Julian," Elora spoke, her voice dropping into a tone so chillingly flat it made the temperature around them seem to drop.
"Fuck off.
Politely."
Julian’s smug smile faltered.
His hand dropped to his side.
"Excuse me?"
"You heard me," Elora stared him down with her eyes completely dead.
"You are embarrassing the family name.
Weren’t you meant to be serious here?
Father only secured you a slot in this raid because your core progression has completely stagnated.
If you don’t do well here, and you fail to secure a high-yield artifact from this vault... he is going to banish you to the outer wards."
Julian’s face instantly drained of color.
Then, the realization that she had just aired his deepest, most shameful familial secret in front of a group of "commoners" hit him.
The cousin reddened, his face turning a brilliant furious shade of crimson.
"You manipulative bitch," Julian cursed her out, completely dropping the facade.
He pointed a shaking, armored finger at her.
"You think you’re so untouchable because you scored high in the Novice Trial!
We’ll see who makes it out of the sand alive!"
He spun on his heel, kicking up a spray of dirt, and walked off, storming back toward his own clique of armed sycophants.
Silas watched him go, letting out a slow breath.
He looked down at Elora with a sliver of genuine respect for her ruthless family dynamics forming in his mind.
Before Silas could even talk or offer a comment about her cousin’s impending doom, the ground beneath their boots violently lurched.
RUMBLE!
The massive ancient stone gate vibrated, sending deep concussive tremors across the Earth.
The grains of sand around their boots began to literally dance and hover in the air from the sheer volume of ambient mana flooding the basin.
The heavy obsidian ring elevated on the stone stands began to glow with blinding searing white light.
The Secret Realm was opening.
Instantly, a familiar glowing blue digital tab appeared directly in front of the eyes of every single Lord in the vicinity of the Secret Realm.
Silas looked at the translucent screen floating in his vision.
[SECRET REALM OF ITITIUS IS OPENING.]
[SPATIAL CAPACITY LIMIT DETECTED.]
[COMMAND: SELECT ONE (1) ENTITY (HERO / TROOP / MOUNT) TO SUMMON FOR DEPLOYMENT.]
Below the command prompt was a comprehensive, scrolling list of everyone currently stationed in his Territory.
He didn’t need to scroll.
Aeli’s name was sitting right at the very up top of the registry, glowing with the distinct golden border of an Epic-Rank Hero.
But before he summoned her, a series of bright flashing magical signatures erupted all across the sandy basin.
Flashes of light came from right beside him.
Jaxon, sweating heavily under his armor, tapped his screen.
He summoned his own Hero first.
In a burst of generic white light, a man materialized on the sand next to the tank.
It was a middle-aged man that was entirely shirtless, showcasing a torso covered in faded scars.
He had two heavy iron sword hilts strapped to the side of his hips, and he was wearing nothing but a pair of loose, dark black trousers.
The man cracked his neck, spitting a wad of saliva into the sand.
He looked and felt to be quite a seasoned swordsman, possessing the rugged heavy-handed aura of a veteran mercenary.
Silas looked the man up and down, instantly evaluating the summon’s physical density, center of gravity, and muscle distribution.
’He’s a brawler,’ Silas thought with a shake of his head. ’But he’s quite slow.
I’m quite confident that he is not taking Brida in a fight.
Brida would catch his blade on her shield and snap his femur in half within ten seconds.’
Comparing like this only made him realize how strong his girls were actually.
A second flash of light illuminated the dune.
Maya’s purple hair whooshed wildly in the dry wind as she tapped her screen and summoned her own Vanguard entity.
A tall and incredibly edgy-looking man appeared beside the Lord.
He was a one-handed guy, his left arm cleanly amputated at the elbow as he was wearing a fitted black shirt with the free, empty sleeve blowing dramatically in the wind.
Strapped across his back was quite a big, heavily recurved longbow, which he supposedly fired using his teeth or a prosthetic hook.
The archer immediately dropped to one knee in the sand, bowing his head.
"I pledge my loyalty to you, Lady Maya.
My arrows shall find your enemies."
’A one-armed archer?’ Silas sighed internally, rubbing his temples. ’She summoned a gimmick character, that’s fantastic.’
To his right, Elora stepped forward as she tapped her screen.
A blinding, freezing pulse of pale blue light erupted.
Elora summoned a woman that had flowing ice-blue hair tied back in a severe, highly disciplined braid.
She wore pristine, tailored scholar robes adorned heavily with her territory’s official corporate emblem.
The woman was holding a thick glowing magic spellbook bound in white leather and she didn’t grovel in the dirt like Maya’s archer.
The ice-mage simply stood tall, offered a crisp perfect military salute, and immediately bowed, pledging her loyalty to Elora.
"At your command, Lady Verinda," the mage spoke.
Silas looked at the three summons.
They were standard, mid-to-high tier entities.
They were exactly the kind of competent, generic soldiers you expected a Lord to bring to a raid.
Silas then sighed, raised his hand, and summoned his own, tapping directly on Aeliana’s name on the glowing blue screen.
The energy in front of him didn’t just flash after that...
It violently swirled.
A roaring vortex of blinding blue-white starlight mana erupted from the sand, tearing a temporary hole in the fabric of the desert.
The ambient temperature around Silas instantly plummeted as in a brilliant, pixelated flash of golden light, Aeliana appeared on the ground.
The Starlight Arcanist was wearing her pristine tailored white spider-silk robes.
Her silver hair cascaded down her back like spun moonlight, and her green eyes glowed with an ethereal presence that completely dwarfed the generic mercenaries standing nearby.
She immediately dropped into a graceful fluid bow with her white robes pooling elegantly on the sand.
"I have arrived, Lord Sy," Aeliana stated, her melodious voice carrying effortlessly over the dry wind then, the Summon stood up.
The reaction was instantaneous.
Harper, who was standing fifty feet away by her rover.
Maya, who was clutching her staff and even Elora.
All three women turned their heads.

They looked at Aeli, taking in the flawless, aristocratic bone structure, the glowing green eyes, the impossibly pristine skin, and the overwhelming high-fantasy beauty radiating from the Epic-Rank Elf.
A single frustrated insecure thought ran simultaneously through their minds.
’Why the hell does she look so pretty?’
Aeli stood up to her full height.
She was an elite fighter and her situational awareness was flawless.
She didn’t blatantly look around the basin, but she could physically feel the envious glares of the people staring at her intensely.
She could easily guess that it was the people interested in her Master.
Aeliana’s silver eyes narrowed slightly.
She remembered the loud but effective words that Morwenna the Pirate Queen had just told her back in the barracks mere hours ago.
’If there are women jealous of you, pointy-ears, then you need to make them more jealous.
Mark your territory before they try to plant their own flags in the Lord’s deck.’
Aeliana didn’t hesitate.
She completely abandoned her usual respectful distance.
So she stood up, took a deliberate half-step forward, and went directly to her Master’s side.
She didn’t just stand near him... she aggressively closed the gap, pressing her soft, considerable breasts firmly and deliberately against his muscular right bicep.
She looked up at Silas through her long silver eyelashes as her voice dripped with an overwhelming devotion.
"Thank you for giving me the opportunity to be here with you, my Lord," Aeliana purred softly, ensuring her voice carried just enough to be heard by the surrounding women.
Silas froze.
’What is she doing?’ Silas thought. ’Why is she touching me like this in public?
She’s a fighter, not a succubus!’
Five feet away, Maya gritted her teeth instantly.
An audible grinding sound of pure jealousy escaped her lips as she glared at the gorgeous Elf clinging to Silas’s arm.
Elora simply sighed, pinching the bridge of her nose.
The City Lord’s daughter wasn’t prone to petty jealousy, but she recognized an overwhelming high-tier threat when she saw one.
This summon felt very strong... the starlight bleeding off her robes was suffocating but Elora was not too convinced.
’My summon over here has the same feeling...
I need to see her in action.’
She needed to see her actual combat capabilities in the field before she considered Silas to be the true target.
Elora stepped forward, cutting through the romantic tension with ruthless efficiency.
"The Secret Realm will be opening shortly so listen closely," Elora commanded, reaching into a small leather pouch on her belt.
"These are spatial tether bands."
She brought out a handful of glowing black metal bands.
"With this band, we can meet up together after being separated in the Secret Realm," Elora explained, handing them out.
"Because upon entering a high-tier Secret Realm through a raw portal, the entry fractures.
While you and the specific member of your territory will be tethered together and deposited in the same location, the same could not be said for others.
Our strike team will be scattered across the first floor.
Wear these, and we can track each other’s coordinates to regroup."
All four of the Lords took the bands and wore them, snapping the metal around their wrists.
She even gave them to the summons, producing four more bands so all eight of them were wearing it.
Silas took Aeliana’s band.

Because she was currently holding a staff Thora had made in one hand and pressing herself against his arm, Silas had to physically reach out, grab her delicate wrist, and wear Aeli her own band, snapping it into place for her.
The Elf smiled up at him and before Maya could complain about the intimate display, a deafening roar shattered the silence of the desert.
BOOM!
The massive white portal rippled once again.
The blinding light violently expanded, surging outward like a tidal wave.
The gravitational force came out of the gate, exerting massive pressure on the Lords and their summons as the sand beneath their feet was instantly stripped away, sucked into the swirling vortex.
WHOOSH!
It immediately sucked everybody into it and Silas didn’t fight the pull.
He grabbed Aeliana’s hand, bracing his core.
The world went black.
Silas once again felt the agonizing nauseating teleportation thing.
His stomach flipped into his throat as his physical mass was forcefully shoved through the spatial sieve of the dead god’s vault.
It felt like falling down an endless and suffocatingly tight elevator shaft.
Then, reality slammed back into place.
THUD!

chapters.title: Chapter 164: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [III / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas’s combat boots hit solid ground.
He didn’t stumble as he instantly bent his knees, dropping his center of gravity with his right hand immediately resting on the hilt of the mythril broadsword strapped to his hip.
He opened his eyes.
He wasn’t in a desert anymore.
He appeared in a massive subterranean cavern of a cave.
The ceiling was lost in impenetrable darkness, and the walls were constructed from unworked sandstone.
The ground beneath his boots was solid bedrock, but it still had thick drifts of loose dry sand blown into the corners and the air was suffocatingly hot.
He looked to his right.
Aeli, who was standing perfectly poised next to him, had safely survived the transition. Her white robes glowed faintly in the pitch-black cavern, providing the only source of illumination.
Silas didn’t waste a single microsecond on sightseeing.
He immediately reached over to his left wrist. He grabbed the sleek glowing black metal location band Elora had given him.
’Fuck it...’
Silas didn’t unclip it. He squeezed his fist, channeling raw power into his fingers.
CRACK!
Silas completely shattered the metal band, breaking the tracking runes into useless pieces, and let the fragments drop into the sand.
He looked at Aeli as he told her his first command.
"Crush the band," Silas ordered her flatly.
Aeliana didn’t question him and she didn’t hesitate either.
She raised her left wrist, summoned a pulse of crushing starlight, and instantly obliterated her own tracker.
"We don’t need to meet up with the others," Silas explained his logic as he sighed. "So now we’re free..."
They crushed their bands because Silas wasn’t interested in doing any sort of group project.
He had no intention of babysitting a one-armed archer, or pulling Jaxon out of traps, or dealing with Elora’s politics while her idiot cousin wandered the halls.
In fact he was planning to kill that fucker too.
’That’s just a little side quest.’ Silas thought.

All he was trying to get were Secret Items. If he stayed with the group, he would have to split the high-tier loot, and worse, he would expose the terrifying combat superiority of Aeliana to the City Lord’s daughter.
He operated better in the dark.
"We just need to move fast and get everything we can..." Silas declared, drawing his broadsword.
The heavy mythril blade scraped against the scabbard with the sound echoing loudly in the quiet cave.
Suddenly, a sharp high-pitched TWANG echoed from the darkness directly above them.
There were the unmistakable sounds of an arrow cutting through the stagnant air and it was not just one but a dozen.
Silas didn’t even have time to swing his sword.
Aeli immediately appeared directly at his side.
The Starlight Arcanist didn’t even need to chant. She simply raised her left hand, aggressively expanding her Royal Arcane Aegis shield forward.
A massive multi-layered dome of blinding, compressed blue-white starlight snapped into existence, covering them both like a fortress of glass.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
Six glowing green mana arrows slammed violently into the surface of the Aegis shield, shattering into useless sparks upon impact and completely failing to pierce the A-Rank barrier.
Aeliana didn’t flinch as the magical shrapnel rained down over her shield.
She kept her hand raised with her green eyes glowing as they pierced through the pitch-black darkness of the cavern ceiling, locking onto the hidden hostile signatures.
She turned her head slightly, offering her Lord a calm composed smile.
"Lord Sy," Aeliana reported smoothly, perfectly blocking the barrage. "I believe we have an intruder."

The glowing green mana arrows shattered violently against the convex surface of Aeliana’s Aegis shield, dropping harmlessly into the hot dry sand of the subterranean cavern like pieces of broken glass.
Silas stood perfectly still behind the multi-layered dome of blue-white starlight.

His golden-ringed eyes tracked the trajectory of the shattered magical shrapnel upward, tracing the ballistic arc through the copper-scented air until his gaze locked onto a jagged sandstone outcropping shrouded in the impenetrable darkness near the cavern ceiling.

’If an archer was the one that attacked us with those kind of high-density, armor-piercing mana arrows, that means it was probably a Hero...’ Silas analyzed. ’I mean Baseline monsters don’t use enchanted longbows with elemental resonance and if it was a Hero up on that ledge, taking a sniper’s vantage point, then the Lord who summoned them has to be standing nearby.’
Silas didn’t draw his weapon into an attacking stance yet.
He didn’t want to alert whoever was hiding in the shadows to the terrifying weight of the forty-pound mythril blade strapped to his hip.
He simply looked into the dark shadows beneath the ledge with his deep voice carrying easily over the vast cavern without a single trace of intimidation or fear.

"Tell your Hero to stand down," Silas commanded, his tone completely flat and pragmatic. "We don’t want to attack you and as long as you stand down, we could probably walk away from each other right now without spilling any blood on the sand."
There was a tense silence in the dark and the oppressive heat of the Secret Realm seemed to magnify the quiet, pressing down on their shoulders.
Then, the soft grinding sound of expensive leather boots slipping on loose sandstone echoed from the shadows directly ahead of them.
The hostile Lord finally stepped out of the shadows.
It was some short, obnoxiously dressed guy wearing an impractical dark velvet coat adorned with cheap gaudy silver trim that completely clashed with the desert environment.

He had a black, featureless cloth mask strapped tightly over his face, completely obscuring his features from the nose down. He was twirling a long ornate iron spear in his right hand, the heavy iron tip sparking with red mana that smelled of burning sulfur.
The short guy stopped ten feet away from the outer edge of Aeliana’s glowing starlight barrier.
He looked at the massive constructed Aegis shield, then slowly tilted his head backward, looking up at Silas’s sharp handsome face and his broad towering shoulders.
The masked guy let out a bitter and incredibly resentful scoff.
"I really do hate attractive guys like you," the masked Lord spat.
He didn’t bother trying to negotiate.
He didn’t even attempt to utilize a basic ocular scanning spell to evaluate the disparity in their ambient mana densities.
If he had, he would have realized he was pointing a stick at someone that was much more powerful than him.
The masked Lord aggressively spun his spear, planting his boots in the sand and pointing the sparking iron tip directly at Silas’s chest.
"Kill them both!" the masked Lord ordered, sending his own Hero after Silas and Aeli.
From the shadows of the elevated ledge above, the cloaked archer Hero obeyed instantly.
He started by shooting more arrows. A rapid hissing volley of three glowing green projectiles ripped through the darkness, aimed directly at Silas’s unprotected face.
THWIP! THWIP! THWIP!
Aeli didn’t even blink.
The Starlight Arcanist casually flicked her left wrist, her green eyes completely lacking any sort of concern.
The Royal Arcane Aegis instantly expanded outward by three inches, catching all three arrows in mid-air and violently deflecting them.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
The arrows ricocheted off the barrier and slammed harmlessly into the cavern ceiling, raining a small shower of dust down upon the masked Lord’s velvet coat.
Silas let out a tired sigh.
He gripped the hilt of his broadsword, fully intending to draw the heavy blade, step through the starlight barrier, and end the pathetic ambush with a single brutal cleave.
But before his fingers could tighten around the grip, Aeli stepped slightly in front of him with her pristine white spider-silk robes brushing against his trousers.
"Lord Sy," Aeliana asked smoothly, her melodious voice chillingly calm as her green eyes glowed with a cold bloodlust. "May I have permission to kill the both of them."
Silas paused, looking down at the elegant Elf.
’Aeli wants to kill someone? It really doesn’t fit her but sure...’
Silas really didn’t want to kill a Lord in the first five minutes of the raid.
It was messy, it usually involved a lot of fallout if they were connected to a Valoria guild, and he was strictly here to secure the vault loot.
But there was obvious killing intent in the air.
The guy had already launched two lethal volleys and explicitly ordered their execution.

Silas couldn’t just let it slide, turn his back, and walk away. If he left the rat alive, the guy could easily get in contact with a larger posse of mercenary Lords and jump him later along the line when he was busy fighting a boss monster or dealing with a trap.
In the Sovereign Realm, mercy was just a delayed death sentence.
"Permission granted," Silas told her flatly with his golden-ringed eyes hardening. "Make it quick."
Aeliana didn’t hesitate at all. Once he gave her permission, she ran forward.
The Elf dropped her Aegis shield entirely with the blue-white starlight shattering into ambient pixels as she completely abandoned her defensive posture.
Utilizing her passive Elven Swiftness, she caught the stagnant thermal currents of the cavern and blurred across the hot sand.
Aeli closed the ten-foot gap between herself and the masked Lord in a fraction of a microsecond.
The short Lord panicked with his eyes going wide beneath his black mask.
He thrust his iron spear forward with both hands, desperately trying to impale the beautiful white-robed woman rushing him.
"Die, you bitch!" the masked Lord screamed, pouring all of his low-tier red mana into the thrust.
Aeliana didn’t even break her stride.
She gracefully side-stepped the clumsy telegraphed thrust.
Her pristine white robes fluttered softly as the heated iron spear tip passed harmlessly by her waist, missing her flesh by a solid foot.
Without missing a beat, she reached out with her delicate left hand and grabbed the wooden shaft of the spear just behind the iron head.
Her A-Rank physical density effortlessly overpowered the short Lord’s baseline grip.
Aeliana violently wrenched the weapon out of his hands, ripping the wood through his leather gloves.
She simultaneously spun her body on her lead foot, generating flawless dancer-like momentum.
’Miss Morwenna truly is amazing... she taught me how to move like this.’ Aeliana thought.
As she spun, the archer on the ledge realized his Master had just been disarmed and the Hero frantically nocked another arrow.
THWIP!
Aeliana didn’t even look up.
She casually tilted her head a fraction of an inch to the right, letting the glowing green arrow graze past her silver hair and bury itself into the sand behind her.
She finished her spin, now gripping the stolen iron spear with both hands however at this point, Aeliana didn’t use her starlight magic.
She relied entirely on brutal physical force.
Aeliana drove the spear directly forward, aiming straight for the center of the masked Lord’s face.
CRUNCH!
The heavy iron spearhead punched effortlessly through the black cloth mask, completely shattering the Lord’s nasal cavity, and stabbed directly into the middle of his head.
The force of the thrust drove the iron tip through his brain, erupting out the back of his skull in a violent explosion of dark blood, gray matter, and bone fragments.
The Lord’s body went completely rigid with his hands twitching erratically at his sides as his nervous system instantly shut down.
SHWK!
Aeliana ripped the spear out of his ruined face with a sickening wet sound.
As the dead Lord slumped backward onto the sand with his red mana dissipating into the air, Aeliana fluidly pivoted on her heel.
She looked up at the sandstone ledge where the archer Hero was currently fumbling with his bowstring in a blind panic.

Because his Lord was dead and he was in a Secret Realm, the Hero’s physical form was already beginning to destabilize with the edges of his cloak dissolving into glowing pixels but Aeliana wasn’t going to let him fade away peacefully.
She channeled a concentrated burst of blue-white starlight directly into her right palm.
"Arcane Piercer," Aeliana whispered.
She fired a compressed high-velocity beam of destructive starlight mana.
BOOM!
The laser punched directly through the archer’s chest, instantly vaporizing his heart and blowing a smoking molten hole straight through his torso and the sandstone wall behind him.
The Hero’s terrified scream died in his throat as his body violently dissolved into ambient mana particles, instantly unsummoned.
The entire ambush was over in less than four seconds.
Aeliana stood in the center of the bloody sand with her white robes completely immaculate, without getting hurt or spilling a single drop of blood on herself.
She calmly lowered her hand, the starlight fading from her fingertips.
’I will not only protect my Lord from people like you but those whores outside.’ Aeliana thought.

If he left the rat alive, the guy could easily get in contact with a larger posse of mercenary Lords and jump him later along the line when he was busy fighting a boss monster or dealing with a trap.
In the Sovereign Realm, mercy was just a delayed death sentence.
"Permission granted," Silas told her flatly with his golden-ringed eyes hardening.
"Make it quick."
Aeliana didn’t hesitate at all.
Once he gave her permission, she ran forward.
The Elf dropped her Aegis shield entirely with the blue-white starlight shattering into ambient pixels as she completely abandoned her defensive posture.
Utilizing her passive Elven Swiftness, she caught the stagnant thermal currents of the cavern and blurred across the hot sand.
Aeli closed the ten-foot gap between herself and the masked Lord in a fraction of a microsecond.
The short Lord panicked with his eyes going wide beneath his black mask.
He thrust his iron spear forward with both hands, desperately trying to impale the beautiful white-robed woman rushing him.
"Die, you bitch!" the masked Lord screamed, pouring all of his low-tier red mana into the thrust.
Aeliana didn’t even break her stride.
She gracefully side-stepped the clumsy telegraphed thrust.
Her pristine white robes fluttered softly as the heated iron spear tip passed harmlessly by her waist, missing her flesh by a solid foot.
Without missing a beat, she reached out with her delicate left hand and grabbed the wooden shaft of the spear just behind the iron head.
Her A-Rank physical density effortlessly overpowered the short Lord’s baseline grip.
Aeliana violently wrenched the weapon out of his hands, ripping the wood through his leather gloves.
She simultaneously spun her body on her lead foot, generating flawless dancer-like momentum.
’Miss Morwenna truly is amazing... she taught me how to move like this.’ Aeliana thought.
As she spun, the archer on the ledge realized his Master had just been disarmed and the Hero frantically nocked another arrow.
THWIP!
Aeliana didn’t even look up.
She casually tilted her head a fraction of an inch to the right, letting the glowing green arrow graze past her silver hair and bury itself into the sand behind her.
She finished her spin, now gripping the stolen iron spear with both hands however at this point, Aeliana didn’t use her starlight magic.
She relied entirely on brutal physical force.
Aeliana drove the spear directly forward, aiming straight for the center of the masked Lord’s face.
CRUNCH!
The heavy iron spearhead punched effortlessly through the black cloth mask, completely shattering the Lord’s nasal cavity, and stabbed directly into the middle of his head.
The force of the thrust drove the iron tip through his brain, erupting out the back of his skull in a violent explosion of dark blood, gray matter, and bone fragments.
The Lord’s body went completely rigid with his hands twitching erratically at his sides as his nervous system instantly shut down.
SHWK!
Aeliana ripped the spear out of his ruined face with a sickening wet sound.
As the dead Lord slumped backward onto the sand with his red mana dissipating into the air, Aeliana fluidly pivoted on her heel.
She looked up at the sandstone ledge where the archer Hero was currently fumbling with his bowstring in a blind panic.

Because his Lord was dead and he was in a Secret Realm, the Hero’s physical form was already beginning to destabilize with the edges of his cloak dissolving into glowing pixels but Aeliana wasn’t going to let him fade away peacefully.
She channeled a concentrated burst of blue-white starlight directly into her right palm.
"Arcane Piercer," Aeliana whispered.
She fired a compressed high-velocity beam of destructive starlight mana.
BOOM!
The laser punched directly through the archer’s chest, instantly vaporizing his heart and blowing a smoking molten hole straight through his torso and the sandstone wall behind him.
The Hero’s terrified scream died in his throat as his body violently dissolved into ambient mana particles, instantly unsummoned.
The entire ambush was over in less than four seconds.
Aeliana stood in the center of the bloody sand with her white robes completely immaculate, without getting hurt or spilling a single drop of blood on herself.
She calmly lowered her hand, the starlight fading from her fingertips.
’I will not only protect my Lord from people like you but those whores outside.’ Aeliana thought.

chapters.title: Chapter 165: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [IV / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She walked over to the dead Lord’s body.
With a precise flick of her wrist, she used the edge of the stolen spear to slash the ruined black mask off his face, pulling the blood-soaked fabric away to reveal the guy’s features.
Silas walked up behind her with boots crunching loudly in the dry sand as he looked down at the corpse.
Even if he was a son of an influential person in the upper wards of Valoria City, his face was so incredibly ugly that it made both Aeliana and Silas physically recoil in disgust.

His features were severely asymmetrical, his jaw was completely misshapen, his teeth were jagged as though he was a monster, and his skin possessed a mottled sickly texture that had nothing to do with the spear wound.
"Jesus," Silas muttered, taking a half-step back. "Not even a mother could love this face."
This was very surprising given that everyone paid to be attractive these days, how ugly did one have to be?
Aeliana wrinkled her pristine nose, completely appalled by the visual offense, and dropped the bloody spear into the sand as if it were contaminated.

"I can see why the fucker hated attractive people," Silas sighed, shaking his head. "He probably spent his entire life getting rejected at corporate galas and decided to take his severe genetic insecurities out on anyone with a decent jawline..."
"Shall I search him, my Lord?" Aeliana asked, kneeling beside the corpse despite her obvious distaste for the man.
"Loot him," Silas instructed, stepping back to keep watch over the dark tunnels.
Aeliana swiftly and efficiently searched the dead Lord’s velvet pockets.
She patted down his heavy coat, checked his belt pouches, and even felt along the lining of his boots for hidden spots.
She stood up empty-handed.

"He has nothing, Lord Sy," Aeliana reported, her tone laced with deep aristocratic disdain. "No spatial storage rings, no high-tier artifacts, no beast cores, and not even the currency known as Spirit Credits you showed us... He is destitute."
Silas sighed heavily, pinching the bridge of his nose. They looted his body and found that this guy literally had nothing on him.

"What a complete waste of time," Silas lamented bitterly. "If this was an Official Lord Territory war, I would have at least gotten some more women troops out of his barracks, or forcefully absorbed his raw material stockpiles into my own territory. So far, there is nothing... I just killed a broke, ugly guy in a velvet coat."
He walked over to where the heavy longbow had dropped from the ledge before the Hero dissolved.
It was lying half-buried in the sand. He picked it up, dusting off the grip, and tested the draw weight by pulling the string back.
It was surprisingly sturdy, carved from enchanted darkwood, and hummed with a decent amount of tension.
"Well, it’s not a complete loss," Silas said, slinging the bow over his broad shoulder.
He took the bow of the Hero.
"Fenna could probably use this, or some other archer back at the Keep. It’s significantly better than the standard bows."
He turned his attention back to the Starlight Arcanist, pushing the disappointing encounter out of his mind.
They had a realm to clear.
"Did you bring the contraption?" Silas asked Aeli, holding his hand out.
"I did, my Lord," Aeliana nodded sharply.
She reached into a hidden expanded pocket of her white robes and brought out the scanner.
It was a small and incredibly complex brass radar device.
Thora had made it over the past few days in the sweltering heat of the Warlord Foundry, completely obsessing over the new technology Silas had brought from Valoria.

It worked by passively absorbing the ambient mana in the air of the Secret Realm, using that stolen energy to bounce a highly sensitive sonar-like ping off the spatial layer to reveal exactly where dense concentrations of magical treasures were buried.
Aeliana handed it over to him with the brass casing warm to the touch.
Silas held the heavy device in his palm.
Since this was the First Layer of the anomaly, there was surely not any treasures here.

Eluned had explicitly told him during their briefing that the ancient architects usually started placing the real high-yield loot from the Second Layer downward, leaving the first floor as a barren monster-infested trap specifically designed to bleed out weak strike teams before they even reached the real center.
Silas pressed his thumb against the primary activation rune carved into the side of the brass casing.
HUMMM....
He used it and a low vibration came out as he activated it, buzzing deep into the bones of his forearm.
The pulse emitted from the device was completely invisible, traveling through the dark cavern like a ripple itself.
This was expected, since this particular stealth function had been crafted with Eluned and Morwenna’s help to ensure the radar didn’t trigger any ancient alarm runes left behind by the dead god.
’I am officially naming this thing the Treasure Radar.’ Silas thought, watching the intricate brass dials spin wildly behind the glass screen.
Just when he fully expected that nothing was going to come up on the blank screen and that they would have to find the staircase leading to the Second Layer manually.
PING!
A sharp high-pitched sound echoed from the device as a glowing gold light flared on the surface of the radar.
Silas and Aeli both jolted backward, letting out a synchronized undignified yelp of surprise.
"What?" Silas muttered, staring down at the glowing gold dot illuminating the glass screen.
"A positive signature?" Aeliana gasped, abandoning her composure and leaning over his arm to get a closer look.

"The mana density reading is astronomical, Lord Sy..." Aeliana confirmed, tapping her slender finger against the glass screen. "That is not a malfunction from what I can see... that is a genuine high-tier artifact."
"There is actually treasure on the First Layer?" Silas asked. "Well that completely defies the architectural design of Secret Realms Eluned laid out."
"Perhaps this deity was eccentric, my Lord," Aeliana suggested.

There was a solid glowing golden line projecting from the center of the radar’s screen, going from exactly where they were standing over to where the treasure was located, plotting a direct path deeper into the winding cavern.
"Let’s move," Silas ordered, gripping the brass device tightly.
They went ahead, following the golden line.
The duo moved rapidly through the dark winding sandstone tunnels with their boots kicking up dry dust however the First Layer wasn’t entirely empty.
As they pushed deeper into the suffocating heat, the sand beneath their feet began to violently shift and vibrate.
"SKREEEEEE!"
Some monsters attacked them.
Three massive armored sand-scorpions, each the size of a small transport carriage, erupted from the dunes.
Their thick carapaces were the color of dried bone, and they possessed massiv glowing red stingers dripping with highly corrosive venom.
They charged at the intruders, their massive pincers snapping with enough force to cleanly decapitate a man but Silas didn’t even have to draw his broadsword.
Aeliana cleared them quickly.
The Elf stepped smoothly in front of him with her hands flaring with a brilliant, freezing sapphire light that completely contrasted her usual starlight magic.
"Land Of Frost!" Aeliana chanted, her voice ringing out like chilled bells.
She slammed her palms toward the ground, projecting a sea of absolute-zero ice forward.
The freezing wave crashed over the charging scorpions, instantly halting their momentum.
The absolute zero temperature bypassed their thick armor plating, penetrating deep into their cores, making them freeze up inside out.
CRACK! CRACK! CRACK!
The three massive scorpions violently shattered into a thousand pieces of frozen meat and bloody ice, completely dead before they could even cross the tunnel.
"Clear, my Lord," Aeliana smiled warmly, turning back to him, clearly happy to be of use to her Lord.
"Good work. Keep moving," Silas praised her, stepping effortlessly over the shattered frozen scorpion claws.
Ten minutes later, the narrow tunnel finally opened up. The air grew significantly hotter, and the sound of combat preparations reached their ears.
They reached where they needed to be.
Silas immediately raised his hand, halting Aeliana’s advance.
They crouched down low, utilizing the natural terrain, and hid securely behind a massive wide sandstone rock that overlooked a sprawling, sunken dirt arena.
In the massive clearing ahead, the Guardian of the First Layer was currently being unsealed.
Silas peered carefully over the edge of the rock.

Down in the sunken arena, Elora and the rest of her strike team, including Jaxon and Maya, and the other high-tier Lords that were still alive from the initial drop, had all rounded around the center of the pit.
They had their weapons drawn with their summons positioned defensively in a wide perimeter, all staring intensely at the massive pile of shifting vibrating sand in the middle of the floor.
Silas looked down at the Treasure Radar in his hand.
The bright glowing gold dot on the screen was positioned exactly, perfectly in the dead center of the shifting sand pile.
Silas surmised the situation instantly.
"The radar shows that the treasure is the Boss... The loot is buried inside its chest cavity from what I can see."
"A brilliant defensive mechanism," Aeliana whispered beside him. "Force the invaders to exhaust their resources on the Guardian just to claim the prize."
Silas glanced across the massive arena, scanning the perimeter.
On the exact same kind of elevated rock outcropping on the complete opposite side of the cavern and hidden in the shadows, he saw movement.
Valerius, the arrogant gold-armored Unique Lord Elora had explicitly warned him about earlier at the staging ground, was currently creeping to the edge of his own ledge.
Right beside him was his own Hero, who was surprisingly a little, unassuming girl wearing an oversized gray cloak.
Both Silas and Valerius locked eyes across the massive, two-hundred-foot gap of the arena.
They stared at each other for exactly one second.
Then, completely utilizing mutual common sense, they immediately ignored each other.
Neither of them raised an alarm.
Neither of them shouted a warning to Elora’s team below. They both turned off the sides of their respective rocks, crouching back down into the shadows to observe the battle below in total silence.
Across the cavern, Valerius crouched low against the sandstone with a smug smirk spreading across his handsome face.

’Mia over here has the unique passive ability to sense high-tier treasure,’ Valerius thought, reaching out and affectionately patting the little girl’s hooded head. ’And she can sense a powerful treasure buried right inside that Boss. Once Elora and those other try-hard idiots kill it and exhaust their mana reserves, we’ll just drop down, snatch the loot right out from under them, and go! This is the life, man! Let the others do the heavy lifting!’
Valerius briefly glanced back across the cavern toward Silas’s rock with his smirk faltering slightly as a seed of doubt took root.
’Wait,’ Valerius frowned, his eyes narrowing in the dark. ’That can’t be what he’s here for, right? Is that guy actually trying to steal my strategy? Does he have a treasure-sensing artifact too?’
Down in the arena, the shifting pile of sand violently erupted as the Guardian fully formed.
It was a staggering, utterly terrifying monstrosity.
The monster was a giant, towering sand monster, built like a grotesque mutated centaur.
The lower half of its body was a massive, swirling vortex of hardened, abrasive sandstone that moved like a tornado, while its upper torso possessed eight massive, heavily muscled arms.
Each of the eight hands was holding a different crudely forged weapon made of compacted razor-sharp desert glass... there were jagged swords, heavy maces, and long spears.
Its featureless face possessed no mouth, but its eyes burned with hollow red fire that illuminated the dark arena.
"GRRROOOOAAAARRRRR!"
The Guardian groaned, letting out a deafening sandstorm that blasted across the arena.
The wind pressure threatened to blow the lighter Lords and their summons completely off their feet.
Harper didn’t hesitate. The purple-haired woman wasn’t going to cower as she wanted to establish immediate dominance over the entire raid group.
"Cover your eyes!" Harper screamed to Penelope and the other Lords, bracing her boots in the dirt.
Harper aggressively slammed her hands together, her purple hair whipping wildly in the wind as she rapidly made a complex incantation chant.
"Fulgur Annihilation!" Harper roared.
The air around her violently crackled with raw high-voltage electricity as she thrust her hands forward, firing off a massive powerful blast of violet lightning directly at the centaur’s chest.
CRACK-BOOM!

The lightning struck the monster dead center and the intense superheated energy of the blast was enough to instantly melt a massive gaping hole entirely through the monster’s chest, literally turning a huge part of the sand monster into solid, smoking glass.
’Ah... That woman is quite strong.’ Silas thought.

chapters.title: Chapter 166: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [V / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Got it!" Harper cheered, lowering her hands with a smug victorious smirk but the victory was premature.
The monster didn’t fall.
It didn’t even flinch.
It simply looked down at the smoking glass hole in its chest with its burning red eyes. The eight arms flexed simultaneously, and the Guardian forcefully channeled the ambient mana of the cavern.
CRUNCH!
The glass violently shattered from the inside out, turning instantly back into swirling, abrasive sand.
The hole completely closed up, healing the monster flawlessly in less than two seconds.
"Oh, you have got to be kidding me," Harper cursed loudly, the color draining from her face as she stepped backward.
The monster was a true Guardian.
It was heavily armored by the shifting sand, regenerating with the sand and incredibly lethal in close quarters. It was not weak, and it was going to be a brutally tuff fight.
"Scatter! Flank its legs! Do not let it corner the casters!" Elora commanded with her voice cutting through the deafening roar of the sandstorm.
"I’m drawing its aggro!" Jaxon roared, rushing forward.
The armored tank Lord raised his heavy iron tower shield, aggressively charging the beast to keep its attention away from Harper and Maya.
"GRRROAAAR!"
The centaur swung one of its massive, glass-forged maces downward in a brutal, crushing arc.
CRASH!
The impact drove Jaxon directly to his knees with his heavy boots sliding backward through the dirt, carving two deep trenches into the arena floor.
The iron surface of his shield groaned agonizingly, deep spiderweb cracks forming across the reinforced metal.
"My arm!" Jaxon shouted, gritting his teeth in pure agony as his shoulder threatened to dislocate. "It hits like a freight train! Someone hit its flank!"
Everyone was contributing to the chaos.
Maya’s one-armed archer Hero dropped to one knee, drawing his massive darkwood longbow back with his teeth with his lone arm providing the stability.
"Piercing Volley!" the archer shouted.
THWIP! THWIP! THWIP!
He fired volley after volley of highly explosive mana arrows directly into the monster’s burning red eyes, detonating against its face and blinding it temporarily.
Julian, Elora’s arrogant cousin, was actually proving mildly useful, though it was out of self-preservation.
He stayed in the backline, using his pristine silver armor to deflect stray blasts of abrasive sand while firing bursts at the centaur’s flanks from his ornate, jewel-encrusted wand.

"Keep it away from me, you peasants!" Julian cursed frantically, firing a blast that successfully chipped a massive chunk of sandstone off the monster’s lower leg. "I am not getting my armor scratched in this filthy pit!"
"GRROAAAR!"
The Sand Boss realized the ranged attacks were whittling it down so it didn’t just swing its weapons. It slammed its lower, tornado-like hooves directly into the dirt.
RUMBLE!
The sand around its legs violently coalesced, rising upward and rapidly forming six smaller aggressive mini-versions of itself.
The mini-centaurs, each wielding jagged glass daggers, let out high-pitched screeches and immediately charged the ranged casters.
"Adds! We have adds!" Maya screamed in absolute panic, frantically backing away as a mini-centaur lunged at her with its dagger raised.
"I’ve got them! Stay behind me!" Harper yelled, her purple eyes flashing with raw power.
She unleashed another wide-area web of violent purple lightning, sweeping her hands forcefully across the dirt.
FZZZZZZZZT!
The high-voltage web caught three of the mini-bosses mid-leap, frying them instantly into smoking glass statues that shattered into harmless piles of sand upon hitting the arena floor.
"My turn!" Elora shouted over the din of combat.
The City Lord’s daughter opened her glowing spellbook that was linked with her soul. She didn’t hold back her strength as she was playing for keeps.
"Glacial Barrage!" Elora chanted rapidly.
A massive array of heavy, razor-sharp ice-lances materialized in the freezing air above her head.

She hurled them forward with a sweeping gesture, while her ice-mage summon instantly cast a freezing aura onto the ground directly beneath the centaur’s hooves, desperately trying to lock the massive beast in place.
CRASH! CRASH! CRASH!
The ice-lances slammed violently into the centaur’s torso, burying themselves deep into the sand and freezing the shifting particles into hard brittle chunks of ice-packed mud.
Up on the rock, Silas watched the chaotic raid unfold, his hands resting casually on the hilt of his broadsword.

’They’re wearing it down,’ Silas analyzed, perfectly tracking the monster’s regeneration rate through the swirling dust. ’Every time Harper blasts it with lightning or Elora freezes it with a barrage, it takes slightly longer for the sand to reform and heal the wound so its internal core is running out of mana to pull from the environment.’
Down in the pit, the battle was reaching its bloody climax.
People were wounded.
Jaxon’s left arm was hanging completely limply at his side with his heavy iron shield completely shattered into useless pieces of scrap metal.
Harper was panting heavily, her expensive blazer covered in dirt and soot, her mana reserves nearly entirely depleted.
Julian was screaming terrified curses, his pristine silver armor deeply dented from a glancing near-lethal blow by a glass spear.

It was a true brutal raid fight, and the strike team was running on fumes, well mostly because most of the other Lords weren’t even engaging at full power and nobody except idiots were showing all of their cards
"I can’t hold its aggro much longer!" Jaxon shouted, coughing up a thick mouthful of blood onto the sand.
"Now!" Elora yelled out as he dropped her spellbook into the sand, ignoring the expensive artifact, and threw both of her hands forward.
She unleashed every "single" drop of remaining ice mana she possessed in her Blue Core.

’I’m not an idiot... This isn’t even a quarter of my capabilities and I’m sure it’s the same for that purple haired woman, but I have to make it look like I’m trying.’ Elora thought, she had read a book that said that men loved women who struggled to achieve their goals.
Or something like that...
A blinding howling wave of absolute-zero frost crashed over the monster.
The freezing temperature was so severe it completely halted the centaur’s internal mechanics, freezing its eight massive arms securely to its torso.
"GROOOARR!" The beast let out a final muffled sound as it was encased entirely in a thick immobilizing block of solid crystalline ice.
Lady Seraphina, the striking red-haired daughter of the World Council magistrate, saw her opening.
Seraphina had been stuck on defense for the entire raid, using her curved dagger to parry the mini-bosses and protect the squishy casters, conserving her energy for this exact moment.
She wasn’t on defense anymore.
Seraphina gripped the hilt of her dagger with both hands, her crimson-scaled leather armor shifting as she dropped into a low sprinter’s stance.
She aggressively channeled an immense amount of pure, superheated fire mana directly into the blade.
The steel glowed blindingly white-hot, radiating a wave of heat so intense it instantly evaporated the falling snow and steam lingering in the cavern.
"Burn," Seraphina commanded softly with her red eyes locking onto the frozen beast.
She dashed forward at the frozen monster.

Seraphina moved with explosive velocity, leaving a trailing comet of roaring fire blurring across the sandy arena behind her boots as she ended it in one single, perfectly executed and devastating cut.
SHING!
Seraphina slashed horizontally directly through the frozen sand-packed torso of the massive Guardian.
The concentrated heat of her white-hot blade melted the sand instantly upon contact, completely bypassing its physical density and severing the structural integrity of the beast.
She appeared at its back with her boots skidding to a halt in the dirt as her back was turned to the monster.
A microsecond later, the roaring flames followed her cut.
FWOOSH!
A massive horizontal ring of explosive fire violently erupted from the exact cut line, roaring outward and completely severing the upper half of the centaur from its lower body.
Seraphina calmly stood up, flipping her curved dagger in her hand, and smoothly sheathed the blade at her hip with a sharp sound.
The monster turned entirely to solid brittle glass from the extreme change in temperature then, it violently shattered into a million useless pieces.
CRASH!
It rained harmless glass shards down onto the exhausted panting raid team like a glittering shower.
Jaxon collapsed onto his back in the sand, groaning in pain, while Harper leaned on her knees, wiping sweat and soot from her brow, completely "exhausted."
Floating perfectly in the air, exactly where the center of the monster’s chest had been, was a massive cut golden core.
The treasure...
The golden core floated motionless in the hot air directly over the center of the sunken dirt arena.
It pulsed with a beat of mana illuminating the glass-shattered remains of the centaur Guardian with a warm intoxicating light.
For a single second, the members of the raid team just stared at it with their chests heaving as they caught their breath in the aftermath of Seraphina’s devastating flame-slash.
Then, the greed kicked in.

"I claim the core!" Lady Seraphina announced immediately, her melodious voice ringing out over the quiet pit as she took a firm possessive step forward in her crimson-scaled armor. "My blade severed its structure and dealt the lethal blow. By all standard rules of raid engagement, the primary boss drop belongs to my faction!"
"Like hell it does!" Harper snapped right back, her purple hair messy from the sandstorm as she pushed herself up from her knees.

She pointed a dirt-smeared finger at the World Council magistrate’s daughter. "I blew a glass hole through its chest in the opening three seconds and cleared half the mini-bosses! You spent ten minutes hiding behind a parry stance while my lightning kept it from stepping on our support mages! That core is going to me!"
"Both of you need to calm down and look at the actual distribution metrics!" Elora argued loudly, her City Lord authority flaring up as she aggressively wiped a smudge of soot from her cheek.
She didn’t argue with her words alone as she raised her left wrist and directly activated her Lord tab.
She aimed the scanner lens of her interface straight at the floating golden orb.

A sleek translucent blue holographic window immediately projected outward into the air between the arguing women, displaying the exact system parameters of the boss drop for everyone in the arena to see.
With a special device that Elora had, she could show her tabs to other people.
[Name]: Ititius’s Spatial Key
[Tier]: Tier 2

[Description]: A dimensional transport node forged from the crystallized core of a sand deity. Activating or fracturing this node completely bypasses the standard dungeon progression architecture, forcibly teleporting the user and any physically tethered entities directly to the hidden vault floor where the true unmapped treasures of the Secret Realm are stored.

"Look at the classification!" Elora commanded, gesturing sharply at the floating text. "It isn’t a weapon core or a baseline mana battery! It’s a Tier 2 dimensional teleporter! It’s the direct key to the actual treasure vault! We are not splitting this up based on who got the last hit... we need to coordinate our deployment before we do anything else."
’I’m tired of doing this to impress that ma—’
CRACK!
A deafening violent tremor suddenly shook the entire cavern as the sound of solid bedrock violently shattering echoed from the high ceiling, completely alarming everyone in the dirt pit below.

Before Elora, Harper, or Seraphina could even raise their weapons to defend the floating orb, two distinct high-velocity streaks of pure speed erupted from the elevated rock outcroppings on opposite sides of the arena.
From the dark ledge on the left, Silas and Aeliana shot through the air.

Silas didn’t bother using a ladder or finding a safe path down; he had simply loaded his leg muscles like hydraulic springs and launched himself two hundred feet across the open pit with his dark trench coat whipping wildly behind him like the wings of a predatory bird.
Right beside him, utilizing her passive Elven Swiftness, Aeliana surfed the atmospheric displacement of his jump, blurring through the air with effortless zero-gravity grace.
Simultaneously, from the shadow-shrouded ledge on the right side of the cavern, Valerius and his little cloaked Hero, Mia, launched themselves into the open air with equal greed.
All four airborne figures converged on the exact same coordinate in the center of the arena at the exact same microsecond.
"Mine!" Valerius roared, his golden mythril armor gleaming in the artificial light as he thrust his hand forward.
"Get off it!" Silas barked right back, extending his right arm.
Both of them touched the glowing orb in mid-air simultaneously.

Silas’s large right hand clamped down with crushing vise-like force over the left hemisphere of the golden sphere, while Valerius’s gauntleted fingers locked in an unyielding death-grip over the right hemisphere.
Suspended thirty feet above the glass-littered arena floor, completely defying gravity for a split second by the sheer momentum of their collision, both Lords gritted their teeth at each other.
Their faces were inches apart with their eyes locking in a ferocious battle of dominance.
Veins bulged along Silas’s forearms as he tried to physically rip the artifact out of the gold-armored man’s grasp while Valerius’s jaw set in stubborn refusal-to-lose defiance.
Neither of them let go. Neither of them yielded an inch of kinetic ground.
Under the immense, conflicting pressure of two powerful Lords squeezing it from opposite directions with a lot of power, the fragile Tier 2 artifact couldn’t handle the strain.
The golden sphere began glowing blindingly bright.
CRACK!

chapters.title: Chapter 167: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [VI / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: A sharp agonizing web of deep glowing white fractures instantly raced across the smooth surface of the orb, spreading outward from beneath their fingers like shattering ice.
Silas’s eyes widened in sudden realization and Valerius’s arrogant smirk instantly evaporated into pure panic.
"Fuck," Silas and Valerius said simultaneously with their voices overlapping in universal dread.
The exact second the syllable left their mouths, the cracked orb violently detonated.
It didn’t explode with shrapnel or fire.
An intense wave of pure golden light erupted outward from the exact point of impact between their palms.
The light expanded at the speed of a supernova, instantly swallowing Silas, Valerius, Aeliana, and Mia, before washing down over the sunken dirt arena below.
The golden wave slammed over Elora, Harper, Seraphina, Julian, Jaxon, Maya, and all of their summoned Heroes... everyone else really.
The light completely ignored their physical shields and magical barriers, saturating their biology with overwhelming spatial relocation mana.
The entire cavern violently folded in on itself.
Everyone in the arena was forcibly teleported out of the First Layer, dragged kicking and screaming through the dimensional floorboards toward the next layer down.
THUD!
Silas awoke with an involuntary gasp, his back slamming hard against solid, scorching ground.
The wind was briefly knocked out of his lungs, leaving him blinking up at a blinding deep amber sky that radiated an oppressive dry heat.
He slowly raised his right hand.
His fingers were still tightly clamped around his half of the shattered golden orb with the broken edge of the crystallized sand pulsing in a dying magical resonance.
Right next to him, lying flat on his back in the coarse sand, Valerius was laid out as well.
The gold-armored Lord let out a low, painful groan with his gauntleted fingers identically gripping the right hemisphere of the broken sphere.
The two Lords blinked up at the strange sky at the exact same time.
Then, operating on synchronized survival instincts, they both violently rolled to the side away from each other.
They pushed themselves up onto one knee in the sand, raising their respective halves of the broken orb between them like makeshift shields while aggressively analyzing the item.
The familiar glowing blue system tab immediately popped up in front of Silas’s vision, except the structural identity of the artifact had completely changed following the fracture:
[Name]: Ititius’s Fractured Key (Exhausted)
[Tier]: Tier 2 (Broken Remnant)

[Description]: A successfully activated dimensional transport node. By forcefully cracking the crystallized core before the standard, slow-burn portal to the second floor could naturally open, the users have successfully bypassed the labyrinthine intermediate layers and arrived directly on the True Vault Floor, where the genuine unlooted treasures of this Secret Realm are preserved.

[Note]: "Ah, ambitious little mortals! I see you possessed the greedy impatience required to shatter my core rather than walking down the stairs like civilized scholars! I congratulate you on not wasting your time in the dirt above. I sincerely hope you survive long enough for me to see your adorable terrified reactions to the special gifts I have left buried in the sand for you down here. Do try to die entertainingly! — Ititius."
Silas read the floating text with his jaw tightening as a massive migraine-inducing throb pulsed behind his temples.

’An ancient sand god left a patronizing sticky note in the system interface?’ Silas thought as he dismissed the blue screen with a flick of his wrist. ’Of course he did... Every single one of these ancient dead deities is an irredeemable troll. They build complex, multi-layered dungeons just to mock anyone who actually figures out how to speed-run their traps...’
Both of them sat up fully in the sand, lowering the useless broken halves of the orb and casting a wary glance at each other.
They had both planned on keeping the treasure entirely for themselves.

If both of them hadn’t lunged at it across the arena at the exact same microsecond, and if they hadn’t applied enough conflicting physical pressure to violently crack the core in mid-air, then they might have been stuck fighting a pointless drawn-out territorial skirmish against Seraphina and Harper back in the First Layer while the real loot sat down here untouched.
Their mutual greed had paradoxically saved them hours of dungeon crawling.
Silas slowly stood up, brushing the hot coarse sand off his dark trousers, and looked forward to survey their new surroundings.
They were in a desert.
An endless rolling sea of massive, towering sand dunes that stretched out toward a distant heat-shimmering horizon under the burning amber sky.
The air was very dry and sitting a few yards away on a low, wind-carved sandstone rock was Aeliana.

The Starlight Arcanist looked completely unbothered by the brutal heat or the violent spatial transition, her white spider-silk robes remaining immaculately clean but what made Silas pause was the little girl currently sitting comfortably on her lap.
It was Mia, Valerius’s summoned Hero.
The little girl was leaning her head against Aeliana’s shoulder, looking completely relaxed and content as the Elf gently smoothed down the hood of her gray cloak.
Valerius pushed himself up from the sand, his mythril armor clanking loudly, and stared at the sight in genuine shock.
Mia had never been comfortable with anyone else apart from him since the day he had summoned her to his territory; she usually hid behind his cape and hissed at stranger Lords like a feral cat.
Seeing her sitting happily on another Lord’s summon made his jaw drop slightly.
Both of them turned back as Silas walked closer to the rock.
As Silas approached, he got a clear look at the little girl’s face beneath her oversized hood.

She had messy, snow-white hair that framed her round cheeks, large, brilliant green eyes that glowed with an intuitive light, and... most noticeably long, delicately pointed ears that peeked out from her locks.
She had long ears just like Aeli.
Both Lords blinked, looking back and forth between the tall, pristine silver-haired Elf and the small, white-haired girl sitting on her lap.
The resemblance was unmistakable... they both possessed the distinct, high-fantasy elven bone structure and the same ethereal aura.
Aeliana looked up from the little girl, meeting Silas’s questioning gaze with a soft warm smile of her own.

"Lord Sy," Aeliana explained smoothly. "This little girl... is actually a direct relative of mine from the high astral branches. An elven girl of my lineage who I hadn’t seen in a very long time before I was summoned to this place."
Aeli was not going to mention that this Little girl was her Grand-Aunt of course, that felt quite strange to say out loud.
She turned her glowing silver eyes toward Valerius, offering the gold-armored Lord a formal respectful inclination of her head.
Because she had never bothered to ask for his identity, she didn’t use his name.

"I must extend my sincere thanks to you, Sir Lord," Aeliana said gracefully to Valerius. "By summoning her to your territory and bringing her into this Secret Realm today, you have given us the opportunity to see each other again across the void. I am deeply in your debt for keeping her safe."
Mia looked up from Aeliana’s lap with her big green eyes locking onto Silas’s towering frame.
She offered him a bright incredibly adorable smile that completely lacked any standard deception or scheming.

"Thank you too, Mister Lord!" Mia chirped happily, thanking Silas as well despite not knowing his name either. "If you hadn’t jumped and grabbed the shiny ball with my Master, we wouldn’t have broken it and ended up here together!"
She suddenly clapped her small hands together, her pointed ears twitching excitedly as a brilliant idea popped into her head.

"Hey!" Mia suggested enthusiastically, looking between Silas and Valerius with wide hopeful eyes. "Why don’t we all stick together and be friends while we’re down here? If we don’t fight each other, and we all work together as a big team, I can use my special tracking magic to help us find lots and lots of hidden treasures buried in the sand! There’s enough for everyone!"
’I don’t know why she’s roleplaying like a little girl though...’ Aeliana thought.
The entire desert fell dead silent for two seconds.
Valerius’s eyes bugged out of his skull.
The gold-armored Lord slapped his gauntleted hand directly over his face, letting out a loud painful groan of pure frustration.

"Mia!" Valerius scolded her frantically, waving his hands in the air. "You shouldn’t have told them that! Why are you broadcasting our primary strategic advantage to a rival Lord?! You’re supposed to keep the tracking passive a secret so we can monopolize the drops!"
Mia simply blinked her big green eyes, tilting her head to the side with an expression of complete innocence.
"Master, were we hiding it?" Mia asked genuinely. "You never told me it was a secret! You just told me to point at the shiny things!"
Valerius groaned again with his shoulders slumping in defeat.

One annoying, highly consistent thing about this little elven girl was that she had a terrible non-existent memory for complex military orders or covert operational parameters; if an instruction wasn’t explicitly repeated three times, she just followed her own wholesome instincts.
But looking at her happy face, and realizing she had just been reunited with an elder of her lineage, Valerius couldn’t bring himself to stay mad.
He let out a long sigh, completely forgiving her blunder, and turned to face Silas properly.
He straightened his gold-trimmed mythril armor, brushing a layer of desert dust off his chest plate, and extended his right hand toward the Warlord with a crisp, formal aristocratic posture.
"I am Lord Valerius of the House of Sterling," Valerius introduced himself formally, stating his prominent surname with clear pride.
He looked Silas dead in the eye.

"Despite what my armor might suggest, I don’t care about City politics. I don’t discriminate whether a man was summoned from the lowest mud-drenched slums of the outer wards or born into the highest silk-sheeted echelon of society. In the Sovereign Realm, all that matters is whether you have the physical power and the core strength to fight when the monsters surround you."
Silas looked at the extended hand.
He didn’t see the slimy backstabbing arrogance of a corporate parasite. He saw a warrior who valued strength above bloodlines and he liked it.
Silas reached out and took his hand, gripping the iron gauntlet firmly.
"Silas Graves," Silas introduced himself smoothly, matching the grip. "It’s an honor to meet a Lord whose brain isn’t entirely made of mush."
He paused, his golden-ringed eyes narrowing slightly as he added his fundamental condition for their newfound alliance.

"This temporary truce will go nicely between our factions... just as long as you don’t get in the way of my treasure hunting. If we spot a high-tier core, we split it cleanly or we fight for it honestly. No backstabbing."
Valerius smiled, a fierce expression that bared his teeth. He aggressively tightened his grip around Silas’s hand, pouring his physical strength into the handshake.
Silas didn’t flinch. He squeezed right back with his muscle density.
The two towering Lords stood there in the baking desert sun, actively squeezing each other’s hands with terrifying bone-crushing force.

The leather of Silas’s glove creaked against the iron of Valerius’s gauntlet, and thick, vascular veins popped out along the sides of their forearms and temples as they silently tested each other’s physical limits in a mutual show of dominance.
After five agonizing seconds of neither man yielding a single millimeter of grip strength, Valerius let out a low chuckle through clenched teeth.
"Likewise, Graves..." Valerius ground out with his jaw muscles flexing. "Likewise. No backstabbing."
They released their hands simultaneously, stepping back and shaking out their fingers with mutual respect.
Valerius turned toward the sandstone rock where Mia was still sitting with Aeliana.

"Alright, Mia!" Valerius commanded, clapping his gauntleted hands together to shift their focus to the mission. "Rev up the engines! Scan the horizon and find us a high-tier treasure! We didn’t crack an ancient god’s teleportation sphere just to stand around burning our skin in this desert for nothing!"
"Yay!" Mia cheered loudly, hopping down off Aeliana’s lap onto the hot sand.
The little white-haired girl closed her eyes, planting her small boots firmly in the dirt, and started her magical tracking process.
Silas watched her closely, expecting her to pull out a mechanical brass contraption like Thora’s radar or cast an glowing eye-spell into the sky.
Instead, Silas’s underlying suspicion regarding her unique utility was instantly confirmed.
She didn’t need an artifact. She could detect hidden treasures naturally, but not at all in the conventional line-of-sight way he had expected.
An invisible pressurized wave of ambient mana violently erupted outward from the little girl’s small frame.
The pulse didn’t travel through the air... it traveled directly through the ground, causing the trillions of sand grains across the desert floor to physically vibrate and hum in unison.

The wave spread outward in a massive, three-hundred-degree radius around the woman, moving across the dunes as if she was the living radar herself, mapping the subterranean density of the entire Secret Realm floor in real time.
Two seconds later, Mia’s green eyes snapped open, glowing with a brilliant light.
She lifted her small hand and pointed directly toward a massive, shifting sand dune located about four hundred yards forward across the desert basin.
"I can sense treasure right over there, up ahead!" Mia announced excitedly, her pointed ears quivering with positivity. "It’s buried just beneath the surface of that big hill!"

sentences.text: A sharp agonizing web of deep glowing white fractures instantly raced across the smooth surface of the orb, spreading outward from beneath their fingers like shattering ice.
Silas’s eyes widened in sudden realization and Valerius’s arrogant smirk instantly evaporated into pure panic.
"Fuck," Silas and Valerius said simultaneously with their voices overlapping in universal dread.
The exact second the syllable left their mouths, the cracked orb violently detonated.
It didn’t explode with shrapnel or fire.
An intense wave of pure golden light erupted outward from the exact point of impact between their palms.
The light expanded at the speed of a supernova, instantly swallowing Silas, Valerius, Aeliana, and Mia, before washing down over the sunken dirt arena below.
The golden wave slammed over Elora, Harper, Seraphina, Julian, Jaxon, Maya, and all of their summoned Heroes... everyone else really.
The light completely ignored their physical shields and magical barriers, saturating their biology with overwhelming spatial relocation mana.
The entire cavern violently folded in on itself.
Everyone in the arena was forcibly teleported out of the First Layer, dragged kicking and screaming through the dimensional floorboards toward the next layer down.
THUD!
Silas awoke with an involuntary gasp, his back slamming hard against solid, scorching ground.
The wind was briefly knocked out of his lungs, leaving him blinking up at a blinding deep amber sky that radiated an oppressive dry heat.
He slowly raised his right hand.
His fingers were still tightly clamped around his half of the shattered golden orb with the broken edge of the crystallized sand pulsing in a dying magical resonance.
Right next to him, lying flat on his back in the coarse sand, Valerius was laid out as well.
The gold-armored Lord let out a low, painful groan with his gauntleted fingers identically gripping the right hemisphere of the broken sphere.
The two Lords blinked up at the strange sky at the exact same time.
Then, operating on synchronized survival instincts, they both violently rolled to the side away from each other.
They pushed themselves up onto one knee in the sand, raising their respective halves of the broken orb between them like makeshift shields while aggressively analyzing the item.
The familiar glowing blue system tab immediately popped up in front of Silas’s vision, except the structural identity of the artifact had completely changed following the fracture:
[Name]: Ititius’s Fractured Key (Exhausted)
[Tier]: Tier 2 (Broken Remnant)
[Description]: A successfully activated dimensional transport node.

By forcefully cracking the crystallized core before the standard, slow-burn portal to the second floor could naturally open, the users have successfully bypassed the labyrinthine intermediate layers and arrived directly on the True Vault Floor, where the genuine unlooted treasures of this Secret Realm are preserved.
[Note]: "Ah, ambitious little mortals!
I see you possessed the greedy impatience required to shatter my core rather than walking down the stairs like civilized scholars!
I congratulate you on not wasting your time in the dirt above.
I sincerely hope you survive long enough for me to see your adorable terrified reactions to the special gifts I have left buried in the sand for you down here.
Do try to die entertainingly!
— Ititius."
Silas read the floating text with his jaw tightening as a massive migraine-inducing throb pulsed behind his temples.
’An ancient sand god left a patronizing sticky note in the system interface?’ Silas thought as he dismissed the blue screen with a flick of his wrist. ’Of course he did...
Every single one of these ancient dead deities is an irredeemable troll.
They build complex, multi-layered dungeons just to mock anyone who actually figures out how to speed-run their traps...’
Both of them sat up fully in the sand, lowering the useless broken halves of the orb and casting a wary glance at each other.
They had both planned on keeping the treasure entirely for themselves.

If both of them hadn’t lunged at it across the arena at the exact same microsecond, and if they hadn’t applied enough conflicting physical pressure to violently crack the core in mid-air, then they might have been stuck fighting a pointless drawn-out territorial skirmish against Seraphina and Harper back in the First Layer while the real loot sat down here untouched.
Their mutual greed had paradoxically saved them hours of dungeon crawling.
Silas slowly stood up, brushing the hot coarse sand off his dark trousers, and looked forward to survey their new surroundings.
They were in a desert.
An endless rolling sea of massive, towering sand dunes that stretched out toward a distant heat-shimmering horizon under the burning amber sky.
The air was very dry and sitting a few yards away on a low, wind-carved sandstone rock was Aeliana.

The Starlight Arcanist looked completely unbothered by the brutal heat or the violent spatial transition, her white spider-silk robes remaining immaculately clean but what made Silas pause was the little girl currently sitting comfortably on her lap.
It was Mia, Valerius’s summoned Hero.
The little girl was leaning her head against Aeliana’s shoulder, looking completely relaxed and content as the Elf gently smoothed down the hood of her gray cloak.
Valerius pushed himself up from the sand, his mythril armor clanking loudly, and stared at the sight in genuine shock.
Mia had never been comfortable with anyone else apart from him since the day he had summoned her to his territory; she usually hid behind his cape and hissed at stranger Lords like a feral cat.
Seeing her sitting happily on another Lord’s summon made his jaw drop slightly.
Both of them turned back as Silas walked closer to the rock.
As Silas approached, he got a clear look at the little girl’s face beneath her oversized hood.

She had messy, snow-white hair that framed her round cheeks, large, brilliant green eyes that glowed with an intuitive light, and... most noticeably long, delicately pointed ears that peeked out from her locks.
She had long ears just like Aeli.
Both Lords blinked, looking back and forth between the tall, pristine silver-haired Elf and the small, white-haired girl sitting on her lap.
The resemblance was unmistakable... they both possessed the distinct, high-fantasy elven bone structure and the same ethereal aura.
Aeliana looked up from the little girl, meeting Silas’s questioning gaze with a soft warm smile of her own.
"Lord Sy," Aeliana explained smoothly.
"This little girl... is actually a direct relative of mine from the high astral branches.
An elven girl of my lineage who I hadn’t seen in a very long time before I was summoned to this place."
Aeli was not going to mention that this Little girl was her Grand-Aunt of course, that felt quite strange to say out loud.
She turned her glowing silver eyes toward Valerius, offering the gold-armored Lord a formal respectful inclination of her head.
Because she had never bothered to ask for his identity, she didn’t use his name.
"I must extend my sincere thanks to you, Sir Lord," Aeliana said gracefully to Valerius.
"By summoning her to your territory and bringing her into this Secret Realm today, you have given us the opportunity to see each other again across the void.
I am deeply in your debt for keeping her safe."
Mia looked up from Aeliana’s lap with her big green eyes locking onto Silas’s towering frame.
She offered him a bright incredibly adorable smile that completely lacked any standard deception or scheming.
"Thank you too, Mister Lord!" Mia chirped happily, thanking Silas as well despite not knowing his name either.
"If you hadn’t jumped and grabbed the shiny ball with my Master, we wouldn’t have broken it and ended up here together!"
She suddenly clapped her small hands together, her pointed ears twitching excitedly as a brilliant idea popped into her head.
"Hey!" Mia suggested enthusiastically, looking between Silas and Valerius with wide hopeful eyes.
"Why don’t we all stick together and be friends while we’re down here?
If we don’t fight each other, and we all work together as a big team, I can use my special tracking magic to help us find lots and lots of hidden treasures buried in the sand!
There’s enough for everyone!"

Valerius’s eyes bugged out of his skull.
The gold-armored Lord slapped his gauntleted hand directly over his face, letting out a loud painful groan of pure frustration.
"Mia!" Valerius scolded her frantically, waving his hands in the air.
"You shouldn’t have told them that!
Why are you broadcasting our primary strategic advantage to a rival Lord?!
You’re supposed to keep the tracking passive a secret so we can monopolize the drops!"
