chapters.title: Chapter 168: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [VII]
paragraphs: "You heard the radar! Let’s move!" Valerius barked.
Silas and Valerius didn’t waste a singe second.
Driven by pure greed, the two men sprinted forward across the burning sand side-by-side with their heavy boots kicking up trailing clouds of dust as they raced toward the designated coordinates.
Aeliana and Mia followed right behind them, the tall Elf effortlessly pacing her strides to keep the little girl safe as they blurred across the desert floor.
They crested the top of the massive sand dune less than a minute later and then looked down into the shallow wind-scoured basin on the other side of the ridge, the group immediately saw it.
Protruding three feet out of the packed, baking sand was a strange, fascinating artifact.
It didn’t look like a standard weapon hilt or a glowing chest of coins. It was carved from solid gleaming yellow ivory, shaped exactly like a massive golden tooth the size of a man’s forearm.
The surface of the ivory was etched with intricate glowing crimson runes that slowly pulsed with an intoxicating mana signature.
Both Silas and Valerius immediately raised their left wrists, opening their respective digital system tabs to scan the protruding structure and see its exact classification.
The blue holographic screens materialized in their vision simultaneously:
[Name]: Ititius’s Golden Fang
[Tier]: Tier 3

[Description]: A pristine high-density mana item crystallized from the primary biting force of the sand deity Ititius. When ingested or melted down in an upgraded smithy, this fang permanently increases the user’s baseline terrestrial Vitality by +50 points and grants passive permanent immunity to all forms of environmental heat and fire-based debuffs.
Upon seeing the game-changing permanent stat boost and heat immunity displayed on the system tab, all thoughts of polite cooperation and diplomatic truces completely evaporated from their minds.
"Haah! That belongs to me!"
"Get back here, greedy bastard!"

They ran down the slope of the dune toward the artifact at full sprint with their boots sliding in the loose sand. They arrived at the exact same second, both of them reaching down and grabbing the thick shaft of the golden tooth with both hands.
"Keep your grubby, mud-stained hands away from my Vitality boost!" Valerius roared, planting his iron boots into the dirt and trying to hip-toss Silas away from the prize.

"Get your spoiled paws off my fire immunity, Sterling!" Silas barked right back, dropping his center of gravity and throwing his broad shoulder directly into Valerius’s chest plate to block his leverage.

Grunting and cursing at each other, both men aggressively yanked upward on the ivory shaft with their combined physical might, trying to tear it out of the sand before the other could establish a secure grip.
CLICK!
As they forcefully yanked the tooth upward, a loud mechanical sound of heavy stone gears slotting into place echoed from directly beneath their boots.
The moment something slotted deep within the subterranean bedrock, the massive golden tooth they were holding violently destabilized.
The ivory dissolved into a cloud of useless, yellow ambient mana particles, completely vanishing from between their grasping hands.
Silas and Valerius stumbled backward, their hands clutching empty air.
"What the—?" Silas started.
Before either of them could process the disappearance of the loot, the entire desert floor surrounding the basin began to violently quake and churn.
RUMBLE! RUMBLE! RUMBLE!
Massive swirling vortexes of abrasive sand erupted from the dunes all around them as the desert floor literally stood up.
Thousands of tons of packed, heavy sandstone and flowing desert glass rapidly coalesced, pulling together to form towering, monstrous humanoid shapes.

Within five seconds, different golems of sand that were pretty tall... each standing over fifteen feet in height, with thick tree-trunk limbs and glowing, hollow blue runes carved into their sandstone chests completely surrounded all of them in a tight, inescapable thirty-foot circle.
There were exactly six of the towering behemoths, stepping forward with earth-shattering footfalls that shook the basin.
They had formed directly out of the sand, triggered by the removal of the decoy tooth.
Valerius threw his hands in the air, his face turning bright red with absolute, explosive rage as he realized they had been baited again.

"This is the second damn trap!" Valerius cursed at the top of his lungs, kicking a pile of dirt in frustration. "What the actual fuck is wrong with this dungeon?! Are there literally any real treasures down here, or is this entire Secret Realm just a giant, elaborate prank designed by a bored sand god to waste my time?!"

"I am going to find Ititius’s actual physical tomb when we get out of here," Silas ranted furiously right alongside him with his patience completely exhausted by the constant trolling. "I don’t care if he’s been dead for ten thousand years! I will dig up his skeleton, throw his bones into fire, and melt him into scrap iron! Who builds a fake, stat-boosting tooth just to trigger a gank squad?!"

Because they were both so aggressively busy screaming curses at the sky and complaining about ancient architectural ethics, they hadn’t even properly noticed that the six fifteen-foot-tall Golems had already raised their massive boulder-sized fists, preparing to smash them into paste.

"Lord Sy! Sir Sterling!" Aeliana’s melodious voice called out from the edge of the circle, smoothly bringing their attention back to the immediate tactical reality of these massive Sand Golems closing in on their positions.
Silas and Valerius both stopped mid-rant, slowly turning their heads to look at the towering, fifteen-foot sandstone behemoths looming directly over them.
Both men let out a simultaneous annoyed sigh of mutual exhaustion with their shoulders slumping as they complained some more.
Watching the two towering armored Lords stand in the middle of a monster ambush and whine like grumpy teenagers made Aeliana laugh out loud.
Right beside her, Mia laughed as well, giggling behind her small hands at how funny and silly the two big men were acting.
They were very funny together...
Regardless of the comedic timing, Valerius drew a sleek high-tier mythril longsword from the scabbard at his waist.

"We need to handle these Golems before they compress the sand and trap us in a pit," Valerius stated, all traces of his earlier whining vanishing as he shifted seamlessly back into a military commander.
"Agreed," Aeliana nodded sharply.
The Starlight Arcanist immediately dropped her maternal demeanor.
She gently set Mia down on the safe, flat surface of a nearby sandstone rock, stepping forward with her hands flaring with blue-white starlight as she agreed to join the frontline clearing.
"Let’s just break them and move on," Silas agreed as well, drawing his massive, forty-pound mythril broadsword.
The heavy blade caught the amber light of the desert sky, projecting a cold shadow across the sand.
Valerius rapidly assessed the battlefield... There were six fifteen-foot Golems surrounding their position.

"We split the aggro evenly," Valerius commanded, his tactical brain assigning targets. "Everyone should take on one of the frontline constructs directly to break their encirclement. I’ll take the two on the left flank! Graves, you take the two on the right! Elf, you hold the center line!"
"Understood," Aeli agreed smoothly, raising her hands to conjure an Arcane Aegis barrier.
Silas paused, his broadsword held low. He blinked, looking around the formation, catching a glaring flaw in Valerius’s assignment math.

’Wait a second,’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing in deep confusion as he looked from the six massive fifteen-foot-tall, boulder-fisting Sand Golems over to the tiny, white-haired elven girl sitting on the rock. ’There are six Golems... Valerius is taking two. I’m taking two, Aeli is taking one. That leaves one fifteen-foot rock monster completely unaccounted for on the rear flank.’
Silas turned his head, pointing a calloused finger at the remaining golem that was currently lumbering straight toward the outcropping where Mia was sitting.
"Valerius," Silas said flatly. "Mia is a little girl. Why the hell are we leaving her alone to deal with a golem?"
Valerius didn’t even look back over his shoulder.
The gold-armored Lord simply smirked, swinging his mythril sword in a practice arc. "Watch her."
Mia however was not at all terrified by the fifteen-foot sandstone behemoth lumbering toward her rock. In fact, she was visibly excited as well.
The little girl stood up on the edge of the sandstone outcropping with her gray cloak blowing wildly in the desert wind.
Her large green eyes flashed with an intense blue light.
Mia didn’t pull a weapon, instead she brought both of her small hands up in front of her chest, pressing her palms together as she began making a formal incantation chant.
As she spoke, her voice completely changed.
It no longer sounded like the cute chirping voice of an adorable little child.
It resonated with the deep suffocating weight of an endless, crushing ocean, carrying an ancient power that caused the very moisture in the dry desert air to violently condense around her skin.
"Hear me, dark waters... Tide that swallows the sun... Crush the shore, bind the sky... Rise from the abyss and drown the light."
The exact second she finished the final syllable of the chant, the atmosphere inside the desert basin violently inverted.
A swirling sphere of deep pressurized blue water gathered directly between her small outstretched hands.
Silas, standing twenty feet away with his broadsword raised, felt the magical frequency bleeding off the little girl’s hands.
His golden-ringed eyes widened in sudden recognition. He was well aware of this specific spell.

’Wait, It was the exact same water spell that Morwenna taught me! It’s the standard Tier-1 Aqua Bolt... according to her, That is literally a basic foundational spell designed for novice spellcasters to practice water gathering! It shouldn’t even leave a scratch on a sandstone golem!’
It wasn’t a basic spell anymore though, not in her hands.
The spinning sphere of dark water gathering around her small hands simply multiplied.
In a fraction of a second, the single sphere split into ten distinct globes of pressurized water and then it tripled.
Ten became thirty, swirling around her little body like a localized orbital ring of crushing marine kinetic energy.
And then it quadrupled...
ROOAAAR!
The desert air was completely displaced by the deafening sound of a localized tsunami.
Over one hundred and twenty massive compressed pressurized boulders of deep water materialized in the sky directly above the little girl’s head.
The volume of water she had pulled out of a dry desert atmosphere completely blotted out the burning amber sky, casting a massive cool shadow over the area.
The fifteen-foot Sand Golem lumbering toward her stopped dead in its tracks.
The hollow blue runes on its chest flickered erratically with its rudimentary artificial intelligence completely failing to process how a tiny entity had just conjured an entire ocean above its head.
Mia dropped her small hands forward, pointing her finger directly at the towering sandstone beast.
"Splash!" Mia chirped happily.
She shot it at the Golem.
KA-BOOM!
The entire orbital array of one hundred and twenty compressed water boulders launched forward simultaneously with the speed and velocity of naval siege torpedoes.
The impact was simply... erasure.
The torrent of dark water slammed directly into the chest of the fifteen-foot Sand Golem.
There was no struggle and there was no resistance.
The crushing hydraulic pressure of the water instantly destroyed the whole thing upon impact.
The solid sandstone torso, the tree-trunk limbs, and the reinforced mana core were violently pulverized into microscopic grains of wet mud in less than a tenth of a second.

The explosion of the water blast didn’t just obliterate her target... the residual hydraulic shockwave blasted outward across the desert area, kicking up a massive torrential rain that showered down over the remaining five Golems.
HISSSSSSS! SKREEEE!

The freezing pressurized rain saturated the remaining Sand Golems. Because they were constructed entirely from dry desert sand, the sudden deluge of deep water instantly turned their outer layers into thick immobile sludge.
The other Golems let out agonizing screeches of structural failure as their joints locked up with their movements completely paralyzed by the sudden mud-conversion.
Silas lowered his broadsword, his jaw slightly slack as he stared at the empty, cratered patch of wet mud where a fifteen-foot siege construct had been standing three seconds ago.
He slowly turned his head, looking up at the sandstone rock.
Little Mia was standing there, shaking a few drops of water off her ragged gray cloak. She lowered her small hands, looking down at the shocked Lord and the smiling Elf.
She tilted her head, flashed a bright and adorable toothy smile that bared her fangs, and proudly declared her true individual value to the raid team.
"Despite how small and squishy I look," Mia giggled, placing her hands on her hips with absolute, unshakeable elven pride. "I’m actually almost a Grandmaster in Water Magic!"

"Get back here, greedy bastard!"
They ran down the slope of the dune toward the artifact at full sprint with their boots sliding in the loose sand.
They arrived at the exact same second, both of them reaching down and grabbing the thick shaft of the golden tooth with both hands.
"Keep your grubby, mud-stained hands away from my Vitality boost!" Valerius roared, planting his iron boots into the dirt and trying to hip-toss Silas away from the prize.

"Get your spoiled paws off my fire immunity, Sterling!" Silas barked right back, dropping his center of gravity and throwing his broad shoulder directly into Valerius’s chest plate to block his leverage.

Grunting and cursing at each other, both men aggressively yanked upward on the ivory shaft with their combined physical might, trying to tear it out of the sand before the other could establish a secure grip.
CLICK!
As they forcefully yanked the tooth upward, a loud mechanical sound of heavy stone gears slotting into place echoed from directly beneath their boots.
The moment something slotted deep within the subterranean bedrock, the massive golden tooth they were holding violently destabilized.
The ivory dissolved into a cloud of useless, yellow ambient mana particles, completely vanishing from between their grasping hands.
Silas and Valerius stumbled backward, their hands clutching empty air.
"What the—?" Silas started.
Before either of them could process the disappearance of the loot, the entire desert floor surrounding the basin began to violently quake and churn.
RUMBLE!
RUMBLE!
RUMBLE!
Massive swirling vortexes of abrasive sand erupted from the dunes all around them as the desert floor literally stood up.
Thousands of tons of packed, heavy sandstone and flowing desert glass rapidly coalesced, pulling together to form towering, monstrous humanoid shapes.

Within five seconds, different golems of sand that were pretty tall... each standing over fifteen feet in height, with thick tree-trunk limbs and glowing, hollow blue runes carved into their sandstone chests completely surrounded all of them in a tight, inescapable thirty-foot circle.
There were exactly six of the towering behemoths, stepping forward with earth-shattering footfalls that shook the basin.
They had formed directly out of the sand, triggered by the removal of the decoy tooth.
Valerius threw his hands in the air, his face turning bright red with absolute, explosive rage as he realized they had been baited again.
"This is the second damn trap!" Valerius cursed at the top of his lungs, kicking a pile of dirt in frustration.
"What the actual fuck is wrong with this dungeon?!
Are there literally any real treasures down here, or is this entire Secret Realm just a giant, elaborate prank designed by a bored sand god to waste my time?!"
"I am going to find Ititius’s actual physical tomb when we get out of here," Silas ranted furiously right alongside him with his patience completely exhausted by the constant trolling.
"I don’t care if he’s been dead for ten thousand years!
I will dig up his skeleton, throw his bones into fire, and melt him into scrap iron!
Who builds a fake, stat-boosting tooth just to trigger a gank squad?!"

Because they were both so aggressively busy screaming curses at the sky and complaining about ancient architectural ethics, they hadn’t even properly noticed that the six fifteen-foot-tall Golems had already raised their massive boulder-sized fists, preparing to smash them into paste.
"Lord Sy!

Sir Sterling!" Aeliana’s melodious voice called out from the edge of the circle, smoothly bringing their attention back to the immediate tactical reality of these massive Sand Golems closing in on their positions.
Silas and Valerius both stopped mid-rant, slowly turning their heads to look at the towering, fifteen-foot sandstone behemoths looming directly over them.
Both men let out a simultaneous annoyed sigh of mutual exhaustion with their shoulders slumping as they complained some more.
Watching the two towering armored Lords stand in the middle of a monster ambush and whine like grumpy teenagers made Aeliana laugh out loud.
Right beside her, Mia laughed as well, giggling behind her small hands at how funny and silly the two big men were acting.
They were very funny together...
Regardless of the comedic timing, Valerius drew a sleek high-tier mythril longsword from the scabbard at his waist.

"We need to handle these Golems before they compress the sand and trap us in a pit," Valerius stated, all traces of his earlier whining vanishing as he shifted seamlessly back into a military commander.
"Agreed," Aeliana nodded sharply.
The Starlight Arcanist immediately dropped her maternal demeanor.
She gently set Mia down on the safe, flat surface of a nearby sandstone rock, stepping forward with her hands flaring with blue-white starlight as she agreed to join the frontline clearing.
"Let’s just break them and move on," Silas agreed as well, drawing his massive, forty-pound mythril broadsword.
The heavy blade caught the amber light of the desert sky, projecting a cold shadow across the sand.
Valerius rapidly assessed the battlefield...
There were six fifteen-foot Golems surrounding their position.
"We split the aggro evenly," Valerius commanded, his tactical brain assigning targets.
"Everyone should take on one of the frontline constructs directly to break their encirclement.
I’ll take the two on the left flank!
Graves, you take the two on the right!
Elf, you hold the center line!"
"Understood," Aeli agreed smoothly, raising her hands to conjure an Arcane Aegis barrier.
Silas paused, his broadsword held low.
He blinked, looking around the formation, catching a glaring flaw in Valerius’s assignment math.

’Wait a second,’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing in deep confusion as he looked from the six massive fifteen-foot-tall, boulder-fisting Sand Golems over to the tiny, white-haired elven girl sitting on the rock. ’There are six Golems...
Valerius is taking two.
I’m taking two, Aeli is taking one.
That leaves one fifteen-foot rock monster completely unaccounted for on the rear flank.’
Silas turned his head, pointing a calloused finger at the remaining golem that was currently lumbering straight toward the outcropping where Mia was sitting.
"Valerius," Silas said flatly.
"Mia is a little girl.
Why the hell are we leaving her alone to deal with a golem?"
Valerius didn’t even look back over his shoulder.
The gold-armored Lord simply smirked, swinging his mythril sword in a practice arc.
"Watch her."
Mia however was not at all terrified by the fifteen-foot sandstone behemoth lumbering toward her rock.
In fact, she was visibly excited as well.
The little girl stood up on the edge of the sandstone outcropping with her gray cloak blowing wildly in the desert wind.
Her large green eyes flashed with an intense blue light.
Mia didn’t pull a weapon, instead she brought both of her small hands up in front of her chest, pressing her palms together as she began making a formal incantation chant.
As she spoke, her voice completely changed.
It no longer sounded like the cute chirping voice of an adorable little child.
It resonated with the deep suffocating weight of an endless, crushing ocean, carrying an ancient power that caused the very moisture in the dry desert air to violently condense around her skin.
"Hear me, dark waters...
Tide that swallows the sun...
Crush the shore, bind the sky...
Rise from the abyss and drown the light."
The exact second she finished the final syllable of the chant, the atmosphere inside the desert basin violently inverted.
A swirling sphere of deep pressurized blue water gathered directly between her small outstretched hands.
Silas, standing twenty feet away with his broadsword raised, felt the magical frequency bleeding off the little girl’s hands.
His golden-ringed eyes widened in sudden recognition.
He was well aware of this specific spell.
’Wait, It was the exact same water spell that Morwenna taught me!
It’s the standard Tier-1 Aqua Bolt... according to her, That is literally a basic foundational spell designed for novice spellcasters to practice water gathering!
It shouldn’t even leave a scratch on a sandstone golem!’
It wasn’t a basic spell anymore though, not in her hands.
The spinning sphere of dark water gathering around her small hands simply multiplied.
In a fraction of a second, the single sphere split into ten distinct globes of pressurized water and then it tripled.
Ten became thirty, swirling around her little body like a localized orbital ring of crushing marine kinetic energy.
And then it quadrupled...
ROOAAAR!
The desert air was completely displaced by the deafening sound of a localized tsunami.
Over one hundred and twenty massive compressed pressurized boulders of deep water materialized in the sky directly above the little girl’s head.
The volume of water she had pulled out of a dry desert atmosphere completely blotted out the burning amber sky, casting a massive cool shadow over the area.
The fifteen-foot Sand Golem lumbering toward her stopped dead in its tracks.
The hollow blue runes on its chest flickered erratically with its rudimentary artificial intelligence completely failing to process how a tiny entity had just conjured an entire ocean above its head.
Mia dropped her small hands forward, pointing her finger directly at the towering sandstone beast.
"Splash!" Mia chirped happily.
She shot it at the Golem.
KA-BOOM!
The entire orbital array of one hundred and twenty compressed water boulders launched forward simultaneously with the speed and velocity of naval siege torpedoes.
The impact was simply... erasure.
The torrent of dark water slammed directly into the chest of the fifteen-foot Sand Golem.
There was no struggle and there was no resistance.
The crushing hydraulic pressure of the water instantly destroyed the whole thing upon impact.
The solid sandstone torso, the tree-trunk limbs, and the reinforced mana core were violently pulverized into microscopic grains of wet mud in less than a tenth of a second.

The explosion of the water blast didn’t just obliterate her target... the residual hydraulic shockwave blasted outward across the desert area, kicking up a massive torrential rain that showered down over the remaining five Golems.
HISSSSSSS!
SKREEEE!
The freezing pressurized rain saturated the remaining Sand Golems.
Because they were constructed entirely from dry desert sand, the sudden deluge of deep water instantly turned their outer layers into thick immobile sludge.
The other Golems let out agonizing screeches of structural failure as their joints locked up with their movements completely paralyzed by the sudden mud-conversion.
Silas lowered his broadsword, his jaw slightly slack as he stared at the empty, cratered patch of wet mud where a fifteen-foot siege construct had been standing three seconds ago.
He slowly turned his head, looking up at the sandstone rock.
Little Mia was standing there, shaking a few drops of water off her ragged gray cloak.
She lowered her small hands, looking down at the shocked Lord and the smiling Elf.
She tilted her head, flashed a bright and adorable toothy smile that bared her fangs, and proudly declared her true individual value to the raid team.
"Despite how small and squishy I look," Mia giggled, placing her hands on her hips with absolute, unshakeable elven pride.
"I’m actually almost a Grandmaster in Water Magic!"

chapters.title: Chapter 169: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [VIII]
paragraphs: Silas blinked, the blinding spray of wet mud and pulverized sandstone raining down over his heavy leather boots.
He stared at the massive empty crater where the fifteen-foot golem had been standing mere seconds ago with his brain violently trying to process what he had just witnessed.
"Grandmaster in magic...?" Silas muttered, his golden-ringed eyes wide with genuine, shock.
He knew the academic magical rankings perfectly.
They were drilled into every student at the Valoria Academy. Novice, Adept, Master, Grandmaster, and Deity.

A Grandmaster was not just a title... it was a walking, breathing natural disaster. It was the highest mortal classification in existence, sitting directly right behind the threshold of a literal Deity.
Silas looked at the tiny, adorable eleven-year-old girl standing on the rock in her gray cloak.

’This little girl is that high up the magical ladder?’ Silas thought, his mind reeling. ’What the hell had she been doing? Practicing high-density hydro-manipulation since the time when she was in the womb?’
Before Silas could interrogate the terrifying child, the battlefield demanded their attention.
The torrential rain from Mia’s abyssal water strike had turned the outer carapaces of the remaining five Sand Golems into thick heavy sludge, but it hadn’t destroyed their mana cores.
"SKREEEE!"
The five massive sandstone behemoths groaned, their joints cracking as they forcibly pushed through the heavy mud, raising their massive boulder-sized fists to resume their encirclement.
Valerius tightened his grip on his mythril longsword, preparing to charge. "Watch the flanks! They’re pushing through the wet sand!"
"On it," Aeliana said smoothly, stepping past Silas without a trace of hesitation.
The Starlight Arcanist didn’t bother with defensive barriers.
She raised both of her slender hands, pointing her index fingers directly at the lumbering mud-soaked monsters.
Her A-Rank Epic mana core violently flared, illuminating the dark desert surrounding with blinding blue-white light.
"Arcane Piercer," Aeliana commanded.
She didn’t fire a single beam, Aeliana instead unleashed a devastating continuous volley.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Five compressed high-velocity beams of pure, destructive starlight mana lanced across the desert air in rapid succession.

The beams were perfectly aimed, possessing pinpoint sniper accuracy. They punched directly through the thick wet sludge coating the golems’ chests and shattered the hollow blue cores buried deep inside their sandstone torsos.
The five towering Sand Golems instantly froze in place as the magical light faded from their carved chests.
With a deafening crumble, the massive monsters completely collapsed, falling apart into nothing but massive useless piles of wet sand.
Aeliana lowered her hands, brushing a stray lock of silver hair behind her pointed ear, completely unfazed by the localized destruction she had just caused.
Silas lowered his forty-pound mythril broadsword, resting the heavy blade against his shoulder as he turned his full attention back to the little girl standing on the rock.

"How much have you been practicing?" Silas asked bluntly, staring down at Mia. "How do you even become a Grandmaster in elemental magic at your age? The mana density required to hold that much water would rupture a child’s internal pathways."
Mia giggled, a bright, highly mischievous sound.
Suddenly, she bent her small knees and launched herself into the air with terrifying superhuman leg strength.

She jumped a full eight feet straight up, completely clearing Silas’s towering frame, and landed perfectly, sitting directly on top of Silas’s shoulders. She wrapped her small legs around the back of his neck, making herself completely comfortable on his head, just like Thora.
It seemed everybody wanted to use him to do a pillow.
"You are quite misguided about my age, boy," Mia replied.
Silas froze.
Her voice hadn’t just changed... it had transformed! The cute, chirping, adorable tone of an eleven-year-old child completely vanished.
Her voice suddenly sounded incredibly deep and old.
It carried the unmistakable rasp of a woman who had lived for a very, very long time.
He immediately knew that this was an old woman.

"I am over centuries old," the voice spoke from the top of his head. "And you may refer to me as Aeliana’s Grand-Aunt, which is exactly why I possess the rank of a Grandmaster. My mana pathways matured before your current territory area was even fully formed by the Cataclysm."
Valerius, who had been resting his mythril sword on his hip, completely dropped his weapon.
The heavy blade hit the sand with a dull thud.
The gold-armored Lord stared at the little girl sitting on Silas’s shoulders with his jaw hanging open in horrified betrayal.
"You’re an old woman?!" Valerius shouted with his voice cracking slightly.
He pointed an accusatory gauntleted finger at her. "What the hell?! Why haven’t you told me that since the day I summoned you to my territory?!"
Mia looked down at her Master with a cheeky unapologetic grin spreading across her youthful face.

"Well," Mia replied with amusement. "I wanted to have some fun! The other Lords always treat ancient elven scholars with so much boring stuffy respect. Being a cute little girl lets me get away with so much more! I hope you don’t mind, my Lord."
Valerius stared at her.
He looked at the massive craters of wet sand where the golems used to be and he looked at the literal deception he had just endured.
Valerius gritted his teeth with his face turning a shade of dark red. He let out a deeply exhausted sigh, reached down to pick up his mythril sword, and looked the completely other way.
"Whatever," Valerius grumbled to the desert wind, sliding the blade back into his scabbard. "As long as you keep blowing up the monsters, I don’t care if you’re a thousand years old."
Silas watched the interaction with a genuine smirk crossing his face. Silas could get one thing about Valerius.
Honestly, the guy wasn’t that strict at all. He didn’t care about the deception or the broken whatever.

He was very much like Silas; as long as it wasn’t a matter of life or death or something too serious, and as long as his people performed in combat, he wasn’t going to enforce strict useless discipline.
Suddenly, Mia leaned forward. She reached down, her small hands grabbing a fistful of Silas’s dark, messy hair.
"So," Mia dragged his hair slightly, leaning her face upside down directly in front of his eyes. "You’re the one my Aeli loves, huh?"
Silas’s eyes widened.
Aeliana, standing a few feet away, instantly flushed a brilliant hot shade of crimson, looking away toward the dunes in embarrassment.
"You really give off the exact same vibes as that All-Father gu—" Mia continued, her ancient voice analyzing his sovereign frequency.
Silas didn’t let her finish the sentence.
His right hand shot up with blinding speed. He forcefully, firmly clamped his large, calloused palm directly over the little girl’s mouth, completely cutting off her words.

’Is she out of her mind?!’ Silas panicked internally with his heart slamming against his ribs. ’The hell... is she actively trying to reveal that I was a Gold Core?! Or that I possess the same Gold core as Odin?! Right in front of a rival City Lord?!’
Valerius, who was busy dusting the wet sand off his golden armor didn’t notice the massive lore drop being smothered.
Mia grabbed Silas’s wrist, easily pulling his hand away from her mouth with her terrifying physical strength.
She leaned in close to his ear, dropping her voice into a secure conspiratorial whisper.

"You’re hiding it, huh?" Mia whispered, a knowing mischievous glint in her green eyes. "Fair, fair. Earth politics are a messy business. I won’t tell anyone your little secret... just as long as you tell me exactly how far you’ve gone with my Aeli. Should I be expecting to be a Grand-Aunt to a half-human heir anytime soon?"
Silas closed his eyes, fighting off a massive headache.
’I sincerely preferred this woman when she was still acting like a mute kid,’ Silas thought bitterly. ’Not being so incredibly naggy about my personal life.’
Silas leaned his head slightly, whispering back so Valerius and Aeliana wouldn’t hear.
"We haven’t even kissed," Silas whispered bluntly. "I’m busy."
Mia gasped in horrified outrage.
THWACK!
She violently kicked the back of his neck with the heel of her small leather boot.
"Ow!" Silas barked, stumbling a half-step forward in the sand from the unexpected strike.

"Are you one of those oblivious dense protagonists in these terrestrial Earth novels?!" Mia whispered furiously, aggressively pulling his hair again. "You possess a Prime Body and a loyal elven arcanist! Knock her up already!"
Silas reached up, grabbed her small face with his large hand, and physically pushed her head back away from his ear.
"Stop reading trashy literature..." Silas grumbled.
Before he could properly reply to that perverted sentence, the environment around them violently changed.
FWOOSH!
A massive, howling gust of dry wind ripped across the desert basin as a dense blinding sandstorm instantly kicked up, swirling around their boots and reducing visibility to less than thirty feet.
Simultaneously, the brass Treasure Radar still gripped in Silas’s left hand began wildly vibrating.
PING! PING! PING!
"I’m guessing that’s your tracker right?" Valerius shouted, drawing his sword again as he squinted into the blowing sand.
Silas looked down at the radar. The screen wasn’t just showing a dot... it was tracking a fast-moving erratic magical signature directly above them.
He looked up into the howling sandstorm that was starting to blot out the amber sky.
Cutting through the thick clouds of dust, glowing with a brilliant pure golden light, was a massive object.
It was a golden kite, soaring through the turbulent winds on its own accord, trailing long razor-sharp ribbons of condensed wind mana behind it.
Both Silas and Valerius immediately raised their eyebrows, aiming their Lord tabs at the flying object to analyze it through the storm.
The blue holographic screens flashed in their vision.
[Name]: Ititius’s Golden Wing
[Tier]: Tier 3

[Description]: A flight item forged from the compacted desert winds of the Secret Realm. When equipped, this artifact completely bypasses baseline gravity laws, granting the user permanent, sustained, high-velocity flight capabilities and a passive +40 boost to their base Agility stat.
Once they read the description and saw the game-changing gains displayed on the system tab, all diplomacy evaporated instantly.
Permanent sustained flight? In a world where spatial control dictated survival, it was a priceless artifact!
Valerius didn’t negotiate.
He bent his knees with his mythril boots digging into the sand, and aggressively dashed forward first, launching himself toward the nearest towering sand dune to gain elevation.
"Hehehehee~ Mine!" Valerius cheered with his noble dignity completely abandoned in the face of raw loot.
"Wait up, you bastard!" Silas shouted, completely ignoring the sand whipping against his face as he launched himself into a dead sprint right after the gold-armored Lord.
Aeliana stood in the swirling dust, watching the two powerful men aggressively race each other up a massive sand dune like greedy children chasing a balloon.
The Starlight Arcanist chuckled softly with a genuine warm sound that carried over the wind as she tapped her white staff against the ground.
"Let us secure the prize, Grand-Aunt," Aeliana said.
Her body dissolved into a flash of blue-white light as she utilized her Spatial Teleportation, going right after them into the storm with pure Starlight.
Unfortunately for the other people scattered across the brutal unforgiving expanse of this desert, survival wasn’t that easy at all.
Miles away from the golden kite, on a vast flat plain of scorching cracked sandstone, the reality of the True Vault Floor was enforcing a brutal bloody tax on the weak.
Maya lay flat on her back with her sleek lightweight robes soaked through with freezing sweat and coated in abrasive dirt.
She was currently half-buried in the shifting sand, completely unable to move as her left ankle was twisted at a sickening unnatural angle, shattered by a heavy shockwave.
Lying right beside her, completely unresponsive, was Jaxon.

The Lord was knocked out cold. His thick reinforced armor was violently rent open across the chest plate, and thick dark crimson blood was steadily pouring out onto the baking sandstone, pooling around his motionless body.
Maya’s hands were shaking violently.
Her chest heaved with short hyperventilating gasps of pure terror.
She was frantically tapping the smooth black surface of the spatial tether band strapped to her wrist, desperately trying to send a distress signal to Elora.
"Help!" Maya screamed at the top of her lungs with tears streaming down her dirty face. "Elora! Silas! Please, help!"

Before he could properly reply to that perverted sentence, the environment around them violently changed.
FWOOSH!
A massive, howling gust of dry wind ripped across the desert basin as a dense blinding sandstorm instantly kicked up, swirling around their boots and reducing visibility to less than thirty feet.
Simultaneously, the brass Treasure Radar still gripped in Silas’s left hand began wildly vibrating.
PING!
PING!
PING!
"I’m guessing that’s your tracker right?" Valerius shouted, drawing his sword again as he squinted into the blowing sand.
Silas looked down at the radar.
The screen wasn’t just showing a dot... it was tracking a fast-moving erratic magical signature directly above them.
He looked up into the howling sandstorm that was starting to blot out the amber sky.
Cutting through the thick clouds of dust, glowing with a brilliant pure golden light, was a massive object.
It was a golden kite, soaring through the turbulent winds on its own accord, trailing long razor-sharp ribbons of condensed wind mana behind it.
Both Silas and Valerius immediately raised their eyebrows, aiming their Lord tabs at the flying object to analyze it through the storm.
The blue holographic screens flashed in their vision.
[Name]: Ititius’s Golden Wing
[Tier]: Tier 3
[Description]: A flight item forged from the compacted desert winds of the Secret Realm.
When equipped, this artifact completely bypasses baseline gravity laws, granting the user permanent, sustained, high-velocity flight capabilities and a passive +40 boost to their base Agility stat.
Once they read the description and saw the game-changing gains displayed on the system tab, all diplomacy evaporated instantly.
Permanent sustained flight?
In a world where spatial control dictated survival, it was a priceless artifact!
Valerius didn’t negotiate.
He bent his knees with his mythril boots digging into the sand, and aggressively dashed forward first, launching himself toward the nearest towering sand dune to gain elevation.
"Hehehehee~ Mine!" Valerius cheered with his noble dignity completely abandoned in the face of raw loot.
"Wait up, you bastard!" Silas shouted, completely ignoring the sand whipping against his face as he launched himself into a dead sprint right after the gold-armored Lord.
Aeliana stood in the swirling dust, watching the two powerful men aggressively race each other up a massive sand dune like greedy children chasing a balloon.
The Starlight Arcanist chuckled softly with a genuine warm sound that carried over the wind as she tapped her white staff against the ground.
"Let us secure the prize, Grand-Aunt," Aeliana said.
Her body dissolved into a flash of blue-white light as she utilized her Spatial Teleportation, going right after them into the storm with pure Starlight.
Unfortunately for the other people scattered across the brutal unforgiving expanse of this desert, survival wasn’t that easy at all.
Miles away from the golden kite, on a vast flat plain of scorching cracked sandstone, the reality of the True Vault Floor was enforcing a brutal bloody tax on the weak.
Maya lay flat on her back with her sleek lightweight robes soaked through with freezing sweat and coated in abrasive dirt.
She was currently half-buried in the shifting sand, completely unable to move as her left ankle was twisted at a sickening unnatural angle, shattered by a heavy shockwave.
Lying right beside her, completely unresponsive, was Jaxon.
The Lord was knocked out cold.
His thick reinforced armor was violently rent open across the chest plate, and thick dark crimson blood was steadily pouring out onto the baking sandstone, pooling around his motionless body.
Maya’s hands were shaking violently.
Her chest heaved with short hyperventilating gasps of pure terror.
She was frantically tapping the smooth black surface of the spatial tether band strapped to her wrist, desperately trying to send a distress signal to Elora.
"Help!" Maya screamed at the top of her lungs with tears streaming down her dirty face.
"Elora!
Silas!
Please, help!"

chapters.title: Chapter 170: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [IX]
paragraphs: The band remained completely dark.
The tracking runes Silas had shattered earlier had completely disrupted the network for his own so she was completely alone.
In fact, the paralyzing terror of her impending death completely overrode her bodily functions.
Maya began pissing herself with the warm urine soaking through her robes and rapidly sinking into the dry thirsty sand below her thighs.
Fifty feet away, the cause of her terror was currently executing a flawless slaughter.
Lady Seraphina, the striking red-haired daughter of the World Council magistrate was fighting two of their Heroes up front.
The desert wind whipped Seraphina’s crimson-scaled leather armor as she casually twirled her curved dagger in her right hand as the blade was already dripping with fresh smoking blood.

Jaxon’s summoned Hero... the rugged and shirtless middle-aged swordsman let out a furious desperate roar as he charged at the noble woman, swinging his two heavy iron swords in a wild overlapping cross-slash aimed directly at Seraphina’s neck.
"Die!" the swordsman roared.
Seraphina didn’t retreat as she stepped directly into the pocket of his strike.
She raised her curved dagger, aggressively channeling a dense superheated burst of fire mana into the steel.
CLANG!
Seraphina parried the dual-sword strike with effortless precision.
The sheer thermal heat radiating from her dagger instantly superheated the iron of the swordsman’s blades, making the metal glow a dull painful orange.
"You swing like a drunken, half-blind blacksmith," Seraphina insulted his swordsmanship coldly with her red eyes lacking any pity.
She smoothly slid her dagger down the length of his glowing swords, completely bypassing his guard.
SHWK!
Seraphina slashed her blade horizontally across the swordsman’s exposed scarred torso.
The white-hot edge of the dagger easily parted his flesh, instantly cauterizing the deep wound as it cut, filling the dry air with the sickening sweet smell of searing meat.
The swordsman gasped as his eyes went wide with agony.
Seraphina didn’t let him fall. She grabbed the collar of his trousers, pulled him close, and pressed the flat superheated blade of her dagger directly against his throat.
"Burn," Seraphina whispered.
A violent explosion of roaring flames erupted directly from the blade. The fire engulfed the swordsman’s head and chest entirely.
He didn’t even have time to scream.
His body turned into a charred smoking husk in less than a second, violently dissolving into dead mana particles as he was permanently unsummoned from the Secret Realm and even back in the territory.
He was dead.
"No!" Maya shrieked from the sand, watching her only physical defense turn to ash.
Before Seraphina could turn her attention to the crippled Lord, a sharp hiss cut through the air.
Maya’s one-armed archer Hero stepped out from behind a jagged sandstone pillar.
He dropped to one knee, drawing his massive darkwood longbow back with his teeth, pulling the string to maximum tension.
"Piercing Volley!" the archer shouted, spitting the string loose.
He shot at her repeatedly. Three heavy armor-piercing mana arrows blurred through the air, aimed directly at Seraphina’s chest, thigh, and head.
Seraphina didn’t panic as she moved with the fluid grace of a predator.
She gracefully ducked beneath the first arrow, spun her body to avoid the second, and aggressively swung her dagger upward to deflect the third.
CLANG!
The third arrow shattered against her blade but Seraphina didn’t stop her spin. She used the momentum to launch herself forward, rapidly closing the distance between herself and the archer.
The archer desperately tried to nock another arrow with his lone hand and his teeth, but he was too slow.
Seraphina closed the gap. She slashed her dagger downward in a brutal diagonal arc.
SNAP!
The superheated blade cleanly cut through the thick enchanted darkwood of his heavy longbow, completely snapping the weapon in half and rendering his primary offense utterly useless.
"You’re done," Seraphina stated coldly, raising her dagger for a lethal thrust to his heart but the archer was a veteran combatant. He didn’t freeze.
As Seraphina thrust her blade forward, the archer violently threw his body to the right.
He perfectly dodged her lethal slash, slipping just past the burning edge of her dagger.
Using his momentum, the archer drew a jagged rusted iron hunting dagger from his boot with his lone hand.
He lunged forward and brutally stabbed the blade directly into the lower left side of Seraphina’s stomach.
SHWK!
The iron blade pierced through the gaps in her crimson-scaled armor, sinking two inches deep into her flesh.
Seraphina gasped with her eyes going wide as a sharp agonizing spike of pain registered in her brain but the pain didn’t incapacitate her.
It infuriated her instead.
The ambient fire mana radiating from her core violently flared. The rusted iron dagger buried in her stomach instantly began to glow white-hot, burning the archer’s hand.
"Aargh!" the archer cried out, forced to release the hilt of his weapon as the metal seared his palm.
Seraphina gritted her teeth, ignoring the blade sticking out of her gut.
She pivoted her weight, loaded her hips, and delivered a devastating committed front kick directly into the center of the archer’s chest.
CRUNCH!
The sheer kinetic force of the A-Rank kick shattered his sternum.
The archer was violently launched upward into the air. He flew backward for fifteen feet before his back slammed heavily onto the hard unyielding sandstone ground.
"Gaaah!" the archer cried out in pureagonizing pain with his body violently throbbing from side to side in the dirt as he clutched his caved-in chest, completely paralyzed and unable to stand.
Seraphina didn’t finish him off. She reached down, gripped the glowing hilt of the dagger embedded in her stomach, and pulled it out with a sickening squelch.
She tossed the bloody blade into the sand with her advanced Lord vitality already beginning to clot the wound.
She turned her attention back to the primary target.
Seraphina slowly walked over the hot sand, proceeding directly toward Maya.
As she walked, she casually flicked her wrist.
The superheated energy of her curved blade instantly vaporized the blood coating the steel, burning the blood off her blade with a sharp hissing sizzle.
She stopped directly over the terrified trembling Lord mage.
Seraphina looked down at the puddle of urine soaking the sand beneath Maya’s robes and a look of disgust crossed her beautiful features.
She pressed the tip of her white-hot dagger directly against the soft skin of Maya’s throat.
"Give me the exact spatial coordinates and the location of Silas Graves," Seraphina demanded coldly. "Tell me where he is, and I will let you bleed out peacefully instead of roasting you alive."
Maya sobbed, her whole body shaking violently against the sand.

"I don’t know!" Maya cried out, her voice cracking with desperation. "I swear to the gods, I don’t know! The spatial tether bands broke! We got separated in the teleportation! I haven’t seen him since the First Layer!"
Seraphina stared down at her, reading the terror in the woman’s eyes.
She knew Maya wasn’t lying as a coward didn’t have the mental fortitude to lie with a burning blade at her throat.
Seraphina sighed, a heavy, disappointed sound.
"Get gone, then," Seraphina told her bluntly.
She raised her dagger, fully intending to stab forward and plunge the blade directly through Maya’s skull to eliminate a potential rival asset.
FWOOSH!
Before the blade could descend, a howling gust of freezing absolute-zero cold wind violently shot through the dry desert air.
The blizzard slammed directly into Seraphina’s flank like a physical battering ram.
The force of the frozen wind caught the red-haired noble completely off guard and Seraphina let out a startled gasp as she was forcefully thrown off her feet.
She rolled violently across the scorching sand with her armor scraping against the abrasive dirt, until she finally skidded to a hard stop ten feet away.
Seraphina immediately pushed herself up into a low defensive crouch, raising her burning dagger as she looked toward the source of the attack.
Standing thirty feet away, her dark corporate blazer perfectly intact and her posture radiating authority, was Elora Verinda.
The City Lord’s daughter had just arrived. Standing right beside her, holding her glowing leather-bound spellbook, was her own Hero... the pristine disciplined ice-mage.
Elora’s eyes were completely devoid of warmth.
She stared directly at the World Council magistrate’s daughter, projecting her dense aggressive Purple Core aura across the desert basin.

"I strongly suggest you keep your burning knives to yourself, Seraphina," Elora warned her. "I do not care who your father sits next to on the Council. You are actively touching my people. If you attempt to execute her, I will freeze the blood in your veins and leave you as a statue in this desert."
Seraphina narrowed her red eyes, calculating the odds.
Her stomach was bleeding, her mana was depleted from the fight with the Heroes, and Elora’s ice-mage was currently standing at full operational capacity.
It was a losing fight... unless she used her own Hero.
Elora didn’t stop there.
She looked past Seraphina with her gaze locking onto the charred smoking pile of ash that used to be Jaxon’s middle-aged swordsman Hero.
Elora’s jaw tightened.
A combat summon like that being lost when he was someone that could use the Sword God style was a massive financial loss for the guild she planned to make.

"You permanently killed his frontline physical combatant," Elora stated coldly, turning her gaze back to Seraphina. "That is a direct destruction of Verinda Guild assets... I require immediate corporate compensation and by that, I request a Hero Summoning Card from you for this."
Seraphina scoffed, a bitter angry sound escaping her lips but she knew the unwritten rules of Sovereign Realm engagement between major political houses.
If she refused to pay the blood tax, Elora had full legal justification to execute her right here in the sand.
Seraphina let out a heavy frustrated sigh.
She reached into the dimensionally expanded pocket of her crimson-scaled armor, accessing her Lord Inventory that she linked there then she pulled out a glowing silver-bordered Hero Summoning Card.
"Take your trash," Seraphina spat.
She threw the valuable card directly to the ground, letting it fall into the hot sand between them.
Seraphina slowly backed away, keeping her dagger raised defensively. Her red eyes bypassed Elora entirely, locking onto the vast open desert behind them.
"When I find Silas Graves..." Seraphina promised with her voice dropping into a dark whisper. "I am going to kill him."
Without waiting for a response, Seraphina spun on her heel.
Utilizing an advanced burst of fire-mana to boost her agility, she sprinted off into the dunes, rapidly disappearing into the heat-shimmering horizon.
Elora watched her go until she was completely out of sight.
Only then did the City Lord’s daughter let out a long exhausted sigh, rubbing the bridge of her nose to fend off an impending migraine.
She slowly walked forward, picking up the valuable Hero Summoning Card from the dirt and sliding it into her own inventory then, she walked over to where Maya was still lying in her own urine.
Elora looked down at the trembling support mage, trying as much as humanly possible to hide her a disgust at the pathetic display of cowardice.
"Get up, Maya," Elora ordered flatly. "And heal Jaxon before he bleeds out completely."
As Maya frantically began channeling low-tier restorative green mana over Jaxon’s chest wound, Elora reached into her Lord Inventory again.
She pulled out something incredibly complex and expensive.
It was a high-tier fully articulated mechanical prosthetic arm, forged from lightweight mythril and etched with highly responsive neural-sync runes.
Elora held the heavy mechanical arm out, offering it to Maya.
"Put that on your archer’s other hand," Elora commanded, gesturing toward the crippled one-armed Hero groaning in the dirt nearby. "The neural runes will adapt to his biology within seconds."
Maya stared at the expensive prosthetic, her hands shaking as she took it. "Y-yes, Lady Elora. Thank you."
Elora crossed her arms over her chest, her expression shifting into absolute, ruthless tactical focus.
"Silas’s wristband seems to have undergone a suspicious mechanical issue," Elora noted coldly.
She didn’t believe for a single second that Silas had accidentally broken his tracking device.
He was playing his own game in the dark.
Elora leaned forward, her eyes locking onto Maya’s terrified face.

"So, your primary mission parameters have changed," Elora instructed her, her voice leaving absolutely no room for failure. "You are going to take your newly repaired Hero, and you are going to track the ambient mana currents across this desert. You will find Silas Graves, wherever he is hiding."
Elora stood up straight. Her eyes began glowing with a dense terrifying blue light that completely dominated the immediate vicinity.
"Now."

chapters.title: Chapter 171: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [X]
paragraphs: The rain was coming down in relentless, jagged sheets across the endless desert basin.
Of course, in the subterranean layers of a dead god’s Secret Realm, it wasn’t regular rain.
It was a torrential downpour of razor-sharp glass shards falling directly from the burning featureless amber sky.

The millions of condensed desert glass fragments plummeted downward with the ballistic velocity of fired arrows, completely shredding the rolling sand dunes outside and filling the cavernous atmosphere with a deafening continuous high-pitched screech that grated heavily against the eardrums.
Silas was seated with his legs folded together in a calm, highly disciplined meditative posture on the ground.
He wasn’t out in the storm as he was currently sheltered securely inside a massive reinforced cover made entirely of magically conjured ice.
The frozen structure was quite huge, curving upward like a subterranean cavern onto itself, providing a freezing sanctuary against the lethal weather outside.
The walls were thick and translucent, allowing the small ambient amber light of the sky to filter into their temporary base camp.
Silas opened his eyes, listening to the violent pinging and shattering of the glass rain striking the exterior of the dome.
He reached out from his seated position, pressing his bare, calloused hand flat against the freezing wall of the shelter.
He didn’t just touch it... he channeled a dense pulse of physical energy directly into his palm and hit his hand aggressively against the ice.
THUD!
The ice didn’t even tremble.
It didn’t crack, it didn’t splinter, and it didn’t shed a single drop of ice.
The frozen water was fundamentally as strong as a corporate skyscraper’s reinforced foundation.
Silas let out a slow appreciative sigh, watching his breath fog in the chilled enclosed air.

"Magic is truly amazing," Silas murmured quietly to himself, staring at his palm. "The structural density you can achieve just by manipulating ambient moisture is terrifying... If I could reinforce my physical strikes with this kind of elemental compression, my strength in close quarters would double."
He really wanted to learn more of it, to understand the intricate pathways that governed elemental manipulation, but right now he had to focus on the important stuff.
He held a glowing, high-tier treasure in his left hand... an intricately carved sapphire amulet they had dug out of the sand hours ago.
He ran his thumb over the smooth gemstone, feeling the dense mana humming beneath the surface, before looking over at the other side of the ice cavern.
Valerius was seated right next to him.
The gold-armored Lord was holding his own treasure in his gauntleted hand... a glowing silver-forged bracer etched with avian runes.
Valerius was currently in a deep meditative stance with his eyes closed as he worked to calm his breath and cycle his depleted mana core after their frantic exhausting sprints across the dunes.
Silas watched him closely, tracking the mana flow in the room.
Every single time the aristocratic Lord breathed out, a sharp burst of green wind followed the exhale.

The wind rippled outward from Valerius’s lips, rattling some of the loose glass shards that had fallen near the entrance of the ice dome, blowing them harmlessly away across the sand before they could enter the shelter.
’It seems that Valerius has a Wind affinity from what I can see,’ Silas noted, analyzing the elemental discharge. ’That perfectly explains his ridiculous burst speed during the dune sprints earlier.’
Valerius’s eyes suddenly snapped open.

Upon feeling the scrutinizing weight of Silas’s golden-ringed eyes focused directly on him, the gold-armored Lord immediately shoved his silver bracer straight into his Lord Inventory with a rapid flash of spatial light.

"Don’t you dare try to steal this, Graves," Valerius warned him, narrowing his eyes suspiciously at Silas with his hand resting defensively on the hilt of his sheathed longsword. "I dug this out of the dirt with my own two hands and we still haven’t found that kite yet."
Silas leaned back against the ice wall, casually crossing his arms over his chest.
Valerius wasn’t wrong at all.
The Golden Wing kite... the Tier 3 Sovereign Mobility Artifact that granted permanent flight was the entire reason that they had come over in this specific direction of the desert in the first place.
It seemed that this entire sector of the wasteland was completely full of hidden treasures, at least according to the Elf’s ability and the erratic pinging of their brass radar.
But out of the fifty distinct magical signatures they had tracked and dug up over the last three hours, only two were real.

"I’m not trying to steal your shiny bracelet, Sterling..." Silas replied flatly, his tone laced with exhaustion. "I’m just annoyed. Fifty signatures... we dug fifty massive holes in the baking heat, and forty-eight of them were just glowing rocks radiating false mana."

"This Secret Realm is incredibly annoying!" Valerius complained bitterly, running a gauntleted hand through his sweat-dampened hair. "It’s using high-density elemental mirages! The mana of the dungeon is actively mirroring the exact frequency of actual artifacts... all that preparation for nothing."
"And the radar can’t filter it out," Silas added, glancing over at where Aeliana and Mia were resting. "And Mia couldn’t tell the difference either."

"It’s probably because this is the domain of a God..." Valerius sighed, throwing his hands up in frustration. "The laws here completely override baseline tracking magic! Ititius deliberately flooded the floor with false positives just to waste our stamina and bleed our mana reserves dry..."
After the small talk, Valerius stood up with his heavy mythril boots clanking loudly against the solid ice floor. He stretched his broad shoulders, his joints popping in the quiet chilled cavern.
"I am retiring inside," Valerius announced, gesturing toward the deeper recesses of the ice shelter.
He looked down at Silas with his suspicious glare fading, replaced by a begrudging genuine smirk. "I have to admit, Graves... I quite enjoyed spending time with you today."
Silas raised an eyebrow. "Is that right?"

"Yes," Valerius nodded firmly, adjusting his armor. "Regardless of how slimy and cutthroat you are, it is actually a refreshing change of pace from the people who usually spend time with me in Valoria City. The elites only tolerate my presence because they want political benefits and lucrative guild contracts."
Valerius pointed an armored finger directly at Silas’s face. "You just want to steal my treasures! It’s honest! I can respect that!"
Silas couldn’t help it. He let out a low chuckle, shaking his head at the bizarre logic but he wasn’t lying though.
"Get some sleep, Valerius," Silas wished him goodnight with a smirk. "Keep one eye open, though. I might take your boots while you’re snoring."
"You can try," Valerius snorted, turning on his heel and walking deeper into the shelter.
The interior of the massive ice cavern had been structurally modified for their overnight stay.
There were two thick splits of solid ice going through from the main entrance, dividing the shelter into private quarters.
One side was specifically designated for Valerius and his summon, and the other side was reserved for Silas and Aeliana.
Silas remained seated near the entrance, acting as the frontline sentry. From his side of the dividing wall, he could clearly see Aeliana sleeping.
She was curled up gracefully on a smooth slab of ice with her white spider-silk robes draped over her like a blanket.
Even though Elves didn’t biologically need much sleep, or to sleep at all under normal conditions, the physical and magical toll of the raid had caught up to her.
Aeliana had been constantly training and expanding her mana capacity for this whole Secret Realm operation for the past three days back at the territory.
She was exhausted.

Furthermore, she had used her Spatial Teleportation repeatedly over the last few hours to help Silas rapidly reach some highly elevated treasures hidden atop the dunes, only to find out they were useless mirages.
She had earned the rest.
On the other side of the ice wall, Silas heard Valerius’s heavy armor clatter against the ground as the Lord removed his breastplate.
Less than a minute later, the distinct sound of deep snoring echoed through the cavern.
Valerius had laid down and fallen asleep instantly.
Silas stared at the ice wall, completely bewildered. He couldn’t help but sigh, rubbing his temples in utter disbelief.

’Does this bastard really trust me that much?’ Silas thought. ’He is sleeping like a baby... Even I wouldn’t trust myself to fall asleep in front of Elora, and we are literally classmates that had known each other for years. If I wanted to, I could walk over there right now and slit his throat, though I won’t be able to take his inventory.’
Silas shook his head, deciding to accept the strange camaraderie they had formed.
He faced forward, staring out through the translucent ice wall at the relentless storm of falling glass.
Then, he heard the soft virtually silent crunch of light footsteps behind him.
Mia stepped next to him.
The little white-haired girl didn’t look sleepy at all. Her large green eyes were wide, glowing with a bright light.
Before Silas could ask her why she was out of bed, Mia raised her small hands.
"Silent void, swallow the sound. Let the air turn to stone, and seal the breath of the world," Mia chanted softly.
The air around them instantly rippled as a shimmering dome of pressurized moisture expanded outward from her small frame, creating a sound barrier that completely enveloped the two of them.
"There," Mia assured him, dropping her hands. "The others will not be able to hear a single syllable we speak."

Then, moving with a speed that completely defied her diminutive physical stature, she stepped forward and forcefully tapped her small index finger directly against the dead center of his chest before he could even react.
The moment her skin made contact with his sternum, an overwhelming wave of resonance occurred.

Silas’s chest literally illuminated from the inside out. His Gold Core violently reacted to her ancient mana, beginning to glow with a blinding golden light that shone straight through the dark fabric of his shirt.
Mia grinned with a wide satisfied smirk spreading across her youthful face.
"Ooh~ I was correct," Mia purred with her voice echoing inside the sound barrier. "You really have a Gold Core."
Silas immediately slapped her hand away, stepping backward and hastily crossing his arms over his glowing chest to physically muffle the light.
"What the hell are you doing?!" Silas complained in a furious whisper with his heart hammering against his ribs. "How did you do that?! And what if the other people saw?!"
Mia rolled her green eyes, completely unfazed by his panic.

"I am not a noob, boy," she said dismissively, waving her hand. "I am a Grandmaster. I have secured that visual variable as well. The light cannot pierce the exterior walls of this sound barrier as we are entirely concealed from Valerius’s perception as well as Aeliana."
She took a slow step closer to him, her ancient eyes looking up at him with profound reverence.

"In my long, long life," she continued, her voice becoming absolutely serious, "I have only ever met one other individual who possessed a true Gold Core... There are not even five of them in the entire endless vastness of the Sovereign Realm."
Silas froze with his anger completely evaporating, replaced by a sudden thirst for actual historical knowledge.
"They are all destined to become gods," Mia stated softly.
She looked away, staring into the dark ice.

"The one I met... the only other Gold Core I have ever laid my eyes upon... is All-Father Odin himself. I met him when he was making a territorial treaty deal with the Elf King, several centuries ago."
Silas felt a massive cold chill run directly down his spine.
"Odin..." Silas breathed out.

"Yes," Mia nodded, turning her gaze back to him. "He carried the exact same terrifying gravity that you do. Though, it is painfully clear to me that you are not using your Gold Core to its full potential."
Silas blinked, thoroughly confused. "What do you mean?"
