chapters.title: Chapter 172: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [XI]
paragraphs: "Gold Cores are not held back by the pathetic normality of regular Lords," Mia explained, dropping into the role of a stern instructor. "Like other baseline cores, there are several distinct stages of the Core which lead to Core Advancement."
Silas perked up, leaning forward slightly.
He was genuinely confused about Core Advancement.
When he had first awakened his Lord core in the beginning, he was already informed that the higher his levels got, the more the Core was being refined and compressed into a smaller denser state.
At Level 20, the first major Core Advancement was supposed to happen, but Silas didn’t feel any structural changes to his own core as he now approached that threshold.
"Why isn’t it refining automatically?" Silas asked.

"Because the advancement parameters for Gold Cores are quite different from what the regular humans now," she corrected him bluntly. "You do not simply level up by butchering beasts...To achieve the Second Stage of Core Advancement, a Gold Core Lord needs to have achieved an Adept Mastery in at least eight different elemental affinities."
Silas’s jaw dropped. He choked on his own spit, almost spitting out in disbelief.
"Eight?!" Silas hissed as his eyes wide. "The hell?! Why is it so complicated? Most Lords spend their entire lives just trying to master one or two!"

"Because you are forging the foundation of a divine territory," Mia stated simply, as if the answer was incredibly obvious. "An octagonal lattice of elemental mana is required to safely contain the density of a sovereign soul... Once you reach the Second Stage of Core Advancement, you will then be able to freely use and assimilate other higher-tier affinities. You will be able to harness the Soul affinity, and the Star Affinity like my Aeliana, who was born with it. Furthermore, the volume expansion is astronomical."
She paused, making sure he understood the scale of the power she was describing.
"In standard Lord terminologies," Mia said, "a Second Stage Gold Core holds an ambient capacity of about 30,000 mana."
Silas stared at her.
Thirty thousand mana?
He currently operated in the two-thousands and the overwhelming destructive potential of thirty thousand mana made him both surprised and incredibly excited to learn.
He could drop meteor strikes with that kind of juice.
Mia suddenly leaned forward, closing the distance between them. She tilted her small head up and took a long invasive sniff of his dark trench coat.
Silas stiffened.
’The hell is she doing?’
"I can smell Goddess Eluned on you," Mia murmured with her green eyes softening slightly with a strange warmth. "The scent of ancient nature mana is unmistakable."
She looked up at him.
"Please... make sure you keep her safe," Mia requested softly. "And happy, too. She deserves everything in the world."
Silas looked down at the little girl, recognizing the unspoken pain in her eyes as Silas nodded firmly.
"That was the plan," Silas said softly. "I protect my people."
Mia smiled, it was a bright and genuinely happy expression. It looked a lot like when Aeliana smiled.
Then, the Grandmaster’s demeanor completely vanished, replaced by the expression of a drill instructor.
Mia reached out, grabbed Silas tightly by the collar of his coat, and violently dragged him downward.
"Hey!" Silas grunted.
She dragged him directly under the sand.
The sound barrier actively spread over them, expanding into the earth like a drill, forcefully pushing the sand away and hollowing out a chamber directly beneath the ice shelter.
Above them, through the translucent ceiling of their new underground bunker, the shards of glass that were raining outside fell harmlessly around them as the barrier expanded outward.

"Since you’ve already started learning the basics of water magic," Mia announced, dusting the sand off her cloak as the barrier settled and solidified into a glowing dome. "I am going to teach you three spells today... These are water magic techniques fitting of a Gold Core Lord. They are advanced, but not too advanced for your current capacity, and they will be incredibly helpful, especially in the Sand dunes like these where moisture is scarce."
Silas dusted off his coat, rolling his shoulders as he fully committed to the training arc.
"I’m listening."

"The first is Abyssal Sever..." Mia lectured, pacing in front of him. "It allows you to compress ambient water into a razor-thin pressurized blade of fluid aqua energy capable of cleanly slicing through solid mythril armor. The chant is as follows... ’Currents of the deep, compress and divide. Water that shears the stone, form the edge.’ Try it."
Silas raised his hand.
He focused on drawing the moisture from the subterranean air.
"Currents of the deep, compress and divide. Water that shears the stone, form the edge."
A sloppy unfocused blob of water materialized in his palm, completely lacking a sharp edge as it fell to the sand with a wet splash.
THWACK!
Mia kicked him in the shin.
"You are not trying to wash your hands! You are trying to sever a spine! Compress the mana!"
Silas gritted his teeth, forced the mana tighter into a stream, and chanted again.
This time, a crescent-shaped blade of pressurized water formed over his knuckles, humming with force.

"Better," Mia nodded. "The second attacking form is Tidal Impact... It is a blunt-force projectile technique that condenses a massive volume of heavy water into a cannonball, designed to completely shatter the internal organs of heavily armored beasts through hydraulic shock and the chant is... ’Weight of the ocean, gather in the palm. Crushing depths, release the tide.’"
Silas didn’t hesitate.
He thrust his right hand forward, locking his feet in the sand. "Weight of the ocean, gather in the palm. Crushing depths, release the tide!"
A massive sphere of dark blue water formed in front of his palm.
The weight of the spell dragged his arm downward for a fraction of a second before he stabilized it with his strength.
"Good," Mia praised. "Now, the third spell. It is pure utility for gathering water magic and turning it directly into Ice."
Mia paced back and forth across the sand chamber with her hands behind her back.

"The spell is Ice Transformation, and it is categorized under Water magic, not Ice magic, because Water mages can use Ice the exact same way that Fire mages who are strong enough and can release enough intense heat can use raw plasma. It is simply extreme manipulation of your own elemental output. The chant is: ’Still the currents, banish the heat. Let the fluid sleep in absolute zero.’"

Silas listened intently, absorbing the mechanics of the spell then over the next few minutes, he practiced the spells over and over again with his hands glowing with blue light as he formed the water constructs, failed, adjusted the temperature, and formed them again.
It would be easier if this was an area with a body of water but forming water out of the moisture of the air was simply too hard... It wasn’t impossible though.
"Alright," Mia announced, stopping her pacing and dropping into a low balanced combat stance. "Theory is over as you must defend yourself."
They began to spar and it started the moment she finished speaking.
"Try this first, big guy!"
Three water bullets shot from her fingertips before Silas even finished blinking.
The first one clipped his ribs, the second smashed into his collarbone and snapped his head sideways, and the third caught him right between the eyes.
His skull rang like a bell and he tasted copper in his mouth.
’The hell... She’s really fast with it.’ Silas thought, but then again, the woman had lived centuries so of course she was fast.
"Still the currents, banish the—" he started, raising a palm and trying to form the ice shield.
She hit him again on the shoulder this time. The pressurized water bullet spun him halfway around and sent him stumbling through the wet sand.
The force of the water was high and he was suppressing his usual stats this time since he was trying to learn.
"Stop chanting!" she barked with her voice sharp as shattered glass. "Your core already knows the shape! You’re just wasting air and getting your face beaten in!"
Silas wiped his eyes.
’Is that so...?’
He just shoved his mana into the mold she’d shown him and pushed and the Abyssal Sever came out unstable but sharp enough to make the air hum.
He threw it at her.
WHOOSH!
She sidestepped with a hair’s breadth of room.
The water blade carved a deep trench into the sand wall behind her as sand poured into the cut like blood from a wound.
"That was much better," she admitted. "Again."
He threw another then another...
Wild, sloppy arcs that hissed past her ears and shredded the walls around her.
She weaved through them like they were nothing, but he caught the shift in her footwork as she was moving quicker now and actually paying attention instead of just humoring him.
’Alright then, let me take it up a notch.’ Silas thought as he switched to Tidal Impact.
He summoned the sphere and immediately regretted it as he’d overloaded the spell.
The mass of dark blue water was too heavy and his arms dropped under the weight. He almost ate sand trying to hold it up.

’That’s what I get for limiting myself...’ Silas thought but he wasn’t going to stop it, he had insane physical strength and he didn’t want to hurt her less Aeli came out and started looking at him different.
"WEIGHT OF THE—" he started, then cut himself off. ’Trust the core, dumbass.’
He launched it and the sphere shot forward, dragging a tail of mud and debris behind it.
Mia raised a single hand, flicked a needle-thin blade of water into its center, and the whole thing detonated in his face.
BOOM!
The shockwave threw him flat on his back as water and sand rained down on him like a coffin lid.
"Come on Lord Sy, get up~" she said.
He got up.
"Could you stop speaking like that...?" Silas muttered and then he looked at the puddles around him. "Honestly, how do pure mages manage this? I’d rather stick with being a swordsman."
But then he noticed it... all the water from his failed spells and all the moisture in the air from the water spells.
’This could work... Ice Transformation!’
He reached out with his mana and drained the heat.
PSSSSSSS!
The temperature cratered as ice crept across the floor, climbing up Mia’s boots and frost spiderwebbed across the walls.
His own breath turned to thick mist and the entire chamber went from a swamp to a freezer in three seconds flat.
Mia looked down at her frozen feet then up at him with one eyebrow raised.
"Tha’ts quite clever... You’ve gotten the hang of Ice Transformation quite quickly, I can see why you Gold Cores are monsters. I spent almost a decade doing what you just did."
Mia flexed and the ice shattered into a thousand pieces but Silas didn’t wait.
He was already moving.
"I thought you were quite talented, a decade for Ice Transformation, really?" Silas asked as he closed the distance and threw a heavy punch, trailing a wake of pressurized water.
She caught it on her forearm and the impact shuddered through both of them.
"Not quite talented at all, you could say the reason why I’m a Grandmaster now is simply because of hardwork, Hmph!"
She threw his hand back and he retaliated by throwing a hook but she ducked.
"Well then, I still believe you’re amazing."
He brought a knee up and she twisted away.
’A-amazing?’ Mia thought, she hadn’t heard of that one before and Silas followed with a Tidal Impact pressed against his palm like a hydraulic knuckle and drove it straight into her crossed guard.
BOOOOOM!
The impact was thunderous with her boots carving twin trenches through the sand as she slid backward.
Mia looked up.
"Ah... you flirted to make me lose my cool, that’s not manly at all Mr. Lord!" Mia said while her face turned pink.
"Flirting?" Silas asked while blinking, was he flirting with her?
The Grandmaster’s face reddened as she realized that she had misread the whole thing.
"U-uh, forget I said that! Regardless, today was really good and I’m quite surprised by what you’ve managed to accomplish."
"Thanks, same time tomorrow?" Silas asked and Mia nodded slowly as she took a step toward him with her hands clasped behind her back.
She was close now with her small frame looked almost fragile in the dim blue light of the water-drenched chamber.
"Of course, I’ll teach you more."
Silas blinked.
"However," Mia murmured. "there is one lesson you haven’t learned right now."
Silas tensed.
"Never," Mia breathed, "drop your guard after a short person."
She blurred... One moment she was in front of him.
The next moment she was behind him with her small hand already raised and before he could react, Mia’s hand came down.
CHOP!
Her fingertips connected with the exact pressure point at the base of his neck... the junction where his skull met his spine, where the nerves bundled together like a coiled serpent.
A razor-thin pulse of mana channeled directly into his central nervous system, bypassing his physical defenses entirely as Silas’s vision went white.
’I’m being knocked out again... Fuck!’
[The Next day]
Silas awoke with a groggy groan with his cheek pressed flat against the cold, hard ice of the cavern floor.
"Lord Sy! Wake up!"
He blinked his eyes open with his vision slowly clearing.
He had been dragged back up to the surface level of the shelter.
Silas looked up and saw Aeliana standing directly above him.
The silver-haired Elf was folding her hands tightly in front of her waist, her flawless face completely lacking its usual warmth.
Her green eyes were narrowed into an unimpressed glare.
"Lord Sy..." Aeliana said. "I wasn’t aware you liked my grand-aunt that much."
Silas frowned as he slowly looked down at his own body.
He was laid across the ground right in front of the cavern entrance and curled up comfortably against his side, sleeping in his arm like a teddy bear, was Mia.
The "little girl" was fast asleep, softly snoring with her white hair splayed out across his chest.
Silas stared at the ceiling of the ice cavern with the memory of the brutal training session flooding back into his aching skull.
’Fuck...’ Silas thought, letting his head drop back against the ice in pure defeat. ’Why do these women like knocking me out?’

sentences.text: "Gold Cores are not held back by the pathetic normality of regular Lords," Mia explained, dropping into the role of a stern instructor.
"Like other baseline cores, there are several distinct stages of the Core which lead to Core Advancement."
Silas perked up, leaning forward slightly.
He was genuinely confused about Core Advancement.
When he had first awakened his Lord core in the beginning, he was already informed that the higher his levels got, the more the Core was being refined and compressed into a smaller denser state.
At Level 20, the first major Core Advancement was supposed to happen, but Silas didn’t feel any structural changes to his own core as he now approached that threshold.
"Why isn’t it refining automatically?" Silas asked.
"Because the advancement parameters for Gold Cores are quite different from what the regular humans now," she corrected him bluntly.

"You do not simply level up by butchering beasts...To achieve the Second Stage of Core Advancement, a Gold Core Lord needs to have achieved an Adept Mastery in at least eight different elemental affinities."
Silas’s jaw dropped.
He choked on his own spit, almost spitting out in disbelief.
"Eight?!" Silas hissed as his eyes wide.
"The hell?!
Why is it so complicated?
Most Lords spend their entire lives just trying to master one or two!"
"Because you are forging the foundation of a divine territory," Mia stated simply, as if the answer was incredibly obvious.
"An octagonal lattice of elemental mana is required to safely contain the density of a sovereign soul...
Once you reach the Second Stage of Core Advancement, you will then be able to freely use and assimilate other higher-tier affinities.
You will be able to harness the Soul affinity, and the Star Affinity like my Aeliana, who was born with it.
Furthermore, the volume expansion is astronomical."
She paused, making sure he understood the scale of the power she was describing.
"In standard Lord terminologies," Mia said, "a Second Stage Gold Core holds an ambient capacity of about 30,000 mana."
Silas stared at her.
Thirty thousand mana?
He currently operated in the two-thousands and the overwhelming destructive potential of thirty thousand mana made him both surprised and incredibly excited to learn.
He could drop meteor strikes with that kind of juice.
Mia suddenly leaned forward, closing the distance between them.
She tilted her small head up and took a long invasive sniff of his dark trench coat.
Silas stiffened.
’The hell is she doing?’
"I can smell Goddess Eluned on you," Mia murmured with her green eyes softening slightly with a strange warmth.
"The scent of ancient nature mana is unmistakable."
She looked up at him.
"Please... make sure you keep her safe," Mia requested softly.
"And happy, too.
She deserves everything in the world."
Silas looked down at the little girl, recognizing the unspoken pain in her eyes as Silas nodded firmly.
"That was the plan," Silas said softly.
"I protect my people."
Mia smiled, it was a bright and genuinely happy expression.
It looked a lot like when Aeliana smiled.
Then, the Grandmaster’s demeanor completely vanished, replaced by the expression of a drill instructor.
Mia reached out, grabbed Silas tightly by the collar of his coat, and violently dragged him downward.
"Hey!" Silas grunted.
She dragged him directly under the sand.
The sound barrier actively spread over them, expanding into the earth like a drill, forcefully pushing the sand away and hollowing out a chamber directly beneath the ice shelter.
Above them, through the translucent ceiling of their new underground bunker, the shards of glass that were raining outside fell harmlessly around them as the barrier expanded outward.
"Since you’ve already started learning the basics of water magic," Mia announced, dusting the sand off her cloak as the barrier settled and solidified into a glowing dome.
"I am going to teach you three spells today...
These are water magic techniques fitting of a Gold Core Lord.
They are advanced, but not too advanced for your current capacity, and they will be incredibly helpful, especially in the Sand dunes like these where moisture is scarce."
Silas dusted off his coat, rolling his shoulders as he fully committed to the training arc.
"I’m listening."
"The first is Abyssal Sever..." Mia lectured, pacing in front of him.
"It allows you to compress ambient water into a razor-thin pressurized blade of fluid aqua energy capable of cleanly slicing through solid mythril armor.
The chant is as follows... ’Currents of the deep, compress and divide.
Water that shears the stone, form the edge.’ Try it."
Silas raised his hand.
He focused on drawing the moisture from the subterranean air.
"Currents of the deep, compress and divide.
Water that shears the stone, form the edge."
A sloppy unfocused blob of water materialized in his palm, completely lacking a sharp edge as it fell to the sand with a wet splash.
THWACK!
Mia kicked him in the shin.
"You are not trying to wash your hands!
You are trying to sever a spine!
Compress the mana!"
Silas gritted his teeth, forced the mana tighter into a stream, and chanted again.
This time, a crescent-shaped blade of pressurized water formed over his knuckles, humming with force.
"Better," Mia nodded.
"The second attacking form is Tidal Impact...

It is a blunt-force projectile technique that condenses a massive volume of heavy water into a cannonball, designed to completely shatter the internal organs of heavily armored beasts through hydraulic shock and the chant is... ’Weight of the ocean, gather in the palm.
Crushing depths, release the tide.’"
Silas didn’t hesitate.
He thrust his right hand forward, locking his feet in the sand.
"Weight of the ocean, gather in the palm.
Crushing depths, release the tide!"
A massive sphere of dark blue water formed in front of his palm.
The weight of the spell dragged his arm downward for a fraction of a second before he stabilized it with his strength.
"Good," Mia praised.
"Now, the third spell.
It is pure utility for gathering water magic and turning it directly into Ice."
Mia paced back and forth across the sand chamber with her hands behind her back.

"The spell is Ice Transformation, and it is categorized under Water magic, not Ice magic, because Water mages can use Ice the exact same way that Fire mages who are strong enough and can release enough intense heat can use raw plasma.
It is simply extreme manipulation of your own elemental output.
The chant is: ’Still the currents, banish the heat.
Let the fluid sleep in absolute zero.’"

Silas listened intently, absorbing the mechanics of the spell then over the next few minutes, he practiced the spells over and over again with his hands glowing with blue light as he formed the water constructs, failed, adjusted the temperature, and formed them again.
It would be easier if this was an area with a body of water but forming water out of the moisture of the air was simply too hard...
It wasn’t impossible though.
"Alright," Mia announced, stopping her pacing and dropping into a low balanced combat stance.
"Theory is over as you must defend yourself."
They began to spar and it started the moment she finished speaking.
"Try this first, big guy!"
Three water bullets shot from her fingertips before Silas even finished blinking.
The first one clipped his ribs, the second smashed into his collarbone and snapped his head sideways, and the third caught him right between the eyes.
His skull rang like a bell and he tasted copper in his mouth.
’The hell...
She’s really fast with it.’ Silas thought, but then again, the woman had lived centuries so of course she was fast.
"Still the currents, banish the—" he started, raising a palm and trying to form the ice shield.
She hit him again on the shoulder this time.
The pressurized water bullet spun him halfway around and sent him stumbling through the wet sand.
The force of the water was high and he was suppressing his usual stats this time since he was trying to learn.
"Stop chanting!" she barked with her voice sharp as shattered glass.
"Your core already knows the shape!
You’re just wasting air and getting your face beaten in!"
Silas wiped his eyes.
’Is that so...?’
He just shoved his mana into the mold she’d shown him and pushed and the Abyssal Sever came out unstable but sharp enough to make the air hum.
He threw it at her.
WHOOSH!
She sidestepped with a hair’s breadth of room.
The water blade carved a deep trench into the sand wall behind her as sand poured into the cut like blood from a wound.
"That was much better," she admitted.
"Again."
He threw another then another...
Wild, sloppy arcs that hissed past her ears and shredded the walls around her.
She weaved through them like they were nothing, but he caught the shift in her footwork as she was moving quicker now and actually paying attention instead of just humoring him.
’Alright then, let me take it up a notch.’ Silas thought as he switched to Tidal Impact.
He summoned the sphere and immediately regretted it as he’d overloaded the spell.
The mass of dark blue water was too heavy and his arms dropped under the weight.
He almost ate sand trying to hold it up.

’That’s what I get for limiting myself...’ Silas thought but he wasn’t going to stop it, he had insane physical strength and he didn’t want to hurt her less Aeli came out and started looking at him different.
"WEIGHT OF THE—" he started, then cut himself off. ’Trust the core, dumbass.’
He launched it and the sphere shot forward, dragging a tail of mud and debris behind it.
Mia raised a single hand, flicked a needle-thin blade of water into its center, and the whole thing detonated in his face.
BOOM!
The shockwave threw him flat on his back as water and sand rained down on him like a coffin lid.
"Come on Lord Sy, get up~" she said.
He got up.
"Could you stop speaking like that...?" Silas muttered and then he looked at the puddles around him.
"Honestly, how do pure mages manage this?
I’d rather stick with being a swordsman."
But then he noticed it... all the water from his failed spells and all the moisture in the air from the water spells.
’This could work...
Ice Transformation!’
He reached out with his mana and drained the heat.
PSSSSSSS!
The temperature cratered as ice crept across the floor, climbing up Mia’s boots and frost spiderwebbed across the walls.
His own breath turned to thick mist and the entire chamber went from a swamp to a freezer in three seconds flat.
Mia looked down at her frozen feet then up at him with one eyebrow raised.
"Tha’ts quite clever...
You’ve gotten the hang of Ice Transformation quite quickly, I can see why you Gold Cores are monsters.
I spent almost a decade doing what you just did."
Mia flexed and the ice shattered into a thousand pieces but Silas didn’t wait.
He was already moving.
"I thought you were quite talented, a decade for Ice Transformation, really?" Silas asked as he closed the distance and threw a heavy punch, trailing a wake of pressurized water.
She caught it on her forearm and the impact shuddered through both of them.
"Not quite talented at all, you could say the reason why I’m a Grandmaster now is simply because of hardwork, Hmph!"
She threw his hand back and he retaliated by throwing a hook but she ducked.
"Well then, I still believe you’re amazing."
He brought a knee up and she twisted away.
’A-amazing?’ Mia thought, she hadn’t heard of that one before and Silas followed with a Tidal Impact pressed against his palm like a hydraulic knuckle and drove it straight into her crossed guard.
BOOOOOM!
The impact was thunderous with her boots carving twin trenches through the sand as she slid backward.
Mia looked up.
"Ah... you flirted to make me lose my cool, that’s not manly at all Mr.
Lord!" Mia said while her face turned pink.

chapters.title: Chapter 173: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [XII / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Aeli, I can explain," Silas whispered with his voice hushed as he tried to carefully untangle his numb right arm from beneath the sleeping girl’s head. "It was a training session. We sparred with water magic. I dropped my guard, and she literally chopped me in the neck and knocked me out... I didn’t invite her to use me as a mattress."
Aeliana didn’t say a single word. She simply turned her face the completely other way, refusing to meet his eyes.
Her delicate pointed elven ears twitched with silent indignation.
Before Silas could attempt to salvage his dignity any further, the weight on his arm shifted.
Mia stirred.
The little white-haired Grandmaster let out a soft, highly exaggerated yawn, stretching her small arms high above her head.
"Haaahhh~"
She blinked her large green eyes open, looking completely innocent as she effortlessly rolled off of him, hopped to her feet, and casually dusted the frost off her gray cloak.
Silas let out an exhausted sigh as he pushed himself up off the freezing ice floor, sitting up and rubbing the sore muscles at the base of his neck where she had struck him.
From the other side of the dividing ice wall, the loud clank of boots echoed through the cavern.
Valerius stepped out from his private quarters, fully armored and eager to start the day.
He adjusted the thick leather straps on his iron gauntlets with a confident smirk plastered across his handsome face as he looked toward the cavern exit.
"Alright," Valerius announced loudly, clapping his metal hands together with a sharp sound. "Let’s get treasure hunting. I want at least three artifacts before noon—"
He paused mid-sentence.
The gold-armored Lord looked between Silas’s exhausted stiff posture on the floor, Aeliana’s icy glare facing the wall, and Mia’s innocent smile.
Valerius raised a skeptical eyebrow with his combat intuition instantly sensing the incredibly awkward tension filling the frozen room.
"Did something happen?" Valerius asked, his eyes darting between the three of them.
Before Silas could even open his mouth to address the bizarre dispute, a voice shattered the absolute silence of the desert layer.
It didn’t come from outside the ice cavern nor did it come from a hidden mechanical speaker.

The sound resonated directly inside their skulls, echoing through the very fabric of the spatial layer itself, causing the solid ice walls of their shelter to boom with a strange high-frequency magical sound.
"Hello, my lovely, greedy little intruders!"
It was a goofy obnoxiously cheerful voice that sounded out of place in a dungeon built by a dead deity.
Valerius didn’t hesitate for a microsecond.

His Lord instincts flared instantly as he drew his mythril longsword with a sharp, ringing sound and his eyes darting wildly around the corners of the ice shelter as he stepped aggressively toward the entrance.
"Show yourself!" Valerius demanded to the empty air, his mana core flaring.

Valerius was already lowering his center of gravity, charging outside to confront the speaker and swing his blade at whoever had breached their perimeter, but Silas lunged forward from his seated position.
He firmly grabbed the gold-armored Lord by the back of his shoulder plate, holding him back with raw physical strength.

"Hold on, Sterling," Silas warned, his golden-ringed eyes narrowing as he analyzed the ambient mana flowing through the air. "That’s not a person standing outside. It’s a broadcast from what I can see..."
The goofy voice continued, ignoring Valerius’s aggressive outburst completely.

"First of all, I want to formally thank everybody for entering my little domain!" the voice chimed happily, like it was that of a stage host. "It has been dreadfully boring down here for the last ten thousand years! Now, if you are currently drawing your weapons and wanting to shout at the sky to challenge me, please lower your blades. It is completely useless! This is just a spatial recording left behind by me... the great Ititus before I gracefully passed on from the mortal coil!"
Valerius slowly lowered his sword with his jaw tightening as he stared up through the translucent ice ceiling at the featureless amber sky.

"If this specific recording was triggered," the dead god continued cheerfully, "then surely this is your second day in here which means you successfully bypassed my beautiful upper labyrinth. Clever! But be warned, the structural integrity of this Secret Realm will only last for about six days before it violently collapses and throws you all out! So you really don’t have much time~!"
The incredibly cheerful and almost musical tone of the dead God’s voice discussing like this made Silas aggressively grit his teeth.

"Now," Ititus’s recording shifted, taking on a deeply patronizing, highly mocking tone. "As for the people down here who possess the rare magical ability to sense treasures, or who brought expensive little mechanical gadgets from the surface to track my loot..."
The god paused for dramatic effect.
"How were the mirages?" Ititus taunted them directly, his voice practically dripping with smug satisfaction. "Did you enjoy digging up ordinary rocks?"
"You son of a bitch!" Valerius roared at the ceiling with his composure completely shattering.

"I am going to find your tomb and turn your skeleton into a coffee table!" Silas complained furiously right alongside him with his calloused hands balling into tight fists as the exhaustion of digging fifty useless holes in the baking sun burned in his memory.
The recording actually laughed... a booming laugh that echoed across the endless dunes.

"I knew you would hate that!" Ititus chuckled warmly. "Now... enough games. For your first goal of today, if you wish to find real treasure, all of you will be facing a mandatory battle against one of my very personal guardians."
All of them paused.

Beneath their heavy boots, the solid ice of the shelter vibrated as the entire layer violently rumbled with a deep tectonic groan that shook the massive sand dunes outside and caused loose granules of dirt to cascade down the slopes like miniature avalanches.

"Don’t worry," the God’s voice reassured them breezily. "The guardian’s baseline stats will be tuned down quite a lot from its original divine peak! However, embedded deep inside this very monster is a peculiar treasure that I know will be immensely beneficial to any Lord and their terrestrial territories."
Silas perked up, his tactical Lord logic immediately engaging, pushing past his annoyance.

"It is a Realm Seed," Ititus announced proudly. "Consuming this seed and planting it within the borders of your territory will permanently expand your territory by five miles in every direction... progressively though! It will fortify your existing defensive structures with unbreakable bedrock, drastically increase your mana density, and expand your maximum population cap! But not only that... whoever assimilates the core of this seed into their own body will be granted a permanent, high-tier affinity for Sand Magic!"
The transmission clicked sharply, and the voice vanished leaving only the hollow howling of the desert wind.
All of them perked up instantly.

’A Realm Seed?’ Silas thought rapidly, his mind spinning with the immense tactical possibilities. ’I already have a Sand Affinity from being a Gold core, but who’s to say I couldn’t give it to someone like Rowenna back at the territory?’
The image of his Head Maid flashed in his mind.
Rowenna already possessed a devastating Gravity affinity that allowed her to crush enemies into the dirt.
If she could manipulate the mass of gravity while simultaneously commanding an ocean of abrasive slicing sand... she would become an unstoppable walking natural disaster.
She would have gravity and different kinds of magic as well as Sand, which would be a terrifying upgrade to their defensive line.
"We are getting that seed," Silas declared flatly, turning to Valerius.
"Try and stop me," Valerius challenged right back, slamming his sword into its scabbard with a sharp click.
They departed for the coordinates immediately.
The distant continuous rumble of the Guardian forming provided a clear undeniable tectonic beacon across the wasteland.
Stepping out of the freezing ice shelter into the blinding, baking heat of the desert, Mia clapped her small hands together.
"Currents freeze, carve the dunes!" Mia chanted smoothly, her voice commanding and precise, completely lacking the playful tone of a child.
She didn’t create a defensive shield.

She utilized the moisture from the air to rapidly construct a massive and perfectly smooth sled made of solid dark blue ice. It hovered exactly an inch above the baking sand, actively chilling the air around it.
"Get on!" Mia cheered.
She jumped up, gracefully landing and clinging to her Lord, planting her boots firmly on Valerius’s broad armored shoulders like a surfer preparing to ride a wave.
Mia looked back over her shoulder. "Aeliana, cling to your own!"
Aeliana, still acting cold and distant toward Silas, hesitated for a fraction of a second but the ice sled was already beginning to hum with mana.
She stepped onto the back of the construct, reached out, and wrapped her slender arms tightly around Silas’s stomach, pressing her chest flush against his back.
"Sorry for acting like that with you Lord Sy but you’ve never held me to sleep before."
Silas’s eyes widened.
"So—"
Then, Mia made them move.
She aggressively channeled a continuous high-pressure stream of water magic directly from the rear of the sled.
The propulsion was instantaneous and violent.
WHOOSH!
The ice sled launched forward across the desert dunes with terrifying breakneck velocity, completely ignoring the friction of the sand.

Valerius was actively surfing the front of the construct with Mia on his shoulders, laughing loudly as the hot wind whipped his hair, while Silas stood planted in the center, bracing his heavy boots against the brutal G-force.
Behind him, Aeliana completely lost her stoic composure.

"Ahhhhh!" Aeliana screamed, burying her face directly into the back of Silas’s dark trench coat and clinging to his stomach for dear life as the sled launched fifty feet into the air over the crest of a massive sand dune.
Minutes later, they violently skidded to a halt.
The massive ice sled shattered into a cloud of harmless snow as they arrived at the edge of the designated arena.
Silas and Valerius immediately dropped low, dragging their respective Heroes down with them.
They slid securely behind a massive, towering sandstone boulder overlooking a sprawling perfectly flat expanse of baked desert glass.
Down in the massive clearing, the monster was currently forming.
The other Lords from the drop were already gathering, forming a loose perimeter around the epicenter.
Silas peered around the jagged edge of the rock, scanning the battlefield geometry.
He saw Harper, her purple hair whipping in the wind as she stood aggressively at the front line, electricity already sparking erratically from her fingertips.
Twenty yards to her left was Elora Verinda, her glowing soul-bound spellbook open as her disciplined Ice-Mage Hero prepared a defensive ward.
Julian was there too, hiding cowardly behind a jagged rock, occasionally poking his wand out to check if the coast was clear.
There was also that other Lord Elora had explicitly warned them to be careful of... the arrogant gold-armored spear-wielder who commanded a massive, heavily plated rhino summon.
He was currently barking loud, useless orders at the lesser nobles, trying to force them to form a crude shield wall in front of him.
The only one notably missing from the clearing was Seraphina.
"Let them take the whole thing..." Valerius whispered, crouching next to Silas with a wicked smile on his face.
Down in the exact center of the glass arena, the sand monster fully formed.
It was utterly bizarre, yet undeniably terrifying.
The monster was an eight-foot-tall humanoid constructed entirely of densely packed, shifting yellow sand.
The grains of its body constantly rotated like a sandstorm but it wasn’t wielding desert glass or sandstone.
It possessed two massive clawed hands, and it was holding a massive swirling staff made entirely of snow and ice.
The elemental contradiction was glaring, a testament to the dead god’s twisted sense of humor.
"Come," the Sand Guardian rumbled, its voice sounding like grinding tectonic plates dragging across each other.
It didn’t wait to be surrounded as it immediately seized the initiative, starting the engagement by rushing forward with explosive unnatural speed directly at one of the Lords in the front line.
The young Lord in heavy iron armor raised his kite shield, bracing his boots against the smooth glass.
The Guardian swung the massive staff made of snow in a brutal overhead arc.
CRACK!
The sheer force behind the blow was astronomical.
The impact completely shattered the Lord’s steel shield into useless, flying shrapnel.
"Ahhhhh!"

The Lord screamed as the physical blow bypassed his broken guard and connected directly with his chest plate, physically lifting him off his feet and making him fly backward through the air like a discarded ragdoll.
He crashed into a dune fifty feet away, completely incapacitated in a single strike.

"First of all, I want to formally thank everybody for entering my little domain!" the voice chimed happily, like it was that of a stage host.
"It has been dreadfully boring down here for the last ten thousand years!
Now, if you are currently drawing your weapons and wanting to shout at the sky to challenge me, please lower your blades.
It is completely useless!
This is just a spatial recording left behind by me... the great Ititus before I gracefully passed on from the mortal coil!"
Valerius slowly lowered his sword with his jaw tightening as he stared up through the translucent ice ceiling at the featureless amber sky.
"If this specific recording was triggered," the dead god continued cheerfully, "then surely this is your second day in here which means you successfully bypassed my beautiful upper labyrinth.
Clever!
But be warned, the structural integrity of this Secret Realm will only last for about six days before it violently collapses and throws you all out!
So you really don’t have much time~!"
The incredibly cheerful and almost musical tone of the dead God’s voice discussing like this made Silas aggressively grit his teeth.
"Now," Ititus’s recording shifted, taking on a deeply patronizing, highly mocking tone.
"As for the people down here who possess the rare magical ability to sense treasures, or who brought expensive little mechanical gadgets from the surface to track my loot..."
The god paused for dramatic effect.
"How were the mirages?" Ititus taunted them directly, his voice practically dripping with smug satisfaction.
"Did you enjoy digging up ordinary rocks?"
"You son of a bitch!" Valerius roared at the ceiling with his composure completely shattering.

"I am going to find your tomb and turn your skeleton into a coffee table!" Silas complained furiously right alongside him with his calloused hands balling into tight fists as the exhaustion of digging fifty useless holes in the baking sun burned in his memory.
The recording actually laughed... a booming laugh that echoed across the endless dunes.
"I knew you would hate that!" Ititus chuckled warmly.
"Now... enough games.
For your first goal of today, if you wish to find real treasure, all of you will be facing a mandatory battle against one of my very personal guardians."
All of them paused.

Beneath their heavy boots, the solid ice of the shelter vibrated as the entire layer violently rumbled with a deep tectonic groan that shook the massive sand dunes outside and caused loose granules of dirt to cascade down the slopes like miniature avalanches.
"Don’t worry," the God’s voice reassured them breezily.
"The guardian’s baseline stats will be tuned down quite a lot from its original divine peak!
However, embedded deep inside this very monster is a peculiar treasure that I know will be immensely beneficial to any Lord and their terrestrial territories."
Silas perked up, his tactical Lord logic immediately engaging, pushing past his annoyance.
"It is a Realm Seed," Ititus announced proudly.
"Consuming this seed and planting it within the borders of your territory will permanently expand your territory by five miles in every direction... progressively though!
It will fortify your existing defensive structures with unbreakable bedrock, drastically increase your mana density, and expand your maximum population cap!
But not only that... whoever assimilates the core of this seed into their own body will be granted a permanent, high-tier affinity for Sand Magic!"
The transmission clicked sharply, and the voice vanished leaving only the hollow howling of the desert wind.
All of them perked up instantly.

’A Realm Seed?’ Silas thought rapidly, his mind spinning with the immense tactical possibilities. ’I already have a Sand Affinity from being a Gold core, but who’s to say I couldn’t give it to someone like Rowenna back at the territory?’
The image of his Head Maid flashed in his mind.
Rowenna already possessed a devastating Gravity affinity that allowed her to crush enemies into the dirt.
If she could manipulate the mass of gravity while simultaneously commanding an ocean of abrasive slicing sand... she would become an unstoppable walking natural disaster.
She would have gravity and different kinds of magic as well as Sand, which would be a terrifying upgrade to their defensive line.
"We are getting that seed," Silas declared flatly, turning to Valerius.
"Try and stop me," Valerius challenged right back, slamming his sword into its scabbard with a sharp click.
They departed for the coordinates immediately.
The distant continuous rumble of the Guardian forming provided a clear undeniable tectonic beacon across the wasteland.
Stepping out of the freezing ice shelter into the blinding, baking heat of the desert, Mia clapped her small hands together.
"Currents freeze, carve the dunes!" Mia chanted smoothly, her voice commanding and precise, completely lacking the playful tone of a child.
She didn’t create a defensive shield.
She utilized the moisture from the air to rapidly construct a massive and perfectly smooth sled made of solid dark blue ice.
It hovered exactly an inch above the baking sand, actively chilling the air around it.
"Get on!" Mia cheered.
She jumped up, gracefully landing and clinging to her Lord, planting her boots firmly on Valerius’s broad armored shoulders like a surfer preparing to ride a wave.
Mia looked back over her shoulder.
"Aeliana, cling to your own!"
Aeliana, still acting cold and distant toward Silas, hesitated for a fraction of a second but the ice sled was already beginning to hum with mana.
She stepped onto the back of the construct, reached out, and wrapped her slender arms tightly around Silas’s stomach, pressing her chest flush against his back.
"Sorry for acting like that with you Lord Sy but you’ve never held me to sleep before."
Silas’s eyes widened.
"So—"
Then, Mia made them move.
She aggressively channeled a continuous high-pressure stream of water magic directly from the rear of the sled.
The propulsion was instantaneous and violent.
WHOOSH!
The ice sled launched forward across the desert dunes with terrifying breakneck velocity, completely ignoring the friction of the sand.

Valerius was actively surfing the front of the construct with Mia on his shoulders, laughing loudly as the hot wind whipped his hair, while Silas stood planted in the center, bracing his heavy boots against the brutal G-force.
Behind him, Aeliana completely lost her stoic composure.

"Ahhhhh!" Aeliana screamed, burying her face directly into the back of Silas’s dark trench coat and clinging to his stomach for dear life as the sled launched fifty feet into the air over the crest of a massive sand dune.
Minutes later, they violently skidded to a halt.
The massive ice sled shattered into a cloud of harmless snow as they arrived at the edge of the designated arena.
Silas and Valerius immediately dropped low, dragging their respective Heroes down with them.
They slid securely behind a massive, towering sandstone boulder overlooking a sprawling perfectly flat expanse of baked desert glass.
Down in the massive clearing, the monster was currently forming.
The other Lords from the drop were already gathering, forming a loose perimeter around the epicenter.
Silas peered around the jagged edge of the rock, scanning the battlefield geometry.
He saw Harper, her purple hair whipping in the wind as she stood aggressively at the front line, electricity already sparking erratically from her fingertips.
Twenty yards to her left was Elora Verinda, her glowing soul-bound spellbook open as her disciplined Ice-Mage Hero prepared a defensive ward.
Julian was there too, hiding cowardly behind a jagged rock, occasionally poking his wand out to check if the coast was clear.
There was also that other Lord Elora had explicitly warned them to be careful of... the arrogant gold-armored spear-wielder who commanded a massive, heavily plated rhino summon.
He was currently barking loud, useless orders at the lesser nobles, trying to force them to form a crude shield wall in front of him.
The only one notably missing from the clearing was Seraphina.
"Let them take the whole thing..." Valerius whispered, crouching next to Silas with a wicked smile on his face.
Down in the exact center of the glass arena, the sand monster fully formed.
It was utterly bizarre, yet undeniably terrifying.
The monster was an eight-foot-tall humanoid constructed entirely of densely packed, shifting yellow sand.
The grains of its body constantly rotated like a sandstorm but it wasn’t wielding desert glass or sandstone.
It possessed two massive clawed hands, and it was holding a massive swirling staff made entirely of snow and ice.
The elemental contradiction was glaring, a testament to the dead god’s twisted sense of humor.
"Come," the Sand Guardian rumbled, its voice sounding like grinding tectonic plates dragging across each other.
It didn’t wait to be surrounded as it immediately seized the initiative, starting the engagement by rushing forward with explosive unnatural speed directly at one of the Lords in the front line.
The young Lord in heavy iron armor raised his kite shield, bracing his boots against the smooth glass.
The Guardian swung the massive staff made of snow in a brutal overhead arc.
CRACK!
The sheer force behind the blow was astronomical.
The impact completely shattered the Lord’s steel shield into useless, flying shrapnel.
"Ahhhhh!"

The Lord screamed as the physical blow bypassed his broken guard and connected directly with his chest plate, physically lifting him off his feet and making him fly backward through the air like a discarded ragdoll.
He crashed into a dune fifty feet away, completely incapacitated in a single strike.

chapters.title: Chapter 174: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [XIII / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Mages, hit it with moisture!" the spear-wielding Lord shouted frantically from behind his rhino. "Turn its sand to mud! Disable its joints!"
A Hero who was a water mage stepped forward from the backline. He rapidly chanted, raising his wooden staff to the sky.
"Gather the weeping sky, drown the earth!" the mage shouted, casting a high-tier, localized rain spell.

A dark storm cloud rapidly formed directly over the Guardian’s head, and heavy torrential rain began to fall, aiming to saturate the monster’s sandy exterior however the monster didn’t dodge the rain.
It simply looked up at the cloud.
It bent its thick sandy knees, leaped thirty feet straight up into the air with terrifying leg strength, and violently stabbed its staff directly into the very center of the magical cloud.
SHWK!
The density of the absolute-zero ice weapon literally punctured the magical structure in the middle.
The magic circle of the cloud violently destabilized, bursting apart into a massive wave of harmless white mist before the rain could even soak the monster’s shoulders.
’I have to seize this opportunity...’
Harper seized the opening as the heavy Guardian landed back on the glass.
"Fulgur Strike!"
She fired a massive, blinding blast of purple lightning directly into its chest.
At the same time, the other Lords attacked it with a barrage of explosive fireballs and wind slices.
The clearing became a deafening warzone of exploding magic, blinding light, and flying sand.
All the while, Valerius chuckled from the safety of the back of the stone.

"Look at them burn their mana reserves..." Valerius smirked, leaning his armored shoulder against the sandstone. "We just need to wait and take it and let them wear down its regeneration cycles. The first one there to snatch the core out of its chest when it shatters gets the seed."
"Agreed," Silas nodded, his eyes tracking the Guardian’s movements through the smoke and fire but in the middle of the frantic fight, the Guardian suddenly stopped swinging its ice staff.
It completely ignored Harper’s secondary bolt of lightning with the electricity simply grounding out harmlessly through its thick sandy legs into the glass floor.
It slowly turned its featureless sand face away from the main raid group, looking directly over toward the massive boulder where Silas and Valerius were hiding.
"People who are hiding are nothing more than cowards," the Guardian stated, its grinding voice echoing across the chaotic arena, perfectly audible over the explosions.
"It can talk!"
"Damn, who’s hiding!"
"Is it those two fuckers from before?!"
Valerius’s eyes widened in horror.
"Fuck..."
The Guardian raised its snow staff, pointing the jagged tip directly at their boulder.
It didn’t cast an ice spell as it actively manipulated the ambient atmospheric pressure of the desert itself.
"Begone!"
It blasted a massive wind wave directly at their position.
The invisible shockwave slammed into the boulder with the force of a detonating artillery shell.
BOOM!
The impact cracked the massive sandstone rock clean in half, sending massive chunks of debris flying in all directions.
However, due to the strange erratic spatial distortion of the Secret Realm’s physics or perhaps just the sheer targeted malice of the dead god’s spell... the shockwave didn’t hit everyone evenly.
It completely bypassed Valerius, Mia, and Aeliana with the force flowing harmlessly around them like a stream around a rock in a river.
It only caught Silas.
The Lord was violently ripped from the ground, caught perfectly in the dead center of the ascending violently swirling wind tunnel.
"Fuck!" Silas yelled at the top of his lungs as he was forcefully ejected from his hiding spot with his trench coat whipping wildly around him.
He was thrown through the air, soaring helplessly in a massive parabolic arc over the heads of the battling Lords below.
He sailed entirely over the dunes, completely out of the arena bounds with the crushing G-force pressing him against the sky before gravity finally reasserted itself and he began descending.
CRASH!
He landed incredibly heavily on the ground, his body absorbing the brunt of the impact as his heavy boots carved a deep twenty-foot trench into the slope of a distant sand crater.
"Fucking hell..."
Silas groaned loudly with his entire skeletal structure rattling from the sheer force of the fall.
He pushed himself up onto his hands and knees, spitting a mouthful of dry bitter sand onto the dirt.
He was quite far away from the arena place now, surrounded entirely by tall, silent dunes that completely muffled the sounds of the ongoing raid.
"Fucking wind magic..." Silas muttered darkly, rubbing his sore bruised shoulder as he stood up.
He dusted the loose dirt off his dark trench coat, rolling his neck until it popped, and looked around to get his bearings.
Then, he saw something.
Fifty feet away, partially obscured by the shadow of a sloping wind-carved dune, a woman was squatting in the sand.
Her crimson-scaled leather armor was unbuckled with her expensive enchanted utility belts discarded casually on the dirt beside her.

She had her dark leather trousers pulled down to her knees as she was currently finishing up a very private and necessary biological function with the last bits of pee coming down and soaking into the dry desert sand beneath her boots.
Silas froze, completely paralyzed by the absurdity of the situation.
Because of his elevated angle on the slope and the harsh unforgiving amber light of the desert, Silas could clearly see Seraphina’s incredibly sexy and flawlessly toned legs.

The smooth pale curve of her thighs contrasted sharply against the crimson armor, and the curvaceous athletic figure of a woman who had spent her entire life training in high-tier physical combat was fully exposed.
He could see everything...
Seraphina heard the crunch of sand beneath Silas’s boots and she slowly turned her head over her shoulder.
Her fiery red eyes locked directly onto Silas Graves’s golden-ringed eyes.
For one long suffocating second, neither of them breathed.
The world-ending humiliation hit Seraphina like a physical blow to the stomach as her noble face instantly flushed a brilliant hot shade of red that completely rivaled the color of her fiery hair.

"S-s-s-silas G-g-graves!" Seraphina stuttered wildly with her voice cracking in a high-pitched squeak as genuine furious tears of embarrassment began gathering in the corners of her eyes. "Y-you... what are you... you perverted—!"
Silas took a slow calculated step backward, raising both of his hands in a gesture of non-combative surrender.
"O-oh..." Silas said brilliantly.
He didn’t try to explain the physics of the wind wave and he didn’t offer a polite apology.
He immediately turned on his heel, dug his boots into the sand, and began running for his life!
Behind him, chaos erupted.
Seraphina frantically pulled up her trousers as her hands were shaking so violently with rage that she almost tripped.
She snatched her curved superheated dagger from the sand as her aura flared with terrifying unrestrained murderous intent.
She chased directly after him, sprinting across the dunes like a vengeful bloodthirsty demon.

"I hate you!" Seraphina shouted at the top of her lungs with her voice echoing across the wasteland as she hurled a roaring blast of fire magic that barely missed Silas’s head. "I hate you! I hate you!"
Silas sprinted up the steep slope of a massive dune with his boots kicking up heavy clouds of sand as he ducked under another roaring fireball that seared the air above him.
’Why the hell is she going after me?!’ Silas thought frantically. ’It’s a mistake! I didn’t mean to look! I literally got thrown here by a giant sand monster! This woman is completely insane!’
Back at the shattered boulder overlooking the arena, the dust finally settled from the wind blast.
Aeliana coughed, waving the thick cloud of sand away from her flawless face.
She looked to her right, where Silas had been crouching just seconds ago. The space was completely empty.
"Lord Sy?" Aeliana called out, her voice laced with sudden concern.
She immediately realized he had been launched entirely out of the combat zone so Aeliana’s glowing silver eyes narrowed with her loyalty completely overriding her previous annoyance with him.
She didn’t hesitate for a single microsecond.
Aeliana teleported instantly with her body dissolving into a brilliant flash of blue-white starlight, completely leaving Mia and Valerius behind to face the music of the raid.
Valerius stepped out from behind the broken rock with his mythril sword drawn as a deeply exhausted sigh escaped his lips.
"Well, so much for waiting," Valerius muttered, cracking his neck from side to side.
He held his ground as the battle in the arena fully escalated into a chaotic bloodbath.
"Let’s show this pile of dirt how a Lord fights!" Valerius roared with his aura flaring green.
Valerius and Mia charged directly into the fray, seamlessly joining Elora, Harper, and the remaining Lords as they all jumped that monster.
"Rageeeee!"
The arrogant Lord with the spear yelled a command, pointing his weapon forward.
His massive plated rhino summon lowered its thick iron horn and charged the Guardian at full terrifying speed.
BOOM!
The Guardian didn’t even flinch.

It dropped its stance, caught the charging rhino directly by the horn with its free massive sandy hand with the abrasive grains grinding harshly against the metal plating, and brutally slammed its snow staff directly into the side of the beast’s skull.
The rhino let out an agonizing screech with its heavy legs buckling as it fell to its knees.
The physical force of the blow fractured its skull, bringing it near to death in a single devastating strike as its summoner desperately chanted to recall it before it shattered completely.
"Frail sparks!" the Guardian roared with its voice shaking the glass floor as it swung the staff in a wide, incredibly fast horizontal arc.
A Lord wielding dual iron axes, who had foolishly tried to flank the monster from the right blind spot, didn’t raise his guard in time.
KRA-THOOM!
The impact of the heavy ice staff violently crushed the Lord’s ribcage inward with a sickening crunch.
The Lord spat a massive geyser of dark crimson blood, dying instantly before his broken body even hit the glass ground.
His corpse dissolved into ambient particles as his Hero was forcibly unsummoned in a flash of dead light.
"Fuck!"
Julian shrieked in absolute terror, diving behind a rock and curling into a pathetic ball, completely abandoning the fight.
Because Maya and Jaxon weren’t here, the raid lacked a dedicated Vanguard tank to absorb the heavy kinetic blows. That highly dangerous duty fell entirely to Valerius.
And Valerius himself was excellent.
The gold-armored Lord moved like a literal hurricane.

It was clear to anyone with sense that nobody was using their full power yet as everyone was selfishly conserving their deepest mana reserves for the final, lethal strike to steal the seed but Valerius was still incredibly strong without his ultimate techniques.
He utilized his Wind Affinity flawlessly, channeling high-pressure gales directly into the soles of his boots to rapidly dash around the Guardian’s lumbering earth-shattering strikes.
WHOOSH!
Valerius dodged a downward smash that cracked the glass floor, pivoting cleanly on his heel.
He breathed in, drawing the air into his core, and completely dropped the atmospheric pressure around his blade.
"Vacuum Domain: Severing Gale!" Valerius commanded, his eyes glowing with fierce intensity.
He swung his mythril blade, unleashing a massive razor-sharp arc of compressed green wind.
The technique didn’t just push the sand... it completely severed the molecular bonds of the monster’s torso, slicing a deep gaping trench directly into the center of the Guardian’s chest.
SHWK!
Mia contributed heavily from his flank.
The little Grandmaster didn’t use massive flashy mana-draining spells.
"Heheh~"

She raised her small hands and fired hyper-pressurized microscopic jets of water... miniature Abyssal Severs the size of sewing needles that drilled straight through the Guardian’s knees and elbows, severely compromising its structural integrity and causing its heavy sand to clump and fall off in wet chunks.
"Fulgur Strike! Fulgur Strike! Fulgur Strike!"
Harper unleashed continuous deafening volleys of Fulgur Strikes with the thick purple lightning heavily scorching the Guardian’s remaining sand armor into patches of brittle black glass.
Elora stood back with her eyes glowing a chilling blue.
"Glacial Bind!"
The moment she uttered the spell, the ground beneath the monster began to freeze, locking its sandy boots securely to the floor.
Under the combined coordinated assault, the Guardian began to falter.
Its massive movements grew sluggish with the yellow sand beginning to heavily fall away from its internal core.
Of course, the divine monster was not that easily defeated.

"Vacuum Domain: Severing Gale!" Valerius commanded, his eyes glowing with fierce intensity.
He swung his mythril blade, unleashing a massive razor-sharp arc of compressed green wind.
The technique didn’t just push the sand... it completely severed the molecular bonds of the monster’s torso, slicing a deep gaping trench directly into the center of the Guardian’s chest.
SHWK!
Mia contributed heavily from his flank.
The little Grandmaster didn’t use massive flashy mana-draining spells.
"Heheh~"

She raised her small hands and fired hyper-pressurized microscopic jets of water... miniature Abyssal Severs the size of sewing needles that drilled straight through the Guardian’s knees and elbows, severely compromising its structural integrity and causing its heavy sand to clump and fall off in wet chunks.
"Fulgur Strike!
Fulgur Strike!
Fulgur Strike!"
Harper unleashed continuous deafening volleys of Fulgur Strikes with the thick purple lightning heavily scorching the Guardian’s remaining sand armor into patches of brittle black glass.
Elora stood back with her eyes glowing a chilling blue.
"Glacial Bind!"
The moment she uttered the spell, the ground beneath the monster began to freeze, locking its sandy boots securely to the floor.
Under the combined coordinated assault, the Guardian began to falter.
Its massive movements grew sluggish with the yellow sand beginning to heavily fall away from its internal core.
Of course, the divine monster was not that easily defeated.

chapters.title: Chapter 175: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [XIV / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: It violently ripped its boots free from the ice, shattering Elora’s bind.
CRUNCH!
"That was good..."
It raised its snow staff high above its head with the ice glowing with a blinding light, and slammed it down directly into the center of the arena.
A blizzard erupted with the freezing wind physically pushing all the Lords back twenty feet.
"It’s time to go Phase tw—" the Guardian rumbled, preparing to initiate its second health bar and regenerate its sand armor.
It never got the chance.
From the high ridge of the dunes directly behind the arena, they all heard a furious tear-soaked scream of rage that completely drowned out the howling wind of the blizzard.
"SILAS GRAVES!"
Seraphina burst over the crest of the dune, sprinting at full terrifying speed.
Silas was running for his life just ten yards ahead of her, his dark trench coat flapping wildly as he inadvertently led the furious flushed red-haired noble directly back into the combat arena.
Seraphina didn’t care about the raid.
She didn’t care about the Guardian and she didn’t even care about the Realm Seed.
The noblewoman was completely consumed by humiliation and a burning desire for murder.
She aggressively channeled every single drop of her remaining fire mana in her core into her weapon as she didn’t hold back a single percentage of her power.
She threw her curved dagger forward with all her might, putting her full strength into the projectile and it burned like a descending meteor.

The dagger tore through the air, radiating so much intense superheated energy that it literally burned the sand floating in the air where it touched, turning the dust into trailing glowing sparks of molten glass.
Silas heard the roaring flames closing in behind him and he didn’t look back to check the distance.
He simply threw his entire body sideways, diving face-first into the dirt and rolling aggressively.

’It’s a fucking curse to limit my physical abilities anytime I’m around these fuckers!’ Silas thought as the meteor-strike dagger flew right past the exact coordinate where his head had been a microsecond prior.
It continued its blazing trajectory, soaring straight past him and directly into the center of the arena.
KA-BOOOOOOM!

The superheated dagger impacted the Guardian directly in the center of its chest, striking exactly where Valerius had just carved a deep trench with his wind magic and Mia had drilled with her pressurized water.
The explosion was catastrophic.

The overwhelming thermal shock of a fully powered fire strike, combined perfectly with the structural damage caused by the help of the other previous attacks, was simply too much for the divine construct to withstand.
The Guardian’s core violently destabilized as the packed sand melted into useless slag.
"A fitting... end..." the monster made a final, grinding remark as its existence collapsed then, it popped.
The entire eight-foot monster violently exploded into a massive harmless shower of dry sand, steam, and melted snow, washing over the exhausted Lords.
Floating perfectly in the air, right where the monster’s chest had been seconds prior, a glowing smooth Gold Seed was revealed.
Valerius was the closest and his eyes went wide with pure greed.
He immediately used a concentrated explosive burst of wind magic directly beneath his boots to reach it, launching himself straight up into the air.
He reached out with his iron gauntlet, zoning in on the priceless prize.
Everything turned into slow motion.
Valerius could see the intricate, pulsing runes carved deep into the surface of the golden seed as his gauntleted fingers were mere inches away from claiming the ultimate territorial upgrade!
’Hah!’ Valerius thought triumphantly, a massive, victorious grin spreading across his handsome face. ’It’s min—’
VWOOP!
A hand appeared out of thin air and snagged the seed right out of the sky.
Valerius blinked with his hand, grasping completely empty space.
His momentum died, and he began to fall back toward the sand as he looked up, his brain desperately trying to process the theft.
Hanging in the air directly above him, bathed in the fading blue-white glow of spatial magic, was Silas.

The Lord had a tight secure grip on the Gold Seed and clinging tightly to his back, her arms wrapped securely around his neck, was Aeliana, who had flawlessly timed her high-tier Spatial Teleportation to intersect precisely with the loot drop.
Valerius stared up at the duo as gravity pulled him down with a smug look washing over his features.
"Fu... fuck me," Valerius whispered, realizing he had just been flawlessly robbed by a coordinated team effort.
Aeliana appeared right behind Silas as his boots touched the glass, hugging him tighter as the starlight flared again.
"Got it." Silas smirked, tossing the seed into his inventory.
With a blinding flash of silver starlight, they vanished entirely from the arena, teleporting away with the loot and leaving Valerius to fall face-first into the sand to face his fate.
THUMP!
Valerius dropped out of the sky like a stone with his heavy mythril boots hitting the scorched melted glass of the arena floor with a ringing sound.
He didn’t stumble as he bent his knees, smoothly absorbing the impact of the fall, and slowly stood up to his full height.
The wind whipped his long blond hair across his face, sticking to the sweat on his forehead.
Sitting perfectly balanced on his armored shoulder, Mia looked up at the completely empty stretch of sky where Silas and Aeliana had been floating just moments prior.
"They’re quite some cheaters..." Mia stated flatly, her small hands resting on her hips. ’That’s my student!’
Valerius reached up, running a gauntleted hand through his blond hair to push it out of his eyes.
He let out a long exhausted sigh with the adrenaline of the massive Guardian raid finally bleeding out of his muscles.
"He got me good," Valerius muttered with a begrudging smirk playing at the corner of his lips.
He didn’t throw a tantrum.

He had been completely outplayed by a perfectly timed and coordinated heist. He could respect the audacity of the execution as Silas had read the battlefield geometry, waited for the perfect second, and stolen the prize right out of his hands.
Valerius turned his gaze away from the empty sky and looked out across the sprawling devastated dunes.
About two hundred yards away, a cataclysmic disaster was currently unfolding.
Massive pillars of roaring, superheated fire were erupting into the amber sky.
Entire sand dunes were being violently blasted apart, the sand instantly melting into pools of molten glass from the output.
Seraphina was currently crashing out in the distance.

She was screaming at the top of her lungs with her voice carrying over the wasteland as she hurled devastating blast after blast of fire magic at completely empty stretches of desert, actively hunting a ghost.
The volume of mana she was expending was staggering.
Valerius watched the explosive display of raw Purple core mana as he let out another heavy sigh with the arrogance fading from his eyes for just a fraction of a second as he observed the destruction.
"Even with all I do to optimize my core..." Valerius murmured quietly to himself, "Seraph is still stronger than me."
It was a simple undeniable truth of the century.
Valerius had known Seraphina since they were children.
They had grown up attending the same insufferable noble galas and high-society guild functions. They knew each other so well that they even had small nicknames for each other... Seraph and Val.
It wasn’t because they were actually close friends.
Far from it.

They found each other highly annoying, locked in a perpetual state of snobby, upper-class competition but they had met when they were toddlers, and their formal names were simply quite long and exhausting to say all the time during formal greetings.
The familiarity bred a strange unspoken sibling rivalry and because Valerius knew her so well, he knew exactly how rare it was to see her completely lose her composure.
There were very few things in the entire world that could get her that mad.
"Valerius Sterling!"
The demanding voice of Harper cut through his internal thoughts.

The other Lords were rapidly converging on his position as they had just survived a brutal Guardian raid that had caused one of them to die, only to watch the massive reward get snatched directly out from under their noses by a man Valerius had been hiding with.
Immediately, the other girls started aggressively pressing him.
"Where the hell did your friend go?!" Harper demanded, electricity violently sparking from her fingertips as she stormed up to him. "You were standing right next to him! Where has he been hiding?!"
’I have to act like I don’t know him for now...’ Harper thought, plus she wanted the location.
Elora stepped forward with her glowing blue eyes narrowed into a cold glare.
"You attempted to monopolize the drop, Valerius. Explain how you were about to steal a Realm Seed right in front of the entire group."
Before Valerius could even attempt to craft a sarcastic dismissive response, the temperature in the arena violently spiked.
The air warped and shimmered with intense heat as the glass beneath their boots began to crackle and hiss.
Seraphina stormed into the clearing.

She wasn’t just angry... Pure fire mana was literally leaking from her body. Actual, visible flames were coming out of her ears, her crimson-scaled armor radiating a thermal aura so intense it felt like standing in front of an open blast furnace.
Her fiery red eyes locked directly onto Valerius.
Valerius immediately flinched, instinctively taking a half-step backward.
’Oh,’ Valerius thought with his Lord intuition screaming at him to run. ’She’s mad mad...’
Seraphina stormed forward, completely ignoring Harper and Elora. She stopped three feet away from Valerius, pointing a trembling smoke-trailing finger directly at his chest plate.
"If you know the exact spatial location of where Silas Graves is right now," Seraphina demanded, her voice shaking with pure fury, "you are going to spill it immediately! Give me his coordinates!"
"Seraph, calm down," Valerius tried to deflect, raising both of his armored arms in a placating gesture.
"I am going to hunt him down, and I am about to go kill that bastard!" Seraphina screamed, her aura flaring so violently that the glass floor beneath her boots shattered into spiderwebs.
Valerius took another step back, genuinely bewildered by the intensity of her murderous intent.
"I don’t know where he went! He teleported! And besides, why are you so incredibly mad about it? We lost the seed, yes, but you look like you want to flay him alive!"
Without thinking, completely overwhelmed by her blinding world-ending humiliation, Seraphina threw her head back and shouted at the top of her lungs with a violently red face.
"IT’S BECAUSE HE SAW ME NAKED!"
The words echoed across the entire, glass-shattered arena as there was a whole lot of silence.
The roaring of the ambient desert wind seemed to completely vanish.
Harper’s jaw dropped so fast she almost bit her own tongue and Elora blinked with her cold brain completely flatlining as it tried to process the implications of that highly specific statement.
’Ah... If he goes around seeing other people’s bodies, how am I supposed to seduce him with mine?’
Julian, hiding behind a rock, let out a tiny, high-pitched gasp as nobody moved and nobody breathed.
Then, one of the Lords broke the silence.
It was Julius, the arrogant gold-armored spear-wielder who had just finished hastily tending to the crushed skull of his rhino summon.
Julius saw the chaos, the confusion, and the sheer vulnerability of the moment, and he immediately tried to capitalize on it to eliminate a major political rival.
He gripped his heavy iron spear, pointing it directly at Valerius.

"You!" Julius shouted, attempting to rally the stunned Lords. "You are the one who broke the first Artifact back in the First Layer! The teleportation sphere that brought us to this Hellscape where all the treasures buried in the sand are fake!"
The lesser nobles slowly began to draw their weapons with their greed shifting toward a new isolated target.
"And you were just about to actively steal the Realm Seed from the entire group!" Julius accused him loudly. "You are colluding with the pervert Silas Graves! Seize him!"
Valerius didn’t hesitate as he took that exact declaration as an opportunity to dash back with the wind.
He instantly channeled high-pressure mana into his boots with his core flaring though they could not see it.
However, Julian chose to come out of hiding at that exact moment.
Seeing Valerius isolated, Elora’s cowardly cousin decided to rush him in order to gain the political favor of Lord Julius and the surrounding mob.
Julian pulled a silver dagger, sprinting clumsily across the glass.
"For Valoria!"
Valerius didn’t even draw his mythril sword.
He simply watched the pathetic approach with exasperation. Julian’s weight was shifted too far forward with his grip on the dagger white-knuckled and completely lacking any fluid technique.
’How did this guy graduate...?’

As Julian stumbled into striking range, Valerius smoothly pivoted on the ball of his foot, letting the silver blade sail past his chest plate by an inch then, Valerius casually lifted his heavy mythril boot and hooked it directly behind Julian’s leading ankle.
He flipped the guy over with his foot, utilizing Julian’s own reckless momentum against him.
CRUNCH!
