chapters.title: Chapter 176: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [XV]
paragraphs: Julian let out an agonizing shriek as he was forcefully made to land face-first entirely on the hard unforgiving glass floor with the sound of his nose instantly shattering echoed through the clearing.
"Pathetic," Valerius scoffed.
He violently expelled the compressed air from his boots, shooting off into the air with a massive, localized wind spell.
WHOOSH!
Valerius launched himself fifty feet into the sky, riding a swirling cyclone of green mana but Seraphina was not letting him go that easy.
"VALERIUS!" Seraphina screamed, her humiliation converting into destructive output.
She raised both of her hands with her palms glowing white-hot, and rapidly fired several massive condensed fireballs directly at his ascending form.
FWOOSH! FWOOSH! FWOOSH!
The roaring spheres of flame tore through the air like artillery shells, radiating blistering heat that warped the atmosphere.
Valerius gritted his teeth with his eyes tracking the thermal signatures.
He needed to pull off something completely unorthodox to escape the tracking power of her flames.
’Ah yes...’
He didn’t just push himself with wind, Valerius instead utilized an experimental technique.
"Aero-Displacement," Valerius muttered.
He actively removed the air friction directly in front of his body, creating a momentary vacuum, while simultaneously condensing the air behind him into a solid explosive platform.
BANG!
He kicked off the invisible wall of air, moving at supersonic speeds as he snapped his body to the right, violently twisting his torso in mid-air.
The first fireball completely missed his shoulder by an inch with the heat singing the edge of his blond hair.
He cast the technique again.
BANG!
He dropped straight down in a jagged unpredictable zig-zag pattern. The second fireball roared over his head, detonating harmlessly in the amber sky.
He flipped backward, letting the third fireball pass right beneath his boots.
Seeing the fireballs fail, Julius stepped forward on the ground.
The spear-wielding Lord gripped his heavy iron weapon, leaning his entire body weight back, channeling dense earth mana into the shaft to increase its piercing weight.
"Fall!" Julius roared.
He threw the heavy spear directly at Valerius.
SHWK!
The weapon blurred through the air with terrifying, armor-piercing velocity, tracking perfectly toward Valerius’s chest.
Valerius was out of rotational momentum from the vacuum steps so he couldn’t dodge in time.
"Mia!" Valerius commanded.
Sitting securely on his shoulder, Mia didn’t blink. She raised her small hands with her voice sounding calm and steady.
"Veil of the unseen, wash away the light!" Mia chanted rapidly.
She cast a high-tier cloaking spell at the exact same second the heavy spear arrived.
A shimmering bubble of bent light and distorted moisture instantly wrapped entirely around Valerius and his Hero, completely refracting the visual spectrum.
All the Lords on the ground watched in stunned silence as the heavy iron spear went slicing through the empty air, hitting absolutely nothing.
It sailed through the space where Valerius had just been, before losing momentum and falling flat onto the dunes a bit away.
Valerius had completely vanished from visual and magical perception and he had escaped.
A long distance away from the chaotic arena, Valerius smoothly hopped through the air, riding continuous sweeping bursts of green wind mana from dune to dune.
The cloaking spell had faded, leaving him alone under the harsh amber sky.
The silence of the deep desert was absolute, save for the whistling of the wind against his mythril armor.
Valerius landed softly on the crest of a massive sweeping sand dune. He let out a long breath, looking out over the endless wasteland.
"Fuck..."
He didn’t want to admit it to himself, but the silence was actually incredibly boring.
He secretly wanted to hang around with Silas some more.
The dark-haired Lord was unpredictable and easy to hang around.
It was a refreshing change of pace from the rigid predictable sycophants of Territula City and Valerius especially did want to hunt for more high-tier treasure with him.
"Down there," Mia suddenly spoke up, pointing her small finger directly at the base of the dune.
Mia’s passive radar pinged. "I sense a fluctuation and there is a treasure buried below."
Valerius didn’t hesitate.
He dropped down the slope with his boots sliding in the loose dirt as he landed on the ground and immediately began rapidly digging into a dense dune of sand with his gauntleted hands.
Two feet deep, his fingers brushed against cold metal.
Valerius pulled it out and brushed the dirt away. It was a sleek, silver ring etched with glowing blue runes and he immediately opened his Lord tab to analyze it.
[Name]: Zephyr’s Loop
[Tier]: Tier 1 (Utility Artifact)

[Description]: A minor atmospheric conduit. When equipped, this ring actively thins the ambient air resistance around the user’s mana pathways, effectively increasing one’s elemental spell casting speed by 1.5x.
Valerius read the description and hissed in profound disappointment.
"Tier 1?" Valerius scoffed, tossing the ring lightly in his palm. "I dug through boiling dirt for a baseline trinket? This Secret Realm is a joke."
But logic won out over his pride as he slid the silver ring onto his index finger, put it on regardless of the low tier, and channeled his mana.
He cast another Wind spell to send himself into the air again.
WHOOSH!
The casting time was noticeably faster now. The cyclone formed almost instantly, completely lacking the usual half-second of elemental drag and the ring was actually incredibly efficient.
As he soared smoothly into the air, riding the slipstream, Mia leaned against his armored neck.
"Do you want to see Lord Silas again?" Mia asked with her voice sounding too innocent.
Valerius stiffened. He looked away, his cheeks reddening a bit under the harsh sunlight.
"Not at all," Valerius denied quickly, crossing his arms over his chest plate as he flew. "He is a thief and a scoundrel... I am perfectly fine operating solo."
Mia raised a single judgmental white eyebrow as she leaned forward, hanging upside down over his shoulder to look him dead in the eye.
"Is that so?" Mia asked, her tone dripping with smug knowingness. "Because I distinctly remember a certain gold-armored Lord pacing around his private study just last month."
Valerius stiffened, refusing to look at her. "I don’t know what you’re talking about."

"Oh, I think you do," Mia grinned, poking his cheek. "You were whining. ’Oh, everyone in high-society is so fake! No one is real! I just want one single person in this entire miserable Realm I can talk to who doesn’t have a hidden political agenda!’ Does that ring a bell, Master?"
Valerius avoided her gaze, his jaw tightening as the truth hit home.
"Well," Valerius argued weakly, "Seraph is there and she is honest, my twin sister is back at her own territory."
Mia didn’t say a word as she just gave him a long, incredibly knowing look.
Valerius knew she was right.

He also knew that those were entirely not an option as well. Seraphina currently wanted to murder every male in a ten-mile radius, and his twin sister was a completely different brand of exhausting...
Valerius sighed heavily with his broad shoulders slumping in defeat.
"Fine," Valerius muttered. "Well, if he gives me a signal, the—"
FLASH!
A burst of pure blue-white starlight suddenly flashed in the distance, illuminating the horizon like a small supernova for a second.
Mia smirked, pointing a small finger toward the fading light. "There’s your signal."
Valerius didn’t even try to hide his grin.
He leaned into the wind currents and shot over there at maximum velocity.
Standing atop a sprawling plateau of solid desert glass, Silas lowered his hand.
"I’m only doing this because you explicitly wanted to meet Mia again," Silas told Aeliana, keeping his voice flat and professional.
Aeliana stood beside him with the lingering starlight fading from her fingertips. She nodded, a bright warm smile finally breaking through her previous icy demeanor.
"Of course, Lord Sy," Aeliana replied smoothly.
But internally, Aeliana was genuinely happy.
She was deeply relieved to see that her Lord was actually making friends.
It wasn’t like she wanted him to stop being fiercely focused on the territory’s expansion, or anything like that but Aeliana was happy that her Lord was making guy friends.
WHOOSH!
The sharp sound of cutting wind announced his arrival.
Valerius landed gracefully on the glass plateau with his boots clinking softly.
He stood up straight, brushing a speck of dust off his mythril armor, trying to look incredibly nonchalant about responding to the beacon.
Silas turned, a wicked smirk crossing his face. He casually waved his hand at the blond Lord.
"Quick, catch..." Silas said.
Valerius tensed instinctively as Silas suddenly threw a heavy black orb directly at him.
Valerius’s reflexes kicked in. He snatched the projectile out of the air with his gauntlet and he immediately opened his Lord tab to see what kind of high-tier grenade had just been lobbed at him.
The blue screen flickered:
[Name]: Gale Trap
[Tier]: Tier 2 (Prank Artifact)
Valerius saw that it was actually a treasure. However, before Valerius could even react to the classification, the artifact destabilized.
FWUMP!
It exploded but it didn’t release shrapnel or fire.
It released a massive pressurized burst of pure chaotic wind directly into Valerius’s face.
The force violently pulled his meticulously groomed blond hair straight back, tangling it into a chaotic frizzy mess and making it stand completely on end like he had just been struck by lightning.
Valerius stood there with his hair pointing in every direction as his eyes were wide with disbelief.
He glared at Silas.
"You miserable rat!" he cursed.
Silas threw his head back and laughed loudly, a genuine, booming sound that echoed across the dunes.
"You should see your face," Silas chuckled, wiping a tear of amusement from his eye as he stepped forward, cracking his knuckles. "Where are we going hunting ne—"
"Ahem."
The annoying omnipresent recording of the dead god started again, cutting off Silas’s sentence and making them all instantly stiffen.
"It seems all of you have successfully dealt with my General!" Ititus’s voice boomed happily across the sky. "What a great guy he was! He absolutely loved to battle!"
The god didn’t immediately reveal the next objective. Instead, he launched into an incredibly long unnecessary monologue.

"He was fiercely loyal, yes, but he had incredibly specific tastes," Ititus continued, his voice taking on a gossipy conspiratorial tone. "He loved his constructs. Especially the sand women! I had to carve them with extra... structural density... just to keep him entertained during the long centuries!"
Valerius and Silas completely groaned, rubbing their temples in absolute irritation.
"We don’t care about your dead General’s fetishes!" Valerius shouted at the sky.
"Skip to the loot!" Silas grumbled.
They didn’t care about this shit.

"Now," Ititus finally shifted gears with his voice turning sinisterly cheerful. "If you seek the next major treasure, I will gracefully help you find it! You’re here for treasure after all! But first, you must survive the second trial."
The ground beneath their boots began to vibrate faintly.

"You see," Ititus explained, "all of you are currently given exactly ten minutes to find the nearest designated structural shelter! Or else... you’ll be sent entirely down into an even deeper darker layer. A dungeon where I keep all of the people I killed."
The Lords tensed with their hands dropping to their weapons.

"And trust me," Ititus whispered, his voice echoing with genuine malice. "You do not want to be sent into the dungeon... I have starved the Abyssal Sand-Crawlers for millennia. Their carapaces are immune to magic, their venom melts mythril, and they hunt entirely by the sound of a beating heart. Now start. Your timer begins, and it’s in the sky!"
The god’s voice completely vanished.
High above them, burning brightly against the amber sky, a massive glowing red timer appeared.
It began clicking downward fast.
Valerius didn’t hesitate.
He immediately channeled his mana. "Let’s get moving. If we ride the wind, we can scan the horizon for a shelter before—"
"Hold on," Silas said sharply, raising his hand to stop the Lord.
Valerius stopped, turning to him in disbelief. "Hold on? Did you not hear the dead god? There are magic-immune beasts down there! Even prankster gods lie about safety!"
Silas crossed his arms, his golden-ringed eyes narrowing.
"Prankster gods lie for sure," Silas agreed flatly. "And even when they tell the truth, they twist it but look at the things from my point of view."
He pointed to the sky.
"What if there were actually incredible treasures hidden down in the dungeon? Think about it."

chapters.title: Chapter 177: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [XVI]
paragraphs: Valerius frowned, slowly lowering his sword. "Explain."
Silas laid out the logic perfectly.

"Ititus said he throws the people he defeated down there... His enemies. If you are powerful enough to be considered a personal enemy of a literal god, you are not a baseline peasant and are a high-tier entity. Powerful entities carry their own artifacts."
Silas stepped closer, his voice dropping into a greedy one.

"The enemies of gods would probably hold their own legendary treasures on their corpses so the god wouldn’t bother looting them all. He just buried them and the next best place to find unfiltered loot in this entire Secret Realm is a dungeon full of dead rivals, instead of a rigged treasury full of fake mirages."
Valerius stared at him. The logic was completely and undeniably solid. It was suicidal, yes, but it made perfect sense.
Valerius slowly grinned.
"You are a madman... I like that about you."
They all agreed. Even Mia nodded her small head, actively agreeing that the ancient enemies of gods would be loaded with pristine artifacts.
So, they waited.
They stood on the glass plateau, doing nothing as the timer clicked down.
They were honestly getting bored. For a deadly divine trial that started so fast and sounded so incredibly urgent, it sure was going remarkably slow.
Then, it happened.
The solid desert glass beneath their boots completely liquefied as the sand instantly latched violently around their ankles, drawing them downward with terrifying inescapable gravitational force.
"Hold your breath!" Silas yelled.
They were violently sucked into the earth.
All of them sunk downward, plummeting through suffocating darkness for ten agonizing seconds before they were violently spat out into a completely different world.
THUD!
Silas hit the ground hard, rolling to a stop as he pushed himself up, coughing.
This layer was entirely different. It was a world of only pitch-black sand.
Towering around them were different kinds of massive, heavy iron cells that looked like they were made of solid reinforced dark sand.
"Welcome to my dungeon~" the god’s voice laughed sadistically through the dark corridors.
However, Silas completely ignored the taunt and the looming armor as he was staring directly at the heavy brass Treasure Radar gripped tightly in his left hand.
PING! PING! PING! PING! PING!
The radar was going crazy.
The screen was completely lit up with massive, high-density magical blips. There were twenty... no, thirty different signatures buried in the area around them!
There were no mirages down here or were they?
"We just hit the jackpot," Silas whispered with a greedy grin spreading across his face.
Valerius laughed out loud and thrilled laugh as he raised his gauntleted hand for a high-five.
Silas was in such an incredibly good mood that he didn’t even hesitate.
He stepped forward and high-fived the aristocratic guy right back as the leather slapped against the iron with a loud sound.
However, all that joyous camaraderie drained completely out of the room the very next moment.
The air distorted heavily to their left.
Seraphina appeared completely out of nowhere, teleporting into the dungeon right beside them.

As soon as her fiery red eyes locked directly onto Silas’s face, she practically vibrated with pure rage as she took a furious step forward, immediately opening her mouth to yell at the top of her lungs and cast a devastating spell.
However, she couldn’t.
She opened her mouth, but no sound came out and no fire emerged from her lips.
Silas blinked with his perception, catching the detail instantly.
Clamped tightly around Seraphina’s pale throat, its metallic legs digging securely into her skin, was a specific advanced spider-shaped jewelry.
It was a silencing artifact, completely suppressing her vocal cords and severing her casting chants, which made her unable to speak.
Nothing happened.
Not a single decibel of sound left her lips and not a single spark of fire ignited in her palms as the air remained cold, silent, and lacking of the heat that they knew.
Valerius raised an eyebrow, stepping cautiously forward. He slowly waved his armored gauntlet directly in front of her flushed face.
"Seraph?" Valerius called out, his voice dripping with genuine confusion. "Are you casting a silent incantation, or did you finally lose your mind?"
Seraphina slapped at his iron hand with a vicious, silent snarl.

She stepped back, frantically clawing at her own throat, desperately trying to force her mana pathways to ignite as she pushed her Lord core to its limit, attempting to blast her flames outward in an explosive omni-directional wave.
Still, nothing worked. Her mana violently sputtered and died the second it reached her chest.
Silas didn’t ask useless questions. He immediately focused on the strange, metallic gleam catching the dim light on the side of her neck.
He narrowed his golden-ringed eyes, activating his Lord inspection tab to scan the foreign object.
A glowing blue interface immediately manifested in his vision, organizing the data into a standard tab.
[Name]: Arachne’s Mute Parasite
[Type]: Tier 2 (Cursed Suppression Artifact)
[Duration]: 24:00:00 (Counting Down)

[Effect]: A clamp engineered for high-tier prisoner subjugation. Upon latching to the host’s nervous system, it forcibly compresses the mana core, bringing down the maximum mana output of the user by 50%. Simultaneously severs the vocal cords from the magical circulation, rendering verbal incantations and speech completely impossible.

[Warning]: The artifact is physically tethered to the host’s carotid artery. Applying external brute force or attempting to prematurely destroy the clamp will destabilize the core, immediately exploding the host’s neck. It safely unlatches and disappears automatically after 24 hours.
Silas read the red warning text twice. He slowly deactivated his interface, letting out a long exhausted sigh as he looked at the trembling girl.

"Well, the good news is you’re not going to blow up if we leave it alone," Silas remarked flatly, crossing his arms over his dark coat. "And honestly? At least you’re calm right now and not actively trying to kill me."
Seraphina’s eyes widened in outrage.
’Calm?!’ She wanted to do nothing more than slaughter Silas Graves right where he stood.
She wanted to summon a sun and melt his bones into glass. This miserable commoner had humiliated her beyond mortal comprehension.
He had seen her in the most compromising undignified position imaginable, and now he was casually mocking her inability to speak!
She stepped forward to throw a physical right hook, but the moment her muscles tensed for an erratic combat movement, the metallic spider clamped tighter.
ZZZTS!
A sharp agonizing jolt of suppression magic spiked directly through her brainstem.
Seraphina gasped silently with her knees buckling as her depleted mana core violently shuddered.
She quickly realized she didn’t have an option at all. If she performed erratic movements or aggressive attacks, the artifact actively punished her.
She could only stand there, breathing heavily and shooting daggers at Silas with her eyes without physically touching him.
Before Valerius could question the artifact’s origins, the air around them vibrated.
"Ahem!"
The dead God’s voice boomed through the dark dungeon, echoing off the towering iron cells with a deafening hearty laugh.

"Welcome, my unfortunate little souls, to the deep Abyss!" Ititus cheered happily. "If you are hearing this broadcast, it means you either failed the timer, or you actually chose to jump down here voluntarily! That makes you either the unluckiest, or the greediest bastards ever born to the Sovereign Realm!"
Valerius crossed his arms, glaring up at the dark ceiling.

"Now," Ititus continued, his tone shifting into a sadistic sneer. "Even if you were clever enough to realize that I buried my legendary treasures down here, you aren’t getting them for free! You will have to survive the reanimated bodies of this zone! You see, all of the elite enemies and rival Lords I defeated during my ascension were thrown down here. The treasures you seek are deeply embedded inside their very flesh and armor! You have to slaughter them to get the loot!"
Valerius instantly lost his aristocratic temper. He raised his fist at the ceiling.
"You are a twisted, honorless bastard!" Valerius called the god out loudly.
The audio broadcast flickered, a burst of static buzzing through the air before Ititus’s voice surprisingly responded.
"I’m not a bastard~" Ititus mocked in a sing-song tone. "Oops! Did I forget to mention? Some of these recordings have interactive trigger algorithms! Enjoy the bloodbath!"
The voice completely vanished, leaving a heavy, suffocating silence in its wake.
All of them blinked, staring at the empty air. Was this not a standard recording, or had the god left a fragment of his actual consciousness behind to troll them?
Regardless of the answer, the dungeon didn’t give them time to debate.
GRIND! GRIND! GRIND!

The heavy reinforced iron gates of the surrounding cells began to lift. From the suffocating darkness of the corridors, the first enemies of the god or rather, his ancient prisoners made their way into the clearing.

They weren’t fleshy undead as they were massive, eight-foot-tall piles of shifting, condensed black sand, shaped into humanoid gladiators with hollow glowing red eyes and agonizing faces screaming from their torsos.
Valerius immediately cursed under his breath.
"More sand?! I am sick of this element!"
He didn’t wait for them to surround the group as Valerius dropped his center of gravity, his mythril boots sliding across the stone floor as he rushed forward.
He drew his blade, his green mana flaring brilliantly.
"Vacuum Domain: Cross-Sever!" Valerius roared.
He didn’t use a basic wind slice as he utilized another aggressive style of his Vacuum Domain attack.
Valerius slashed his sword horizontally, then vertically, creating a massive X-shaped vacuum rift that violently sucked the air out of the corridor before imploding.
BOOOOM!
The explosive decompression violently ripped through the group of the sand prisoners, cleanly cutting through them and scattering their black sand bodies across the stone walls.
Valerius stepped into the wreckage, his eyes scanning the debris. He kicked a shattered sand torso.
"Nothing," Valerius spat, turning back to Silas. "Inside them were no treasures. These front-line trash are just decoys."
"Then we keep moving until we hit the high-density signatures," Silas said.
He checked his brass radar, which was pointing deeper into the labyrinth.
Silas and Valerius chose to move forward immediately.
They walked side-by-side with their summoned heroes with Aeliana and Mia guarding their flanks as they advanced down the dark corridor, completely leaving Seraphina trembling behind in the clearing.
Seraphina stood alone in the dark, her chest heaving as she hyper-ventilated.
’Why?!’ she wondered desperately, hot frustrated tears finally spilling out of her eyes and cutting clean lines through the soot on her cheeks. ’Why is this Secret Realm so utterly hellish?!’
Her entire world had collapsed in less than an hour.
Not only had she been seen peeing like some uncivilized barbarian in the dirt, but a man who was not her future husband had seen her completely naked!

And not only that, she was now wearing a cursed collar that reduced her A-Rank power to a pathetic fraction, she couldn’t speak a single syllable, and she couldn’t even try to convince Val to help her because she had literally attacked him with lethal fireballs in a fit of her own uncontrollable rage!
And as for Silas Graves...
’That filthy rat!’ Seraphina thought, her jaw trembling with fury. ’I wouldn’t be caught dead asking him for—’
The angry thoughts violently stopped as she looked up.
The glowing lights of Silas, Valerius, and their heroes had vanished.
They had turned a corner, leaving her line of sight and going completely into the dark labyrinth, leaving her entirely alone in a dungeon filled with reanimated god-killing monstrosities.
From the shadows behind her, the grinding sound of shifting sand echoed as two more black sand gladiators were reforming from the floor, their hollow red eyes locking onto her solitary figure.
Seraphina’s legs were actually trembling. Without her vocal cords to chant and with her fire mana suppressed by fifty percent, she couldn’t output enough heat to turn them to glass.
She took a terrified wobbly step backward, breathing harder and harder as the monsters raised their heavy stone swords.
Suddenly, a hand reached out from the darkness and grabbed her shoulder.
Seraphina flinched violently, raising her fists, but someone popped up right beside her.
It was Silas.
The dark-haired Lord had doubled back. He stood there with his trench coat covered in desert dust, looking down at her with a calm resigned expression.
He let out a heavy sigh, gesturing with his thumb toward the lighted corridor ahead.
"Do you want to come along with us?" Silas asked simply. "If you stay here, you’re going to get turned into fertilizer so come."

sentences.text: Valerius frowned, slowly lowering his sword.
"Explain."
Silas laid out the logic perfectly.
"Ititus said he throws the people he defeated down there...
His enemies.
If you are powerful enough to be considered a personal enemy of a literal god, you are not a baseline peasant and are a high-tier entity.
Powerful entities carry their own artifacts."
Silas stepped closer, his voice dropping into a greedy one.
"The enemies of gods would probably hold their own legendary treasures on their corpses so the god wouldn’t bother looting them all.
He just buried them and the next best place to find unfiltered loot in this entire Secret Realm is a dungeon full of dead rivals, instead of a rigged treasury full of fake mirages."
Valerius stared at him.
The logic was completely and undeniably solid.
It was suicidal, yes, but it made perfect sense.
Valerius slowly grinned.
"You are a madman...
I like that about you."
They all agreed.
Even Mia nodded her small head, actively agreeing that the ancient enemies of gods would be loaded with pristine artifacts.
So, they waited.
They stood on the glass plateau, doing nothing as the timer clicked down.
They were honestly getting bored.
For a deadly divine trial that started so fast and sounded so incredibly urgent, it sure was going remarkably slow.
Then, it happened.
The solid desert glass beneath their boots completely liquefied as the sand instantly latched violently around their ankles, drawing them downward with terrifying inescapable gravitational force.
"Hold your breath!" Silas yelled.
They were violently sucked into the earth.
All of them sunk downward, plummeting through suffocating darkness for ten agonizing seconds before they were violently spat out into a completely different world.
THUD!
Silas hit the ground hard, rolling to a stop as he pushed himself up, coughing.
This layer was entirely different.
It was a world of only pitch-black sand.
Towering around them were different kinds of massive, heavy iron cells that looked like they were made of solid reinforced dark sand.
"Welcome to my dungeon~" the god’s voice laughed sadistically through the dark corridors.
However, Silas completely ignored the taunt and the looming armor as he was staring directly at the heavy brass Treasure Radar gripped tightly in his left hand.
PING!
PING!
PING!
PING!
PING!
The radar was going crazy.
The screen was completely lit up with massive, high-density magical blips.
There were twenty... no, thirty different signatures buried in the area around them!
There were no mirages down here or were they?
"We just hit the jackpot," Silas whispered with a greedy grin spreading across his face.
Valerius laughed out loud and thrilled laugh as he raised his gauntleted hand for a high-five.
Silas was in such an incredibly good mood that he didn’t even hesitate.
He stepped forward and high-fived the aristocratic guy right back as the leather slapped against the iron with a loud sound.
However, all that joyous camaraderie drained completely out of the room the very next moment.
The air distorted heavily to their left.
Seraphina appeared completely out of nowhere, teleporting into the dungeon right beside them.

As soon as her fiery red eyes locked directly onto Silas’s face, she practically vibrated with pure rage as she took a furious step forward, immediately opening her mouth to yell at the top of her lungs and cast a devastating spell.
However, she couldn’t.
She opened her mouth, but no sound came out and no fire emerged from her lips.
Silas blinked with his perception, catching the detail instantly.
Clamped tightly around Seraphina’s pale throat, its metallic legs digging securely into her skin, was a specific advanced spider-shaped jewelry.
It was a silencing artifact, completely suppressing her vocal cords and severing her casting chants, which made her unable to speak.
Nothing happened.
Not a single decibel of sound left her lips and not a single spark of fire ignited in her palms as the air remained cold, silent, and lacking of the heat that they knew.
Valerius raised an eyebrow, stepping cautiously forward.
He slowly waved his armored gauntlet directly in front of her flushed face.
"Seraph?" Valerius called out, his voice dripping with genuine confusion.
"Are you casting a silent incantation, or did you finally lose your mind?"
Seraphina slapped at his iron hand with a vicious, silent snarl.

She stepped back, frantically clawing at her own throat, desperately trying to force her mana pathways to ignite as she pushed her Lord core to its limit, attempting to blast her flames outward in an explosive omni-directional wave.
Still, nothing worked.
Her mana violently sputtered and died the second it reached her chest.
Silas didn’t ask useless questions.
He immediately focused on the strange, metallic gleam catching the dim light on the side of her neck.
He narrowed his golden-ringed eyes, activating his Lord inspection tab to scan the foreign object.
A glowing blue interface immediately manifested in his vision, organizing the data into a standard tab.
[Name]: Arachne’s Mute Parasite
[Type]: Tier 2 (Cursed Suppression Artifact)
[Duration]: 24:00:00 (Counting Down)
[Effect]: A clamp engineered for high-tier prisoner subjugation.
Upon latching to the host’s nervous system, it forcibly compresses the mana core, bringing down the maximum mana output of the user by 50%.
Simultaneously severs the vocal cords from the magical circulation, rendering verbal incantations and speech completely impossible.
[Warning]: The artifact is physically tethered to the host’s carotid artery.
Applying external brute force or attempting to prematurely destroy the clamp will destabilize the core, immediately exploding the host’s neck.
It safely unlatches and disappears automatically after 24 hours.
Silas read the red warning text twice.
He slowly deactivated his interface, letting out a long exhausted sigh as he looked at the trembling girl.
"Well, the good news is you’re not going to blow up if we leave it alone," Silas remarked flatly, crossing his arms over his dark coat.
"And honestly?
At least you’re calm right now and not actively trying to kill me."
Seraphina’s eyes widened in outrage.
’Calm?!’ She wanted to do nothing more than slaughter Silas Graves right where he stood.
She wanted to summon a sun and melt his bones into glass.
This miserable commoner had humiliated her beyond mortal comprehension.
He had seen her in the most compromising undignified position imaginable, and now he was casually mocking her inability to speak!
She stepped forward to throw a physical right hook, but the moment her muscles tensed for an erratic combat movement, the metallic spider clamped tighter.
ZZZTS!
A sharp agonizing jolt of suppression magic spiked directly through her brainstem.
Seraphina gasped silently with her knees buckling as her depleted mana core violently shuddered.
She quickly realized she didn’t have an option at all.
If she performed erratic movements or aggressive attacks, the artifact actively punished her.
She could only stand there, breathing heavily and shooting daggers at Silas with her eyes without physically touching him.
Before Valerius could question the artifact’s origins, the air around them vibrated.
"Ahem!"
The dead God’s voice boomed through the dark dungeon, echoing off the towering iron cells with a deafening hearty laugh.
"Welcome, my unfortunate little souls, to the deep Abyss!" Ititus cheered happily.
"If you are hearing this broadcast, it means you either failed the timer, or you actually chose to jump down here voluntarily!
That makes you either the unluckiest, or the greediest bastards ever born to the Sovereign Realm!"
Valerius crossed his arms, glaring up at the dark ceiling.
"Now," Ititus continued, his tone shifting into a sadistic sneer.
"Even if you were clever enough to realize that I buried my legendary treasures down here, you aren’t getting them for free!
You will have to survive the reanimated bodies of this zone!
You see, all of the elite enemies and rival Lords I defeated during my ascension were thrown down here.
The treasures you seek are deeply embedded inside their very flesh and armor!
You have to slaughter them to get the loot!"
Valerius instantly lost his aristocratic temper.
He raised his fist at the ceiling.
"You are a twisted, honorless bastard!" Valerius called the god out loudly.
The audio broadcast flickered, a burst of static buzzing through the air before Ititus’s voice surprisingly responded.
"I’m not a bastard~" Ititus mocked in a sing-song tone.
"Oops!
Did I forget to mention?
Some of these recordings have interactive trigger algorithms!
Enjoy the bloodbath!"
The voice completely vanished, leaving a heavy, suffocating silence in its wake.
All of them blinked, staring at the empty air.
Was this not a standard recording, or had the god left a fragment of his actual consciousness behind to troll them?
Regardless of the answer, the dungeon didn’t give them time to debate.
GRIND!
GRIND!
GRIND!
The heavy reinforced iron gates of the surrounding cells began to lift.
From the suffocating darkness of the corridors, the first enemies of the god or rather, his ancient prisoners made their way into the clearing.

They weren’t fleshy undead as they were massive, eight-foot-tall piles of shifting, condensed black sand, shaped into humanoid gladiators with hollow glowing red eyes and agonizing faces screaming from their torsos.
Valerius immediately cursed under his breath.
"More sand?!
I am sick of this element!"
He didn’t wait for them to surround the group as Valerius dropped his center of gravity, his mythril boots sliding across the stone floor as he rushed forward.
He drew his blade, his green mana flaring brilliantly.
"Vacuum Domain: Cross-Sever!" Valerius roared.
He didn’t use a basic wind slice as he utilized another aggressive style of his Vacuum Domain attack.
Valerius slashed his sword horizontally, then vertically, creating a massive X-shaped vacuum rift that violently sucked the air out of the corridor before imploding.
BOOOOM!
The explosive decompression violently ripped through the group of the sand prisoners, cleanly cutting through them and scattering their black sand bodies across the stone walls.
Valerius stepped into the wreckage, his eyes scanning the debris.
He kicked a shattered sand torso.
"Nothing," Valerius spat, turning back to Silas.
"Inside them were no treasures.
These front-line trash are just decoys."
"Then we keep moving until we hit the high-density signatures," Silas said.
He checked his brass radar, which was pointing deeper into the labyrinth.
Silas and Valerius chose to move forward immediately.
They walked side-by-side with their summoned heroes with Aeliana and Mia guarding their flanks as they advanced down the dark corridor, completely leaving Seraphina trembling behind in the clearing.
Seraphina stood alone in the dark, her chest heaving as she hyper-ventilated.
’Why?!’ she wondered desperately, hot frustrated tears finally spilling out of her eyes and cutting clean lines through the soot on her cheeks. ’Why is this Secret Realm so utterly hellish?!’
Her entire world had collapsed in less than an hour.
Not only had she been seen peeing like some uncivilized barbarian in the dirt, but a man who was not her future husband had seen her completely naked!

And not only that, she was now wearing a cursed collar that reduced her A-Rank power to a pathetic fraction, she couldn’t speak a single syllable, and she couldn’t even try to convince Val to help her because she had literally attacked him with lethal fireballs in a fit of her own uncontrollable rage!
And as for Silas Graves...
’That filthy rat!’ Seraphina thought, her jaw trembling with fury. ’I wouldn’t be caught dead asking him for—’
The angry thoughts violently stopped as she looked up.
The glowing lights of Silas, Valerius, and their heroes had vanished.
They had turned a corner, leaving her line of sight and going completely into the dark labyrinth, leaving her entirely alone in a dungeon filled with reanimated god-killing monstrosities.
From the shadows behind her, the grinding sound of shifting sand echoed as two more black sand gladiators were reforming from the floor, their hollow red eyes locking onto her solitary figure.
Seraphina’s legs were actually trembling.
Without her vocal cords to chant and with her fire mana suppressed by fifty percent, she couldn’t output enough heat to turn them to glass.
She took a terrified wobbly step backward, breathing harder and harder as the monsters raised their heavy stone swords.
Suddenly, a hand reached out from the darkness and grabbed her shoulder.
Seraphina flinched violently, raising her fists, but someone popped up right beside her.
It was Silas.
The dark-haired Lord had doubled back.
He stood there with his trench coat covered in desert dust, looking down at her with a calm resigned expression.
He let out a heavy sigh, gesturing with his thumb toward the lighted corridor ahead.
"Do you want to come along with us?" Silas asked simply.
"If you stay here, you’re going to get turned into fertilizer so come."

chapters.title: Chapter 178: The Secret Realm Of Ititius [XVII]
paragraphs: He reached out, offering his open hand to her.
Silas was not doing this because she was cute, or because he felt some romantic chivalrous obligation toward a crying noble.
It was quite far from it.
In this specific political situation, he was actually at a massive disadvantage.
Apart from accidentally seeing her naked behind that dune, he had also offended her earlier during the drop for some unknown reason.
And most importantly, Seraphina was not a regular girl... she was the direct favored daughter of a World Council Magistrate. He was a commoner from the slums of Sector 4 who had clawed his way up.
If she survived this Secret Realm and reported to her father that Silas Graves had humiliated her, left her to die, and watched her suffer... the political backlash would be catastrophic.
Hell, if she died down here and the Magistrate’s soul-trackers traced her last moments to Silas’s proximity, he would be the very first one off that assassination list!
In the overarching Sovereign Realm, he was a terrifying Gold Core Lord with the potential of a god.
But right here, in the legal reality of the mortal world, he was just a Blue Core upstart from the slums.
He needed her alive, and he needed her mildly indebted to him so, he decided to help.
Seraphina didn’t contemplate her pride for a single second.
The moment she saw his hand, she ran over and aggressively clutched his hand with both of hers with her fingers locking around his palm like a drowning sailor grabbing a lifeline.
She didn’t let go.
Silas didn’t say anything more about her sudden change in attitude.
He just looked at her desperate grip and nodded.
"Oh? Let’s walk back to the others then."
They walked back together, turning the corner into the wider corridor where Valerius, Mia, and Aeliana were waiting.
As they approached, the group turned to look at them. Their eyes immediately dropped to their locked hands.
Aeli’s silver eyes narrowed instantly. Her pointed ears stood straight up, and her flawless face tightened into a deeply unimpressed jealous glare.
She stepped forward, her white spider-silk robes swirling as she looked Silas dead in the eye, silently demanding an explanation for why he was holding hands with a screaming fire-mage.
Silas raised his free hand in defense. "What? I have to pacify her in some way so we can move. She can’t fight properly with that collar."

Valerius leaned against his longsword, waving his gauntleted hand with a wicked, mocking smirk. "Good luck with that, Graves. You saw her naked... she’s never letting that go for the rest of her natural life."

The blunt reminder made Seraphina’s face completely melt into a fresh wave of violently hot crimson humiliation. She hid her face behind Silas’s shoulder, wishing the floor would open up and swallow her.
However, Silas frowned, shaking his head with genuine confusion.
"I didn’t even see her fully naked," Silas corrected him, trying to be accurate to the facts. "It was just the lower half."
Valerius froze. His smirk vanished, replaced by an expression of shock as he slowly looked at the man like he was completely crazy.
’Just the lower half?!’

In noble society, seeing a lady’s lower half without her express permission was ten times worse than seeing her standing normally without clothes in a changing room! It was the ultimate breach of honor!

Seraphina’s immediate reaction to Silas’s casual clarification was violent. Her eyes went wide with horror as she aggressively pulled her hand away from his palm, stepping back as if his skin had caught fire.
Before Silas could ask what he said wrong,
Aeliana stepped firmly into the gap.
"Hmph!"
She aggressively took his hand, locking her slender fingers through his without a sound as she pulled him slightly closer to her side as they continued walking down the dark corridor.

As they advanced deeper into the prison, they also noticed that the iron cells in question did not actually hold the creatures anymore. The bars were shattered outward with the doors hanging limply on rusted hinges.
Silas stopped, lifting his brass radar. The glowing green screen beeped rapidly.
"The signatures aren’t in the cells," Silas noted, his eyes narrowing as he tapped the glass. "All of the treasures have shifted. They’re moving together up ahead."
They accelerated their pace, climbing a steep rocky ridge that overlooked a massive amphitheater.
They reached the edge, dropping low and looking downward.
The sight below made them all stiffen.

Milling around in the massive torch-lit basin were easily a hundred creatures made of black sand but these weren’t simple foot soldiers. They were massive, four-armed centurions, beasts riding sand-sculpted hounds, and towering brutes wielding heavy weapons forged from compressed desert bedrock.
The mana radiating from the horde was suffocating.
Before they could formulate a plan, the God’s voice boomed from the cavern ceiling once more.

"Beautiful, isn’t it?" Ititus laughed proudly. "Before you will be able to proceed to the final zone, you have to slaughter the monsters... all of them! Every single one! But here is the fun part... only some out of all of them actually possess an artifact embedded in their cores! You aren’t getting my loot that easy! Happy hunting!"
Silas, Valerius, and the others let out a collective groan of sheer exhaustion.
Down in the basin, the hundred sand monsters heard the echo of their voices.
Simultaneously, a hundred glowing red eyes snapped upward, locking directly onto the ridge.
"RAHHHHH!"
The horde let out a deafening unified roar that shook the stone walls with their heavy weapons raising as they began to charge up the slope.
Valerius didn’t retreat. A massive arrogant grin spread across his face as his core ignited, flaring with intense wind mana.
"The one that slaughters more monsters gets all the Artifacts!" Valerius declared loudly.
Without waiting for agreement, he immediately shot downward off the ridge with anexplosive burst of wind from his boots.
WHOOSH! CRASH!

Valerius dived directly into the center of the charging horde like a falling meteor. He landed with a deafening sound with a shockwave of green wind exploding outward from his impact point, instantly blowing three sand centurions into flying dust.
"Let’s dance!" Valerius roared, spinning his mythril blade into a devastating whirlwind.
Silas sighed, shaking his head at the aristocrat’s recklessness. He turned his head slightly, calling out to his Starlight Arcanist.
"Aeliana," Silas commanded, his voice dropping an octave into pure, cold authority. "Go wild."
Aeliana’s silver eyes flashed with starlight as a breathtaking smile crossed her face as she offered a crisp flawless bow.
"Yes, My Lord," Aeliana finished smoothly.
She stepped off the ledge with her body dissolving into a beam of pure starlight. She materialized fifty feet below, directly above the densest cluster of monsters.
She raised both of her slender arms, her palms pointing downward.
SHING! SHING! SHING! SHING! SHING!
Dozens of powerful Arcane Piercers materialized in the air around her... beams of condensed white starlight that looked like spears of solid diamonds.
She brought her hands down, and the orbital bombardment began.
The starlight spears rained down with terrifying accuracy, punching clean glowing holes through the skulls and chests of the sand beasts below, turning the dark room into a light show.
Silas didn’t stay on the sidelines.
He jumped from the ledge too with his heavy trench coat billowing behind him as he descended into the chaos.
He didn’t use any verbal chants as his Gold Core, perfectly attuned to the runic pathways Mia had drilled into him, mapped the spells instantly.
While falling through the air, Silas slashed his right hand horizontally three times.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
Three razor-thin pressurized crescent blades of water of Abyssal Severs erupted from his empty knuckles.
They were completely flawless, vibrating with such intense frequency that they hissed through the air.
The water blades struck the charging vanguard right at neck height, cleanly slicing five massive sand centurions apart in a single fluid motion before Silas’s boots even touched the ground.
THUD!
Silas landed in the center of the pack with his physical body absorbing the impact as a four-armed brute swung two heavy sandstone clubs down at his head.
Silas didn’t dodge.
He planted his left foot, compressed ambient moisture directly into his right palm, and thrust his hand upward without uttering a word.
TIDAL IMPACT!
A massive cannonball of heavy water detonated directly against the brute’s chest.
The hydraulic shockwave exploded outward with the force of a breaching dam.
BOOOOM!

The brute was instantly vaporized into wet mud, and the massive volume of heavy water violently washed over twenty surrounding monsters, soaking their sand bodies and turning the dry basin floor into a flooded swampy mess.
Silas smirked with his eyes glowing gold as he immediately pivoted to his third spell.
He reached out with his mana, gripping the saturated, flooded battlefield, and executed Ice Transformation.
KRKKKKKK!
The temperature in the basin violently cratered to absolute zero in a microsecond.
All that heavy water he had just dumped across the battlefield instantly froze solid.
The wet sand monsters were trapped with their legs and torsos encased in jagged blue ice.
The sudden violent expansion of the ice field spread so fast it almost tripped Valerius too.
"Hey! Watch your target zone, Graves!" Valerius grumbled loudly, jumping over a waist-high glacier that suddenly sprouted from the floor while he was mid-swing.
"Sure sure..."

He dashed forward across the frozen floor, utilizing his physical strength as he broke off massive ice shards from the frozen ground, wielding them like improvised greatswords, and began stabbing directly into the frozen monsters’ cores, ending them with efficiency.
CRUNCH! SHWK! CRUNCH!
As he shattered the torso of a particularly large sand hound, something clattered against the ice.
Silas reached down and snatched it up. It was a heavy glowing bronze bracer... he had found an artifact!
Meanwhile, on the far side of the clearing, Valerius was having his own peak combat moment.
The gold-armored Lord was a blur of green wind with his longsword parrying heavy stone weapons with terrifying speed.
"Mia! Water pulse on my six!" Valerius shouted while dodging a swinging axe.
Sitting securely on his shoulder, Mia yawned, looking completely lazy.
She didn’t even stand up as she lazily pointed a single tiny index finger over Valerius’s shoulder without looking.
Pew!
A microscopic compressed needle of water shot from her fingertip, silently drilling a hole straight through the forehead of a beast about to ambush Valerius from behind.
The monster collapsed into dust before Valerius even turned around.
"You could at least act like you’re trying," Valerius complained, spinning and severing two more monsters with a Zephyr Slash.
"You’re doing fine, My Lord." Mia mumbled sleepily, resting her chin on his iron shoulder plate as he slaughtered the horde.
High above the chaotic warzone, Seraphina stood alone on the ridge, watching the devastation below.
Her lips slowly parted in genuine awe, though no words came out of her silenced throat.
Her fiery red eyes tracked Silas as he seamlessly blended devastating physical brawling with high-tier water and ice magic, tearing through the horde.
’He’s... not bad...’ Seraphina thought reluctantly with her heart beating slightly faster.

At first, back in the upper layers, she had genuinely thought Silas Graves was just some useless arrogant Lord who had tried to make trouble for everybody but watching him now, the truth was undeniable.
Not only did he command an incredibly competent powerful Hero like Aeliana, but he was also quite competent himself.
His combat IQ was flawless, his elemental transitions were instant, and his physical strength was monstrous.
Seraphina slowly nodded her head, a strange grudging respect settling over her prideful heart.
’As expected of the man who has seen me naked, at least,’ she thought, rationalizing his strength in her own twisted noble logic.
If a commoner was going to humiliate her, he at least had the decency to be a monster on the battlefield!
As for how she knew that he was a commoner... that was simple, she could smell it.
Refusing to be completely left out of the raid, Seraphina drew her curved dagger and jumped down from the ledge to join the fray.
THUD!
She hit the ground, but she immediately stumbled with her legs feeling dangerously wobbly.
’Ugh!’ she winced internally as she remembered... the parasite artifact didn’t just mute her; it actively lowered her physical strength by 50% as well as her mana!
Her limbs felt heavy, like she was moving through deep mud. Every step hurt, and swinging her dagger required double the effort.
Still, she gritted her teeth, pushing her wobbly legs forward to slash at the remaining stragglers, refusing to show weakness in front of Silas.
Ten minutes later, the place was completely silent.
Over a hundred sand monsters had been reduced to piles of harmless dirt and melting ice shards.

Without waiting for agreement, he immediately shot downward off the ridge with anexplosive burst of wind from his boots.
WHOOSH!
CRASH!
Valerius dived directly into the center of the charging horde like a falling meteor.
He landed with a deafening sound with a shockwave of green wind exploding outward from his impact point, instantly blowing three sand centurions into flying dust.
"Let’s dance!" Valerius roared, spinning his mythril blade into a devastating whirlwind.
Silas sighed, shaking his head at the aristocrat’s recklessness.
He turned his head slightly, calling out to his Starlight Arcanist.
"Aeliana," Silas commanded, his voice dropping an octave into pure, cold authority.
"Go wild."
Aeliana’s silver eyes flashed with starlight as a breathtaking smile crossed her face as she offered a crisp flawless bow.
"Yes, My Lord," Aeliana finished smoothly.
She stepped off the ledge with her body dissolving into a beam of pure starlight.
She materialized fifty feet below, directly above the densest cluster of monsters.
She raised both of her slender arms, her palms pointing downward.
SHING!
SHING!
SHING!
SHING!
SHING!
Dozens of powerful Arcane Piercers materialized in the air around her... beams of condensed white starlight that looked like spears of solid diamonds.
She brought her hands down, and the orbital bombardment began.
The starlight spears rained down with terrifying accuracy, punching clean glowing holes through the skulls and chests of the sand beasts below, turning the dark room into a light show.
Silas didn’t stay on the sidelines.
He jumped from the ledge too with his heavy trench coat billowing behind him as he descended into the chaos.
He didn’t use any verbal chants as his Gold Core, perfectly attuned to the runic pathways Mia had drilled into him, mapped the spells instantly.
While falling through the air, Silas slashed his right hand horizontally three times.
SWISH!
SWISH!
SWISH!
Three razor-thin pressurized crescent blades of water of Abyssal Severs erupted from his empty knuckles.
They were completely flawless, vibrating with such intense frequency that they hissed through the air.
The water blades struck the charging vanguard right at neck height, cleanly slicing five massive sand centurions apart in a single fluid motion before Silas’s boots even touched the ground.
THUD!
Silas landed in the center of the pack with his physical body absorbing the impact as a four-armed brute swung two heavy sandstone clubs down at his head.
Silas didn’t dodge.
He planted his left foot, compressed ambient moisture directly into his right palm, and thrust his hand upward without uttering a word.
TIDAL IMPACT!
A massive cannonball of heavy water detonated directly against the brute’s chest.
The hydraulic shockwave exploded outward with the force of a breaching dam.
BOOOOM!

The brute was instantly vaporized into wet mud, and the massive volume of heavy water violently washed over twenty surrounding monsters, soaking their sand bodies and turning the dry basin floor into a flooded swampy mess.
Silas smirked with his eyes glowing gold as he immediately pivoted to his third spell.
He reached out with his mana, gripping the saturated, flooded battlefield, and executed Ice Transformation.
KRKKKKKK!
The temperature in the basin violently cratered to absolute zero in a microsecond.
All that heavy water he had just dumped across the battlefield instantly froze solid.
The wet sand monsters were trapped with their legs and torsos encased in jagged blue ice.
The sudden violent expansion of the ice field spread so fast it almost tripped Valerius too.
"Hey!
Watch your target zone, Graves!" Valerius grumbled loudly, jumping over a waist-high glacier that suddenly sprouted from the floor while he was mid-swing.
"Sure sure..."

He dashed forward across the frozen floor, utilizing his physical strength as he broke off massive ice shards from the frozen ground, wielding them like improvised greatswords, and began stabbing directly into the frozen monsters’ cores, ending them with efficiency.
CRUNCH!
SHWK!
CRUNCH!
As he shattered the torso of a particularly large sand hound, something clattered against the ice.
Silas reached down and snatched it up.
It was a heavy glowing bronze bracer... he had found an artifact!
Meanwhile, on the far side of the clearing, Valerius was having his own peak combat moment.
The gold-armored Lord was a blur of green wind with his longsword parrying heavy stone weapons with terrifying speed.
"Mia!
Water pulse on my six!" Valerius shouted while dodging a swinging axe.
Sitting securely on his shoulder, Mia yawned, looking completely lazy.
She didn’t even stand up as she lazily pointed a single tiny index finger over Valerius’s shoulder without looking.
Pew!
A microscopic compressed needle of water shot from her fingertip, silently drilling a hole straight through the forehead of a beast about to ambush Valerius from behind.
The monster collapsed into dust before Valerius even turned around.
"You could at least act like you’re trying," Valerius complained, spinning and severing two more monsters with a Zephyr Slash.
"You’re doing fine, My Lord." Mia mumbled sleepily, resting her chin on his iron shoulder plate as he slaughtered the horde.
High above the chaotic warzone, Seraphina stood alone on the ridge, watching the devastation below.
Her lips slowly parted in genuine awe, though no words came out of her silenced throat.
Her fiery red eyes tracked Silas as he seamlessly blended devastating physical brawling with high-tier water and ice magic, tearing through the horde.
’He’s... not bad...’ Seraphina thought reluctantly with her heart beating slightly faster.

At first, back in the upper layers, she had genuinely thought Silas Graves was just some useless arrogant Lord who had tried to make trouble for everybody but watching him now, the truth was undeniable.
Not only did he command an incredibly competent powerful Hero like Aeliana, but he was also quite competent himself.
His combat IQ was flawless, his elemental transitions were instant, and his physical strength was monstrous.
Seraphina slowly nodded her head, a strange grudging respect settling over her prideful heart.
’As expected of the man who has seen me naked, at least,’ she thought, rationalizing his strength in her own twisted noble logic.
If a commoner was going to humiliate her, he at least had the decency to be a monster on the battlefield!
As for how she knew that he was a commoner... that was simple, she could smell it.
Refusing to be completely left out of the raid, Seraphina drew her curved dagger and jumped down from the ledge to join the fray.
THUD!
She hit the ground, but she immediately stumbled with her legs feeling dangerously wobbly.
’Ugh!’ she winced internally as she remembered... the parasite artifact didn’t just mute her; it actively lowered her physical strength by 50% as well as her mana!
Her limbs felt heavy, like she was moving through deep mud.
Every step hurt, and swinging her dagger required double the effort.
Still, she gritted her teeth, pushing her wobbly legs forward to slash at the remaining stragglers, refusing to show weakness in front of Silas.
Ten minutes later, the place was completely silent.
Over a hundred sand monsters had been reduced to piles of harmless dirt and melting ice shards.

chapters.title: Chapter 179: Ititius’s Riddle
paragraphs: Valerius stood in the center of the carnage, breathing as he wiped sweat from his forehead.
He checked the glowing cores of the monsters he had personally slain.
Nothing...
He checked another ten.
Nothing too...
Valerius’s face fell.
He walked over to Silas, reaching into his pocket, and was begrudgingly forced to hand Silas the only other artifact that had been dropped in the entire basin... a glowing silver ring.
"Two artifacts," Valerius grumbled, throwing his hands up in disgust. "Out of a hundred elite monsters, only two dropped loot! It seemed that the god had been lying about everything again!"
Silas took the ring, tossing it into his inventory with a smirk. "That was not surprising in the least. He’s a god of a Secret Realm and the house always wins."
Before they could rest, the God resumed his broadcast.
"Congratulations, my brutal little gladiators!" Ititus clapped his hands over the audio feed. "You actually survived the horde! What an impressive display of violence!"
All of them stopped wiping their weapons and looked up at the ceiling, collectively thinking the exact same thing.
’You know we don’t think you’re dead right...?’
There was absolutely no way a pre-recorded message from so long ago could actively comment on their specific combat performance and timing with such perfect accuracy.
The god was either actively watching them through a viewing orb, or his consciousness was bound to the dungeon core.
However, the God completely ignored their suspicion and continued his monologue.
"Now that the courtyard is cleared," Ititus announced, "it is time to proceed to the inner sanctum! Ahead of you lie three massive caves!"
At the far end of the place, the stone wall rumbled, grinding upward to reveal three identical, dark archways leading into the deep earth: Left, Center, and Right.

"To decide your path, I shall give you a divine riddle!" the god proclaimed cheerfully. "If this riddle is answered correctly... you will walk the true path and find the way out toward the grand treasury! But if it is answered incorrectly... the wrong cave will violently break off from the spatial grid and send the person who entered it even deeper into the dungeon!"
The group tensed.

"Don’t worry too much!" Ititus laughed lightly. "Even if you fall into the deep Abyss, you won’t die immediately! You will be let out automatically when the 24-hour dungeon cycle is dismissed. However... you will completely miss all remaining chances on high-tier treasure! Now, listen closely to my words!"
The god cleared his throat.
"I have no voice, but I tell of the end.
I sit in the middle, where broken roads mend.
The hand on the left seeks the gold in the dark,
While the path on the right leaves no trace of a mark.
If you seek what is real, leave the shadow behind,
Walk where the left and the center entwine!"
The broadcast clicked off, leaving the three dark cave entrances looming silently before them.
Valerius immediately stepped close to Silas, leaning in as they whispered among themselves after the riddle was done.

"What do you think, Graves?" Valerius muttered, keeping his voice low so the girls wouldn’t interrupt. "The phrasing at the end is completely literal. ’Walk where the left and the center entwine.’ It seemed like Center and Left were the obvious, correct answers based on the riddle."
Silas rubbed his chin, his golden-ringed eyes staring at the dark tunnels. "It sounds obvious but exactly too obvious."
"Explain," Valerius frowned.

"The god is a pathological liar, Sterling," Silas whispered back with his paranoia working overtime. "We just agreed five minutes ago that he twists every word. If he explicitly tells us in the final line to take the Left and Center caves, why the hell would we trust him? He’s known to lie! So... shouldn’t we apply reverse logic? What if the real paths are Right and Center, and the Left is the trap?"
Valerius stared at the tunnels, agonizing over the decision.
For two full minutes, the two Lords debated the semantics of ancient divine psychology, weighing the probability of a double-bluff versus a straight lie.
In the end, Valerius shook his head, sighing deeply.

"We’re overthinking it," Valerius decided, gripping his sword. "If it’s a double-bluff, we screw ourselves by guessing random directions. We play the board as written. We go with what the riddle literally said... Left and Center."
"Fine," Silas agreed grudgingly. "We split the risk."
They assigned the routes immediately. Valerius and his Hero, Mia, took the Left cave.
However, before they entered, Silas broke away from Aeliana, walking over to Seraphina who was standing near the Right cave entrance.
Seraphina hadn’t understood the riddle yet since she had been too busy focusing on breathing through the pain of her 50% stat reduction to analyze the poem.
Silas stopped in front of her, looking down at her exhausted, wobbly posture.
"You take the Right cave," Silas told her quietly.
Seraphina blinked her red eyes, looking at the dark right tunnel, then back at him with deep suspicion.
Silas leaned in slightly.

"I listened to the breakdown. I’m purposely sending you down the right path to make sure you’re safe. Based on the riddle, the right path ’leaves no trace of a mark.’ It’s an empty transit tunnel. There are no monsters, no traps, and no combat trials down there. You can’t fight with that collar on, so you need the safest route."
Seraphina narrowed her eyes, staring at his calm face.
’He must be lying...’ Seraphina thought instinctively, her aristocratic cynicism flaring.
Why would this Lord give her the easiest safest route for free?
But as she looked at his steady gaze, and felt the aching exhaustion in her wobbly legs, she didn’t argue.
She did it regardless.
Even if he was lying, the last room sounded like absolutely no trouble compared to fighting another hundred sand beasts.
She gave him a short, silent nod, turned around, and walked into the dark Right cave alone.
Soon, the group was fully separated into the three tunnels.
On the far left, Mia and Valerius were walking in there, their footsteps echoing on the damp stone.
On the far right, Seraphina was in there alone with her hand resting defensively on her dagger as she navigated the quiet dark.
And in the middle cave, Silas and Aeliana were walking in there together with the silver glow of Aeliana’s starlight illuminating the smooth stone walls around them.
For a few minutes, the middle tunnel was completely peaceful.
Then, the God’s voice boomed directly inside the center cavern, vibrating the very air they breathed.
"Did you really believe me?!" Ititus laughed hysterically, his voice dripping with pure, unadulterated sadistic glee. "I told you! I’m a god of secrets! It’s time for one of you to fall!"
Silas froze.
CRACK! KRA-THOOM!
The solid bedrock ground directly below Silas and Aeliana violently cracked as massive fault lines shot across the floor in a microsecond with the stone completely giving way beneath their boots.
"Better luck next time!" the God mocked loudly as the structural integrity of the tunnel collapsed entirely.
"Lord Sy!" Aeliana cried out, reaching for him.
The ground broke open like a shattering eggshell, revealing a bottomless, pitch-black void beneath them.
Gravity seized them instantly, violently swallowing both the Lord and the Elf below into the absolute darkness of the deep Abyss.
Over in the left and right tunnels, Valerius and Seraphina barely had time to register the structural failure.
The floor completely gave way beneath their heavy boots, shattering into thousands of useless, crumbling fragments.

"Did you really believe there was a right answer?!" Ititus’s voice echoed through the collapsing tunnels, dripping with pure, unadulterated sadistic glee. "I’m a god of secrets! Every path leads down!"
Valerius felt the sickening lurch of zero gravity.
He threw his arms out, his green aura flaring as he desperately tried to catch an updraft, but the spatial magic of the trap actively suppressed his wind affinity.
"You honorless bastard!" Valerius roared with his voice echoing into the dark as he plummeted out of sight.

In the right tunnel, Seraphina fell in terrifying silence. Her mouth was open in a silent scream with her red hair whipping violently upward as the pitch-black abyss swallowed her whole, the cursed spider artifact clamped tightly to her throat rendering her mute.
In the center cavern, as gravity seized them and dragged them downward with terrifying velocity, Aeliana didn’t hesitate.
"Lord Sy! I’m here!" Aeliana cried out, her pristine white robes fluttering wildly as the rushing wind tore at her silver hair.
She reached her slender hand out toward him in the dark but Silas didn’t panic.

His combat instincts took over the instant the floor collapsed as he twisted his torso mid-air, ignoring the vertigo, and kicked off a falling slab of bedrock to launch himself horizontally across the void.
He closed the distance in a heartbeat, wrapping his muscular arms tightly around Aeliana’s waist and pulling her flush against his chest.
"I’ve got you," Silas said, his voice calm and steady near her ear.
He shifted his weight, rotating their falling bodies so that his back was facing the ground and he braced his legs, channeling dense mana into his calves and boots to absorb the impending shock.
They fell for what felt like an eternity through the suffocating blackness.
THUD!
Silas hit the ground incredibly hard.

The impact shuddered through his heavy boots and sent a violent shockwave up his spine, but his durability held firm. He bent his knees, sliding backward through a thick loose layer of sediment to completely arrest their momentum.
He didn’t drop Aeliana. He held her securely until they came to a complete halt, then gently set her down on her feet.
"Are you hurt?" Silas asked, his golden-ringed eyes rapidly scanning her for injuries.
"I am perfectly fine, My Lord," Aeliana assured him, smoothing out her white spider-silk robes, though her chest was heaving slightly from the adrenaline of the fall. "Thank you."
Silas nodded, turning his attention to their surroundings.
The environment was completely different from the arena above.
The ground beneath their boots wasn’t stone or regular black sand again...

It was an ocean of pitch-black sand, so dark it seemed to actively absorb the light radiating from Aeliana’s starlight mana. The dark sand was constantly, unnervingly shifting around their ankles, whispering like dry leaves rubbing together.
The air was freezing.
"Welcome, little intruders, to the absolute deepest depths of my Dungeon!"
The voice of the dead god resonated through the cavernous space, no longer cheerful but sounding quite harsh.
"This is the Abyss," Ititus announced proudly. "The final holding cell where the most dangerous, the most unkillable of my ancient enemies were kept in the dark for millennia."

The god paused with a sinister chuckle echoing off the unseen walls. "But you shouldn’t be that worried! The rot of time has taken its toll. They aren’t too harmful anymore! Good luck finding a way out!"
Silas let out a deeply exhausted sigh, reaching into his trench coat.
"Gods are such dramatic pricks," Silas muttered. "Could never be my Elu though..."
He pulled out his heavy brass Treasure Radar, tapping the glass screen to recalibrate the tracking matrix for the new spatial layer.
The green screen flickered to life. The needle spun once, twice, and then locked onto a single solitary coordinate.
PING!
Silas frowned. He smacked the side of the brass device, assuming the fall had broken the internal runes.
PING!
There was only a singular treasure signature in the entire, massive subterranean cavern.

"You have got to be kidding me," Silas cursed out loud, his voice dripping with pure Warlord annoyance. "One? We fell into the deepest deadliest layer of the god’s prison, and there is only one piece of loot down here?!"
"Quality over quantity, my greedy boy!" Ititus’s voice laughed heartily from the shadows, thoroughly enjoying Silas’s frustration.
Silas ignored the dead god, narrowing his eyes as he looked toward the far end of the cavern, following the radar’s bearing.
Through the gloom, about a hundred yards away, sitting atop a jagged pedestal of black stone, was the treasure.
It wasn’t a sword, a shield, or a glowing crystal.

It was an intricately carved fist-sized artifact that looked exactly like a reptilian eye. The iris was a brilliant, swirling gold, encased in dark, petrified amber, and it radiated an aura of mana so incredibly dense that the air around it was physically rippling.
Silas opened his Lord interface with his pupils locking onto the distant object to trigger the scan.
The translucent blue screen manifested in his vision, and the data that scrolled across it made Silas’s breath completely hitch in his throat.
[Name]: The Warden’s Eye
[Type]: Sealing Artifact
[Tier]: Tier 4
[Description]: An ancient, reality-warping containment vessel forged from the crystallized ocular core of a primordial beast.

By actively pouring mana into the iris, the user can forcefully compress and seal any kind of monster, physical object, or energy construct within its internal pocket dimension. The artifact’s internal space is virtually limitless.
[Warning]: The sealing capacity scales directly with the user’s raw mana output and core density. In the hands of a Supreme entity, this artifact is theoretically capable of sealing actual gods.
