"Quality over quantity, my greedy boy!" Ititus’s voice laughed heartily from the shadows, thoroughly enjoying Silas’s frustration.
Silas ignored the dead god, narrowing his eyes as he looked toward the far end of the cavern, following the radar’s bearing.
Through the gloom, about a hundred yards away, sitting atop a jagged pedestal of black stone, was the treasure.
It wasn’t a sword, a shield, or a glowing crystal.
It was an intricately carved fist-sized artifact that looked exactly like a reptilian eye.
The iris was a brilliant, swirling gold, encased in dark, petrified amber, and it radiated an aura of mana so incredibly dense that the air around it was physically rippling.
Silas opened his Lord interface with his pupils locking onto the distant object to trigger the scan.
The translucent blue screen manifested in his vision, and the data that scrolled across it made Silas’s breath completely hitch in his throat.
[Name]: The Warden’s Eye
[Type]: Sealing Artifact
[Tier]: Tier 4
[Description]: An ancient, reality-warping containment vessel forged from the crystallized ocular core of a primordial beast.
By actively pouring mana into the iris, the user can forcefully compress and seal any kind of monster, physical object, or energy construct within its internal pocket dimension.
The artifact’s internal space is virtually limitless.
[Warning]: The sealing capacity scales directly with the user’s raw mana output and core density.
In the hands of a Supreme entity, this artifact is theoretically capable of sealing actual gods.

chapters.title: Chapter 180: A Dragon?
paragraphs: Silas’s eyes widened to the size of saucers.
Tier 4?
Everyone had been bleeding themselves dry for the past day or so fighting over Tier 1 and Tier 2 trinkets so a Tier 4 artifact wasn’t just a weapon... it was even more than a trump card.

’I didn’t even think Ititius would have something of great value like this... but what if something is inside?’ Silas thought, that was a risk but he was sure as long as one didn’t apply mana into the thing... it was alright.
After all, that was an item that could actively seal gods?
Silas of course wanted it.
"That eye is coming home with us," Silas declared however, the dungeon was not going to hand over a Tier 4 item for free.
HSSSSS.
The ocean of black sand surrounding them began to violently churn and bubble.
Massive mounds of the dark sediment began rising from the floor nut these weren’t the classic, humanoid sand mobs from the arena above.

They were twisted nightmarish amalgamations. Spiked carapaces made of compressed black glass formed over shifting limbs. Scythe-like appendages erupted from their sides, and hollow glowing purple eyes snapped open in the dark.
Silas drew his mythril longsword with the steel ringing sharply in the dark cavern.
"I’ll handle the mob," Silas told her, stepping forward to draw the frontline aggro. "And then take the eye too, you just need to support me Aeliana."
Aeliana stepped up beside him, gently placing her hand on his forearm.

"There is no need for you to dive in recklessly, My Lord," Aeliana said as she looked out at the forming horde with her green eyes calculating the spatial distance to the pedestal. "Allow me to retrieve it... I can bypass the entire frontline with a single spatial step."
Silas looked at the shifting sea of black sand, then back at his Starlight Arcanist.
The logic was quite sound.
"Alright," Silas agreed, tightening his grip on his sword. "You get the eye and I’ll buy you the time but do not touch anything else on that pedestal and don’t put mana into it.."
"No worries," Aeliana assured him with a confident devoted smile. "I shall return in ten seconds."
She didn’t run. Aeliana’s body instantly dissolved into a blinding flash of blue-white starlight, teleporting right past the forming monsters.
The sudden flash of light immediately drew the aggro of the horde.
One of the massive, scythe-wielding sand monsters rotated its upper torso, its purple eyes locking onto Aeliana as she rematerialized near the pedestal.
The beast let out a shriek, raising its arms and violently expanding a massive, razor-sharp net of black sand directly in her direction.
"Don’t look away from me!" Silas roared.
Silas didn’t just step in to intercept as he completely let go of his restraints.
For quite a while, he had been meticulously hiding his true power, suppressing his core to blend in with the baseline Blue and Purple core Lords of the group.
But down here, in the dark, with no witnesses except his most loyal Hero, there was no reason to hide.
Silas fully ignited his Gold Core.

A terrifying aura exploded outward from his chest as blinding, liquid gold mana surged through his veins, traveling down his arm and aggressively coating the entire length of his mythril sword in a brilliant aura of golden light.
SHWK!
Silas swung his sword in a horizontal arc and the golden energy completely disintegrated the net with the holy mana burning the black sediment into harmless white ash.
The monsters immediately turned their attention back to the massive, glowing threat in their midst.
Silas laughed loudly, the sound echoing off the cavern walls. It felt incredibly good to stop hiding. He was tired of holding back.
"Come on!" Silas taunted them.
Ten monsters lunged at him simultaneously with their glass scythes swinging for his neck.
Silas didn’t retreat a single inch.
He ducked under the first swing, driving his golden-coated blade straight up through the jaw of the closest beast.
CRUNCH!
He ripped the blade free and didn’t bother using the chants once more.
Silas threw his left hand forward, pouring his dense, golden mana directly into a water spell.
TIDAL IMPACT!
A massive sphere of heavy golden-tinted water formed in his palm and violently detonated against the chest of a charging brute.
BOOOOM!

The hydraulic shockwave was devastating as usual as the brute was blown into atomic dust, and the heavy water splashed aggressively over a dozen surrounding monsters, soaking their shifting black sand bodies and slowing their movements to a crawl.
Silas didn’t give them a microsecond to recover as he slammed his boot into the ground.
ICE TRANSFORMATION!
He violently stripped the heat from the soaked battlefield as the golden-tinted water instantly flash-froze, completely encasing the twelve monsters in jagged unbreakable blocks of solid ice.
Silas blurred forward as his physical strength combined with his momentum.
He swung his golden sword like a baseball bat, shattering the frozen monsters into thousands of pieces of flying ice and black sand.
KRA-SHATTER!
While Silas was completely dismantling the horde at the frontline, Aeliana reached the objective.
She stood before the jagged black pedestal. Sitting in the center of the stone was the Tier 4 artifact... the petrified, golden-irised eye.
Aeliana was meticulous as she didn’t just grab it blindly.
She closed her eyes, channeling her starlight mana outward to scan the immediate vicinity for hidden pressure plates, runic tripwires, or spatial curses before retracting her mana.
The scan returned completely clean. So far, she couldn’t sense any traps whatsoever.
"Securing the asset, My Lord," Aeliana called out over her shoulder.
She reached out her slender pale hand however the moment her fingertips physically brushed against the cold, petrified amber of the eye, everything went wrong.
The artifact didn’t move.
Instead, the golden iris violently dilated. It snapped awake, the pupil locking directly onto Aeliana’s face, and it began to glow with an intense purple light.
Aeliana gasped, her eyes going wide as the ambient gravity around her completely inverted.
Her physical body immediately began swirling with her form actively stretching and distorting as she was violently pulled into a spatial vortex that erupted directly from the pupil of the eye.
Silas spun around, hearing the violent tear in the spatial fabric. He saw the purple light consuming her.
"AELI!" Silas yelled at the top of his lungs, abandoning the fight and sprinting toward the pedestal with explosive speed but he was too late.
VWOOP!
The spatial vortex collapsed inward with a sharp snapping sound.
Aeliana completely disappeared from the cavern, leaving only the dark pedestal and the dormant eye behind.
[Inside the Artifact.]
Aeliana blinked.
The transition was violently ripping the breath from her lungs.
One moment she was standing in a freezing cavern, and the next, she was standing in a completely different world.
The sky above her was a suffocating, endless expanse of pitch-black nothingness and the ground beneath her boots was cracked obsidian.
But what hit her first wasn’t the visual desolation.
It was the smell.
Aeliana gagged, throwing her hand over her mouth and nose. The smell of festering rot filled the air everywhere, a stench so intensely putrid it physically burned the back of her throat.
It smelled like a millennia of undisturbed decay.
She slowly lowered her hand with her eyes adjusting to the gloom, and located the source of the rot.
Laying sprawled across the cracked obsidian ground, taking up an area the size of a small mountain, was a very huge dragon.
Its scales were a dull, muted crimson, cracked and peeling away from its massive frame. The beast was actively rotting.

Massive sections of flesh were sloughing off its ribs, exposing blackened bone. Disgusting, pale worms the size of anacondas were actively coming out of her open wounds, writhing blindly in the dark dirt.
Aeliana was terrified.
The overwhelming aura of the creature, even in its decaying state, was suffocating but as she looked closer, she noticed something else.
Standing perfectly still at the edge of the dragon’s massive, resting head, gently stroking the decaying scales, was a woman.
She was completely naked.
Her skin was flawlessly pale, glowing softly in the dark. Her hair was a vibrant, cascading waterfall of fiery crimson that matched the dragon’s scales and her figure was quite impossible...
It was curvaceous and toned while exuding a magnetism that completely defied the grotesque rot surrounding her.
Aeliana, despite the terror of the situation, felt a sudden pang of intense, petty elven jealousy.
She instinctively crossed her arms over her own chest, glaring at the woman’s flawless proportions.
The naked woman stopped stroking the dragon. She didn’t turn around, but she tilted her head back, taking a slow, deep sniff of the stagnant air.
"You..." the woman spoke with her voice echoing with a strange dual harmonic resonance. "You smell like humans."
The woman slowly turned around, her glowing crimson eyes locking onto Aeliana.
"And not only that," the woman continued, her eyes narrowing. "But you smell like gods, too. Are you perhaps allied with them? Has Ititius finally come to execute me?"
Aeliana straightened her posture, her pride as an Arcanist of the stars refusing to let her cower before a naked stranger, regardless of the aura she emitted.
"I am allied with no god," Aeliana started, preparing to verbally defend her presence.
Before Aeliana tried to even speak another word, the massive rotting dragon behind the woman suddenly moved.
SQUELCH.
The dragon’s massive decaying jaw parted, exposing rows of yellowed broken teeth. When it spoke, the voice was identical to the naked woman’s, only magnified to a deafening earth-shaking volume.
"Answer the question!" the dragon interrupted her, its voice booming with hostility. "You smell of filthy humans, and the stink of the divine gods clings to your soul! Why is that?!"
Aeliana didn’t flinch. She raised her chin with her green eyes glowing with unwavering loyalty.
"Because I am tethered to a Lord," Aeliana replied firmly. "And he possesses the heart of a Saint."
The word hung in the rotting air.

There was a deafening, sickening cracking sound from the dragon. The beast’s massive spine arched, snapping ancient bones back into place as she roared out, a sound of pure, unadulterated historical agony.

"Lord!" the dragon roared, the soundwave physically pushing Aeliana backward a few inches. "It’s always Humans! It’s always gods! You always try to oppress us! You bind us, you steal our skies, and you lock us in the dark!"
The naked woman turned fully over to Aeliana.
The woman’s flawless face contorted into a mask of pure, feral rage. Her eyes were glowing in brilliant crimson light.
Her pale body began to violently tremble.
CRACK! SNAP!
A sickening sound of breaking bones filled the silent void. The woman’s spine violently elongated, tearing through her pale skin.
Her jaw unhinged, extending outward into a massive snout as thick burning crimson scales began aggressively bursting out from beneath her flesh, covering her entirely.
The transformation was horrific, nothing like what the books said of a Dragon transformation as Aeliana watched the ground.

The delicate humanoid shadow cast on the black ground was violently twisting and expanding, shifting from the silhouette of a curvaceous woman into the massive, winged, horned profile of an apex predator.
Within seconds, the woman was completely gone.
Standing before Aeliana, entirely separate from the rotting carcass on the ground, was a newly formed flawless crimson dragon.
Aeliana immediately got on the defensive. She shifted her stance, dropping her center of gravity and raising her hands.
She was an educated Elf.
She knew exactly what dragons were, their destructive capabilities, and exactly what to do once their territorial rage was ignited.
[You do not run from a dragon. You fight, or you die.]
She didn’t want to resort to this ultimate trump card so early in the Secret Realm raid, but the pressure radiating from the crimson beast left her no alternative.
Aeliana reached over with her left hand and forcefully ripped the right sleeve of her pristine white robes all the way up to her shoulder.
Burning brightly on her pale elven skin, near her bicep, was a glowing intricate green rune.
Lady Eluned, the Goddess of Nature, had personally kissed a Genesis Rune onto her arm back at the territory before the raid commenced.
Aeliana closed her eyes for a microsecond and poured her raw mana directly into the mark, forcefully activating it.
’Thank you my Goddes...’
The green rune flared with blinding natural light.
The effect was instantaneous. As long as the rune existed and remained active on her flesh, her magical stamina was going to be near limitless.
Her core expanded, drawing mana from the rune.
The Crimson Dragon didn’t care about the glowing light.
"Die!" the dragon roared with the sound shaking the black sky.

chapters.title: Chapter 181: Warden’s Seal
paragraphs: "Die!" the dragon screamed with her mind completely shattered by solitary confinement alongside the decaying corpse of her mother.
The beast rushed forward with terrifying speed with her massive claws violently tearing up deep chunks of the obsidian floor after every thunderous step.
"Do you know what your kind did to us?!" the dragon shrieked. "You filthy humans took our skies! You took our Lands!"
She snapped her massive jaws with acidic saliva sizzling against the black stone.
"You stripped away our pride, you stole our magic, and you locked my mother in this suffocating hell to rot in the dark for ten thousand years!"
As the dragon shot forward, rapidly closing the distance, she aggressively spread her massive leathery crimson wings to halt her physical momentum.
Deep within the back of her massive throat, a terrifying superheated ball of white-hot flames began to violently gather, illuminating the dark world like a newborn sun.
"Every single one of you deserves to agonizingly die!" the dragon roared, her throat expanding with pressure. "Burn with us!"
Aeliana didn’t step back as she planted her boots firmly on the black stone.
She raised both of her hands forward, overlapping her palms.
She didn’t hold back a single percentage of her output...
"I see..."
Aeliana violently charging up an Arcane Piercer with her absolute full, unsuppressed mana.
The starlight gathered between her hands, condensing into a blinding spear of pure white-hot arcane energy.
The power was so intense it hummed, actively regenerating her reserves the exact millisecond she spent them.
"Listen to me, Dragon!" Aeliana shouted over the roaring flames. "Even if all the men in this corrupted world deserved to die for what they did to your kind..."
She locked her silver eyes onto the dragon’s throat.
"...my Lord Sy does not! And he never will!"
FWOOSH!
The dragon violently snapped its jaws forward, blasting that apocalyptic sea of fire forward like a localized volcanic eruption.
Aeliana thrust her hands out and fired the Arcane Piercer as the two massive attacks collided perfectly in the dead center of the dark expanse.
KRA-THOOM!
The collision generated enough force to send a visible shockwave violently expanding outward, completely shattering the obsidian ground and throwing shards of black stone miles into the air.
For a fraction of a second, it was a stalemate of pure elemental pressure.
However, the Dragon’s scattered flames lacked the density of the starlight. The fire broke, parting like a sea around a stone.
The dragon’s glowing crimson eyes widened in shock.
SHWK!

The Arcane Piercer didn’t just push the fire back as the blinding white spear of starlight punched a perfectly straight, clean hole directly through the thick scales, bone, and brain matter of the dragon’s massive head.
The beam shot out the back of the beast’s skull, soaring off into the dark sky.
The dragon’s momentum died instantly.
The flames in its mouth sputtered out as it fell to the obsidian ground with a massive thud, completely motionless as its crimson eyes went wide and totally unfocused.
Aeliana lowered her hands, breathing hard despite the near limitless stamina with the mental strain of the attack wearing on her mind.
’I don’t think it’s that easy to kill a dragon...’
She looked at the massive corpse, feeling a brief pang of pity for the imprisoned monster.
Suddenly, the air warped.
The massive, gaping hole in the center of the dragon’s skull began to violently writhe.
Flesh, bone, and scales aggressively knit back together in a fraction of a second as the fatal wound physically sews itself shut.
The dragon’s eyes snapped wide open, burning brighter than before. It regenerated instantly!
The monster didn’t even bother standing up.
"I don’t care about your Lord or anything!" the dragon shrieked, its voice echoing with pure hatred. "They all deserve to die!"
The beast violently twisted its massive hips on the ground and whipped its spiked tail forward with the speed of a snapping whip.
Aeliana didn’t even have time to raise a defensive shield.
The massive tail slammed directly into Aeliana’s side with the force of a speeding freight train.
BOOM!
SHWK!
The massive razor-sharp edge of Silas’s mythril longsword tore effortlessly through the compacted sand.

Silas, standing completely alone on the pitch-black exterior of the deep Abyss, twisted his torso with devastating force as he channeled a dense surge of ambient moisture into the blade, converting it into a pressurized Abyssal Sever right at the point of impact.
The giant, fifty-foot sand snake that had ambushed him from the underground dunes let out a hissing screech of agony.
"PSSSSS!"
Its massive body was cleanly cleaved in twain, the two halves violently falling away and dissolving into useless inert piles of black dirt before they even hit the stone floor.
Silas didn’t even pause to watch the monster die.
His boots slammed against the dark ground, kicking up clouds of ash as he sprinted directly toward the jagged black pedestal at the center of the cavern.
He arrived in front of the stone pillar with his eyes locked onto the Tier 4 artifact.
The Warden’s Eye sat there, perfectly still but the brilliant, swirling gold iris that had been glowing just moments ago was completely gone.
The petrified amber vessel was dull and lifeless..
Silas reached out with his calloused fingers brushing against the cold, dead surface of the artifact.
He tried to touch it, tried to channel his mana into it to establish a tether, but there was nothing inside.
’Fuck...’
The signature was completely hollowed out and Silas’s golden-ringed eyes widened in horror.
"Aeli..." Silas muttered, his voice cracking as he squeezed the cold artifact in his palm.
His heart hammered violently against his ribs.
He should have never let her do this by herself. He should have taken it, or at the very least, he should have tied a physical mana-tether to her waist.
She had leaped directly into a Tier 4 Mythic sealing item completely blind. Who knew what ancient god-killing horror she was stuck in there with?
"Hahahahaha!"
The dead God’s voice suddenly erupted from the cavern ceiling, booming with sadistic joy.

"Oh, the look on your face is absolutely priceless!" Ititus laughed heartily, the sound vibrating the very air. "It is quite over for your little elven pet! She has been completely consumed by the item! And that, my greedy little boy, is exactly what you get for being greedy! You wanted a Mythic artifact? Now you have a very expensive paperweight!"

Silas’s grip on his sword tightened until his knuckles turned completely white but he remained calm, this was the god’s secret realm and if he refused to answer then Silas would simply have to make a query.
"How do I release the seal?" Silas demanded with his voice dropping quickly, however if the God was intimidated by drops in voice, Ititius would have never become a god in the first place..

"Oh, you want a hint?" Ititus teased,. "Very well! I am a generous god! Here is your riddle... I am the lock that has no key, the prison built of eternity. To open the door that has no hinge, you must first find the—"
"Shut the fuck up," Silas interrupted viciously.
Silas immediately discarded the riddle.
There was no way he was trusting a single syllable out of this pathological liar’s mouth ever again.
The god had lied about a lot of things today... he had lied about the safe tunnels, and he was definitely lying right now.
Silas closed his eyes, completely tuning out the god’s annoying laughter.
He turned his focus inward as he decided to ask a direct System Query to the one thing he absolutely trusted... his Upgrade System of course.
’System,’ Silas asked in his internal thoughts. ’How can I release Aeliana from this jewel?’
[Ding!]
The familiar, crisp chime of his personal interface echoed in his mind.
The translucent blue screen manifested behind his closed eyelids, calculating the spatial properties of the Tier 4 artifact he was currently holding.
[Query Acknowledged.]
[Analyzing Target: The Warden’s Eye (Tier 4)]

[Analysis Complete: The reverse-summoning protocol does not work on this specific item. The artifact’s internal pocket dimension has already sealed a living, hostile entity inside it prior to your companion’s entry. To extract any newly sealed matter, the primary containment must be forcibly shattered.]
Silas frowned deeply.
’Shattered? You mean I have to break a Tier 4 Mythic item?’
[Affirmative. You must release what was already inside by breaking the physical vessel.]
Silas asked another question in his thoughts with his mind racing.
’How do I break it? The casing feels like compressed diamond.’
[Calculating Structural Density...]

[Solution Found: A standard physical strike will not pierce the amber. However, a full-power strike utilizing the maximum force of your Gold Core mana will overload the item’s threshold and shatter the seal.]
Silas opened his eyes. He slowly exhaled a long breath, letting the system interface fade away.
The god was still talking, still kept clowning him from the shadows of the ceiling.
"—and so you see, little Lord, you will simply have to wait a hundred years for the internal digestion cycle to finish..."

Silas completely ignored him. He laid the dead petrified eye flat on the surface of the jagged black table as he took a firm hold of his mythril sword with both hands. He planted his boots securely against the stone floor, adjusting his center of gravity.
"Well then..." Silas muttered softly to himself, his golden-ringed eyes locking onto the artifact. "I just have to use the maximum force of my mana, right?"
[Back inside The Artifact]
KRA-THOOM!
Aeliana skidded violently across the cracked barren obsidian ground.
The impact of the dragon’s massive tail whip had launched her backward like a cannonball.
Her leather boots carved twin smoking trenches into the black dirt as she desperately dug her heels in to arrest her momentum.
She didn’t even have time to catch her breath.
"Die!" the newly transformed crimson dragon roared with her massive jaws unhinging.
The dragon didn’t blast fire this time.
The mana in the air warped aggressively, and the dragon blasted her with a massive torrent of crimson lightning.
The red electricity tore through the dark world, completely shattering the sound barrier with a deafening sound.
CRACK!
"Starlight Aegis!" Aeliana commanded.
She threw her hands forward as an interlocking shield of pure white-hot starlight instantly formed in front of her.
BOOOOOM!
The crimson lightning slammed into the shield as the impact generated a shockwave that pulverized the ground in a fifty-foot radius.
Aeliana gritted her teeth with her eyes glowing fiercely as the mana from the Genesis Rune pumped directly into her defensive ward, holding the barrier steady against the overwhelming voltage.
’This is getting quite repetitive.’
Aeliana didn’t stay on the defensive.
The moment the lightning sputtered, she dissolved into a flash of blue-white light, teleporting directly into the dragon’s personal space.
She reappeared directly above the dragon’s massive right shoulder.
"Arcane Sever!" Aeliana shouted.
She condensed her starlight mana into a massive fifty-foot blade of pure radiant energy and she swung her arms downward with all her might.
The blade sheared cleanly through the air, bypassing the dragon’s thick crimson scales entirely.
SHWK!

The blade cut completely through bone, muscle, and sinew and the dragon’s massive right wing was cleanly severed from its back as a massive geyser of boiling superheated dragon blood erupted from the stump, raining down on the obsidian floor like molten lava.
"GAAARGH!"
The beast let out an agonizing earth-shaking shriek with its massive body completely losing its balance and crashing against the ground but Aeliana knew the biology of the Dragon.
She knew it wouldn’t last.
Before the severed wing even hit the dirt, the bloody stump on the dragon’s back began to violently writhe.

Muscle fibers aggressively knit themselves back together in a fraction of a second as a brand-new fully formed crimson wing violently sprouted from the wound with the monster tanking the lethal blow and regenerating instantly.
The dragon roared, twisting its long serpentine neck around to bite Aeliana out of the sky but Aeliana was faster.
WHOOSH!
She dropped completely out of the air like a stone, landing on the back of the dragon’s neck as she grounded the massive beast by channeling pure concentrated starlight into her boots.
"Hup!"
CRASH!
The overwhelming weight forced the dragon’s head down into the dirt with a massive crater and Aeliana lunged forward.
She reached out with her slender, pale hands and grabbed the dragon’s massive black horns.
"Yield!" Aeliana commanded.
She planted her boots against the scales and violently yanked the dragon’s massive head backward, exposing the beast’s vulnerable throat.
The dragon thrashed wildly with its massive claws tearing up the obsidian ground but despite the feral rage consuming its mind, the dragon was deeply confused.
’Why?’ the dragon wondered frantically, its glowing crimson eyes darting up to look at the Elf currently wrestling it into submission. ’Why does she fight for a human?’

chapters.title: Chapter 182: Lord Silas
paragraphs: The dragon sprung out of Aeliana’s headlock by forcefully manipulating its own biology.
It made its entire body incredibly spiky, jagged crimson thorns violently erecting from its scales like a porcupine.
CRK! CRK! CRK! CRK!
Aeliana was forced to release her grip, teleporting backward a dozen feet to avoid being impaled.
’Fuck... Dragons really are one of the most versatile creatures.’ Aeliana thought.

As the dragon reared backward, shaking the dust from its massive head, it didn’t immediately attack. It looked directly at Aeliana with its chest heaving, and asked the question that had been burning in its mind.

"Why?!" the dragon’s booming dual-harmonic voice echoed across the barren world. "Why are you fighting so hard for a filthy human? You are an Elf! Your kind had been terribly wronged by humans! They enslaved your forests! They burned your glades!"
The dragon’s massive tail lashed angrily behind it.
"This is exactly what my Mother told me before she died! Humans are a plague upon all ancient races! Why do you submit to one?!"
Aeliana stood perfectly still with her green eyes locking onto the massive beast.
Aeliana had to admit, the dragon wasn’t wrong.
Historically speaking, the beast was entirely correct.
There was a very specific bloody reason why the Holy Elf Kingdom was originally formed in the Sovereign Realm.

It was formed as a sanctuary, a militarized fortress designed specifically to protect their kind from the rampant enslavement and exploitation perpetrated by human empires but Aeliana’s expression didn’t waver.
Her posture remained completely resolute.

"You speak of history," Aeliana said with her voice sounding clear and carrying over the howling wind. "And history is written in blood but both my Previous Lord, Lord Kal, and my Love, Lord Silas... are not the kind of humans that elves were afraid of."
Aeliana brought her hand forward, the starlight dimming slightly as she spoke with deep conviction.

"You do not know him," Aeliana explained softly. "Lord Silas is a man who loves developing his territory and the people that are inside it. He doesn’t view us as tools or slaves. He views us as his foundation instead..."
The dragon let out a low rumbling growl of disbelief. "Lies."

"It is the truth," Aeliana countered fiercely. "It didn’t matter if someone was an elf, or a goddess like Lady Eluned, or even a demon... as long as they have something to give, as long as they were willing to contribute to the territory, Lord Silas would take them in and protect them with his life."
Aeliana lowered her gaze slightly with a brief shadow passing over her flawless features.

"Lord Silas is actually my second Lord," she revealed quietly. "I had an original Lord before him, Lord Kal, when I had recently been summoned into this world. But... I failed him. Not only did I lose my Lord to the darkness of the dungeon, but I lost my home, my purpose... I lost everything."
The look of profound crushing loss was still deeply etched on her pale face.
The dragon stopped thrashing as the massive beast stared at the tiny Elf.
For a brief fleeting moment, the feral rage in the dragon’s eyes dimmed, replaced by a flicker of genuine understanding.
The dragon knew exactly what it meant to lose everything but then a completely bright and radiant look of pure joy entered Aeliana’s face, entirely erasing the sorrow.
The sudden shift stunned the dragon.

"But then," Aeliana smiled, her green eyes glowing with absolute warmth. "Lord Silas and Miss Eluned saved me from the darkness that covered me... They didn’t cast me aside because I was a failure. They gave me a place to stay and they gave me a home."
Aeliana stepped forward, completely ignoring the massive claws resting just feet away from her.

"And when I made mistakes," Aeliana continued, "when I fucked up... Lord Silas punished me but it was not harsh. He sat me down, he told me what went wrong, and he helped me realize my mistake so I could grow stronger. He treats me as an equal."
A faint blush touched Aeliana’s pale cheeks. "Plus... he’s incredibly handsome."
The dragon blinked, completely thrown off by the sudden romantic pivot.

"Lord Silas tries to act mostly tough on the outside," Aeliana laughed softly, a beautiful, musical sound. "He acts like a ruthless Lord to the rest of the world but he is very kind at heart and he cares about all of us immensely."
She pointed a finger at the dragon.

"If he didn’t care, he wouldn’t have spent a lot of time to build a massive Library in the territory just to teach the uneducated girls how to read. He wouldn’t actively try to capture and breed comfortable mounts just to reduce the pain that our legs feel when we march across the Basin!"
Aeliana pressed both of her hands over her heart.

"However," Aeliana declared with her voice ringing in unshakable devotion. "If you ask me why I love my Lord so deeply... why, even though we have spent such a relatively short time together, why I want to have his children... I can give you a thousand more reasons."
The dragon fell completely silent.
The massive beast slowly turned its head looking away from the glowing Elf. The dragon looked at the massive, decaying corpse of her mother resting in the dark dirt a few hundred yards away.
The dragon remembered earlier.

She had been the one that made her Mother talk earlier with necromantic magic, just to hear her voice one last time before her vocal cords rotted away completely. She had been gone for a while, lost to the decay.
Her Mother had been deeply betrayed by Humans.

She had assumed a human form, she had fallen in love, and she had married a human man and that same man, the man she trusted with her ancient heart, had drugged her and sold her off to a mercenary band of Dragon Slayers for a pathetic sum of 5 coppers.
Five coppers for the life of a primordial queen?
So many terrible things had happened to their bloodline and the trauma was etched into their very DNA.
But as the dragon looked back at Aeliana... even the dragon felt intrigued.
She felt genuinely intrigued to know what kind of human this ’Lord Silas’ was.
How could a human possess a soul so saintly, so utterly devoted to his people, that an immortal Elf would willingly offer to bear his children?
The dragon felt a strange alien desire to meet this human, just to prove that he was not as perfect as Aeliana made him seem.
But the inherited trauma was too deep but the feeling of isolation since the moment she was born had fundamentally broken her mind.
The dragon violently shook her massive head, forcefully burying the curiosity beneath a mountain of inherited rage.
"I DO NOT CARE!" the dragon roared, her voice cracking with emotional agony.
She reared up on her hind legs, her massive wings spreading wide and casting a terrifying shadow over the battlefield.

"ALL humans are evil!" the dragon screamed, her crimson eyes flaring with psychotic light. "They are parasites! And the moment you learn to make peace with that truth, Elf... that is when you will truly be at ease!"
"Then we have nothing left to say..." Aeliana stated coldly with her starlight flaring.
The dragon charged at Aeliana again.
BOOM! KRA-THOOM!

The dragon lunged with her massive jaws snapping shut with enough force to shatter mythril and Aeliana teleported a fraction of an inch out of the way with the teeth clicking shut right next to her ear.
Aeliana spun, driving a heavy, starlight-infused kick directly into the side of the dragon’s snout.
CRACK!
The impact shattered three of the beast’s massive fangs.

The dragon retaliated instantly, swiping its massive claws in a horizontal arc but Aeliana formed a Starlight Aegis, however the physical mass of the blow shattered the shield into glowing shards with the force raking across Aeliana’s ribs and drawing a thin line of elven blood.
"Arcane Barrage!" Aeliana shouted.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
She fired dozens of condensed starlight spheres directly into the dragon’s chest.
The spheres detonated on impact, blowing massive gaping craters through the crimson scales.
But the dragon’s regeneration was absolute as the wounds closed instantly.

"If I find my way out of this prison," the dragon roared, unleashing a massive, sweeping torrent of crimson lightning that scorched the obsidian floor. "I swear upon my mother’s rotting bones... I will kill any human that I can see! I will burn their cities to ash!"
"You will never leave this room!" Aeliana screamed back.
The dragon violently whipped its heavy spiked tail and Aeliana tried to dodge, but the spatial distortion of the lightning blast threw off her timing.
SMASH!
The massive tail connected cleanly with Aeliana’s torso.
Aeliana was hit violently into the air.
She was launched hundreds of feet into the dark sky with the wind violently knocking the breath from her lungs.
"Ugh!"
She soared upward with her body spinning helplessly as the dragon looked up, preparing a final massive blast of superheated fire to execute her mid-air.
Aeliana stabilized herself at the apex of her flight.
She looked down at the roaring beast with her green eyes turning as cold and unyielding as the void of space.
"If you ever threaten to hurt Lord Sy..." Aeliana whispered, her voice carrying an incredibly terrifying promise.
She spread her arms wide, drawing entirely upon the maximum output of the Genesis Rune as the ambient temperature of the entire pocket dimension violently plummeted.
’No...’ The Dragon shot forward heading toward Aeliana. ’You can’t!’
"No!"
She locked her gaze onto the dragon.
"...then I will murder you right here."
Aeliana clasped her hands together.
"LAND OF FROST!"
The spell detonated and contrary to what the dragon expected, it wasn’t a beam of ice.
It was a complete atmospheric rewrite.
A massive and violently expanding dome of frozen energy erupted from Aeliana’s position in the sky and slammed down onto the obsidian floor.
The entire world flash-froze in a microsecond as massive, towering glaciers of jagged blue ice violently erupted from the ground, entirely encasing the battlefield.
Dragons were fundamentally creatures of heat energy and due to their special biology, they were inherently weak to high-tier ice magic.
The Land of Frost slammed into the crimson dragon.
"AGHHHHHH!"

The beast shrieked in paralyzing agony as the absolute-zero temperature violently extinguished its internal flames, freezing its blood in its veins and locking its massive limbs in an unbreakable, towering prison of solid ice.
[Back Outside in the Deep Abyss.]
Silas stood before the jagged black pedestal.
His entire body was radiating a terrifying blinding aura of pure liquid gold mana.
The sovereign energy converged violently around the blade of his mythril sword, the heavy steel humming with a frequency that threatened to completely shatter the spatial fabric of the dungeon.
"What are you doing?!" the God’s voice shrieked from the ceiling, the sadistic joy completely replaced by genuine panicked terror.
Silas didn’t answer.
He raised the golden sword high above his head with the muscles in his arms bulging as he concentrated every single drop of his Gold Core’s maximum output into the tip of the blade.

"Stop!" Ititus complained frantically, his voice echoing rapidly. "You fool! You don’t understand the structure of that artifact! If you break it, you’ll destabilize the entire lower quadrant! Please, stop!"
Silas was absolutely not having it.
"I want my Hero back..."
He took a firm step back, gathered his full unsuppressed power, and slashed downward with all of his might.
The golden blade struck the dead center of the petrified amber eye.
CHINK!
For a microsecond, time seemed to completely stop then, a microscopic crack appeared on the surface of the amber.
The crack violently expanded, tearing into dozens of deep glowing fault lines across the entire artifact.
The overwhelming force of the Gold Core entirely overloaded the Mythic seal’s containment threshold.
"NOOO!" the god shouted, a long desperate agonizing scream that echoed through the entire Secret Realm.
KA-BOOOOOOM!
The Warden’s Eye violently exploded.
The unrestrained release of spatial energy generated a catastrophic shockwave that threw Silas backward off his feet.
He hit the dirt, shielding his eyes from the blinding light and from the epicenter of the shattered artifact, something massive emerged.
It wasn’t Aeliana.
It was a massive and huge rotting dragon body.
The colossal, decaying corpse of the mother dragon violently shot upward, forcefully expelled from the collapsing pocket dimension.
The mass of the corpse broke completely past the ceiling of the cavern.
The rotting beast shot upward like a morbid missile, violently breaking past the bedrock, breaking past the labyrinth layers, and crashing entirely through the miles of earth above.
Miles above them, on the surface of the Secret Realm, the other Lords were currently facing against another massive Sand General in a desperate raid.
Suddenly, the ground beneath them violently erupted.

The massive, rotting skull of a primordial dragon burst through the sand dunes, completely annihilating the Sand General in a shower of black bone and dust before continuing its ascent into the amber sky.
Back down in the deep Abyss, Silas jumped back, coughing as thick clouds of dust and debris rained down from the shattered ceiling.
He watched in awe as the thick skeleton and the rotting body completely filled the upper area of the massive cavern, blocking out what little light remained.
However, because the corpse was completely removed from the temporal stasis of the artifact, the thousands of years of accelerated decay instantly caught up to it.

sentences.text: The dragon sprung out of Aeliana’s headlock by forcefully manipulating its own biology.
It made its entire body incredibly spiky, jagged crimson thorns violently erecting from its scales like a porcupine.
CRK!
CRK!
CRK!
CRK!
Aeliana was forced to release her grip, teleporting backward a dozen feet to avoid being impaled.
’Fuck...
Dragons really are one of the most versatile creatures.’ Aeliana thought.
As the dragon reared backward, shaking the dust from its massive head, it didn’t immediately attack.
It looked directly at Aeliana with its chest heaving, and asked the question that had been burning in its mind.
"Why?!" the dragon’s booming dual-harmonic voice echoed across the barren world.
"Why are you fighting so hard for a filthy human?
You are an Elf!
Your kind had been terribly wronged by humans!
They enslaved your forests!
They burned your glades!"
The dragon’s massive tail lashed angrily behind it.
"This is exactly what my Mother told me before she died!
Humans are a plague upon all ancient races!
Why do you submit to one?!"
Aeliana stood perfectly still with her green eyes locking onto the massive beast.
Aeliana had to admit, the dragon wasn’t wrong.
Historically speaking, the beast was entirely correct.
There was a very specific bloody reason why the Holy Elf Kingdom was originally formed in the Sovereign Realm.

It was formed as a sanctuary, a militarized fortress designed specifically to protect their kind from the rampant enslavement and exploitation perpetrated by human empires but Aeliana’s expression didn’t waver.
Her posture remained completely resolute.
"You speak of history," Aeliana said with her voice sounding clear and carrying over the howling wind.
"And history is written in blood but both my Previous Lord, Lord Kal, and my Love, Lord Silas... are not the kind of humans that elves were afraid of."
Aeliana brought her hand forward, the starlight dimming slightly as she spoke with deep conviction.
"You do not know him," Aeliana explained softly.
"Lord Silas is a man who loves developing his territory and the people that are inside it.
He doesn’t view us as tools or slaves.
He views us as his foundation instead..."
The dragon let out a low rumbling growl of disbelief.
"Lies."
"It is the truth," Aeliana countered fiercely.

"It didn’t matter if someone was an elf, or a goddess like Lady Eluned, or even a demon... as long as they have something to give, as long as they were willing to contribute to the territory, Lord Silas would take them in and protect them with his life."
Aeliana lowered her gaze slightly with a brief shadow passing over her flawless features.
"Lord Silas is actually my second Lord," she revealed quietly.
"I had an original Lord before him, Lord Kal, when I had recently been summoned into this world.
But...
I failed him.
Not only did I lose my Lord to the darkness of the dungeon, but I lost my home, my purpose...
I lost everything."
The look of profound crushing loss was still deeply etched on her pale face.
The dragon stopped thrashing as the massive beast stared at the tiny Elf.
For a brief fleeting moment, the feral rage in the dragon’s eyes dimmed, replaced by a flicker of genuine understanding.
The dragon knew exactly what it meant to lose everything but then a completely bright and radiant look of pure joy entered Aeliana’s face, entirely erasing the sorrow.
The sudden shift stunned the dragon.
"But then," Aeliana smiled, her green eyes glowing with absolute warmth.
"Lord Silas and Miss Eluned saved me from the darkness that covered me...
They didn’t cast me aside because I was a failure.
They gave me a place to stay and they gave me a home."
Aeliana stepped forward, completely ignoring the massive claws resting just feet away from her.
"And when I made mistakes," Aeliana continued, "when I fucked up...
Lord Silas punished me but it was not harsh.
He sat me down, he told me what went wrong, and he helped me realize my mistake so I could grow stronger.
He treats me as an equal."
A faint blush touched Aeliana’s pale cheeks.
"Plus... he’s incredibly handsome."
The dragon blinked, completely thrown off by the sudden romantic pivot.
"Lord Silas tries to act mostly tough on the outside," Aeliana laughed softly, a beautiful, musical sound.
"He acts like a ruthless Lord to the rest of the world but he is very kind at heart and he cares about all of us immensely."
She pointed a finger at the dragon.
"If he didn’t care, he wouldn’t have spent a lot of time to build a massive Library in the territory just to teach the uneducated girls how to read.
He wouldn’t actively try to capture and breed comfortable mounts just to reduce the pain that our legs feel when we march across the Basin!"
Aeliana pressed both of her hands over her heart.
"However," Aeliana declared with her voice ringing in unshakable devotion.
"If you ask me why I love my Lord so deeply... why, even though we have spent such a relatively short time together, why I want to have his children...
I can give you a thousand more reasons."
The dragon fell completely silent.
The massive beast slowly turned its head looking away from the glowing Elf.
The dragon looked at the massive, decaying corpse of her mother resting in the dark dirt a few hundred yards away.
The dragon remembered earlier.
She had been the one that made her Mother talk earlier with necromantic magic, just to hear her voice one last time before her vocal cords rotted away completely.
She had been gone for a while, lost to the decay.
Her Mother had been deeply betrayed by Humans.

She had assumed a human form, she had fallen in love, and she had married a human man and that same man, the man she trusted with her ancient heart, had drugged her and sold her off to a mercenary band of Dragon Slayers for a pathetic sum of 5 coppers.
Five coppers for the life of a primordial queen?
So many terrible things had happened to their bloodline and the trauma was etched into their very DNA.
But as the dragon looked back at Aeliana... even the dragon felt intrigued.
She felt genuinely intrigued to know what kind of human this ’Lord Silas’ was.
How could a human possess a soul so saintly, so utterly devoted to his people, that an immortal Elf would willingly offer to bear his children?
The dragon felt a strange alien desire to meet this human, just to prove that he was not as perfect as Aeliana made him seem.
But the inherited trauma was too deep but the feeling of isolation since the moment she was born had fundamentally broken her mind.
The dragon violently shook her massive head, forcefully burying the curiosity beneath a mountain of inherited rage.
"I DO NOT CARE!" the dragon roared, her voice cracking with emotional agony.
She reared up on her hind legs, her massive wings spreading wide and casting a terrifying shadow over the battlefield.
"ALL humans are evil!" the dragon screamed, her crimson eyes flaring with psychotic light.
"They are parasites!
And the moment you learn to make peace with that truth, Elf... that is when you will truly be at ease!"
"Then we have nothing left to say..." Aeliana stated coldly with her starlight flaring.
The dragon charged at Aeliana again.
BOOM!
KRA-THOOM!

The dragon lunged with her massive jaws snapping shut with enough force to shatter mythril and Aeliana teleported a fraction of an inch out of the way with the teeth clicking shut right next to her ear.
Aeliana spun, driving a heavy, starlight-infused kick directly into the side of the dragon’s snout.
CRACK!
The impact shattered three of the beast’s massive fangs.

The dragon retaliated instantly, swiping its massive claws in a horizontal arc but Aeliana formed a Starlight Aegis, however the physical mass of the blow shattered the shield into glowing shards with the force raking across Aeliana’s ribs and drawing a thin line of elven blood.
"Arcane Barrage!" Aeliana shouted.
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
She fired dozens of condensed starlight spheres directly into the dragon’s chest.
The spheres detonated on impact, blowing massive gaping craters through the crimson scales.
But the dragon’s regeneration was absolute as the wounds closed instantly.
"If I find my way out of this prison," the dragon roared, unleashing a massive, sweeping torrent of crimson lightning that scorched the obsidian floor.
"I swear upon my mother’s rotting bones...
I will kill any human that I can see!
I will burn their cities to ash!"
"You will never leave this room!" Aeliana screamed back.
The dragon violently whipped its heavy spiked tail and Aeliana tried to dodge, but the spatial distortion of the lightning blast threw off her timing.
SMASH!
The massive tail connected cleanly with Aeliana’s torso.
Aeliana was hit violently into the air.
She was launched hundreds of feet into the dark sky with the wind violently knocking the breath from her lungs.
"Ugh!"
She soared upward with her body spinning helplessly as the dragon looked up, preparing a final massive blast of superheated fire to execute her mid-air.
Aeliana stabilized herself at the apex of her flight.
She looked down at the roaring beast with her green eyes turning as cold and unyielding as the void of space.
"If you ever threaten to hurt Lord Sy..." Aeliana whispered, her voice carrying an incredibly terrifying promise.
She spread her arms wide, drawing entirely upon the maximum output of the Genesis Rune as the ambient temperature of the entire pocket dimension violently plummeted.
’No...’ The Dragon shot forward heading toward Aeliana. ’You can’t!’
"No!"
She locked her gaze onto the dragon.
"...then I will murder you right here."
Aeliana clasped her hands together.
"LAND OF FROST!"
The spell detonated and contrary to what the dragon expected, it wasn’t a beam of ice.
It was a complete atmospheric rewrite.
A massive and violently expanding dome of frozen energy erupted from Aeliana’s position in the sky and slammed down onto the obsidian floor.
The entire world flash-froze in a microsecond as massive, towering glaciers of jagged blue ice violently erupted from the ground, entirely encasing the battlefield.
Dragons were fundamentally creatures of heat energy and due to their special biology, they were inherently weak to high-tier ice magic.
The Land of Frost slammed into the crimson dragon.
"AGHHHHHH!"

The beast shrieked in paralyzing agony as the absolute-zero temperature violently extinguished its internal flames, freezing its blood in its veins and locking its massive limbs in an unbreakable, towering prison of solid ice.
[Back Outside in the Deep Abyss.]
Silas stood before the jagged black pedestal.
His entire body was radiating a terrifying blinding aura of pure liquid gold mana.
The sovereign energy converged violently around the blade of his mythril sword, the heavy steel humming with a frequency that threatened to completely shatter the spatial fabric of the dungeon.
"What are you doing?!" the God’s voice shrieked from the ceiling, the sadistic joy completely replaced by genuine panicked terror.
Silas didn’t answer.
He raised the golden sword high above his head with the muscles in his arms bulging as he concentrated every single drop of his Gold Core’s maximum output into the tip of the blade.
"Stop!" Ititus complained frantically, his voice echoing rapidly.
"You fool!
You don’t understand the structure of that artifact!
If you break it, you’ll destabilize the entire lower quadrant!
Please, stop!"
Silas was absolutely not having it.
"I want my Hero back..."
He took a firm step back, gathered his full unsuppressed power, and slashed downward with all of his might.
The golden blade struck the dead center of the petrified amber eye.
CHINK!
For a microsecond, time seemed to completely stop then, a microscopic crack appeared on the surface of the amber.
The crack violently expanded, tearing into dozens of deep glowing fault lines across the entire artifact.

chapters.title: Chapter 183: A Dragon Joining Blessed Land
paragraphs: Before his eyes, the rotting body rapidly started shriveling, turning entirely to harmless grey dust and blowing away in the dungeon’s drafts.
Silas waved the thick smoke away from his face with his golden eyes desperately searching the epicenter of the explosion.
As the dust settled, Silas saw her.
Standing in the center of the clearing, surrounded by falling ash, was Aeli. She was brushing the dust off her white robes, completely without harm.
Silas let out a sigh of relief with his tense shoulders finally dropping.
"Aeli," Silas breathed out, stepping forward.
However, as the dust cleared further, Silas stopped dead in his tracks as standing right next to Aeli in the ash... was another girl.
She was stark naked.
Her skin was flawlessly pale with her long hair was a vibrant,fiery crimson, and protruding from her lower back were two small incredibly cute crimson dragon wings.

The dragon girl had been forcefully expelled from the artifact alongside Aeliana, her massive draconic form violently reverting to her humanoid state due to the extreme magical exhaustion of the Land of Frost.
Upon seeing him approach, the naked dragon girl didn’t cover herself.
She crossed her arms under her breasts and visibly cringed her face in deep disgust as Aeliana gave her the robe she was wearing over her dress.
She looked Silas up and down, taking in his dusty trench coat and exhausted posture.

"This is the saintly human you bragged about?" the dragon girl asked Aeliana, her voice dripping with disappointment. "He did not even look good at all... He is quite average compared to my glorious form."
THWACK!
Aeliana didn’t hesitate. She immediately chopped the dragon girl directly on the top of the head with the edge of her hand.
"Ow!" the girl complained loudly, rubbing her head and pouting.
Silas blinked, completely bewildered by the bizarre dispute currently happening in the middle of a dungeon.
"Aeli... who is this?"
Aeliana turned to Silas, offering a polite, perfectly professional bow.
"Lord Sy," Aeliana introduced her, gesturing to the pouting girl. "This is Talira and she is a dragon."
Silas stared at the naked girl with the small wings. "Okay... why is she here?"
Aeliana smiled brightly. "She told me that she was very interested in joining the Blessed Land and she hates humans as well."
Silas raised an eyebrow, he was very skeptical.
An ancient dragon who hates humans just randomly decided to join his human territory after a fight?
"And as for how she got to be so interested in our territory..." Aeliana added smoothly.
Aeliana looked at Silas and offered a completely devastating, adorable little wink.
"I just beat it into her."
Standing next to the Elf, the naked Dragon girl visibly trembled.
Talira wrapped her arms around herself, terrified.
Dragons were fundamentally weak to high-tier ice magic... and this smiling polite elven woman was just able to spam Land of Frost like it was a baseline cantrip?
’She’s a monster!’ Talira thought, completely traumatized by the sheer brutality of Aeliana’s combat capabilities.
Joining the human’s territory was the only logical choice for survival!
However Talira calmed down.
She stood directly in the center of the settling grey ash with her pale arms crossed tightly over her bare chest as Aeliana’s white spider-silk cloak fluttered around her shoulders.
She narrowed her glowing red eyes, critically reviewing Silas from head to toe in her mind.
He was absolutely not like how the ancient stories described Humans at all.

Her rotting mother, in the suffocating darkness of the spatial prison, had constantly drilled it into her head that Humans were universally hideous, deformed goblins with weak fragile bodies and cowardly souls.
But as Talira looked at the dark-haired Lord standing before her, she had to begrudgingly admit the truth.
He was undeniably handsome.
His jawline was sharp and his body was muscled beneath his dusty trench coat, and those glowing golden-ringed eyes carried a heavy weight that demanded respect.
But Talira didn’t care about that.
Or rather, out of draconic pride, she wouldn’t tell that to his face. She was a proud dragon, and she had just been forcefully humiliated by his subordinate.

"I am freezing!" Talira complained loudly, shivering and wrapping the pale silk cloak tighter around herself. "Is this how your so-called ’saintly’ Lord treats his guests? Letting them freeze in the dark without a single scale of armor?!"
Silas let out a heavy sigh, rubbing the bridge of his nose.
"I literally just saved your life by shattering a Mythic artifact," Silas pointed out flatly. "And Aeliana already gave you her cloak so stop complaining before you catch a cold."
Aeliana stepped forward, placing a gentle, reassuring hand on Talira’s shoulder.
"Listen to me carefully, Talira," Aeliana said. "Lord Sy is incredibly generous. However, there are rules if you wish to stand by his side."
Talira twitched her small crimson wings, sticking her chin up. "I don’t take orders from—"
Aeliana’s grip on her shoulder tightened just enough to let a fraction of frost nip at the dragon’s collarbone.

"Do not insult him," Aeliana interrupted with her green eyes locking onto the dragon’s red ones with a sweet terrifying smile. "Do not raise your voice at him. And if you ever try to bite him... I will personally freeze your tail off and use it as a coat rack. Do we have an understanding?"
Talira swallowed hard, the residual paralyzing terror of the Frozen World flashing brightly in her mind as her defensive posturing instantly dissolved into the grey ash.
"I... I understand," Talira mumbled, looking down at the dirt and wrapping the cloak tighter around herself.
"Alright," Silas interrupted, stepping forward and looking directly down at the shivering dragon girl. "Let’s make this official. You told Aeliana you want to join my territory?"
Talira avoided his piercing golden gaze.
She remembered the promise of endless libraries and a sanctuary where she wouldn’t be hunted for her scales.
Her mother had warned her to avoid humans at all costs, but hearing Aeliana speak of such a saintly devoted ruler had ignited a deep stubborn curiosity within her ancient heart.
She wanted to stay with this Human... if only to prove to herself that he was not as perfect as Aeliana made him seem.
"Yes," Talira agreed with her voice dropping into a begrudging and slightly embarrassed mumble. "I suppose your territory is acceptable."
"Good. Stay still," Silas commanded.
Silas knew he couldn’t just leave her here in the deepest layer of a collapsing dungeon.
He had to formally make her a Hero of his faction right now to secure her existence before another Lord decided to.
He stepped closer and brought his calloused right hand up toward her face.
Talira flinched instinctively with her crimson wings flaring out.
"What are you doing to me?!" she questioned sharply.
Silas didn’t answer. He simply reached out and firmly tapped his index finger directly against the center of her forehead.
FWOOSH!
A blinding warm golden light instantly flooded from Silas’s fingertip, washing entirely over Talira.
The energy penetrated her pale skin, aggressively flooding her damaged core and mapping her draconic mana pathways directly into the Blessed Land territory.
A translucent blue tab immediately materialized in front of Silas’s face.
[The Ancient Crimson Dragon ’Talira’ has been successfully tethered.]
[Talira has been officially registered as a Hero of the ’Blessed Land’ Territory.]
[Initiating automated spatial recall to Blessed Land...]
Before anybody could even react to the notification, the golden light completely enveloped the dragon girl.
VWOOP!
Talira vanished into thin air, instantly teleported completely out of the collapsing dungeon and sent safely over to the fortified territory.
Aeliana blinked, staring at the empty space where the dragon had just been standing. She turned to Silas with a flicker of concern crossing her flawless features.
"Lord Sy... is she—?"
"She’s safe," Silas assured Aeli, dismissing the system tab with a wave of his hand. "She is in the territory so it’s up to Elu and the others."
Before they could share a moment of relief, the very fabric of the dungeon violently protested.
KRA-KRA-KRA-THOOM!
Massive cracks violently spread across the black obsidian floor of the Lower Dungeon, urging them to move immediately.
The structural integrity of the Abyss, severely compromised by Silas shattering the Tier 4 artifact and the mother dragon bursting through the ceiling, was finally giving out.
The ancient groaning sound of billions of tons of bedrock shifting echoed through the dark.
"We need to move. Now," Silas commanded.
Above them, a massive section of the cavern wall violently broke apart, sending car-sized boulders of solid black stone plummeting down toward their position.
Silas and Aeliana looked at each other and they didn’t need to speak.
Silas closed the distance instantly. He swept Aeliana directly into his muscular arms, lifting her off her feet in a tight, secure bridal carry.
"Promise me you won’t dive into unidentified Mythic artifacts by yourself again," Silas said with his voice sounding serious as he looked down at her. "No more reckless stuff."
Aeliana’s pale cheeks immediately flushed a brilliant vibrant shade of pink.
Being held so securely against his broad chest completely scrambled her usually perfect composure.
"I... I promise, My Lord," Aeliana stuttered softly, nodding her head against his shoulder.
Then, despite the chaos of the collapsing cavern around them, Aeliana looked up with a completely adorable shy smile crossing her lips.
"Earlier," Silas whispered with his voice barely audible over the roaring destruction. "You told me that I hadn’t held you to sleep before... right?"
She blushed deeper, burying her face into his trench coat.
CRASH! BOOM!
Massive rocks came raining down around them, completely pulverizing the black sand floor.
The entire cavern ceiling began violently caving in, preparing to crush everything in the Abyss into paste.
Silas let out a genuine breathless laugh, tightening his grip on her waist.
"I’ll hold you tonight," Silas promised her.
He didn’t hesitate for another second.

He channeled a massive explosive burst of his remaining Gold Core mana directly into his boots and violently shot upward out of the collapsing entrance, riding the shockwave of the falling debris toward the upper layers.
Over in the completely separated Right Tunnel, chaos reigned.
Seraphina was fighting for her literal survival.
She was violently swinging her curved dagger in wide desperate arcs, the steel blade blooming in roaring condensed bursts of superheated flames.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH
The tunnel that Silas had sworn was a "safe empty corridor" was currently swarming with dozens of massive eight-foot-tall scorpions forged entirely from compressed abrasive black desert glass.
’You lying, commoner rat!’ Seraphina screamed internally, her vocal cords still completely paralyzed by the metallic spider clamp digging into her carotid artery.
She parried a heavy glass stinger, slicing the appendage off with a burst of fire.
Her chest heaved, her lungs burning as she fought through the brutal 50% physical and magical stat suppression of the cursed artifact.
But despite the imminent danger surrounding her, she couldn’t seem to get the arrogant frustratingly handsome face of Silas Graves out of her head at all.

’He set me up!’ she thought frantically, ducking under a snapping claw. ’He saw me naked behind that dune, humiliated me, and then sent me down this death trap to die so I couldn’t report him to my father!’
A massive glass scorpion lunged from the shadows of the cavern ceiling, pinning her against the stone wall. The beast raised its dripping stinger, aiming directly for her heart.

Seraphina’s eyes went wide. Pure survival instinct overrode her aristocratic training as she gritted her teeth and violently pushed her suppressed Lord core far beyond its safety limits, drawing upon every single drop of latent fire mana in her blood.
FWOOSH!
A catastrophic explosion of white-hot thermal energy erupted from her entire body with the heat was so intense that the stone wall behind her melted into slag.
Clamped tightly to her neck, the metallic spider artifact absorbed the astronomical temperature spike.
The runic structure of the collar overloaded as the metal glowed bright white, hissed violently, and was instantly incinerated into a harmless shower of falling grey ash!
Her vocal cords were instantly liberated from the suppression effect.
"I AM GOING TO FLAY YOU ALIVE, SILAS GRAVES!" Seraphina screamed at the top of her lungs with her voice echoing down the entire length of the dark tunnel with murderous rage.
She violently complained, swinging her flaming dagger like a spinning buzzsaw.
SHWK! SHWK! SHWK!
The superheated steel sliced cleanly through the armored carapaces of three advancing scorpions, melting the black glass into bubbling pools of molten slag.
A fourth beast lunged with its pincers snapping for her waist.
Seraphina pivoted on her heel, driving the burning dagger straight through the center of its head with a sickening sound.
CRUNCH!
She ripped the blade free, kicking the shattered carcass aside as she gasped for air.
"Fu... Fuck..."
More monsters poured from the cracks in the walls.
They were endless. Scorpions with glowing violet eyes scrambled over the melted remains of their brethren with their pincers clicking in a terrifying crescendo.
Seraphina did not back down.
Her crimson aura flared like a dying star, illuminating the pitch-black tunnel in blinding shades of orange and gold.
"Come on then!" she roared, leaping forward.
