"Is this how your so-called ’saintly’ Lord treats his guests?
Letting them freeze in the dark without a single scale of armor?!"
Silas let out a heavy sigh, rubbing the bridge of his nose.
"I literally just saved your life by shattering a Mythic artifact," Silas pointed out flatly.
"And Aeliana already gave you her cloak so stop complaining before you catch a cold."
Aeliana stepped forward, placing a gentle, reassuring hand on Talira’s shoulder.
"Listen to me carefully, Talira," Aeliana said.
"Lord Sy is incredibly generous.
However, there are rules if you wish to stand by his side."
Talira twitched her small crimson wings, sticking her chin up.
"I don’t take orders from—"
Aeliana’s grip on her shoulder tightened just enough to let a fraction of frost nip at the dragon’s collarbone.
"Do not insult him," Aeliana interrupted with her green eyes locking onto the dragon’s red ones with a sweet terrifying smile.
"Do not raise your voice at him.
And if you ever try to bite him...
I will personally freeze your tail off and use it as a coat rack.
Do we have an understanding?"
Talira swallowed hard, the residual paralyzing terror of the Frozen World flashing brightly in her mind as her defensive posturing instantly dissolved into the grey ash.
I understand," Talira mumbled, looking down at the dirt and wrapping the cloak tighter around herself.
"Alright," Silas interrupted, stepping forward and looking directly down at the shivering dragon girl.
"Let’s make this official.
You told Aeliana you want to join my territory?"
Talira avoided his piercing golden gaze.
She remembered the promise of endless libraries and a sanctuary where she wouldn’t be hunted for her scales.
Her mother had warned her to avoid humans at all costs, but hearing Aeliana speak of such a saintly devoted ruler had ignited a deep stubborn curiosity within her ancient heart.
She wanted to stay with this Human... if only to prove to herself that he was not as perfect as Aeliana made him seem.
"Yes," Talira agreed with her voice dropping into a begrudging and slightly embarrassed mumble.
"I suppose your territory is acceptable."
"Good.
Stay still," Silas commanded.
Silas knew he couldn’t just leave her here in the deepest layer of a collapsing dungeon.
He had to formally make her a Hero of his faction right now to secure her existence before another Lord decided to.
He stepped closer and brought his calloused right hand up toward her face.
Talira flinched instinctively with her crimson wings flaring out.
"What are you doing to me?!" she questioned sharply.
Silas didn’t answer.
He simply reached out and firmly tapped his index finger directly against the center of her forehead.
FWOOSH!
A blinding warm golden light instantly flooded from Silas’s fingertip, washing entirely over Talira.
The energy penetrated her pale skin, aggressively flooding her damaged core and mapping her draconic mana pathways directly into the Blessed Land territory.
A translucent blue tab immediately materialized in front of Silas’s face.
[The Ancient Crimson Dragon ’Talira’ has been successfully tethered.]
[Talira has been officially registered as a Hero of the ’Blessed Land’ Territory.]
[Initiating automated spatial recall to Blessed Land...]
Before anybody could even react to the notification, the golden light completely enveloped the dragon girl.
VWOOP!
Talira vanished into thin air, instantly teleported completely out of the collapsing dungeon and sent safely over to the fortified territory.
Aeliana blinked, staring at the empty space where the dragon had just been standing.
She turned to Silas with a flicker of concern crossing her flawless features.
"Lord Sy... is she—?"
"She’s safe," Silas assured Aeli, dismissing the system tab with a wave of his hand.
"She is in the territory so it’s up to Elu and the others."
Before they could share a moment of relief, the very fabric of the dungeon violently protested.
KRA-KRA-KRA-THOOM!
Massive cracks violently spread across the black obsidian floor of the Lower Dungeon, urging them to move immediately.
The structural integrity of the Abyss, severely compromised by Silas shattering the Tier 4 artifact and the mother dragon bursting through the ceiling, was finally giving out.
The ancient groaning sound of billions of tons of bedrock shifting echoed through the dark.
"We need to move.
Now," Silas commanded.
Above them, a massive section of the cavern wall violently broke apart, sending car-sized boulders of solid black stone plummeting down toward their position.
Silas and Aeliana looked at each other and they didn’t need to speak.
Silas closed the distance instantly.
He swept Aeliana directly into his muscular arms, lifting her off her feet in a tight, secure bridal carry.
"Promise me you won’t dive into unidentified Mythic artifacts by yourself again," Silas said with his voice sounding serious as he looked down at her.
"No more reckless stuff."
Aeliana’s pale cheeks immediately flushed a brilliant vibrant shade of pink.
Being held so securely against his broad chest completely scrambled her usually perfect composure.
I promise, My Lord," Aeliana stuttered softly, nodding her head against his shoulder.
Then, despite the chaos of the collapsing cavern around them, Aeliana looked up with a completely adorable shy smile crossing her lips.
"Earlier," Silas whispered with his voice barely audible over the roaring destruction.
"You told me that I hadn’t held you to sleep before... right?"
She blushed deeper, burying her face into his trench coat.
CRASH!
BOOM!
Massive rocks came raining down around them, completely pulverizing the black sand floor.
The entire cavern ceiling began violently caving in, preparing to crush everything in the Abyss into paste.
Silas let out a genuine breathless laugh, tightening his grip on her waist.
"I’ll hold you tonight," Silas promised her.
He didn’t hesitate for another second.

He channeled a massive explosive burst of his remaining Gold Core mana directly into his boots and violently shot upward out of the collapsing entrance, riding the shockwave of the falling debris toward the upper layers.
Over in the completely separated Right Tunnel, chaos reigned.
Seraphina was fighting for her literal survival.
She was violently swinging her curved dagger in wide desperate arcs, the steel blade blooming in roaring condensed bursts of superheated flames.
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH
The tunnel that Silas had sworn was a "safe empty corridor" was currently swarming with dozens of massive eight-foot-tall scorpions forged entirely from compressed abrasive black desert glass.
’You lying, commoner rat!’ Seraphina screamed internally, her vocal cords still completely paralyzed by the metallic spider clamp digging into her carotid artery.
She parried a heavy glass stinger, slicing the appendage off with a burst of fire.
Her chest heaved, her lungs burning as she fought through the brutal 50% physical and magical stat suppression of the cursed artifact.
But despite the imminent danger surrounding her, she couldn’t seem to get the arrogant frustratingly handsome face of Silas Graves out of her head at all.

’He set me up!’ she thought frantically, ducking under a snapping claw. ’He saw me naked behind that dune, humiliated me, and then sent me down this death trap to die so I couldn’t report him to my father!’
A massive glass scorpion lunged from the shadows of the cavern ceiling, pinning her against the stone wall.
The beast raised its dripping stinger, aiming directly for her heart.
Seraphina’s eyes went wide.

Pure survival instinct overrode her aristocratic training as she gritted her teeth and violently pushed her suppressed Lord core far beyond its safety limits, drawing upon every single drop of latent fire mana in her blood.
FWOOSH!
A catastrophic explosion of white-hot thermal energy erupted from her entire body with the heat was so intense that the stone wall behind her melted into slag.
Clamped tightly to her neck, the metallic spider artifact absorbed the astronomical temperature spike.
The runic structure of the collar overloaded as the metal glowed bright white, hissed violently, and was instantly incinerated into a harmless shower of falling grey ash!
Her vocal cords were instantly liberated from the suppression effect.
"I AM GOING TO FLAY YOU ALIVE, SILAS GRAVES!" Seraphina screamed at the top of her lungs with her voice echoing down the entire length of the dark tunnel with murderous rage.
She violently complained, swinging her flaming dagger like a spinning buzzsaw.
SHWK!
SHWK!
SHWK!
The superheated steel sliced cleanly through the armored carapaces of three advancing scorpions, melting the black glass into bubbling pools of molten slag.
A fourth beast lunged with its pincers snapping for her waist.
Seraphina pivoted on her heel, driving the burning dagger straight through the center of its head with a sickening sound.
CRUNCH!
She ripped the blade free, kicking the shattered carcass aside as she gasped for air.
Fuck..."
More monsters poured from the cracks in the walls.
They were endless.
Scorpions with glowing violet eyes scrambled over the melted remains of their brethren with their pincers clicking in a terrifying crescendo.
Seraphina did not back down.
Her crimson aura flared like a dying star, illuminating the pitch-black tunnel in blinding shades of orange and gold.
"Come on then!" she roared, leaping forward.

chapters.title: Chapter 184: Thieving Elf
paragraphs: She spun in mid-air with her dagger leaving a trailing arc of fire that decapitated two scorpions simultaneously.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
She landed heavily, her boots kicking up molten glass, and thrust her palm forward.
A concentrated blast of fire erupted from her empty hand, incinerating a charging beast into a pile of smoking ash.
"Haah! Get that fuckers!"
But the exertion of fighting through the lingering fatigue of the suppression collar was catching up to her.
Her breath came in ragged painful gasps and her limbs felt as heavy as lead.
An eight-foot scorpion lunged from her blind spot on the right.
"Fuck!"
She raised her dagger to parry, but the impact of the heavy glass pincer violently knocked the weapon from her grip.
The dagger clattered across the stone floor, sliding out of reach.
"No!" she gasped.
The beast reared back with its razor-sharp stinger descending toward her unprotected throat but her moment of final resistance was cut short by the environment itself.
KRA-KRA-THOOM!
The massive tectonic chain reaction from Silas shattering the Tier 4 Eye in the Lower Abyss finally reached her isolated right corridor.
The bedrock floor directly beneath her heavy boots violently fractured into spiderwebs.
The stone walls tore apart, the ceiling caved in, and the ground simply dropped out from under her feet.
"No!" Seraphina shrieked as she lost her footing, plummeting helplessly into the suffocating darkness of a bottomless chasm alongside the screeching glass monsters.
She closed her eyes, desperately trying to conjure a thermal updraft to slow her descent, but her mana reserves were completely drained from destroying the collar and incinerating the horde.
The wind roared in her ears as she fell through the black void, debris and jagged glass showering around her.
Suddenly, a dark blur shot down from the collapsing cavern above her at terrifying velocity.
Before Seraphina could even scream, strong calloused hands grabbed her out of the free-fall, effortlessly snatching her out of the air and pulling her securely against a broad armored chest.
"You better not die on me," a calm voice muttered right next to her ear.
Seraphina snapped her fiery red eyes open.
It was Silas.

The dark-haired Lord had bounded across the falling debris to rescue her but because he already had Aeliana clinging securely to his back with her arms wrapped around his neck, Silas had to improvise his carrying mechanics to transport two grown women out of a collapsing pit.

To maintain his physical balance and secure her weight against the brutal G-forces, Silas had his right arm wrapped around her waist, while his left hand was clamped firmly, securely, and unapologetically directly under Seraphina’s ass.
Seraphina’s entire face instantly flushed a violent blinding shade of crimson that completely rivaled her hair.
"Y-you—!"
Before she could even utter an insult, Silas violently kicked off a falling boulder.
BANG! BANG! BANG!
He shot upward through the collapsing chasm like a rocket with his boots physically bouncing off massive, falling chunks of bedrock like stepping stones.
He navigated the vertical destruction with flawless agility, rapidly ascending toward the sunlight streaming from the upper layers.
Every time his boots slammed against a falling rock, the impact jolted through his frame, forcing his grip to tighten around Seraphina to prevent her from slipping out of his grasp.
Seraphina blushed so hard she felt physically dizzy.

She was completely paralyzed by the proximity to the man who had already seen her lower half hours prior, and who was currently holding her firmly by her rear end as they bounded up a collapsing chasm!
’Why does this keep happening to me...?’
She could feel the heat radiating from his chest, the thumping of his heart, and the strength in his arm as he fought gravity itself to keep them both alive.
"Let go of me, you brute!" she tried to protest, her voice muffled against his collarbone, but her arms instinctively wrapped around his broad shoulders to hold on for dear life.
"If I let go, you become desert pavement, Seraphina! Stop squirming!" Silas barked back, his eyes tracking a massive twenty-ton slab of ceiling falling directly toward them.
He didn’t dodge around it.
He planted his right boot against a falling pillar, compressed his mana into his calf, and launched himself directly at the descending slab.
As they closed the distance, Silas thrust his right knee upward, smashing it directly into the center of the falling stone.
KRA-CRASH!
The twenty-ton boulder violently shattered into thousands of harmless fragments, clearing a vertical path to the surface.
’He can do that...?’ Seraphina thought and Silas on the other hand sweatdropped.
’I hope she doesn’t notice...’

Silas carried them both completely to safety. With a final explosive kick against a protruding ledge, he burst through the remaining layer of upper bedrock, landing on the solid, baked surface of the Secret Realm’s desert layer.

They were back outside. Massive, gaping holes in the ice cavern ceilings above them were exposing the harsh amber sun, and continuous heavy streams of hot desert sand were actively pouring down through the fractures into the destroyed dungeon below.
The moment Silas’s boots stabilized on the solid sand, Seraphina violently threw herself out of his grip.

She scrambled backward across the dirt with her face burning so hot it was practically emitting steam and her hands flying instinctively to cover her chest as she glared at him with wide horrified eyes.

"You... you unrepentant pervert!" Seraphina insulted him loudly, her voice cracking with embarrassment as she pointed a trembling finger at his nose. "Don’t ever touch me again! Don’t look at me! I hate you!"
She didn’t give him a single second to explain or apologize.

Seraph instantly channeled her remaining fire mana into the soles of her boots and shot straight up out of the crater, rocketing away across the desert dunes like a fleeing meteor with her face burning red.
Silas stood there in the sand with his trench coat covered in grey dungeon soot, watching her fly away toward the horizon.
He let out a long exhausted sigh, rubbing the back of his neck until it popped.
’Well,’ Silas thought pragmatically, brushing a layer of dust off his sleeves. ’Valerius is a big boy so he will be alright dealing with her when she lands. Let’s just get back to Aeli.’
He turned back toward Aeliana, who had slipped down from his back and was standing gracefully on the hot sand.
She looked in the direction Seraphina had fled, her pointed elven ears twitching with mild disapproval.
"She lacks emotional discipline, My Lord," Aeliana noted calmly, smoothing her white robes. "Should I have frozen her feet to teach her manners?"
"No, let her go," Silas chuckled tiredly. "We have enough problems on our hands. Let’s find a safe zone and assess what we actually gained from that hellhole."
Meanwhile, deep within the Far Left Tunnel, things were transpiring in an entirely different, highly lucrative manner.
Valerius was practically howling with victorious laughter as he surveyed the massive room he had just stumbled into.
"EHAHAHAHAHA!"
This specific side of the subterranean complex wasn’t being destroyed at all.
The violent spatial collapse initiated by Silas in the center had completely missed this isolated reinforced structural pocket.
It was a perfectly preserved chamber carved from polished white marble and it wasn’t a prison or a combat arena.
It was the actual storage treasury where the dead god Ititus had kept the confiscated goods from the ancient enemies he had defeated!
This was the exact source where all the real, high-density treasure signatures on their radar had been originating from!
Valerius and Mia stood in the center of the illuminated treasury, and they both laughed out loud in pure Lordly triumph.
Lining the polished marble walls were dozens of ornate stone pedestals, and resting upon every single one was a glowing, perfectly preserved magical artifact.

There were roughly thirty different items in here... ranging from humming spellbooks and enchanted rings to heavy mythril gauntlets and a quick system scan confirmed they were all solid, undeniably real Tier 2 to Tier 3 Sovereign treasures!
"We hit the motherlode!" Valerius cheered, his eyes shining with absolute greed as he rubbed his iron gauntlets together. "Not a single fake mirage in sight! We are going to clean this place out!"
He stepped toward the nearest pedestal with his boots clicking sharply against the marble floor.
Resting on the stone was a magnificent silver broadsword, its hilt wrapped in pristine blue dragon-leather, radiating a potent wind-affinity aura that made Valerius’s own core hum in resonance.
"Oh, you are a beauty," Valerius murmured, reaching his gauntleted hand out to claim the weapon.
VWOOP.
Suddenly, Aeliana appeared directly behind him in a blinding, instantaneous flash of blue starlight.
Valerius jumped, spinning around with his hand on his sword hilt. "By the gods... Elf! Don’t sneak up on me like that!"
Aeliana offered a brief polite nod, completely ignoring his startled reaction.
"Lord Sterling. I am glad to see you are alright. However, the lower structure has failed so we urgently need to leav—"
Aeliana paused mid-sentence.
Her glowing silver eyes drifted past Valerius’s shoulder, locking onto the thirty glowing Tier 2 artifacts lining the marble pedestals.
The starlight around her form flared brightly as she rapidly calculated the immense financial and military value of the room’s contents.
Valerius saw the exact moment her pupils dilated and his paranoia spiked to maximum.
He immediately stepped in front of the shelves, holding both of his armored arms out wide in a desperate attempt to block her view.
"Now hold on just a second!" Valerius tried to say, his voice rising in panic. "I found this room first! These belong to the me! You shouldn’t take—!"
But before he could even finish the word "them", Aeliana’s fierce devotion to Lord Silas’s territorial expansion completely overrode any concept of manners.
Aeliana blurred forward with terrifying speed.
WHOOSH!

Aeli completely bypassed Valerius’s guard with her pale hands moving like lightning as she aggressively snagged an entire armful of artifacts directly off the stone pedestals... sweeping at least fifteen glowing Tier 2 treasures into her arms in a single flawless motion.
She grabbed enchanted breastplates, runic daggers, utility rings, and even the silver wind-sword Valerius had been eyeing seconds prior.
"Hey! Put that back!" Valerius yelled, lunging forward to grab her wrist.
He grasped completely empty air.
"For Lord Sy," Aeliana stated completely deadpan, looking him dead in the eye with zero remorse.
VWOOP!
She teleported instantly, vanishing back to Silas’s side with half of the room’s priceless inventory before Valerius could even blink.

"YOU THIEVING ELF!" Valerius shouted at the empty air, his face turning bright red as he clutched his meticulously groomed blond hair in agony. "GRAVES! I am going to murder you and your entire household! I swear it upon my family crest!"
Sitting lazily on his armored shoulder, Mia chuckled warmly, resting her chin on her small hand as she mercilessly teased her Lord.

"You really should have been faster on the draw, My Lord," Mia smirked, thoroughly enjoying his financial suffering. "She cleanly outplayed you. While you were busy drooling over a sword, she treated this place like a free market."

"Shut up, Mia! She literally robbed us blind!" Valerius fumed, pacing back and forth in front of the half-empty pedestals. "That was fifteen Tier 2 artifacts! Do you know how much gold that represents in the auction houses?!"
"Enough to buy a small city," Mia yawned. "Which is exactly why you should stop whining and grab whatever is left before the ceiling crushes your skull."
As if on cue, Valerius’s tantrum was cut short by the environment itself.
KRA-THOOM!
The massive walls of the polished marble treasury suddenly began to violently shake.
The protective spatial ward covering the chamber flickered and died, emitting a high-pitched whine as the whole thing collapsed.
The high ceiling above them began to crack, massive fissures of black void tearing through the white stone as heavy chunks of marble showered down around them.
The chain-reaction collapse of the dungeon had finally reached their isolated wing.
"Damn it all!" Valerius cursed loudly.
He didn’t waste another second complaining.

He sprinted along the perimeter of the room, rapidly sweeping his gauntleted arms across the remaining pedestals, hastily shoving the remaining fifteen Tier 2 artifacts directly into his Lord inventory interface.
Rings, boots, belts, and shields vanished into his digital storage in a rapid succession of blue flashes.
A massive section of the marble floor collapsed directly behind him, revealing a bottomless black pit.
Valerius spotted a narrow glowing emergency exit tunnel collapsing at the rear of the chamber.
Channeling high-pressure green wind mana directly into his boots, Valerius violently hopped out of the crumbling treasury.
He pushed off the falling stones, riding the violent air currents through the collapsing tunnel while screaming curses at Silas Graves with every single bound.

"Graves! I am going to bill your territory for this!" Valerius roared as he shot up through the vertical shaft with his armor scraping against the narrowing stone walls before he violently burst out onto the surface sands.

"For Lord Sy," Aeliana stated completely deadpan, looking him dead in the eye with zero remorse.
VWOOP!
She teleported instantly, vanishing back to Silas’s side with half of the room’s priceless inventory before Valerius could even blink.
"YOU THIEVING ELF!" Valerius shouted at the empty air, his face turning bright red as he clutched his meticulously groomed blond hair in agony.
"GRAVES!
I am going to murder you and your entire household!
I swear it upon my family crest!"
Sitting lazily on his armored shoulder, Mia chuckled warmly, resting her chin on her small hand as she mercilessly teased her Lord.
"You really should have been faster on the draw, My Lord," Mia smirked, thoroughly enjoying his financial suffering.
"She cleanly outplayed you.
While you were busy drooling over a sword, she treated this place like a free market."
"Shut up, Mia!
She literally robbed us blind!" Valerius fumed, pacing back and forth in front of the half-empty pedestals.
"That was fifteen Tier 2 artifacts!
Do you know how much gold that represents in the auction houses?!"
"Enough to buy a small city," Mia yawned.
"Which is exactly why you should stop whining and grab whatever is left before the ceiling crushes your skull."
As if on cue, Valerius’s tantrum was cut short by the environment itself.
KRA-THOOM!
The massive walls of the polished marble treasury suddenly began to violently shake.
The protective spatial ward covering the chamber flickered and died, emitting a high-pitched whine as the whole thing collapsed.
The high ceiling above them began to crack, massive fissures of black void tearing through the white stone as heavy chunks of marble showered down around them.
The chain-reaction collapse of the dungeon had finally reached their isolated wing.
"Damn it all!" Valerius cursed loudly.
He didn’t waste another second complaining.

He sprinted along the perimeter of the room, rapidly sweeping his gauntleted arms across the remaining pedestals, hastily shoving the remaining fifteen Tier 2 artifacts directly into his Lord inventory interface.
Rings, boots, belts, and shields vanished into his digital storage in a rapid succession of blue flashes.
A massive section of the marble floor collapsed directly behind him, revealing a bottomless black pit.
Valerius spotted a narrow glowing emergency exit tunnel collapsing at the rear of the chamber.
Channeling high-pressure green wind mana directly into his boots, Valerius violently hopped out of the crumbling treasury.
He pushed off the falling stones, riding the violent air currents through the collapsing tunnel while screaming curses at Silas Graves with every single bound.
"Graves!

I am going to bill your territory for this!" Valerius roared as he shot up through the vertical shaft with his armor scraping against the narrowing stone walls before he violently burst out onto the surface sands.

chapters.title: Chapter 185: Wrong Place, Wrong Time
paragraphs: [That Night]
On the upper surface of the Secret Realm, far away from the collapsing sinkholes of the dungeon drop, the environment was as brutal as ever.
The deadly rain of razor-sharp desert glass was falling again in relentless, vertical sheets, accompanied by a cool howling gale that whipped wildly across the endless sand dunes.
Walking directly through the center of the lethal glass storm, completely unprotected by a magical dome, was Maya.
The young girl looked exhausted.
Her dark leather armor was scored with dozens of minor scratches from the ambient environment, and her face was pale with fatigue but she hadn’t stopped moving.
Trudging right beside her through the deep sand was her remaining companion... her Archer Hero.
The Archer was currently utilizing his mechanical right arm.
He held a long, heavy iron arrow in his mechanical grip and rapidly spun the projectile like a propeller.
He spun the arrow with such terrifying rotational velocity that it generated a high-pressure wind shield directly over their heads.
CLINK! CLINK! SHATTER!
The falling sheets of razor-sharp glass slammed into the spinning arrow shield, violently shattering into harmless clouds of fine white dust before they could even scratch Maya’s leather armor.
The metallic grinding of the mechanical arm was the only sound keeping the crushing isolation of the desert at bay.
Maya walked on her own two feet with her boots sinking into the wet sand as she bitterly cursed under her breath about the miserable hellscape of this Secret Realm drop.

"Stupid sand. Stupid dead god. Stupid glass rain," Maya muttered, kicking a hardened clump of dirt across the dunes. "I swear, if we don’t get at least three drops out of this raid, I am retiring to the coastal sectors and opening a bakery."
Unfortunately she couldn’t because she was now in a government contract... then, she paused at the crest of a high dune.
Through the grey distortion of the falling glass rain, she spotted something about three hundred yards away.

It was a massive smooth structure made of solid blue ice... the original shelter construct Mia had built hours ago and in the inside near the entrance with his dark trench coat billowing slightly in the cool wind, was Silas Graves.
Maya let out a genuine smile of profound relief.
She wasn’t alone anymore.
She raised her left wrist, tapping the glowing communication rune embedded in her leather tether band to contact the leader.

"Boss," Maya reported eagerly, her voice crackling through the static of the comms. "I’ve found him. I’ve found Si-Silas... He’s sitting alone at an ice shelter. Should I go meet him and establish a perimeter?"
A thousand miles away, sitting in the command tent of the Valoria camp, Elora Verinda’s cold voice responded immediately.

"Do not approach him alone, Maya," Elora commanded over the link, her tone sharp and urgent. "Transmit the exact spatial coordinates of his location to my tab immediately as the mana signatures in that sector are highly erratic."
Maya reached out her finger to tap the transmission confirmation rune on her glass screen.
However, before her fingertip could touch the interface, another voice cut cleanly through the howling ambient wind.
"That wouldn’t be alright."
Maya froze. Her blood ran completely cold as that voice didn’t come from her communication band.
It came from directly behind her.
She slowly turned her head and looked up.
Standing at the top of a towering, thirty-foot-tall sand construct directly overlooking Maya’s position, looking down with cold glowing purple eyes, was Harper.
The purple-haired Lord had tracked Maya through the storm.
Harper stood there in the glass rain, her leather armor soaked with her face lacking any sort of emotion.
The wind whipped her long purple hair around her shoulders like a storm cloud as she raised both of her pale hands toward the howling amber sky and her Lord core ignited with terrifying power.

Raw condensed purple electricity began violently sparking and surging down the length of her arms, crackling with so much voltage that the spinning arrow shield of Maya’s Archer began to erratically short-circuit with the mechanical arm grinding and sparking as the electromagnetic interference overwhelmed its runes.
"Lord Harper?!" Maya gasped, taking a stumbling step backward down the dune. "What are you doing?!"
Harper did not answer.

She did not chant her standard frontline Fulgur Strike as she tapped directly into her second devastating spell she knew with her silhouette illuminating the darkened desert with blinding violet light.
"Sovereign’s Judgment..." Harper spoke, her voice vibrating with pure thunder that shook the sand beneath Maya’s boots.
She brought her hands down, pointing two fingers directly at Maya’s chest.
"...Empress Thunder."
The amber sky above the desert violently tore open.
A cataclysmic column of pure white-hot lightning descended from the heavens, completely annihilating the falling glass rain in its path.

All Maya could see after that was an explosion of electrical energy striking the earth directly where she stood, instantly followed by the deafening roar of thunder that cracked the very foundation of the ground below her.
BOOOOOOOOMMMMMM!
The deafening apocalyptic roar of thunder finally began to recede, rolling across the endless desert wasteland in a series of deep tectonic tremors that physically vibrated the ambient dust.
The harsh amber sky, momentarily torn apart by the blinding white flash of the Empress Thunder execution, slowly stitched itself back together.
Where the cataclysmic pillar of raw electricity had struck the earth, the landscape had been completely rewritten.
Massive towering sand dunes had been instantly vaporized, leaving behind a glowing crater of superheated, molten glass that hissed violently against the cool wind.
As the thick acrid smoke of burnt ozone slowly cleared, Harper stood perfectly still at the peak of her towering sand construct.
Her purple eyes, crackling with condensed electrical mana, narrowed as she stared through the haze.
At the far edge of the blast radius, hundreds of yards away, two figures slowly staggered to their feet. It was Maya and her remaining Archer Hero.
They were still alive.
The Archer’s specialized mechanical right arm was completely charred, emitting thick plumes of black smoke and erratic, dying sparks as it failed.

He had spun his iron arrow just fast enough, and just hard enough, to generate a kinetic vacuum shield that deflected the worst of the terminal voltage, saving his Lord’s life by a fraction of a microsecond.
Harper watched them limping away into the punishing glass storm and she didn’t pursue them.
She let out a long deeply exhausted sigh with her pale shoulders slumping slightly.
The mana expenditure of calling down natural lightning had severely drained her Lord core.
’That’s according to plan...’
She stepped off the towering sand pillar, allowing gravity to take her as she dropped down thirty feet, her leather boots hitting the baked desert floor with a soft sound.
As she landed, her eyes caught a pulsing blue light half-buried in the soot.
It was Maya’s severed communication band.
It had been blown off her wrist by the concussive shockwave of the lightning strike and landed directly at Harper’s feet.
Harper crouched down smoothly, her purple hair falling over her shoulder as she picked up the glowing leather band.
From the tiny, cracked communication crystal embedded in the center, Elora Verinda’s cold voice crackled through the static.

"Maya?" Elora’s voice demanded with her voice uncharacteristically tense. "Report your status immediately. What was that sound? The atmospheric pressure in your sector just violently spiked. Do you have a visual on Graves?"
Harper brought the cracked crystal close to her pale lips.
A slow and possessive smile curved across her face.

"Silas Graves belongs to me," Harper whispered into the comms and before the Valoria City Lord’s daughter could even attempt to process or respond to that completely unhinged statement, Harper closed her fist.
CRUNCH!

She squeezed her hand, utilizing a burst of static electricity to completely pulverize the communication crystal into a handful of useless, sparking dust. She let the debris fall from her fingers with the wind immediately carrying it away.
Harper turned her back on the crater, adjusting the collar of her soaked leather armor.
Her purple eyes locked onto the distant, perfectly smooth structure of solid blue ice barely visible through the raging glass storm.
Without another word, she began walking toward the ice construct.
[Inside the Ice Construct.]
The atmosphere was completely, starkly different from the apocalyptic hellscape outside.
The thick, magically reinforced walls of solid blue ice completely blocked out the howling wind and the endless metallic clatter of the razor-sharp glass rain.
It was freezing, yes, but the ambient mana provided a protective calm.
Silas let out a heavy, tired sigh, adjusting his posture slightly to keep the blood flowing to his legs.
He was currently seated flat on the hard ice floor, completely pinned down by two exhausted immortals.
Aeliana had her head resting softly and securely on his left lap, her flawless face buried into the fabric of his dark trench coat as she slept peacefully.
On his right lap, Mia had her small head completely sprawled across his thigh, softly snoring with a tiny bubble of spit expanding and contracting rhythmically from her lips.
Across the small, illuminated cavern space, Valerius was sitting with his back against the ice wall, aggressively polishing his mythril sword and glaring at Silas.
KRA-THOOM!
A massive muffled boom suddenly shuddered through the solid ice walls of the shelter and the entire cavern vibrated, sending a shower of loose frost cascading from the ceiling.
Silas and Valerius both flinched with their combat instincts instantly flaring as they looked toward the entrance.
They waited for a breach, but nothing followed the explosion. It was just the continued, muted howling of the storm.

"A heavy detonation," Valerius muttered, his eyes narrowing as he analyzed the lingering vibrations. "That’s a high-tier elemental discharge... It’s so high that it might be an artifact so that means—"
"Lords are fighting in the distance," Silas agreed softly, careful not to raise his voice.
He looked down at the two white-haired elves completely draped across his lap.
Neither Aeliana nor Mia had even twitched.
They were sleeping completely through the shockwave of a high-tier spell.
Silas smirked, shaking his head. "And these two are completely dead to the world... what incredible situational awareness."
Valerius scoffed loudly, sliding his polishing rag down the steel of his blade.

"Do not attempt to change the subject, Graves," Valerius complained bitterly, pointing his sword directly at Silas. "I am still furious. I found that perfectly preserved marble treasury first! I cleared the entrance! And your little Elf completely bypassed my guard, snagged all of the high-tier treasures right off the pedestals, and teleported away! It was highway robbery!"
Silas sighed with a genuine unapologetic smirk crossing his face.
He slowly reached out, placing his calloused hand firmly onto Valerius’s armored shoulder.

"Valerius," Silas said. "In the Sovereign Realm, it is finders keepers. She secured the assets faster than you did. But... thanks for scouting out the treasures, friend. Your contribution to my territory’s economy is deeply appreciated."
Valerius’s noble face instantly flushed a shade of furious pink. His cheeks heated up a bit as he aggressively pulled his shoulder away from Silas’s grasp, scowling deeply.
"I am not your friend, and I did not scout them for you!" Valerius hissed, violently sheathing his sword with a sharp sound.
CLANG!
He crossed his heavy iron gauntlets over his chest plate, looking away for a moment before his expression changed into one far more serious.
"Speaking of consequences," Valerius muttered, leaning forward slightly. "You saw Seraphina completely naked earlier today, right?"
Silas’s smirk vanished instantly. He rubbed the bridge of his nose, the headache of the impending political fallout returning in full force.
"I only saw the lower half..." Silas corrected him quietly, though he knew it made zero difference to the nobles.

"It doesn’t matter what percentage of her flesh you saw, you fool," Valerius warned, his voice dropping into a serious whisper. "I’m sure you know this already, but her father is a World Council Magistrate. He holds direct administrative authority over three different coastal sectors and commands a private army of high-tier Lords. He is very, very influential. When we return to the City, Seraphina is going to scream for your execution."
Silas let out a long sigh, resting his head back against the cold ice wall.

"I know," Silas admitted, his golden-ringed eyes staring at the ceiling as he mathematically calculated his odds of survival against a Magistrate’s hit squad. "I’m currently wondering how the hell I am going to avoid any sort of legal or physical trouble from this."

chapters.title: Chapter 186: Harper [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Valerius watched the dark-haired Lord for a long moment.
Despite the theft of the artifacts and despite the constant bickering, Valerius felt a strange sense of respect for the man.
Valerius looked away with his cheeks blushing slightly again as he faced sideways toward the ice wall.

"Well," Valerius murmured quietly, picking at a speck of frost on his gauntlet. "If she actually decides to press formal charges with the Council... I will step in. I will try as much as possible to push the charges down as I have enough political capital in the world to delay an execution warrant."
Silas blinked in genuine surprise. He looked at the gold-armored Lord, a slow teasing smile creeping back onto his face.

"Oh?" Silas teased, raising a highly skeptical eyebrow. "And why would the great Lord Valerius Sterling risk his impeccable political standing to defend a slum-born commoner who just robbed him blind?"
Valerius’s face burned brighter. H
e scowled, refusing to look Silas in the eye.
"Because we’re frie—"
THUD!
The heavy, distinct sound of a body collapsing against the exterior ice wall right near the entrance instantly shattered the quiet atmosphere of the cavern.
Silas’s golden eyes snapped toward the tunnel entrance.
He didn’t hesitate.

He carefully shifted his legs, gently lifting Aeliana’s head and placing it softly onto the ice floor, then doing the exact same with Mia then he stood up silently, drawing his mythril longsword in a fluid noiseless motion.
Valerius was already on his feet, his green aura flaring to life.
Both Lords advanced forward down the short, curved entry tunnel with their backs pressed against the freezing walls as they approached the howling opening.
Standing just outside the entrance, completely exposed to the apocalyptic environment, was Harper.
She looked pathetic.
The lethal razor-sharp glass rain was actively bouncing off her leather armor and piercing the unprotected fabric of her clothes, drawing dozens of tiny bloody scratches across her pale skin.
She was shivering violently, using one trembling hand to cover a massive strategically placed rip in her shirt that exposed her cleavage to the biting wind.

"Please!" Harper cried out over the howling gale, her purple eyes wide and filled with desperate, brimming tears as she looked at the two Lords standing in the threshold. "Please, let me in! Allow me to stay inside with you!"
She fell to her knees in the sand, the glass actively cutting into her legs.
"I don’t have anywhere else to stay!" Harper begged, her voice cracking pitifully. "My shelter was destroyed! Please, I’m freezing!"
Silas stood in the entrance with his golden-ringed eyes looking down at her shivering, bleeding form.
He didn’t feel a single ounce of pity.

Silas analyzed the angle of her ripped shirt, the specific positioning of her posture, and the fact that someone with lightning magic could easily generate enough ambient thermal heat to keep herself warm.
It seemed like a fabricated performance.
"No," Silas flatly refused.
"Absolutely not," Valerius agreed immediately from Silas’s flank, his hand resting on his sword. "Find your own rock to hide under, Harper."
Silas didn’t waste time arguing with the shivering girl. He stepped fully into the threshold, raising his left hand toward the desert floor.
He tapped directly into his Gold Core, pushing his mana outward.

He utilized high-tier water magic, forcibly drawing massive volumes of ambient moisture directly from the deep water tables beneath the sand, bringing a torrential geyser of heavy water rushing up to the surface right at the cavern entrance.
"Ice Transformation," Silas commanded coldly.
KRKKKKKK!
The heavy water violently flash-froze.
A massive wall of thick, unbreakable blue ice immediately began to rapidly grow upward from the ground, actively sealing the entrance tunnel to completely shut her out in the storm.
Seeing the door actively closing, Harper panicked as she dropped the innocent maiden act for a fraction of a second.
"Wait!" Harper cried out properly, her voice echoing with a piercing shriek that completely cut through the acoustic dampening of the cavern.
The volume of her scream echoed down the tunnel.
Back in the main chamber, Aeliana’s silver eyes snapped wide open.
She sat up instantly with her starlight flaring as she looked toward the entrance.
Beside her, Mia who had already been awake and actively faking her sleep for the past ten minutes just to use Silas as a pillow let out a highly exaggerated yawn and sat up, rubbing her green eyes.
"Who is screaming?" Aeliana demanded, rushing toward the tunnel.
Outside, Harper pressed her bleeding hands against the rising wall of ice, desperately negotiating.

"I will pay you!" Harper offered, shivering as she looked at Silas through the narrowing gap. "I will give you the treasures I have won today! Please, I am really wounded! I can’t survive the night in this glass storm!"
She reached into her Lord inventory, her hand flashing with blue light.
"I got today’s high-tier treasure drop!" Harper yelled, holding up a heavy, glowing artifact.
It was a magnificent, ornate piece of armor... a Valkyrie’s Helmet, forged from pristine silver and adorned with sweeping feathered wings of polished steel.
It radiated the aura of a treasure.
Silas paused his spell, keeping the ice door halfway open as he scanned the artifact. It was a genuine Tier 2 defensive item.
Valerius stepped forward, his greed instantly overriding his suspicion.
"Hand over the helmet first," Valerius demanded sharply. "Then we talk."
Harper paused for a brief bit.
’Okay so they’re crazy about treasures...’ Harper thought, ’If you wanted treasure, you just had to come with me Silas... I have the map.’
She looked at the helmet, then at the freezing glass bouncing off her shoulders. With a dramatic shiver, she tossed the heavy silver helmet directly over the rising wall of ice.
It sailed through the air. Silas, reacting with reflexes, snatched it out of the air before Valerius could even raise his gauntlet.
"Hey!" Valerius protested loudly, glaring at Silas.
Silas ignored him, inspecting the artifact before tossing it smoothly into his own spatial inventory. He looked back down at Harper, who was still kneeling in the freezing glass.

He didn’t lower the ice wall to let her inside their secure sleeping quarters. Instead, Silas manipulated his mana.
He used the water rushing from the ground to violently expand outward, pushing the heavy liquid over Harper’s head before hitting it with another rapid Ice Transformation.
KRKKKK!
The ice aggressively expanded, creating a crude, ten-foot extended roof and a smooth frozen floor directly outside the main door, effectively giving Harper a sheltered, enclosed antechamber.
It blocked the lethal glass rain and the howling wind, giving her a safe space to stay, but completely segregated her from the main inner cavern.
"You stay out here," Silas instructed her coldly.
Mia trotted down the tunnel, completely ignoring the tension.
She nimbly hopped up, scaling Silas’s trench coat like a tree, and climbed securely onto his broad back, wrapping her small arms loosely around his neck.
"Not bad, boy," Mia commended him, patting his cheek. "You are getting the hang of Ice Transformation. Your crystallization speed is improving."
"Just don’t die today Harper, or your sister would be sad."
Harper nodded as she bowed and climbed over the fence to the cover.
"Thank you for giving me a place to stay, Lord Silas and Lord Valerius... I will remember your mercy."
Silas glanced over his shoulder at the Grandmaster clinging to him like a backpack and Valerius who was standing nearby, rolled his eyes so hard he nearly pulled a muscle.

"You seem to know literally all the women in the Sovereign Realm, Graves," Valerius commented, crossing his arms and shaking his head in disbelief. "First Seraphina, now Harper... is there anybody you don’t know?"
Aeliana, standing at Silas’s flank, pouted slightly with her green eyes narrowing as she agreed with Valerius’s assessment.
"Lord Sy does possess a rather... extensive social network."
Silas chuckled.
"That wasn’t true at all. I just pay attention to stuff."
Harper, sitting on the cold ice floor of the newly constructed antechamber, hugged her knees to her chest.
"Once again thank you," Harper said softly, looking up through her wet purple eyelashes, playing the grateful victim flawlessly. "Thank you for the shelter."
Valerius completely dropped his casual banter.
He stepped up to the ice threshold, his green eyes burning with uncompromising lethality as he looked down at the lightning mage.

"Listen to me carefully, Harper," Valerius continued, his voice dropping to a dangerous whisper. "If you cast a single spell... if you output even a fraction of an attacking aura while we rest... we will not hesitate. We will kill you where you sit."
Harper widened her eyes, nodding frantically.
"I assure you, I would not! I just want to rest!"
Valerius stared at her for two more seconds, ensuring the threat had landed. He then turned back to Silas, rolling his shoulders to loosen his tired muscles.

"I am retiring for a few hours," Valerius announced, stifling a yawn. "My core is practically empty. Silas, you take the first watch. We will figure out how exactly we are going to share that Valkyrie helmet later."
Without waiting for an argument, Valerius turned and walked deep into the inner cavern, finding a smooth patch of ice to lay his bedroll down.
Aeliana stepped up to Silas. She gently reached out, straightening the collar of his dusty trench coat.
"By the next watch," Aeli murmured softly, her green eyes looking deeply into his golden ones, "you better come inside and keep your promise, My Lord."
She offered a devastating beautiful smile, then turned and gracefully walked back into the cavern to claim her own spot on the ice floor.
Silas was left completely alone in the threshold.
He sat down heavily on a protruding block of ice at the entrance, leaning his back against the wall.
Mia remained securely draped over his shoulders, her small chin resting comfortably on the top of his head.
In the antechamber directly in front of him, Harper sat down facing forward, looking out into the howling darkness which was still aggressively raining in shattered glass.
The glass shards were incredibly sharp, bouncing violently off the magical boundaries of the ice roof.

Harper ran her pale fingers over the ripped fabric of her leather shirt. She had purposefully ripped up her clothes prior to her arrival, ensuring her pale skin and cleavage were highly visible in the dim light.
Now, she had to proceed to the next critical part of her twisted agenda.
She needed to seduce Silas Graves...
She desperately needed to have his kid to trigger the next stage of the plan in taking Blessed Land from him and to have his kid, she needed them to have sex tonight.

’I’m only working with a little amount of time now,’ Harper thought frantically with her pulse racing as she mentally calculated the watch schedule. ’Valerius is asleep an the Elf is asleep. It’s just him and his tiny summon. Let’s start the conversation.’
Harper slowly turned around on the ice floor, shifting her legs to ensure her ripped shirt fell perfectly, and looked directly at Silas.
Silas wasn’t even looking at her.
He was holding his right hand out, palm facing upward.
Hovering perfectly two inches above his calloused skin was a sphere of pure crystal-clear water.
Silas was actively manipulating the fluid, smoothly morphing the sphere into a spinning ring, then a complex multi-layered geometric cube.
It looked quite beautiful, the water refracting the dim light of the cavern with flawless control.
"Your mana control is incredible, Lord Silas," Harper complimented him softly, her voice dripping with sweetness.
She genuinely loved it though.
Silas and the tiny elf on his head completely, utterly ignored her. Silas didn’t even blink, keeping his golden-ringed eyes locked onto the spinning water.
Mia, resting her chin on his hair, observed the geometric cube.
"You are quite close to adept mastery," Mia noted approvingly, entirely dismissing Harper’s existence. "If not already there... Your elemental transition speed is phenomenal."
Mia then leaned down, placing her small lips directly next to Silas’s ear.

"I would teach you far more advanced techniques right now," Mia whispered, her voice carrying a terrifying, ancient lethality, "if this pathetic bitch wasn’t sitting right there watching us. Do not worry. The moment I sense even a fraction of an attacking aura from her core, I will spike a pressurized icicle directly through her chest cavity."
Silas didn’t react to the threat, keeping his face perfectly stoic.
"For now, Use Ice Transformation," Mia instructed him, shifting back to teacher mode.
Silas sighed softly. He channeled his intent, instantly freezing the complex water geometric cube into solid unbreakable blue ice.

"Good," Mia nodded. "Now, I am going to teach you the chant for Water Transformation. It is the exact inverse. It focuses on forcefully injecting raw aqua mana directly into the crystalline lattice of the ice in order to violently revert it back to its liquid state."

chapters.title: Chapter 187: Harper’s Failures [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Mia slowly taught him the chant and Silas listened closely with his Gold Core instantly churning as he spoke the chant aloud.
FWOOSH.
Immediately, the solid ice cube hovering over his palm violently destabilized, melting instantly back into a sphere of swirling water.
"Excellent," Mia praised. "Practice it."
Silas had him practice the transition a few more times.
Solid Ice... Liquid water... Solid ice... Liquid water...
The speed of his transformations was terrifying, happening in fractions of a second.
Watching him completely ignore her, Harper felt a surge of desperate impatience. She couldn’t seduce him if he wouldn’t even look at her.
Harper began walking.
She stood up from the ice floor and took three slow, deliberate steps toward the threshold where Silas was sitting.
Silas didn’t even look up.
SHWK!
In a single blindingly fast motion, Silas forcefully expanded the hovering water sphere, violently elongating it into a three-foot-long razor-sharp blade of ice.
He lifted it effortlessly, pointing the lethal, jagged tip directly at Harper’s pale throat, stopping her dead in her tracks just inches from the blade.
Harper froze with her breath hitching as the freezing cold radiating from the ice blade bit into the skin of her neck.
She slowly raised both of her hands up in a gesture of complete surrender.

"Why are you acting like this?" Harper asked, her voice trembling as she looked down at him with wide, pleading purple eyes. "Why are you acting like you didn’t know me? I just wanted to come closer to ask you something."
Silas didn’t lower the blade a single millimeter. His golden-ringed eyes remained completely devoid of warmth.
"I really don’t know you, Harper," Silas explained flatly, what? She had been stalking him for a while since the first time he got to Weaver’s Spire and their sisters were in the same school.
Did that even mean they knew each other?

"And in a Secret Realm where everyone is actively slaughtering each other for loot, you could easily be here to kill me while I sleep after all. To take whatever artifacts I have on me so stay exactly where you are."
Harper stared at the ice blade with her heart hammering against her ribs as she slowly shook her head.
"I assure you, I wouldn’t kill you," Harper whispered softly, completely dropping the innocent victim act.
She slowly lowered her raised hands, looking down directly at the freezing ground.
Her cheeks flushed a violent feverish shade of red, and her purple eyes dilated.

"I actually have an incredibly big crush on you, Silas-kun..." Harper confessed, her voice trembling with twisted affection. "That’s exactly why I love stalking you through the Valoria sectors... so I can know all of your private hobbies, your routines, your secrets..."
Silas and Mia physically recoiled.
Mia’s jaw dropped, and Silas actually choked on his own saliva, almost spitting out a lungful of air in disbelief.
’Is she completely insane?’ Silas thought frantically.
Was she genuinely not aware of how absolutely, terrifyingly crazy she sounded right now?! Stalking him because she had a crush on him?
Regardless of their horrified reactions, Harper reached into the waistband of her leather armor.
"This is what I wanted you to check out," Harper said, completely ignoring the ice blade at her throat.
She quickly threw a thick sealed roll of parchment directly at Silas’s face.
Silas immediately treated the sudden movement as a lethal attack. He tensed his arm to swing the ice blade and bisect her head from her shoulders.
However, Mia reacted faster.
"Hold!" Mia commanded.

Mia’s glowing green eyes flared with arcane power as she used high-tier telekinesis to violently arrest the parchment’s momentum mid-air, holding the roll completely suspended and pinned down by invisible force two feet away from Silas’s face.
Silas stopped his swing, narrowing his eyes as he used his Lord interface to analyze the floating scroll.
The blue system tab imediately popped up, identifying the item.
[Name: Ititus’s Map To Wealth]
[Tier: 1 (Navigation Artifact)]
[Description: An ancient magically encoded topography chart of the Secret Realm’s desert layer... Bypasses standard spatial mirages.]
Mia carefully scanned the parchment for explosive runes or poison traps.
Once she verified there were completely no traps embedded in the paper, she released her telekinetic grip and brought it over to Silas.
Silas took it, unrolling the heavy scroll and holding it firmly in his calloused hand.
"Let’s see what this is about..."
It was a detailed and constantly shifting magical map of the desert layer they were currently in.

Also drawn directly in the center, completely bypassing the massive maze of dunes, was a massive glowing red X marking a specific place where the dead god explicitly kept his primary surface treasure.
Silas looked up from the map, his golden-ringed eyes locking onto Harper’s flushed face.
His paranoia was screaming at maximum volume.
"Why would you give me this?" Silas asked, his voice laced with heavy, uncompromising suspicion. "You could have easily monopolized this loot for your own self. Isn’t that why you’re here?"
Harper stood there in the freezing antechamber, the biting wind howling behind her.
She violently trembled where she stood with her hands clutching the ripped edges of her shirt as a lovesick smile stretched across her beautiful face.
She blushed so hard her skin practically glowed in the dark.
"I uh..." Harper giggled softly, a disturbing, manic sound that made Silas’s blood run completely cold. "...I just want you to love me, Silas-kun~"
"Love you?" Silas asked, his voice sounding flat, echoing within the freezing, isolated antechamber of the ice construct.
His golden-ringed eyes narrowed, lacking any sort of romantic reciprocation or warmth as he stared down at the lightning mage before him.
Harper knelt on the solid ice floor, the howling glass storm raging just inches behind her protective barrier.
Her pale, flawless skin was flushed a violently feverish red.

"Yes!" Harper blurted out, her hands flying up to nervously twiddle her thumbs together. It was a remarkably childish vulnerable gesture, completely at odds with the terrifying spellcaster she usually projected on the battlefield. "Since the very moment I laid eyes on you during when you sold those cores... I’ve wanted to learn more about you."
She shifted on her knees, the torn fabric of her ruined leather armor sliding lower, exposing the soft curve of her collarbone.

"And it’s not just about your beautiful face, Silas," Harper continued rapidly with her voice taking on a sweet and almost desperate tone that made Silas flinch. "Though I do like that very much but it’s about your kind heart, the way you lead, and you—"
"Cut the bullshit, Harper," Silas interrupted viciously.
His voice sliced through the freezing air like a physical blade.
He was a slum-born survivor who had fought, bled, and clawed his way up to a Gold Core.
He knew exactly what it looked like when someone was trying to sell him a poisoned chalice wrapped in silk.
Harper froze, her sweet nervous facade cracking slightly.
She realized standard noble courtship tactics were absolutely useless against a man this hardened so, Harper decided to completely bypass the aristocratic dance and go straight for the point.
"Uh," Harper blinked, her face flushing an even deeper darker shade of crimson as she looked him dead in the eye. "I want you to breed me?"
Cough! Cough! Cough!
Silas violently choked on his own saliva.
He lurched forward with his heavy boots scraping against the ice as he pounded his fist against his own chest, desperately trying to clear his airway.
Sitting atop his head, Mia let out a genuine snort of disbelief with her tiny hands gripping his dark hair.
Harper sat there on her knees, blinking innocently.
She truly wasn’t educated in the subtle nuances of romance or proper seduction.

She had grown up in the highest and heavily guarded echelons of Valoria City’s aristocracy though she was not a noble... Her father owned at least 4 of the 6 LA Buildings in Valoria City which made him very influential and he worked as the manager just to be able to identify talent.
Harper was quite used to her overwhelming natural beauty getting her whatever she wanted, whenever she wanted it, without having to ask twice.
After all, in the modern society, physical attractiveness was a deeply skewed metric.

In a world where unattractive or average-looking people could easily fix their physical flaws in a day or two by swallowing a low-tier alchemical Body-Refining pill, general attractiveness became the baseline.

Everyone with a handful of silver coins was beautiful. Therefore, what truly mattered... what truly held astronomical social, political, and genetic weight were the exceptionally rare people who were born flawlessly beautiful without the aid of magic or alchemy.
Harper was one of those people.
She possessed perfect unblemished genetics.

Her entire life, high-tier Lords and wealthy merchants had fallen to their knees the moment she smiled, offering her entire fortunes just for a fraction of her attention but for some incredibly frustrating, mind-bending reason, that stuff didn’t work on Silas Graves.
He didn’t fawn over her.
He didn’t stare at her ripped shirt.
He didn’t grovel and he looked at her like she was a liability so in Harper’s twisted mind, the fact that he was actively ignoring her natural perfection only made him so much hotter.
It drove her absolutely crazy.
"Are you completely out of your mind?!" Silas gasped, finally catching his breath and glaring at her.
Harper bit her lower lip, a dangerous blush spreading across her neck as she suggested the next step without missing a beat.
"I’m serious," Harper whispered, leaning forward and resting her hands on the ice near his boots. "Let’s go for it. Right now. While the others are sleeping."
Silas completely stiffened.
He slowly looked over his shoulder.
Deep inside the dimly lit interior of the main ice cavern, Aeliana was fast asleep with her chest rising and falling peacefully in her white robes.
On the opposite side of the room, Valerius was completely out cold, snoring softly with his head resting against his mythril shield.
Silas turned his golden-ringed eyes back to Harper.
On a normal, civilian occasion back in the slums, if a gorgeous noblewoman threw herself at him in the middle of the night, he would have absolutely taken the opportunity without a second thought.
He was a healthy male, and her proposition was incredibly blunt and highly appealing but he honestly didn’t trust Harper even a fraction of an inch.
"No," Silas denied her flatly, his voice echoing with unyielding Lordly discipline.
Harper’s jaw dropped slightly.
She was quite surprised as her purple eyes widened in genuine shock. "What? Why not? I’m literally offering myself to you!"

"Because I am supposed to keep watch, Harper," Silas stated, crossing his arms over his heavy trench coat. "When the others are awake to take the next shift, who knows what kind of traps, curses, or roaming monsters are out there? I need my core focused. I need my mind clear and I am not burning my stamina to sleep with someone I don’t trust."
Harper sat back on her heels, staring at him in genuine awe.
Her purple eyes softened with the look in her eyes momentarily replaced by profound respect.
She was quite surprised at his cool-headedness.

Any other Lord in this place especially Julian would have instantly taken the bait, dropping their guard for a moment of pleasure but Silas prioritized the survival of his faction over his own desires.
"You are incredible," Harper commended him softly, a genuine smile touching her lips. "You really are a good friend, Silas. Anyone else in this situation would have taken it."
Silas just rolled his eyes, resting the back of his head against the ice wall and dismissing the conversation entirely. "Just sit quietly until the storm passes."
The howling wind outside violently whipped against the ice barrier, sending a chilling draft through the small opening near the ceiling.
Harper shivered violently, her teeth audibly chattering in the freezing air.
"Silas..." Harper requested softly, wrapping her arms around her shoulders. "Could I... could I at least lay my head on your lap? Just for a little bit?"
"Absolutely not," Silas dismissed it instantly, waving his hand. "Sleep on the floor."
But Harper didn’t give up. S
he went down on her knees, shuffling forward across the frost until she was right in front of him. She looked up, pleading with wide teary purple eyes.

"Please," Harper pleaded with her voice cracking. "I usually need physical contact like this when I am quite stressed out. It grounds my lightning mana so it doesn’t short-circuit my nervous system and it has been an incredibly long, traumatic day today after all..."
Silas stared at her, completely unmoved by the emotional performance.
Seeing that pity wasn’t working, Harper decided to do some extra convincing, instantly switching to a negotiation.

"I will compensate you!" Harper offered quickly, leaning closer. "I will transfer one hundred thousand Spirit Credits directly into your bank account the moment we extract from this realm! Just let me rest my head."

sentences.text: Mia slowly taught him the chant and Silas listened closely with his Gold Core instantly churning as he spoke the chant aloud.
FWOOSH.
Immediately, the solid ice cube hovering over his palm violently destabilized, melting instantly back into a sphere of swirling water.
"Excellent," Mia praised.
"Practice it."
Silas had him practice the transition a few more times.
Solid Ice...
Liquid water...
Solid ice...
Liquid water...
The speed of his transformations was terrifying, happening in fractions of a second.
Watching him completely ignore her, Harper felt a surge of desperate impatience.
She couldn’t seduce him if he wouldn’t even look at her.
Harper began walking.
She stood up from the ice floor and took three slow, deliberate steps toward the threshold where Silas was sitting.
Silas didn’t even look up.
SHWK!
In a single blindingly fast motion, Silas forcefully expanded the hovering water sphere, violently elongating it into a three-foot-long razor-sharp blade of ice.
He lifted it effortlessly, pointing the lethal, jagged tip directly at Harper’s pale throat, stopping her dead in her tracks just inches from the blade.
Harper froze with her breath hitching as the freezing cold radiating from the ice blade bit into the skin of her neck.
She slowly raised both of her hands up in a gesture of complete surrender.
"Why are you acting like this?" Harper asked, her voice trembling as she looked down at him with wide, pleading purple eyes.
"Why are you acting like you didn’t know me?
I just wanted to come closer to ask you something."
Silas didn’t lower the blade a single millimeter.
His golden-ringed eyes remained completely devoid of warmth.
"I really don’t know you, Harper," Silas explained flatly, what?
She had been stalking him for a while since the first time he got to Weaver’s Spire and their sisters were in the same school.
Did that even mean they knew each other?
"And in a Secret Realm where everyone is actively slaughtering each other for loot, you could easily be here to kill me while I sleep after all.
To take whatever artifacts I have on me so stay exactly where you are."
Harper stared at the ice blade with her heart hammering against her ribs as she slowly shook her head.
"I assure you, I wouldn’t kill you," Harper whispered softly, completely dropping the innocent victim act.
She slowly lowered her raised hands, looking down directly at the freezing ground.
Her cheeks flushed a violent feverish shade of red, and her purple eyes dilated.
"I actually have an incredibly big crush on you, Silas-kun..." Harper confessed, her voice trembling with twisted affection.
"That’s exactly why I love stalking you through the Valoria sectors... so I can know all of your private hobbies, your routines, your secrets..."
Silas and Mia physically recoiled.
Mia’s jaw dropped, and Silas actually choked on his own saliva, almost spitting out a lungful of air in disbelief.
’Is she completely insane?’ Silas thought frantically.
Was she genuinely not aware of how absolutely, terrifyingly crazy she sounded right now?!
Stalking him because she had a crush on him?
Regardless of their horrified reactions, Harper reached into the waistband of her leather armor.
"This is what I wanted you to check out," Harper said, completely ignoring the ice blade at her throat.
She quickly threw a thick sealed roll of parchment directly at Silas’s face.
Silas immediately treated the sudden movement as a lethal attack.
He tensed his arm to swing the ice blade and bisect her head from her shoulders.
However, Mia reacted faster.
"Hold!" Mia commanded.

Mia’s glowing green eyes flared with arcane power as she used high-tier telekinesis to violently arrest the parchment’s momentum mid-air, holding the roll completely suspended and pinned down by invisible force two feet away from Silas’s face.
Silas stopped his swing, narrowing his eyes as he used his Lord interface to analyze the floating scroll.
The blue system tab imediately popped up, identifying the item.
[Name: Ititus’s Map To Wealth]
[Tier: 1 (Navigation Artifact)]
[Description: An ancient magically encoded topography chart of the Secret Realm’s desert layer...
Bypasses standard spatial mirages.]
Mia carefully scanned the parchment for explosive runes or poison traps.
Once she verified there were completely no traps embedded in the paper, she released her telekinetic grip and brought it over to Silas.
Silas took it, unrolling the heavy scroll and holding it firmly in his calloused hand.
"Let’s see what this is about..."
It was a detailed and constantly shifting magical map of the desert layer they were currently in.

Also drawn directly in the center, completely bypassing the massive maze of dunes, was a massive glowing red X marking a specific place where the dead god explicitly kept his primary surface treasure.
Silas looked up from the map, his golden-ringed eyes locking onto Harper’s flushed face.
His paranoia was screaming at maximum volume.
"Why would you give me this?" Silas asked, his voice laced with heavy, uncompromising suspicion.
"You could have easily monopolized this loot for your own self.
Isn’t that why you’re here?"
Harper stood there in the freezing antechamber, the biting wind howling behind her.
She violently trembled where she stood with her hands clutching the ripped edges of her shirt as a lovesick smile stretched across her beautiful face.
She blushed so hard her skin practically glowed in the dark.
"I uh..." Harper giggled softly, a disturbing, manic sound that made Silas’s blood run completely cold.
"...I just want you to love me, Silas-kun~"
"Love you?" Silas asked, his voice sounding flat, echoing within the freezing, isolated antechamber of the ice construct.
His golden-ringed eyes narrowed, lacking any sort of romantic reciprocation or warmth as he stared down at the lightning mage before him.
Harper knelt on the solid ice floor, the howling glass storm raging just inches behind her protective barrier.
Her pale, flawless skin was flushed a violently feverish red.
"Yes!" Harper blurted out, her hands flying up to nervously twiddle her thumbs together.
It was a remarkably childish vulnerable gesture, completely at odds with the terrifying spellcaster she usually projected on the battlefield.
"Since the very moment I laid eyes on you during when you sold those cores...
I’ve wanted to learn more about you."
She shifted on her knees, the torn fabric of her ruined leather armor sliding lower, exposing the soft curve of her collarbone.
"And it’s not just about your beautiful face, Silas," Harper continued rapidly with her voice taking on a sweet and almost desperate tone that made Silas flinch.
"Though I do like that very much but it’s about your kind heart, the way you lead, and you—"
"Cut the bullshit, Harper," Silas interrupted viciously.
His voice sliced through the freezing air like a physical blade.
He was a slum-born survivor who had fought, bled, and clawed his way up to a Gold Core.
He knew exactly what it looked like when someone was trying to sell him a poisoned chalice wrapped in silk.
Harper froze, her sweet nervous facade cracking slightly.
She realized standard noble courtship tactics were absolutely useless against a man this hardened so, Harper decided to completely bypass the aristocratic dance and go straight for the point.
"Uh," Harper blinked, her face flushing an even deeper darker shade of crimson as she looked him dead in the eye.
"I want you to breed me?"
Cough!
Cough!
Cough!
Silas violently choked on his own saliva.
He lurched forward with his heavy boots scraping against the ice as he pounded his fist against his own chest, desperately trying to clear his airway.
Sitting atop his head, Mia let out a genuine snort of disbelief with her tiny hands gripping his dark hair.
Harper sat there on her knees, blinking innocently.
She truly wasn’t educated in the subtle nuances of romance or proper seduction.
She had grown up in the highest and heavily guarded echelons of Valoria City’s aristocracy though she was not a noble...
Her father owned at least 4 of the 6 LA Buildings in Valoria City which made him very influential and he worked as the manager just to be able to identify talent.
Harper was quite used to her overwhelming natural beauty getting her whatever she wanted, whenever she wanted it, without having to ask twice.
After all, in the modern society, physical attractiveness was a deeply skewed metric.

In a world where unattractive or average-looking people could easily fix their physical flaws in a day or two by swallowing a low-tier alchemical Body-Refining pill, general attractiveness became the baseline.
Everyone with a handful of silver coins was beautiful.

Therefore, what truly mattered... what truly held astronomical social, political, and genetic weight were the exceptionally rare people who were born flawlessly beautiful without the aid of magic or alchemy.
Harper was one of those people.
She possessed perfect unblemished genetics.

Her entire life, high-tier Lords and wealthy merchants had fallen to their knees the moment she smiled, offering her entire fortunes just for a fraction of her attention but for some incredibly frustrating, mind-bending reason, that stuff didn’t work on Silas Graves.
He didn’t fawn over her.
He didn’t stare at her ripped shirt.
He didn’t grovel and he looked at her like she was a liability so in Harper’s twisted mind, the fact that he was actively ignoring her natural perfection only made him so much hotter.
It drove her absolutely crazy.
"Are you completely out of your mind?!" Silas gasped, finally catching his breath and glaring at her.
Harper bit her lower lip, a dangerous blush spreading across her neck as she suggested the next step without missing a beat.
"I’m serious," Harper whispered, leaning forward and resting her hands on the ice near his boots.
"Let’s go for it.
Right now.
While the others are sleeping."
Silas completely stiffened.
He slowly looked over his shoulder.
Deep inside the dimly lit interior of the main ice cavern, Aeliana was fast asleep with her chest rising and falling peacefully in her white robes.
On the opposite side of the room, Valerius was completely out cold, snoring softly with his head resting against his mythril shield.
Silas turned his golden-ringed eyes back to Harper.
On a normal, civilian occasion back in the slums, if a gorgeous noblewoman threw herself at him in the middle of the night, he would have absolutely taken the opportunity without a second thought.
He was a healthy male, and her proposition was incredibly blunt and highly appealing but he honestly didn’t trust Harper even a fraction of an inch.
"No," Silas denied her flatly, his voice echoing with unyielding Lordly discipline.
Harper’s jaw dropped slightly.
She was quite surprised as her purple eyes widened in genuine shock.
"What?
Why not?
I’m literally offering myself to you!"
"Because I am supposed to keep watch, Harper," Silas stated, crossing his arms over his heavy trench coat.
"When the others are awake to take the next shift, who knows what kind of traps, curses, or roaming monsters are out there?
I need my core focused.
I need my mind clear and I am not burning my stamina to sleep with someone I don’t trust."
Harper sat back on her heels, staring at him in genuine awe.
Her purple eyes softened with the look in her eyes momentarily replaced by profound respect.
She was quite surprised at his cool-headedness.

Any other Lord in this place especially Julian would have instantly taken the bait, dropping their guard for a moment of pleasure but Silas prioritized the survival of his faction over his own desires.
"You are incredible," Harper commended him softly, a genuine smile touching her lips.
"You really are a good friend, Silas.
Anyone else in this situation would have taken it."
Silas just rolled his eyes, resting the back of his head against the ice wall and dismissing the conversation entirely.
"Just sit quietly until the storm passes."
The howling wind outside violently whipped against the ice barrier, sending a chilling draft through the small opening near the ceiling.
Harper shivered violently, her teeth audibly chattering in the freezing air.
"Silas..." Harper requested softly, wrapping her arms around her shoulders.

Just for a little bit?"

"Sleep on the floor."

S
he went down on her knees, shuffling forward across the frost until she was right in front of him.

It grounds my lightning mana so it doesn’t short-circuit my nervous system and it has been an incredibly long, traumatic day today after all..."
