Seeing that pity wasn’t working, Harper decided to do some extra convincing, instantly switching to a negotiation.
"I will compensate you!" Harper offered quickly, leaning closer.
"I will transfer one hundred thousand Spirit Credits directly into your bank account the moment we extract from this realm!
Just let me rest my head."

chapters.title: Chapter 188: Dragon In Blessed Land [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: A hundred thousand Spirit Credits.
Silas paused.
That was a massive influx of capital however, his survival instincts demanded certainty.
"Mia," Silas whispered so low that Harper couldn’t hear "Scan her core. Does she have any attacking aura currently charging? Is she hiding a spell?"
Sitting on top of his head, Mia closed her glowing green eyes with her Grandmaster perception effortlessly penetrating Harper’s physical form.

"No," Mia whispered back directly into his mind. "Her core is completely dormant and you shouldn’t worry. The microsecond I sense her heart rate spike or her mana condense, I will snipe a high-pressure water bullet straight through her brainstem."
Armed with the assurance of a lethal fail-safe, Silas let out a long begrudging sigh.
"Fine," Silas agreed coldly. "A Hundred Thousand Spirit Credits and no funny business. Lay down."
Harper’s face lit up with a brilliant victorious smile.
’With this... I can find a way to seduce him.’
She quickly shifted forward, laying down completely flat on the cold ice floor of the antechamber, and gently placed her head directly onto Silas’s right thigh.
As she did, her purple eyes widened a bit in genuine shock.
She had expected him to be cold and uncomfortable but she immediately felt quite some overwhelming comfort.
Silas possessed an amazing body fueled by a strong Core.
The density of the mana thrumming within his veins radiated a steady warm heat that completely bypassed the freezing air of the cavern.
It was like resting her head on a sun-baked stone.
It was so incredibly warm that Harper couldn’t help herself.
"Mmnn~" Harper let out a soft, inappropriate moan of comfort. ’I can do the mission later...’
She turned her face inward, wrapping both of her pale arms securely around his muscular leg and hugging it tightly to her chest.
"Hey!" Silas complained sharply, trying to pull his leg back. "I said rest your head, not grapple me."
"S-sorry," Harper mumbled an apology, her voice already growing heavy and thick with exhaustion. "So warm..."
Her eyes fluttered shut.
The adrenaline of the Empress Thunder execution, combined with the brutal physical fatigue of surviving the desert, completely crashed down on her.
Before long, she fell fast asleep, her grip on his leg remaining iron-clad.
Silas looked down at the sleeping lightning mage, shaking his head.

"Ignore her," Mia whispered, hopping down from Silas’s head and landing nimbly on his left knee. "We have hours to kill before Valerius wakes up. I am going to teach you two more water spells so pay attention. Let’s get you to Adept properly then tomorrow, we do Lightning."
Silas shifted his focus entirely, his golden-ringed eyes locking onto the tiny Grandmaster.

"The first spell is an area-denial ward," Mia instructed. "It is called Aqueous Severance. You draw the moisture in the air into a microscopic razor wire. The chant is: ’Tears of the abyss, sharpen the tide, sever the flesh and part the sea.’"
Silas held his free left hand out. He closed his eyes, mapping the specific runic syllables directly into his core.
"Tears of the abyss, sharpen the tide..." Silas muttered, his voice a low rumble. "...sever the flesh and part the sea."
FWOOSH!
A hyper-pressurized, nearly invisible ring of spinning water violently erupted around his palm, vibrating with enough kinetic frequency to slice through solid steel.
"Good," Mia nodded approvingly. "The second is a crushing blow. Hydraulic Press. The chant is: ’Weight of the ocean, crush the stone, bury the light in depths unknown.’"
Silas practiced both spells relentlessly in the dark.

He muttered the chants over and over, his Gold Core flawlessly integrating the magical matrixes into his muscle memory, using the new spells to manipulate small spheres of water in the air while completely ignoring the sleeping noblewoman drooling slightly onto his trench coat.
Hours passed in the freezing dark.
The howling of the glass storm outside slowly began to die down as the Secret Realm’s weather cycle shifted.
Mia stood up on his knee, turning toward the interior of the cavern. She fired a tiny harmless bead of water directly at Valerius’s face.
Smack!
Valerius grunted, his eyes snapping open. He sat up, shaking the sleep from his head, and grabbed his mythril shield.
"Thank you Mia..."
He stood up, stretching his broad shoulders until they popped, and walked out into the entrance tunnel to relieve Silas.
As Valerius stepped into the dim light, he completely froze.
He looked down at the ground. Harper was curled up into a ball, deeply asleep, aggressively hugging Silas’s right leg like it was a stuffed animal.
Valerius stared at the scene for five solid seconds.
He slowly dragged his gauntleted hand down his face, letting out a long sigh of pure exhaustion.
"I don’t even want to know," Valerius sighed, shaking his head. "I will take the shift until the glass rain completely stops. Go get some sleep, Graves."
"Thanks," Silas replied softly.
He carefully reached down, prying Harper’s pale fingers off his leg one by one.
He took Harper up by the shoulders, dragging her forward a few inches. She was mumbling incoherently in her sleep about claiming his territory, which made Valerius physically cringe.
Silas gently placed her forward, laying her completely flat on the ice floor so she wouldn’t wake up.
Silas stood up, rolling his stiff neck, and walked deep into the main cavern to where Aeliana was sleeping peacefully on her bedroll.
Mia trotted after him, stopping in front of Valerius.
"Hey, blondie," Mia whispered, looking up at Valerius. "Permission to sleep over there too?"
Valerius looked at the tiny Grandmaster, then at Silas laying down next to the beautiful Elf.
He let out another deeper sigh, utterly defeated by the dynamics of this whole thing.
"Permission granted," Valerius muttered, turning his back to watch the storm.
Mia grinned, a flash of sharp teeth, and scurried over to the sleeping arrangements, seamlessly joining him.
Silas lay down on the cold ice.
He didn’t hesitate.
"I’m here..."
He pulled the sleeping Aeliana close, cuddling up directly against her back.
Aeliana groaned softly in her sleep, leaning back into his warmth.
Silas rested his chin softly against her shoulder, placing his face securely and intimately in her breasts as he wrapped his arm around her waist.
A second later, Mia arrived.
She climbed onto the bedroll and aggressively hugged Silas directly from behind, completely sandwiching him between the two white-haired elves.
Silas lay there in the freezing dark, staring at the far ice wall.

’I wonder how these people can actually fall asleep here... It’s not like I don’t trust Valerius but still... He can still slit my throat while I sleep, I really need to keep my eyes open and I’m a Gold core so it’s not like I feel exhaust—’
Silas’s eyes fluttered shut.
The warmth of Aeliana in front of him and Mia behind him, combined with the warmth of his Gold Core, hit him like a blow to the face.
Silas fell asleep instantly.
[Over In Blessed Land]
Thousands of miles away from the freezing death traps of the Secret Realm, the atmosphere was different.
The air was warm, filled with the rich savory smell of roasted meats, fresh bread, and the loud echoing chatter of dozens of voices.
They were currently gathered in the massive, heavily fortified stone mess hall of the Warlord’s Barracks, the central military structure of the Blessed Land territory.
"How is Lord Silas?" Brida asked loudly, leaning over the long wooden table with a tankard of alcohol in her hand.
Almost all the high-ranking girls of the territory were completely surrounding the new arrival.
Sitting in the center of the wooden bench, looking completely overwhelmed, was Talira.
The new red-haired dragon was blushing a brilliant vibrant shade of crimson from all the intense, unyielding attention.
She was no longer naked.

She was wearing a perfectly tailored, comfortable set of dark crimson combat robes, woven from highly durable magical silk that perfectly accommodated the small dragon wings protruding from her lower back.
Talira looked around the table.
Dozens of human women were staring at her, offering her fresh food, pouring her drinks, and asking her rapid-fire questions about the outside world.
Talira wanted to insult Silas.

She wanted to loudly declare that the Lord of this territory was a brutal thieving primate who had kidnapped her from her rightful domain but then she vividly remembered the terrifying warning that Aeli had given her back in the ash.
Talira gulped heavily with the phantom chill of the frozen spell making her wings twitch.
"He... he is very good looking," Talira admitted softly, taking a cautious bite of a roasted turkey leg. "And he was with that scary elf woman known as Aeliana."
The entire table of faction girls burst out laughing.
"Oh, Aeliana is a sweetheart!" Brida chuckled, waving her hand dismissively. "She just gets a little protective of the Boss!"
Talira didn’t have anything to laugh about.
"She is a psychopath," the dragon muttered darkly, taking another bite of meat.
She proceeded to vividly describe the way Aeli had completely beaten the bricks off of her, flash-freezing her massive dragon form in three seconds flat.
As Talira spoke, her red eyes scanned the bustling room.
Through the crowd, Talira then noticed some dark-haired woman sitting a few tables away, quietly eating her meal.
The dark-haired woman glanced at her for a brief second before smoothly removing her gaze and staring back down at her plate.
Talira shivered slightly.
’This territory is full of dangerous people,’ she thought.
But as she chewed the delicious, perfectly seasoned meat, Talira’s internal hostility began to waver.
Her rotting mother had spent her dying centuries advising her to avoid humans at all costs.

Humans were deceitful and they were cruel but looking around this bustling mess hall, hearing the genuine laughter and seeing the camaraderie among Silas’s subordinates... Talira felt a strange deep sense of belonging.
Aeliana had spoken of a saintly human who built libraries and protected his people.
Talira had wanted to meet him just to prove he was a fraud but sitting here, completely safe, warm, and fed in his sanctuary... she realized she wanted to stay.
"Watch this!" a loud voice cheered from the back of the mess hall.
The crowd shifted, parting slightly to reveal Rowenna and a mage that had arrived just now.
"I want to show you all something... Please use Fire magic," Rowenna said. "Slowly. I want to see the circle."
The young mage nodded rapidly. She held out her hands, closing her eyes.
In the Sovereign Realm, magic wasn’t just raw energy.
Spells contained intricate Magic Circles that dictated their elemental properties, trajectory, and heat.
Even the most basic fundamental spells like a standard fireball were formed with complex, glowing magic circles rotating violently in the dead center of the spell’s core.
The mage said a small chant and summoned flames. A sphere of orange fire sputtered into existence between her palms.
Rowenna leaned forward with her blue eyes narrowing.
She looked directly at it, using her new spell that she had been learning to identify the exact microscopic rotating magic circle hidden inside the flames.
"Disrupt," Rowenna whispered.
She applied a microscopic point of crushing gravity directly onto the center of the magic circle.
SNAP!
The force violently crushed the magic circle and it broke apart like shattered glass.
Instantly, the fireball violently destabilized, completely breaking the spell apart and fizzling out into a harmless wisp of grey smoke before it could even generate heat.
Rowenna pumped her fist in the air.
"Yes!" she cheered loudly.
The entire mess hall erupted.
All the other girls cheered for her too, clapping their hands and whistling at the incredible display of anti-magic combat.
Breaking a spell from the inside out was something they hadn’t seen before however, the joyous, celebratory noise died completely the very next moment.
The heavy oak doors of the mess hall were violently pushed open.
Morwenna entered the room.
The air in the barracks instantly grew heavier.
Morwenna’s dominant aura flooded the space.
She strode into the hall, her heavy boots clicking against the stone as a wild unhinged grin was plastered across her face.
The girls quickly parted, clearing a wide path for her.
Talira sat frozen on the bench, a piece of meat halfway to her mouth.
Even though she had only been in the Blessed Land for a few hours, Talira knew the two bosses who ran the territory while Silas was away.
First was Eluned, the Goddess of Nature.
Eluned was gentle, terrifyingly powerful, and had personally woven the magical clothes Talira was wearing right now to cover her modesty upon arrival and then there was Morwenna.
Morwenna didn’t stop to greet the cheering girls.
She walked in a perfectly straight line, completely ignoring the broken fireball demonstration, and marched directly over to Talira’s table.
Morwenna slammed both of her hands flat onto the wooden table, leaning forward until her face was inches away from the crimson dragon’s.
"So," Morwenna started, her eyes practically sparkling with excitement as she looked at the new arrival. "Are you really a dragon?"

She was mumbling incoherently in her sleep about claiming his territory, which made Valerius physically cringe.
Silas gently placed her forward, laying her completely flat on the ice floor so she wouldn’t wake up.
Silas stood up, rolling his stiff neck, and walked deep into the main cavern to where Aeliana was sleeping peacefully on her bedroll.
Mia trotted after him, stopping in front of Valerius.
"Hey, blondie," Mia whispered, looking up at Valerius.
"Permission to sleep over there too?"
Valerius looked at the tiny Grandmaster, then at Silas laying down next to the beautiful Elf.
He let out another deeper sigh, utterly defeated by the dynamics of this whole thing.
"Permission granted," Valerius muttered, turning his back to watch the storm.
Mia grinned, a flash of sharp teeth, and scurried over to the sleeping arrangements, seamlessly joining him.
Silas lay down on the cold ice.
He didn’t hesitate.
"I’m here..."
He pulled the sleeping Aeliana close, cuddling up directly against her back.
Aeliana groaned softly in her sleep, leaning back into his warmth.
Silas rested his chin softly against her shoulder, placing his face securely and intimately in her breasts as he wrapped his arm around her waist.
A second later, Mia arrived.
She climbed onto the bedroll and aggressively hugged Silas directly from behind, completely sandwiching him between the two white-haired elves.
Silas lay there in the freezing dark, staring at the far ice wall.
’I wonder how these people can actually fall asleep here...
It’s not like I don’t trust Valerius but still...
He can still slit my throat while I sleep, I really need to keep my eyes open and I’m a Gold core so it’s not like I feel exhaust—’
Silas’s eyes fluttered shut.
The warmth of Aeliana in front of him and Mia behind him, combined with the warmth of his Gold Core, hit him like a blow to the face.
Silas fell asleep instantly.
[Over In Blessed Land]
Thousands of miles away from the freezing death traps of the Secret Realm, the atmosphere was different.
The air was warm, filled with the rich savory smell of roasted meats, fresh bread, and the loud echoing chatter of dozens of voices.
They were currently gathered in the massive, heavily fortified stone mess hall of the Warlord’s Barracks, the central military structure of the Blessed Land territory.
"How is Lord Silas?" Brida asked loudly, leaning over the long wooden table with a tankard of alcohol in her hand.
Almost all the high-ranking girls of the territory were completely surrounding the new arrival.
Sitting in the center of the wooden bench, looking completely overwhelmed, was Talira.
The new red-haired dragon was blushing a brilliant vibrant shade of crimson from all the intense, unyielding attention.
She was no longer naked.

She was wearing a perfectly tailored, comfortable set of dark crimson combat robes, woven from highly durable magical silk that perfectly accommodated the small dragon wings protruding from her lower back.
Talira looked around the table.
Dozens of human women were staring at her, offering her fresh food, pouring her drinks, and asking her rapid-fire questions about the outside world.
Talira wanted to insult Silas.

She wanted to loudly declare that the Lord of this territory was a brutal thieving primate who had kidnapped her from her rightful domain but then she vividly remembered the terrifying warning that Aeli had given her back in the ash.
Talira gulped heavily with the phantom chill of the frozen spell making her wings twitch.
"He... he is very good looking," Talira admitted softly, taking a cautious bite of a roasted turkey leg.
"And he was with that scary elf woman known as Aeliana."
The entire table of faction girls burst out laughing.
"Oh, Aeliana is a sweetheart!" Brida chuckled, waving her hand dismissively.
"She just gets a little protective of the Boss!"
Talira didn’t have anything to laugh about.
"She is a psychopath," the dragon muttered darkly, taking another bite of meat.
She proceeded to vividly describe the way Aeli had completely beaten the bricks off of her, flash-freezing her massive dragon form in three seconds flat.
As Talira spoke, her red eyes scanned the bustling room.
Through the crowd, Talira then noticed some dark-haired woman sitting a few tables away, quietly eating her meal.
The dark-haired woman glanced at her for a brief second before smoothly removing her gaze and staring back down at her plate.
Talira shivered slightly.
’This territory is full of dangerous people,’ she thought.
But as she chewed the delicious, perfectly seasoned meat, Talira’s internal hostility began to waver.
Her rotting mother had spent her dying centuries advising her to avoid humans at all costs.
Humans were deceitful and they were cruel but looking around this bustling mess hall, hearing the genuine laughter and seeing the camaraderie among Silas’s subordinates...
Talira felt a strange deep sense of belonging.
Aeliana had spoken of a saintly human who built libraries and protected his people.
Talira had wanted to meet him just to prove he was a fraud but sitting here, completely safe, warm, and fed in his sanctuary... she realized she wanted to stay.
"Watch this!" a loud voice cheered from the back of the mess hall.
The crowd shifted, parting slightly to reveal Rowenna and a mage that had arrived just now.
"I want to show you all something...
Please use Fire magic," Rowenna said.
"Slowly.
I want to see the circle."
The young mage nodded rapidly.
She held out her hands, closing her eyes.
In the Sovereign Realm, magic wasn’t just raw energy.
Spells contained intricate Magic Circles that dictated their elemental properties, trajectory, and heat.
Even the most basic fundamental spells like a standard fireball were formed with complex, glowing magic circles rotating violently in the dead center of the spell’s core.
The mage said a small chant and summoned flames.
A sphere of orange fire sputtered into existence between her palms.
Rowenna leaned forward with her blue eyes narrowing.
She looked directly at it, using her new spell that she had been learning to identify the exact microscopic rotating magic circle hidden inside the flames.
"Disrupt," Rowenna whispered.
She applied a microscopic point of crushing gravity directly onto the center of the magic circle.
SNAP!
The force violently crushed the magic circle and it broke apart like shattered glass.
Instantly, the fireball violently destabilized, completely breaking the spell apart and fizzling out into a harmless wisp of grey smoke before it could even generate heat.
Rowenna pumped her fist in the air.
"Yes!" she cheered loudly.
The entire mess hall erupted.
All the other girls cheered for her too, clapping their hands and whistling at the incredible display of anti-magic combat.
Breaking a spell from the inside out was something they hadn’t seen before however, the joyous, celebratory noise died completely the very next moment.
The heavy oak doors of the mess hall were violently pushed open.
Morwenna entered the room.
The air in the barracks instantly grew heavier.
Morwenna’s dominant aura flooded the space.
She strode into the hall, her heavy boots clicking against the stone as a wild unhinged grin was plastered across her face.
The girls quickly parted, clearing a wide path for her.
Talira sat frozen on the bench, a piece of meat halfway to her mouth.
Even though she had only been in the Blessed Land for a few hours, Talira knew the two bosses who ran the territory while Silas was away.
First was Eluned, the Goddess of Nature.
Eluned was gentle, terrifyingly powerful, and had personally woven the magical clothes Talira was wearing right now to cover her modesty upon arrival and then there was Morwenna.
Morwenna didn’t stop to greet the cheering girls.
She walked in a perfectly straight line, completely ignoring the broken fireball demonstration, and marched directly over to Talira’s table.
Morwenna slammed both of her hands flat onto the wooden table, leaning forward until her face was inches away from the crimson dragon’s.
"So," Morwenna started, her eyes practically sparkling with excitement as she looked at the new arrival.
"Are you really a dragon?"

chapters.title: Chapter 189: Take Flight Dragon
paragraphs: Talira blinked, leaning back slightly from the pressure.
"I... yes. I am a crimson dragon."
Morwenna’s grin widened too far.
She leaned even closer, her voice dropping into a loud shameless whisper that echoed across the silent mess hall.

"Can you turn into your massive dragon form?" Morwenna asked, her eyes darting to the small wings on Talira’s back. "Because I really, really want to ride you... I want to know exactly what riding a dragon feels like when we drop out of the sky!"
Talira sat there, completely stunned into silence by the audacity of the request.
A human with divine power wanted to mount her and use her as a flying beast of burden on her very first day in the territory?
Talira slowly lowered the turkey leg, blinking her glowing red eyes in utter bewilderment.
"Oh?" Talira responded simply.
The sky above the Blessed Land territory was a suffocating bruised black, completely lacking any kind of stars or celestial bodies.
A bitter biting wind howled across the fortified courtyard, whipping fresh layers of pristine white snow across the stone flags.
Talira stood directly in the center of the training grounds, her dark crimson combat robes fluttering wildly against the chill.
She crossed her pale arms over her chest with her small draconic wings twitching defensively behind her back.
Despite the freezing ambient temperature... a temperature that instinctively made her fire-attuned biology sluggish, Talira had to admit something to herself.
She loved the attention.
Lining the elevated stone walkways and crowding around the perimeter of the courtyard were dozens of the territory’s women.
Combatants, mages, and Shieldmaidens alike had completely abandoned their duties just to stare at the newly arrived crimson dragon.
Their eyes were wide with genuine awe, whispering excitedly among themselves as they pointed at her wings and the glowing scales accenting her collarbone.
"By the anvil, would you look at the architecture on that lass?" a loud boisterous voice boomed over the howling wind.
It was Thora.
The dwarven blacksmith was leaning against a stone wall with a massive tankard of alcohol gripped in her calloused soot-stained hand.

Her eyes tracked the curve of Talira’s waist down to her hips with blatant shameless appreciation. Thora let out a raucous whistle, taking a long gulp from her tankard before shouting across the courtyard.

"I’ve forged a thousand breastplates in me time, but none of ’em could hold a candle to what the gods gave you, scaly!" Thora cheered, offering a perverted suggestive wink. "If you ever need your armor fitted or completely removed, you just come down to the forge, aye? I’ll give you a proper thorough inspection!"
Talira’s entire face flushed a violent shade of crimson.
Her reptilian pupils narrowed to sharp vertical slits with her teeth grinding together as a spark of white-hot fire sputtered from her lips.
She glared at the dwarf, actively wondering in her mind if she could simply open her jaws and blast the perverted blacksmith’s head off her shoulders with a condensed fireball.
Before Talira could act on her draconic aggression, a heavy, familiar hand dropped onto her shoulder.
"You will get used to it," Morwenna said casually.
The Pirate Queen was standing right beside her, wearing lightweight leather armor that completely defied the freezing weather.
Morwenna didn’t look at Talira; she was grinning wildly at the assembled crowd, completely reveling in the chaotic energy of the territory.
Around the perimeter, several other veteran women including Rowenna, Tasmin, Fenna, Brida and others knowingly nodded their heads in agreement with Morwenna’s assessment.
Living in Blessed Land meant dealing with Thora’s shameless tavern commentary on a daily basis.
Seeing the entire crowd casually dismiss her flirtations, Thora slammed her tankard against the stone railing.
"Hey! Don’t act like you lot weren’t thinking the exact same thing! Give a dwarf some credit!"
Standing a few paces away from the boisterous crowd, completely silent and isolated in her own aura, was Lady Eluned.
The Goddess of Nature stood with her pale hands clasped loosely in front of her emerald robes.
Unlike the excited soldiers, Eluned’s stunning face was pale, drawn, and deeply shadowed by exhaustion.
Her golden-green eyes stared blankly into the howling snowstorm, completely unfocused.
Morwenna caught sight of the melancholic deity and smirked.
She strolled over, slinging an arm over Eluned’s shoulder and roughly shaking her.

"Cheer up, weed," Morwenna teased mercilessly, poking Eluned’s cheek. "Why the long face? You look like you just watched a forest burn down. We got a literal dragon in the barracks today so celebrate a little!"
Eluned did not even react to the insulting nickname or the physical nudging.
Her divine aura remained completely flat, vibrating with an aching anxiety. That was exactly how worried she was about Silas.
"I miss him," Eluned sighed exhaustedly, her voice barely louder than the falling snow.

She closed her eyes, clutching the fabric of her robes over her heart. "The Hero tether is fluctuating due to the spatial distance. If something happens to his core in the dark... if he does not return..."
Talira watched the grieving goddess.

According to the ancient history her rotting mother had drilled into her skull, Eluned was a divine entity... one of the very gods Talira was inherently supposed to hate with every fiber of her being.
Gods were the oppressors yet, looking at Eluned’s trembling shoulders and the genuine sorrow destroying her divine composure, Talira felt her inherited hatred completely melt away.
She didn’t see a tyrannical deity; she just saw a woman deeply, hopelessly in love with the same human who had spared Talira’s life hours ago.
Talira didn’t want Eluned to feel sad at all.
Talira took two tentative steps forward, clearing her throat to catch the goddess’s attention.

"You do not need to grieve, Miss Eluned," Talira said softly, her dual-harmonic voice cutting clearly through the wind. "Lord Silas... he is doing alright. When I departed the labyrinth, his core was exceptionally dense. He had already claimed several high-tier artifacts, and he had that terrifying elf guarding his flank."
Talira offered a stiff but genuinely reassuring nod. "He is far too stubborn to die in a place like that as he will be back soon."
She was just saying anything at this point.
Eluned’s golden-green eyes snapped wide open.
The stagnant aura surrounding her instantly vanished, replaced by a radiant blooming warmth that melted the snow falling around her boots.
She perked up immediately, stepping forward and taking both of Talira’s pale hands in her own.
"Truly?" Eluned breathed out, a breathtaking relieved smile illuminating her face. "His core was steady? Oh, thank you, Talira. Thank you for telling me."
"Bah! Enough of the emotional weeping!" Morwenna interrupted loudly, clapping her hands together with a deafening sound.
She pointed a finger at Talira, her eyes flaring with anticipation.
"We didn’t come out into the freezing snow to talk about the Boss’s health! Get on with it, dragon! Show us what you look like with all your scales on!"
Talira looked around the courtyard.
The dozens of women were staring at her expectantly, cheering and stamping their boots against the frozen stone to build a rhythm.
Talira’s heart hammered against her ribs. Her draconic pride flared, completely overriding the ambient chill.
"Step back," Talira commanded.
The women rapidly cleared a massive fifty-foot circle in the center of the courtyard.
Talira closed her eyes.
She reached deep into the center of her being, forcibly unlocking the power of her primordial bloodline.
She tapped into the sovereign energy Silas had injected into her core during her tethering.
FWOOSH!
A catastrophic wave of crimson pressure erupted from her skin, instantly vaporizing the snow in the courtyard into a massive hissing cloud of steam.
CRACK! SNAP! KRA-THOOM!
The terrifying symphony of breaking bones and expanding cartilage echoed off the barracks walls.
Talira’s spine violently elongated, tearing through her humanoid silhouette as her body aggressively expanded outward.
Her pale skin hardened, erupting into thick, overlapping layers of burning crimson scales that glowed like molten iron.

Her jaw unhinged, extending into a massive, jagged reptilian snout filled with sword-sized fangs, while two massive leathery wings unfurled with a concussive sound that blew the loose snow off the barracks roofs.
WHOOSH!
Within four seconds, the curvaceous woman was entirely gone.
Standing in the center of the Blessed Land courtyard was a massive, fifty-foot-tall primordial crimson dragon.
"ROOOOOOOOOAAAR!"
Talira reared back on her massive hind legs and unleashed an earth-shattering roar toward the black sky.
The concussive soundwave physically shook the stone foundations of the fortress, rattling the weapons in the armory and vibrating the chest cavities of everyone present.
The assembled women trembled violently with their survival instincts screaming at the sight of an apex predator but a second later, their fear dissolved into joy.
"HELL YES!" Thora roared, raising her tankard high. "LOOK AT THAT BEAST!"
The entire courtyard erupted into deafening cheers.
The combatants and mages screamed her name, whistling and applauding the majestic perfection of her draconic form.
Hearing the overwhelming adoration, Talira let out a low, rumbling growl of satisfaction.
Even in her massive, terrifying reptilian form, she could feel her face heating up, blushing deeply beneath her crimson scales.
Before she could even lower her forelegs to the ground, a blur of movement shot through the steam.
THUD!
Morwenna leaped twenty feet into the air, landing heavily and securely directly between Talira’s massive shoulder blades.
The Pirate Queen grabbed onto two protruding dorsal spikes, her face plastered with a joyous grin.
"I claimed the front seat!" Morwenna yelled down at the courtyard.
Down below, Eluned stepped forward to the edge of the melted circle. She looked up at the massive dragon’s reptilian eye with her emerald robes fluttering.
"Talira," Eluned asked politely, her voice carrying divine grace. "May I have your permission to board as well?"
Talira lowered her massive snout, blinking her glowing red eye, and gave a gentle rumbling nod of consent.
Once the permission was given, Eluned didn’t use stairs or wind magic.

She simply took a single, graceful step forward, her body dissolving into a flurry of glowing green leaves that swirled upward and rematerialized securely on Talira’s broad back, seating herself right behind Morwenna.
"Hold on!" Talira’s booming dual-harmonic voice resonated from deep within her chest.
FLAP! KRA-THOOM!
Talira aggressively brought her massive wings down.
The downward stroke generated a localized hurricane that slammed into the courtyard floor, launching her massive multi-ton body vertically into the freezing black sky with terrifying acceleration.
She soared upward, breaking completely past the cloud layer in seconds.
Feeling the boundless freedom of the open air after years of imprisonment, Talira let loose.
She banked sharply to the left, carving a glowing crimson arc through the dark sky, before diving into a series of breathtaking high-speed vertical loops.

The cold wind howled across her scales as she executed a flawless barrel roll, before suddenly throwing her massive wings completely open, aggressively catching the air currents to come to a dead stop hovering high above the territory.
Down below in the illuminated courtyard, the entire territory went wild.
"TALIRA! TALIRA! TALIRA!"
Everyone cheered for her at the top of their lungs, waving their weapons at her.
Up on her back, Morwenna was throwing her fists in the air, howling with laughter while Eluned clapped her hands together with a brilliant smile lighting up her divine face.
Hovering peacefully in the cool night air, listening to the laughter of a goddess and a Pirate on her back, Talira looked down at the glowing warm lights of the Blessed Land territory.
’This is... amazing!’ Talira thought, her ancient heart swelling with a warmth that had nothing to do with her fire core.
She closed her eyes, letting the wind wash over her scales. ’To be free... to be welcomed instead of hunted... I wonder what that "saintly" human is doing right now.’
Thousands of miles away, inside the Secret Realm, that same saintly human was currently having a very bad morning.
"Die Fuckers!"
A loud aggressive shout echoed across the open desert dunes, instantly accompanied by the feeling of a high-tier wind incantation.
FWOOSH!
A violent pressurized gale of slicing wind blasted across the sand, carrying a dense cloud of abrasive dust and freezing desert air that slammed directly into Silas Graves’s face.
Silas physically flinched with his head jerking back as the grit hit his eyelids.
His Gold Core was still sluggish from the deep sleep with his instincts desperately trying to boot up as he groaned, raising a calloused hand to shield his face.

"Give me five more minutes, Elu..." Silas mumbled sleepily, his mind completely disoriented as he mistook the cold wind for Eluned opening a window back in their bedroom at the territory. "The administrative reports can wait..."
"Lord Sy! Wake up immediately!"

Up on her back, Morwenna was throwing her fists in the air, howling with laughter while Eluned clapped her hands together with a brilliant smile lighting up her divine face.
Hovering peacefully in the cool night air, listening to the laughter of a goddess and a Pirate on her back, Talira looked down at the glowing warm lights of the Blessed Land territory.
’This is... amazing!’ Talira thought, her ancient heart swelling with a warmth that had nothing to do with her fire core.
She closed her eyes, letting the wind wash over her scales. ’To be free... to be welcomed instead of hunted...
I wonder what that "saintly" human is doing right now.’
Thousands of miles away, inside the Secret Realm, that same saintly human was currently having a very bad morning.
"Die Fuckers!"
A loud aggressive shout echoed across the open desert dunes, instantly accompanied by the feeling of a high-tier wind incantation.
FWOOSH!
A violent pressurized gale of slicing wind blasted across the sand, carrying a dense cloud of abrasive dust and freezing desert air that slammed directly into Silas Graves’s face.
Silas physically flinched with his head jerking back as the grit hit his eyelids.
His Gold Core was still sluggish from the deep sleep with his instincts desperately trying to boot up as he groaned, raising a calloused hand to shield his face.
"Give me five more minutes, Elu..." Silas mumbled sleepily, his mind completely disoriented as he mistook the cold wind for Eluned opening a window back in their bedroom at the territory.
"The administrative reports can wait..."
"Lord Sy!
Wake up immediately!"

chapters.title: Chapter 190: Against Lords
paragraphs: Aeliana’s urgent crystal-clear voice echoed directly next to his ear, carrying a sharp spike of elven mana that physically jolted his nervous system.
Silas’s glowing golden-ringed eyes snapped wide open.
The very first thing his perception registered was that he was not in a bed, nor was he walking on solid ground.
He was currently being carried.
Aeliana had him securely in her slender, pale hands, holding him in a protective carry as she sprinted forward across the desert sand at terrifying superhuman speed.
He looked up.

Looping directly ahead of their trajectory, looming a long distance away against the harsh amber sky, was a massive ancient structure... a towering, sixty-story spire constructed entirely of black fused desert glass and swirling sand.
Silas rapidly turned his head, assessing his immediate surroundings.
The whole group was tightly clustered around him in a high-speed defensive formation.
Aeliana was setting the pace at the group.
Directly to her right, running with heavy, thudding strides, was Valerius Sterling, his gold armor clanking rhythmically.
On Valerius’s shoulder, Mia was actively balancing herself, yawning sleepily while keeping one hand pressed against Valerius’s neck to funnel him stabilizing water mana.
And trailing just a few paces behind them, running with light electric grace, was Harper.
And last but not least, Silas realized they were completely out in the open desert and they were absolutely not alone.
Swarming across the dunes half a mile behind them was a massive, thundering horde of rival Valoria coalition Lords and their summoned Heroes.
"Get back here, Sterling!" a deafening arrogant roar echoed across the sand.
Silas looked back.
Leading the pursuers was the armored Spear Lord riding atop a massive, two-ton armored siege Rhino that was violently tearing up the sand as it charged.
Trailing right beside him was Lord Julian, his twin swords drawn, and several other purple core and blue core elites.
"Valerius!" Silas barked, completely shedding his drowsiness as he looked at the blonde aristocrat running beside them. "What the hell is going on?! Why is half the Lords hunting us like dogs?!"
Valerius offered a breathless, grimacing smirk as he hurdled a jagged sand rock.
"Welcome back to the land of the living, Graves! While you were busy snoring away in the Elf’s lap, that sadistic dead god triggered the third Quest for all remaining Lords!"
Silas didn’t wait for permission. He placed his hands on Aeliana’s shoulders and violently pushed off, jumping cleanly out of her hands.
He hit the desert sand running, his boots sinking into the grit as his mana instantly ignited, matching Aeliana’s top speed stride-for-stride.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
Three high-velocity steel-tipped armor-piercing arrows suddenly screamed out of the sky, fired from the backline archers of the pursuing horde directly toward Aeliana’s exposed back.
Silas didn’t even look over his shoulder.
He smoothly drew his mythril longsword in a single fluid motion, bringing the blade up in a lightning-fast horizontal parry.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
He effortlessly deflected all three arrows mid-sprint, shattering their wooden shafts and sending the razor-sharp broadheads spinning harmlessly into the sand dunes.
"Explain the quest!" Silas demanded, keeping his eyes locked on the distant sand spire.

"It’s that damned map you took from Harper!" Valerius shouted over the howling wind of their sprint. "Ititus broadcasted a global notification across the entire Secret Realm! He announced that the Treasure Map leads directly to the Vault inside that Sand Spire where his highest-tier divine treasures and the primary Realm Core are stored!"
Valerius spat a mouthful of sand as his face went dark with rage.

"But here is the catch! The map acts as an active high-frequency magical homing beacon! Every single Lord within fifty miles can currently sense our exact spatial coordinates on their system interfaces! The god literally told all of them to hunt down and slaughter whichever group is holding the scroll before they reach the Spire doors!"
As if on cue, the dead God’s voice boomed from the amber heavens, vibrating with sadistic glee.

"Run, little mice, run!" Ititus laughed hysterically over the broadcast. "The Spire doors will seal the moment the map holder crosses the threshold! If you want my greatest treasures, you must tear the scroll from their cold dead hands! Show me a bloodbath!"
Silas let out a deeply exhausted sigh, sheathing his sword as he ran.
"I hate this go. So what do we do now? We can’t outrun a siege Rhino all the way to the Spire without getting surrounded by their outriders."
Before Valerius could offer a tactical formation, Harper accelerated her stride, pulling up directly alongside Silas.
Her purple eyes were glowing with intense electrical mana.
Unlike her pathetic, shivering performance from the night before, her face was set in an expression of resolve.

"You keep running," Harper told them with her voice clear and commanding over the wind. "I am the one who handed you that map... I am the one who implicated your group in this beacon trap and therefore, I will be the one to deal with the pursuing Lords."
She slid to a halt in the sand, turning her back to the towering Sand Spire and facing the thundering army of rival Lords charging across the dunes.
"I will hold the rear and buy you the time you need to enter the Spire," Harper stated.
Before anyone could speak, before Silas could even open his mouth to question her sudden suicidal heroism, Harper blurred forward with a spark of lightning.
She grabbed the lapels of Silas’s dusty trench coat, pulled him down toward her face, and aggressively pressed her lips directly against his cheek in a firm kiss.
Silas froze mid-stride, his eyes widening in shock.
Harper pulled back, offering him a breathtaking, wild smile that sparkled with violet static.
"If I don’t die out here today, Silas Graves..." Harper whispered, her eyes locking onto his. "...you better take me out on a proper date when we get back to Valoria."

"Hey! Get your filthy lips off my Lord!" Aeliana snarled, her elven pointed ears standing straight up as she reached for her dagger, ready to skin the lightning mage alive. "I better not catch you touching him again!"
However, the verbal reprimand fell on empty ears.
Silas had already stopped moving for a split second due to the shock of the kiss, while Valerius and Mia kept running at full speed toward the Spire.
"Graves! Keep moving! Don’t let her dramatic nonsense slow us down!" Valerius roared from fifty yards ahead.

Silas gritted his teeth, grabbed the furious Aeliana by the arm, and forcibly pulled her along as he resumed his sprint toward the towering black spire, leaving Harper completely alone in the desert sand.
Harper stood perfectly still, watching Silas’s retreating back as he shrank into the distance.
She touched her fingers to her lips with a smirk crossing her face.

’That should be the best way to win his paranoid heart over, right?’ Harper thought to herself, calculating the emotional leverage. ’By selflessly sacrificing myself on the battlefield to save his life? When I survive this, his psychological defenses will be completely shattered. He won’t be able to refuse me.’
She slowly turned around, facing the thundering rival Lords.
The armored Spear Lord and his two-ton siege Rhino were less than two hundred yards away and closing fast.

To his left was Julian, and pushing through the center of the formation, riding a summoned wind-steed with her face contorted in cold rage, was Elora Verinda... the City Lord’s daughter whom Harper had violently betrayed and attacked with natural lightning the previous afternoon.
Harper spread her arms wide. Her Lord core ignited, burning with blinding power.
"Come!" Harper screamed at the incoming army.
CRACK! KRA-THOOM!
A deafening explosion of hyper-condensed purple lightning erupted from her skin, violently whipping around her body in jagged, ten-foot arcs of pure electrical destruction.
The sand beneath her boots instantly flash-melted into a crater of glowing black glass.
She didn’t wait for them to charge her. She tilted her body forward and blasted forward across the dunes like a human bolt of lightning, intercepting the group dead center.
BOOOOOM!
Harper slammed directly into the charging two-ton siege Rhino like a falling meteor.
She didn’t use a weapon as she thrust her open palm directly into the reinforced iron plating protecting the beast’s massive forehead.
"Fulgur Impact!" she roared.
The concussive electrical discharge was so catastrophic that it generated a visible shockwave of white static that ripped across the desert floor.
The iron armor shielding the Rhino’s head was instantly vaporized.
Raw millions-of-volts electricity violently flooded into the beast’s skull, completely frying its brain matter and nervous system in a microsecond.
The massive, two-ton beast let out a digitized shriek of agony, its legs buckling instantly as it skidded across the sand, flipping end-over-end before crashing to a dead smoldering halt.
The Spear Lord riding atop the beast was violently thrown from his saddle, launching forty feet through the air before crashing heavily into the sand dunes, his spear clattering away.
Before Harper could recover her stance, two rival combatants dived from the flanks with their swords slashing for her ribs.
Harper twirled in the sand, her purple hair trailing static. She dodged the first blade, but the second elite predicted her movement, driving a serrated dagger deeply into her left shoulder.
SHWK!
Blood sprayed across the sand.
Of course, when fighting a dozen elite Lords and Heroes simultaneously, she got countered and wounded but Harper didn’t flinch.
In fact, she mostly let herself take the blow to secure a clamp.
The moment the elite’s dagger pierced her flesh, Harper grabbed the man’s wrist with an iron grip, smiling wildly into his horrified eyes.
"Got you," she whispered.
She channeled her signature technique... Thunder Blood.
The spell instantly altered her biological composition, converting the iron in her boiling blood into a hyper-conductive liquid electrical medium.
ZZZZZT!
The blood spraying from her wounded shoulder violently ignited with purple lightning.
The high-voltage current traveled directly up the blood-slicked dagger, bypassing the elite’s magical wards and flooding into his arm.
"AHHHHH!"
The man screamed in agonizing torment as his muscles violently convulsed, his core completely overloading before he collapsed into the sand, smoking and paralyzed.
"You whore!" a furious voice shouted from her right.
It was Lord Julian.
The handsome man dived forward, wielding twin enchanted rapiers that blurred with lethal speed.
He slashed at her legs, trying to sever her mobility while spouting arrogant bullshit.

"You think a woman can hold us the Elite?!" Julian sneered, thrusting his rapier for her throat. "You should have stayed in the ballroom where you belong, playing dress-up for your betters! Know your place and die!"
Harper tilted her head, barely avoiding the rapier tip as it sliced a thin line of blood across her cheek.
Her glowing purple eyes locked onto Julian’s arrogant face.
"My place?" Harper repeated, her voice dropping into an eerily calm, vibrating harmonic.
She stepped directly into his guard, completely ignoring his second sword as it pierced her thigh.
She raised her right hand, pointing her index and middle fingers directly between Julian’s eyes.
"My place is standing over your ash..." Harper said.
"Thunder Lance!"
KRA-THOOM!
A beam of concentrated purple lightning erupted from her fingertips at point-blank range and the beam struck Julian dead center in the forehead.
There was no time for him to scream.
The heat of the spell completely eviscerated him. His magical shields shattered like wet paper, his flesh and armor instantly vaporizing into atomized dust.
The lightning beam continued punching through his skull, scoring a half-mile trench of melted glass through the desert sand behind him.
Julian’s twin swords fell clattering to the dirt, followed a second later by a pile of fine, smoking grey ash... the only physical remains of the arrogant Lord.

Seeing the leaders instantly eviscerated into ash, the remaining purple-core Lords and their summoned Heroes tensed, backing away in terror from the bleeding lightning-draped woman standing in the center of the carnage.
SQUELCH!
Harper pulled the rapier from her thigh with a sickening sound, tossing the bloody steel aside as her electrical blood immediately cauterized the wound.
She breathed heavily with her stamina draining rapidly as she stood alone over the defeated vanguard.
Suddenly, a massive drop in atmospheric temperature froze the air behind her.
SHING!
A razor-sharp lance of solid blue ice shot from the blind spot of a sand dune, aiming directly for the back of Harper’s neck.
Harper violently twisted her torso, throwing herself backward into the dirt just in time.
The ice lance missed her throat by a millimeter, shearing off a lock of her purple hair before embedding itself deeply into the carcass of the dead Rhino.
Harper scrambled to her feet, wiping blood from her mouth as she looked up.
Walking over the crest of the sand dune, surrounded by a swirling blizzard of freezing snow, was Elora Verinda.

chapters.title: Chapter 191: Seraphina’s True Power
paragraphs: The City Lord’s daughter looked terrifying.
Her usually immaculate blond hair was blowing wildly in the freezing wind, and her hands were encased in floating gauntlets of jagged ice.

"You dodged, huh?" Elora stated as she pointed an icy finger at Harper. "You... I have so many things to say to you, not only did you steal the map but you attacked my scout with lightning after I gave an explicit warning... You deserve to die for what you pulled last night, Harper."
Before Harper could summon another burst of lightning to defend herself, the sand to her left exploded.
FWOOSH!
A violent roaring column of white-hot fire erupted from the earth, melting the surrounding ice crystals into instant steam.
Stepping out of the flames, her crimson hair flowing like liquid fire and her curved dagger gripped tightly in her hand, Seraphina arrived.
The fiery noblewoman looked entirely different from her usual frantic screaming self.
Her face was calm and her posture was completely relaxed as her red eyes burned with a cold look.
She looked directly at Harper, completely ignoring Elora.
"Harper," Seraphina asked calmly, her voice entirely devoid of her normal furious, screaming pitch. "Where is Graves? Tell me where he went, quietly, and I will make your death painless."
The three girls stood in a tense three-way triangle in the center of the desert battlefield.
They looked at each other in complete silence.
The ambient atmosphere violently distorted around them as their respective elements sounded in reality.
There was the sharp crackling ZZZZZT of Harper’s purple lightning, the freezing crystalline KRKKKKK of Elora’s expanding ice, and the deep, volcanic FWOOOSH of Seraphina’s roaring flames.
Harper shifted her weight with her heart sinking as she analyzed the positioning.
She was wounded, her core was depleting, and she was trapped between a Noble that prided herself on Ice Magic and one for Fire.
’I’m dead,’ Harper thought desperately, bracing her bleeding arms. ’I am about to get jumped by both of them simultaneously.’
Elora stepped forward first with her ice aura flaring to freeze Harper’s boots to the sand.
"Seraphina. Help me execute this woma—"
BOOOOM!
Before Elora could even finish the sentence, Seraphina pivoted on her heel with terrifying explosive speed.
She didn’t attack Harper though.
She drove a superheated fire-wrapped right hook directly into the side of Elora Verinda’s face!
The impact was so violent that it generated a visible circular shockwave of fire and air that shattered the surrounding ice lances.
Elora’s head violently snapped to the side, her body lifting completely off the ground as she was sent flying thirty feet across the sand, crashing heavily into a sand dune with a muffled thud.

"That’s payback!" Seraphina roared, her calm demeanor instantly evaporating into unbridled rage as she shook her smoking fist at the crater. "That’s payback for making me pay that exorbitant Hero Summoning Card back then and using me yesterday, you scheming blond-haired bitch!"
Without pausing for a single heartbeat, Seraphina spun back around and violently attacked Harper too!
"And you get to die for touching my prey!" Seraphina screamed, lunging forward with her curved dagger slashing in a devastating X-shaped arc of white-hot fire.
Harper’s survival reflexes saved her life.
She violently pushed her electrical blood, blurring backward with a desperate spark of static.
The flaming dagger sliced through the front of her leather armor, scorching her skin as she narrowly dodged the lethal blows, backflipping across the melted sand to gain distance.
Over in the sand dune, the debris violently exploded outward.
Elora rose from the sand, her lip bleeding, her face contorted in pure fury. She had never been so angered and annoyed before.
"You insane uneducated arsonist!" she shrieked.
Elora rapidly made a complex, two-handed runic hand sign.
At the exact same instant, standing half a mile away on a high dune, Elora’s summoned Hero also helped as well!
The Hero slammed her staff into the earth, channeling her mana pool directly into Elora to amplify the spell.
"Glacial Sepulcher!" Elora commanded.
KRKKKKKKKKKKKK!

A massive sixty-foot-tall dome of ultra-dense magical blue ice violently erupted from the desert floor, instantly enclosing all three girls... Elora, Seraphina, and Harper within a sealed, inescapable arena.
The temperature inside the dome cratered to absolute zero instantly.
The walls of the ice dome were actively freezing from the inside out, emitting a terrifying high-frequency dampening field.

The white-hot frost aggressively crept up their leather boots, rapidly scaling their legs and torsos, forcibly freezing their mana pathways and completely stopping their respective elements from taking control of the atmospheric ambient energy!
Harper gasped as the frost encased her knees with her purple lightning violently sputtering and dying out. "My mana... it’s locked!"
Elora spat a wad of blood onto the ice, glaring at Seraphina with cold triumph.
"The internal dampening field suppresses all elemental ignition beneath the Sovereign realm. You can’t cast your fire here, Seraphina. You are just a powerless mortal in a cage..."
However, all Seraphina did was laugh.
She stood in the dead center of the freezing dome with the ice rapidly scaling up to her waist, and let out a loud peal of laughter that echoed off the frozen walls.

"You think I need atmospheric fire, you arrogant fool?" Seraphina mocked, her red eyes flashing with terrifying power. "I am a favored daughter of the World Council! Did you really think I came into this Secret Realm without a trump card?!"
Seraphina raised her hand to her face and called upon her own Hero!
Unlike baseline Lords who summoned physical warriors or mages to walk beside them, Seraphina had utilized a Mythic-tier binding contract.
Her Hero was an ancient formless Primordial Fire Spirit!
FWOOSH!
The space around Seraphina’s head violently distorted.

Instead of a person materializing, the Primordial Fire Spirit instantly appeared directly upon her flesh, manifesting as an intricate glowing white-hot runic mark that violently burned itself across the left side of her face and down her neck!
The thermal density of the Primordial Spirit completely bypassed Elora’s ice dampening field.
The ice encasing Seraphina’s waist violently flash-melted into boiling water, then instantly vaporized into superheated steam.
Seraphina tilted her head back, the glowing mark on her face illuminating the freezing dome like a localized sun.
She looked down at Elora and Harper, who were both staring at her in paralyzed horror.
Seraphina pointed her finger directly at the ceiling of the ice dome, throwing her head back as she laughed at Elora and the two of them with supremacy.
"Boom!" Seraphina said simply.
KA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
What followed was a cataclysmic explosion of primordial flames so pure, so astronomically concentrated, that it completely defied the laws of thermal dynamics.
A blinding white-hot pillar of pure solar energy erupted from Seraphina’s body, violently expanding outward in a fraction of a microsecond.
The sixty-foot dome of ultra-dense blue ice didn’t just melt... it was completely eviscerated into atomized hydrogen and oxygen, annihilated from physical existence!
The concussive shockwave was so immense that the desert ground violently trembled for miles in every direction.
The tectonic vibration shook the entire landscape, physically rattling even Silas, Valerius, and Aeliana who were currently several miles away, climbing the high stone steps of the Spire entrance.
Silas stumbled on the black glass steps, grabbing the doorframe to steady himself as he looked back over his shoulder toward the distant mushroom cloud of white fire rising into the amber sky.
Across the smoking vitrified desert wasteland, the glass rain had been completely vaporized.

Where the ice dome had once stood was now a massive, fifty-foot-deep crater of bubbling white-hot magma and echoing out from the dead center of that apocalyptic inferno, cutting cleanly through the roaring flames and the falling ash, only the sound of Seraphina laughing hysterically could be heard.
Standing on the Spire steps beside Silas, Valerius Sterling watched the distant column of solar fire ascend into the heavens.
He felt his wind core shudder in his chest, a drop of cold sweat rolling down his cheek as he remembered the girl he had grown up with in the city.
Valerius slowly shook his head, gripping his sword hilt tightly as he thought to himself:
’She’s still a monster... through and through.’
FWOOSH!
Out of the apocalyptic column of solar fire that had completely eviscerated the sixty-foot ice dome, a dark silhouette violently broke through the wall of white-hot flames.
It was Harper.
The purple-haired Lord jumped out of the blinding inferno, her ruined leather armor smoking and actively catching fire at the edges.
She didn’t fall to the desert floor as she was floating in the air, utilizing a hyper-dense electromagnetic field beneath her boots to physically repel herself from the superheated ground.
Her chest heaved, her pale skin covered in soot but her purple eyes burned with unyielding defiance.
"Is that the best you have, you pampered arsonist?!" Harper screamed over the roaring flames.
She violently thrust both of her hands forward with her Lord core igniting.

She fired dozens of concentrated, jagged strikes of purple lightning directly into the center of the roaring white flames, the electrical arcs completely tearing through the thermal currents in a desperate attempt to locate her target.
A split second later, out of the opposite side of the fire pillar, a massive, jagged crystal of ultra-dense blue ice violently burst out.
The ice crystal shattered, and Elora Verinda tumbled out onto the baking sand, coughing violently as thick suffocating smoke filled her lungs.
Elora’s usually immaculate blond hair was singed, and the pristine fabric of her City Lord robes was scorched black.
She scrambled to her knees, her eyes wide with terror at the impossible magnitude of the output she had just witnessed.

Still, her survival instincts flared. She raised her hands, wildly blasting erratic desperate torrents of absolute-zero ice back into the flames, trying to suppress the heat that was actively melting her magic.
However, it was all for absolutely naught.
The massive, towering column of white flames violently dispersed, parting like a curtain.
Standing in the dead center of the glassed, molten crater, completely untouched by the lightning and the ice, was Seraphina but she didn’t look like herself.
The fiery red hair that usually tumbled down her back had completely changed color.
It was now a radiant silver, glowing with the pure energy of the Primordial Fire Spirit currently fused to her soul.
The intricate, white-hot runic mark burned brightly across the left side of her face and down her pale neck, illuminating the desert like a newborn star.
Seraphina stood there, laughing.
It wasn’t her usual angry scream. It was a cold and utterly terrifying laugh that resonated with the power she currently wielded.
"How do you like it?!" Seraphina taunted them, her silver hair whipping wildly in the heated updrafts.
She lazily swatted a jagged bolt of Harper’s purple lightning out of the air with the back of her bare hand, completely disintegrating the electrical current before it could even touch her skin.

"Did you honestly think a City Lord’s daughter and a corporate rat could match the raw bloodline of the Bloom Clan?" Seraphina asked, her voice echoing with absolute supremacy. "My first Hero was not a simple swordsman or a baseline elementalist... It was a Primordial Fire Spirit who possessed the unique inherent ability to multiply the baseline fire output of its bonded Mage by a factor of ten!"
She slowly raised her hands, white-hot solar flames aggressively coiling around her slender fingers like obedient serpents.
"And in her hands... I am simply unstoppable," Seraphina declared.
She turned her glowing eyes away from the two kneeling Lords for a brief, fleeting microsecond.
She glanced miles into the distance, looking toward the towering black sand Spire where Silas Graves and the rest of his group had retreated.
As she looked in the direction of the dark-haired Lord who had carried her out of the Abyss by her rear end, a small uncharacteristic blush briefly touched her glowing cheeks.
"And with this power..." Seraphina whispered to herself, the flames flickering around her lips. "...I will kill Silas Graves."
But... the threat lacked her usual vicious bite.
Where was the furious ear-piercing shout?
Where was the unbridled outrage?
Was she actually not mad at him for seeing her naked? For touching her? For humiliating her?

In truth, the overwhelming terror of falling into the Abyss, followed immediately by the suffocating, muscular warmth of his arms wrapping around her to pull her to safety, had completely short-circuited her pampered worldview.
She was incredibly confused, embarrassed, and very terrified of the fluttering sensation in her chest.

Seraphina aggressively shook her head, forcing her silver hair out of her eyes to banish the Lord’s face from her mind as her glowing eyes snapped back to Harper, floating in the air a hundred yards away.

"And you get to die for touching my prey!" Seraphina screamed, lunging forward with her curved dagger slashing in a devastating X-shaped arc of white-hot fire.
Harper’s survival reflexes saved her life.
She violently pushed her electrical blood, blurring backward with a desperate spark of static.
The flaming dagger sliced through the front of her leather armor, scorching her skin as she narrowly dodged the lethal blows, backflipping across the melted sand to gain distance.
Over in the sand dune, the debris violently exploded outward.
Elora rose from the sand, her lip bleeding, her face contorted in pure fury.
She had never been so angered and annoyed before.
"You insane uneducated arsonist!" she shrieked.
Elora rapidly made a complex, two-handed runic hand sign.
At the exact same instant, standing half a mile away on a high dune, Elora’s summoned Hero also helped as well!
The Hero slammed her staff into the earth, channeling her mana pool directly into Elora to amplify the spell.
"Glacial Sepulcher!" Elora commanded.
KRKKKKKKKKKKKK!
A massive sixty-foot-tall dome of ultra-dense magical blue ice violently erupted from the desert floor, instantly enclosing all three girls...
Elora, Seraphina, and Harper within a sealed, inescapable arena.
The temperature inside the dome cratered to absolute zero instantly.
The walls of the ice dome were actively freezing from the inside out, emitting a terrifying high-frequency dampening field.

The white-hot frost aggressively crept up their leather boots, rapidly scaling their legs and torsos, forcibly freezing their mana pathways and completely stopping their respective elements from taking control of the atmospheric ambient energy!
