chapters.title: Chapter 192: Under The Spire [I]
paragraphs: "I promised you that your death would be swift for touching what is mine..." Seraphina stated coldly.
Floating in the air, Harper didn’t cower.
She wiped a trail of blood from her lip, a wild grin stretching across her face as blinding purple lightning violently flashed across her skin.
"Try it, you silver-haired freak," Harper told the woman, her voice crackling with static.
BOOOOM!
Seraphina didn’t hesitate.
She lunged forward with her boots completely melting the glass floor as she moved at supersonic speeds.
She swung her right arm in a massive, sweeping arc, unleashing a devastating, sixty-foot-wide crescent blade of white-hot fire directly at Harper.
Harper didn’t attempt to block the solar-tier heat.
She violently manipulated her electromagnetic field, dropping out of the air like a stone to avoid the blade, then instantly blasting forward across the sand to close the distance.
"Fulgur Lance!" Harper roared.
She thrust her hands forward, firing a dense continuous beam of purple lightning directly at Seraphina’s chest.
KRKKKKK!
Before the lightning could connect, the desert sand violently erupted between them.
Elora Verinda was not going to sit on the sidelines and be ignored.
To match these two terrifying monsters, Elora had completely closed her eyes, biting her lip until it bled as she tapped into her deepest reserves of power.
’These two are truly on another level...’
Elora unleashed the pure power of frost, violently freezing the sand, the ambient moisture, and the melted glass across the entire battlefield.
A massive twenty-foot-thick wall of solid blue ice erupted from the ground, perfectly intercepting Harper’s lightning beam.
The ice violently shattered, sending massive shards flying across the arena like shrapnel as they all went at each other simultaneously.
There were no alliances and there were no truces.
Elora was desperately trying to kill Harper for her betrayal, violently raising massive razor-sharp pillars of ice from the ground to impale the floating lightning mage.
At the exact same time, Elora was desperately trying to kill Seraphina, firing hundreds of high-velocity ice shards to suppress the overwhelming solar heat that was actively melting her armor.
"Die, you rat!" Elora screamed, slamming her hands against the frozen sand.
SHWK! SHWK! SHWK!
Three massive ten-foot-long spears of solid ice shot out of the ground directly beneath Harper.
Harper was attacking as well as desperately defending.
She twisted violently in the air with her purple hair whipping around her face.
She used her blood to violently increase her reaction time, cleanly dodging the first two ice spears but she was fighting a two-on-one battle against monsters.
The third ice spear clipped her right side, brutally tearing through her leather armor and slicing a deep horrific gash across her ribs.
Blood sprayed through the air, immediately vaporizing into steam as Seraphina arrived.
"Burn!" Seraphina roared, completely ignoring the ice.
Seraphina lunged directly through Elora’s freezing barrage, the white-hot flames of the Primordial Spirit effortlessly melting the ice shards before they could even touch her skin.
She closed the distance on Harper, driving a devastating, fire-wrapped punch directly toward the lightning mage’s face.
KRA-THOOM!
Harper barely managed to cross her arms, forming a desperate static shield.
The impact of Seraphina’s punch violently shattered the electrical barrier, sending Harper crashing backward into the frozen sand.
CRUNCH!
Before Harper could even roll to her feet, Elora capitalized on the opening.
She slammed her boot down, violently raising a jagged spike of ice that punched cleanly through Harper’s left calf, physically pinning her to the desert floor!
"AGGGGH!" Harper shrieked in agony with her blood pouring over the blue ice.
Elora panted heavily, her blue hair plastered to her sweaty forehead.

She was deeply wounded herself with her arms covered in severe electrical burns from Harper’s earlier strikes but her summoned Hero... a high level Frost Mage equipped with baseline healing magic was standing safely on a distant dune, desperately channeling green restorative mana into Elora’s back, actively healing her minor wounds over the course of the battle.

Meanwhile, Seraphina’s wounds from the flying ice shrapnel simply burned with white-hot fire, the sheer thermal density of the Primordial Spirit instantly cauterizing and sealing her flesh the microsecond it was cut.
"It’s over, Harper!" Elora declared, raising both hands to summon a final, massive execution block of ice to crush the pinned lightning mage.
But Harper was not done doing damage.
Pinned to the ground, bleeding profusely from her ribs and her impaled leg, Harper’s purple eyes violently flared with completely unhinged, psychotic lethality.
"If I die..." Harper rasped, blood bubbling past her lips as she grabbed the ice spike piercing her leg with both hands. "...I am taking both of you entitled bitches to hell with me!"
ZZZZZZZZZT!
Harper completely abandoned her defensive spells as she poured every single remaining drop of her Lord core directly into the Blood spell.
A catastrophic, blinding wave of purple electricity erupted from her pinned body.
The raw voltage traveled directly through the ice spike pinning her leg, violently back-feeding through the magical connection straight into Elora’s core!
"Ahhhh!" Elora shrieked, dropping to her knees as her nervous system violently convulsed under the massive electrical overload.

At the same time, Harper fired a desperate blast of lightning directly at Seraphina’s chest, managing to cleanly pierce through the solar flames and strike the Magistrate’s daughter, sending Seraphina stumbling backward with a smoking crater in her armor.
At the climax of the brutal bloody battle, when Harper was genuinely near death with her organs actively failing and her vision swimming with dark spots...
Standing at the base of the towering, sixty-story black sand Spire, Silas Graves was currently ignoring the distant explosions entirely.
He stood directly in front of the massive, completely featureless iron doors that sealed the entrance to the Spire.
The doors were engraved with ancient indecipherable runes, and they completely lacked a physical keyhole or a handle.
Valerius, Aeliana, and Mia were clustered around him, staring up at the imposing structure.
"So," Silas sighed, wiping sweat from his brow. "We made it. We have the map. How exactly do we open the damn door?"
As if waiting for the prompt, the dead god’s voice boomed directly from the black glass walls of the Spire itself.

"Congratulations on surviving the sprint, my little Lords!" Ititus laughed cheerfully, his voice echoing across the empty dunes. "To unlock the Vault and claim my ultimate treasures, simply place the Treasure Map directly against the center of the iron door!"
Silas and Valerius immediately looked at each other with their faces identical masks of deep suspicion.
"Absolutely not," Valerius stated flatly, shaking his head. "I am not touching that door."
"Agreed," Silas nodded, crossing his arms.
They stood there for a full minute, arguing on whether to even follow the instructions at all.
They decided they couldn’t trust the pathological lying god enough to do exactly what he said.
The last time they followed his literal directions with the cave riddle, the floor collapsed and dropped Silas as well as the rest of them into the Abyss.
"He probably meant the exact opposite," Silas deduced. "If he says put it on the door, it’s a trap. We should put it on the ground."
"Sound logic," Valerius agreed, stepping back. "Put it on the ground."
Silas didn’t hesitate.
He took the heavy roll of paper out of his coat, crouched down, and placed it completely flat on the black sand directly in front of the door.
For a moment, nothing happened then, the god’s voice echoed again, and this time, the sadistic cheerfulness was completely gone.
"You idiots," Ititus sighed deeply, his voice sounding genuinely exhausted. "This time, I actually wasn’t joking."
Silas’s golden eyes widened.
"Wait—"
KRA-KRA-KRA-THOOM!
Massive, glowing red fault lines violently shot across the entire body of the sixty-story tower.

The structural integrity of the ancient Spire, triggered by the incorrect placement of the map, completely failed as the black glass shattered, the iron doors buckled, and the massive towering structure violently collapsed!
All of their eyes widened in paralyzing horror as millions of tons of black sand, fused glass, and iron plummeted directly down toward them.
"Aeli!" Silas roared, reaching for her.
But it was too late.
The collapsing tower fell, instantly consuming Silas, Valerius, Aeliana, and Mia under an inescapable avalanche of absolute darkness.
The force of the collapsing Spire didn’t just stay there.
It violently spread outward across the desert like a massive, rolling tidal wave of black sand and debris.
The shockwave roared across the dunes, consuming the pursuing Lords that had fallen behind, completely burying their summoned Heroes, their mounts, and their ambitions in seconds.
The tidal wave of destruction continued expanding, racing across the desert miles away until it reached the molten crater where the three girls were fighting to the death.

Seraphina was currently standing over the bleeding broken body of Harper. She had summoned a superheated, white-hot flaming spear and driven it cleanly through Harper’s chest, pinning the lightning mage to the glass.
"Hehe... What did you say about taking us with you, bitch?"

Seraphina was physically lifting her up by the shaft, her silver hair whipping wildly as she looked into Harper’s fading purple eyes, thoroughly enjoying the sight of the blood spilling down the steel.
Suddenly, a massive shadow fell over them and Seraphina slowly turned her head with her glowing red eyes widening as she looked up.
A hundred-foot-tall tsunami of black sand and shattered glass was roaring directly toward them.
The avalanche washed over them instantly, violently consuming Seraphina and the bleeding Harper under millions of tons of suffocating debris.
A hundred yards away, Elora saw the wall of death approaching.
"What the fuck is that?!"
Elora’s summoned Hero desperately tried attacking it, firing massive blasts of ice to shatter the wave.
KKKKT! KKT!

When that didn’t even dent the momentum, the Hero slammed her staff into the ground, summoning a massive, fifty-foot-thick wall of solid blue ice to protect her Lord but the apocalyptic mass of the collapsing Spire was absolute.
CRASH!
The avalanche of black sand violently broke through the ice wall like wet paper, completely consuming Elora and her Hero, dragging them down into the suffocating crushing darkness of the earth.
Drip! Drip!
The echoing sound of water slowly dripping onto stone eventually penetrated the suffocating darkness of Silas’s mind.
"Wake up, my little Lords!"
The god’s voice suddenly boomed, waking Silas up with a violent jolt.
Silas gasped, his eyes snapping open.
He pushed himself up onto his elbows, coughing violently as he expelled a lungful of dry, ancient dust.

"Welcome, survivors!" Ititus cheered happily over the invisible broadcast. "You failed the door puzzle! But fear not! You were not crushed to death! You have simply been dropped into the Treasury Dungeon! This is the true labyrinth where the real treasures were kept safely beneath the Spire!"
Silas forced himself up into a sitting position on the cold stone floor, his head spinning.

"However," the god continued, his voice dripping with sadistic amusement. "In the chaos of the sand collapse, all of your little factions and alliances have been completely separated and randomized across the labyrinth! You are all entirely alone in the dark!"
Silas’s heart hammered in his chest.
Separated?

"Listen closely!" the Lord instructed them, his voice taking on a heavy, serious tone. "Hidden somewhere in this labyrinth is the Realm Core! As long as you find the Core, you can completely absorb its power! Doing so will not only actively destroy this Secret Realm, but it will automatically guide you to my most valuable, divine treasures! Happy hunting!"
The broadcast clicked off, leaving Silas sitting in the damp, dimly lit stone corridor.
Silas coughed out again, wiping soot from his eyes as he sat up properly.
"Aeli?" Silas called out, his voice echoing down the dark tunnels. "Valerius? Mia?"
He rapidly searched his immediate surroundings, looking down the branching corridors but he didn’t find them.
The group had been completely scattered as he was alone then, he heard a wet ragged cough from the shadows nearby.
Silas instantly drew his mythril longsword, his Gold Core flaring as he spun toward the sound.
Lying in a crumple broken heap near a collapsed stone pillar was a body.
Silas slowly lowered his sword, his eyes narrowing as he walked over to investigate.
He winced visibly at the sight.
It was the charred mutilated body of Harper.

sentences.text: "I promised you that your death would be swift for touching what is mine..." Seraphina stated coldly.
Floating in the air, Harper didn’t cower.
She wiped a trail of blood from her lip, a wild grin stretching across her face as blinding purple lightning violently flashed across her skin.
"Try it, you silver-haired freak," Harper told the woman, her voice crackling with static.
BOOOOM!
Seraphina didn’t hesitate.
She lunged forward with her boots completely melting the glass floor as she moved at supersonic speeds.
She swung her right arm in a massive, sweeping arc, unleashing a devastating, sixty-foot-wide crescent blade of white-hot fire directly at Harper.
Harper didn’t attempt to block the solar-tier heat.
She violently manipulated her electromagnetic field, dropping out of the air like a stone to avoid the blade, then instantly blasting forward across the sand to close the distance.
"Fulgur Lance!" Harper roared.
She thrust her hands forward, firing a dense continuous beam of purple lightning directly at Seraphina’s chest.
KRKKKKK!
Before the lightning could connect, the desert sand violently erupted between them.
Elora Verinda was not going to sit on the sidelines and be ignored.
To match these two terrifying monsters, Elora had completely closed her eyes, biting her lip until it bled as she tapped into her deepest reserves of power.
’These two are truly on another level...’
Elora unleashed the pure power of frost, violently freezing the sand, the ambient moisture, and the melted glass across the entire battlefield.
A massive twenty-foot-thick wall of solid blue ice erupted from the ground, perfectly intercepting Harper’s lightning beam.
The ice violently shattered, sending massive shards flying across the arena like shrapnel as they all went at each other simultaneously.
There were no alliances and there were no truces.
Elora was desperately trying to kill Harper for her betrayal, violently raising massive razor-sharp pillars of ice from the ground to impale the floating lightning mage.
At the exact same time, Elora was desperately trying to kill Seraphina, firing hundreds of high-velocity ice shards to suppress the overwhelming solar heat that was actively melting her armor.
"Die, you rat!" Elora screamed, slamming her hands against the frozen sand.
SHWK!
SHWK!
SHWK!
Three massive ten-foot-long spears of solid ice shot out of the ground directly beneath Harper.
Harper was attacking as well as desperately defending.
She twisted violently in the air with her purple hair whipping around her face.
She used her blood to violently increase her reaction time, cleanly dodging the first two ice spears but she was fighting a two-on-one battle against monsters.
The third ice spear clipped her right side, brutally tearing through her leather armor and slicing a deep horrific gash across her ribs.
Blood sprayed through the air, immediately vaporizing into steam as Seraphina arrived.
"Burn!" Seraphina roared, completely ignoring the ice.
Seraphina lunged directly through Elora’s freezing barrage, the white-hot flames of the Primordial Spirit effortlessly melting the ice shards before they could even touch her skin.
She closed the distance on Harper, driving a devastating, fire-wrapped punch directly toward the lightning mage’s face.
KRA-THOOM!
Harper barely managed to cross her arms, forming a desperate static shield.
The impact of Seraphina’s punch violently shattered the electrical barrier, sending Harper crashing backward into the frozen sand.
CRUNCH!
Before Harper could even roll to her feet, Elora capitalized on the opening.
She slammed her boot down, violently raising a jagged spike of ice that punched cleanly through Harper’s left calf, physically pinning her to the desert floor!
"AGGGGH!" Harper shrieked in agony with her blood pouring over the blue ice.
Elora panted heavily, her blue hair plastered to her sweaty forehead.

She was deeply wounded herself with her arms covered in severe electrical burns from Harper’s earlier strikes but her summoned Hero... a high level Frost Mage equipped with baseline healing magic was standing safely on a distant dune, desperately channeling green restorative mana into Elora’s back, actively healing her minor wounds over the course of the battle.

Meanwhile, Seraphina’s wounds from the flying ice shrapnel simply burned with white-hot fire, the sheer thermal density of the Primordial Spirit instantly cauterizing and sealing her flesh the microsecond it was cut.
"It’s over, Harper!" Elora declared, raising both hands to summon a final, massive execution block of ice to crush the pinned lightning mage.
But Harper was not done doing damage.
Pinned to the ground, bleeding profusely from her ribs and her impaled leg, Harper’s purple eyes violently flared with completely unhinged, psychotic lethality.
"If I die..." Harper rasped, blood bubbling past her lips as she grabbed the ice spike piercing her leg with both hands.
"...I am taking both of you entitled bitches to hell with me!"
ZZZZZZZZZT!
Harper completely abandoned her defensive spells as she poured every single remaining drop of her Lord core directly into the Blood spell.
A catastrophic, blinding wave of purple electricity erupted from her pinned body.
The raw voltage traveled directly through the ice spike pinning her leg, violently back-feeding through the magical connection straight into Elora’s core!
"Ahhhh!" Elora shrieked, dropping to her knees as her nervous system violently convulsed under the massive electrical overload.

At the same time, Harper fired a desperate blast of lightning directly at Seraphina’s chest, managing to cleanly pierce through the solar flames and strike the Magistrate’s daughter, sending Seraphina stumbling backward with a smoking crater in her armor.
At the climax of the brutal bloody battle, when Harper was genuinely near death with her organs actively failing and her vision swimming with dark spots...
Standing at the base of the towering, sixty-story black sand Spire, Silas Graves was currently ignoring the distant explosions entirely.
He stood directly in front of the massive, completely featureless iron doors that sealed the entrance to the Spire.
The doors were engraved with ancient indecipherable runes, and they completely lacked a physical keyhole or a handle.
Valerius, Aeliana, and Mia were clustered around him, staring up at the imposing structure.
"So," Silas sighed, wiping sweat from his brow.
"We made it.
We have the map.
How exactly do we open the damn door?"
As if waiting for the prompt, the dead god’s voice boomed directly from the black glass walls of the Spire itself.
"Congratulations on surviving the sprint, my little Lords!" Ititus laughed cheerfully, his voice echoing across the empty dunes.
"To unlock the Vault and claim my ultimate treasures, simply place the Treasure Map directly against the center of the iron door!"
Silas and Valerius immediately looked at each other with their faces identical masks of deep suspicion.
"Absolutely not," Valerius stated flatly, shaking his head.
"I am not touching that door."
"Agreed," Silas nodded, crossing his arms.
They stood there for a full minute, arguing on whether to even follow the instructions at all.
They decided they couldn’t trust the pathological lying god enough to do exactly what he said.
The last time they followed his literal directions with the cave riddle, the floor collapsed and dropped Silas as well as the rest of them into the Abyss.
"He probably meant the exact opposite," Silas deduced.
"If he says put it on the door, it’s a trap.
We should put it on the ground."
"Sound logic," Valerius agreed, stepping back.
"Put it on the ground."
Silas didn’t hesitate.
He took the heavy roll of paper out of his coat, crouched down, and placed it completely flat on the black sand directly in front of the door.
For a moment, nothing happened then, the god’s voice echoed again, and this time, the sadistic cheerfulness was completely gone.
"You idiots," Ititus sighed deeply, his voice sounding genuinely exhausted.
"This time, I actually wasn’t joking."
Silas’s golden eyes widened.
"Wait—"
KRA-KRA-KRA-THOOM!
Massive, glowing red fault lines violently shot across the entire body of the sixty-story tower.

The structural integrity of the ancient Spire, triggered by the incorrect placement of the map, completely failed as the black glass shattered, the iron doors buckled, and the massive towering structure violently collapsed!
All of their eyes widened in paralyzing horror as millions of tons of black sand, fused glass, and iron plummeted directly down toward them.
"Aeli!" Silas roared, reaching for her.
But it was too late.
The collapsing tower fell, instantly consuming Silas, Valerius, Aeliana, and Mia under an inescapable avalanche of absolute darkness.
The force of the collapsing Spire didn’t just stay there.
It violently spread outward across the desert like a massive, rolling tidal wave of black sand and debris.
The shockwave roared across the dunes, consuming the pursuing Lords that had fallen behind, completely burying their summoned Heroes, their mounts, and their ambitions in seconds.
The tidal wave of destruction continued expanding, racing across the desert miles away until it reached the molten crater where the three girls were fighting to the death.
Seraphina was currently standing over the bleeding broken body of Harper.
She had summoned a superheated, white-hot flaming spear and driven it cleanly through Harper’s chest, pinning the lightning mage to the glass.
"Hehe...
What did you say about taking us with you, bitch?"

Seraphina was physically lifting her up by the shaft, her silver hair whipping wildly as she looked into Harper’s fading purple eyes, thoroughly enjoying the sight of the blood spilling down the steel.
Suddenly, a massive shadow fell over them and Seraphina slowly turned her head with her glowing red eyes widening as she looked up.
A hundred-foot-tall tsunami of black sand and shattered glass was roaring directly toward them.
The avalanche washed over them instantly, violently consuming Seraphina and the bleeding Harper under millions of tons of suffocating debris.
A hundred yards away, Elora saw the wall of death approaching.
"What the fuck is that?!"
Elora’s summoned Hero desperately tried attacking it, firing massive blasts of ice to shatter the wave.
KKKKT!
KKT!

When that didn’t even dent the momentum, the Hero slammed her staff into the ground, summoning a massive, fifty-foot-thick wall of solid blue ice to protect her Lord but the apocalyptic mass of the collapsing Spire was absolute.
CRASH!
The avalanche of black sand violently broke through the ice wall like wet paper, completely consuming Elora and her Hero, dragging them down into the suffocating crushing darkness of the earth.
Drip!
Drip!
The echoing sound of water slowly dripping onto stone eventually penetrated the suffocating darkness of Silas’s mind.
"Wake up, my little Lords!"
The god’s voice suddenly boomed, waking Silas up with a violent jolt.
Silas gasped, his eyes snapping open.
He pushed himself up onto his elbows, coughing violently as he expelled a lungful of dry, ancient dust.
"Welcome, survivors!" Ititus cheered happily over the invisible broadcast.
"You failed the door puzzle!
But fear not!
You were not crushed to death!
You have simply been dropped into the Treasury Dungeon!
This is the true labyrinth where the real treasures were kept safely beneath the Spire!"
Silas forced himself up into a sitting position on the cold stone floor, his head spinning.
"However," the god continued, his voice dripping with sadistic amusement.
"In the chaos of the sand collapse, all of your little factions and alliances have been completely separated and randomized across the labyrinth!
You are all entirely alone in the dark!"
Silas’s heart hammered in his chest.
Separated?
"Listen closely!" the Lord instructed them, his voice taking on a heavy, serious tone.
"Hidden somewhere in this labyrinth is the Realm Core!
As long as you find the Core, you can completely absorb its power!
Doing so will not only actively destroy this Secret Realm, but it will automatically guide you to my most valuable, divine treasures!
Happy hunting!"
The broadcast clicked off, leaving Silas sitting in the damp, dimly lit stone corridor.
Silas coughed out again, wiping soot from his eyes as he sat up properly.
"Aeli?" Silas called out, his voice echoing down the dark tunnels.
"Valerius?
Mia?"
He rapidly searched his immediate surroundings, looking down the branching corridors but he didn’t find them.
The group had been completely scattered as he was alone then, he heard a wet ragged cough from the shadows nearby.
Silas instantly drew his mythril longsword, his Gold Core flaring as he spun toward the sound.
Lying in a crumple broken heap near a collapsed stone pillar was a body.
Silas slowly lowered his sword, his eyes narrowing as he walked over to investigate.
He winced visibly at the sight.
It was the charred mutilated body of Harper.

chapters.title: Chapter 193: Under The Spire [II]
paragraphs: She looked horrific.
The white-hot flaming spear that Seraphina had driven through her chest had left a massive cauterized hole directly next to her heart.
Her left leg was completely mangled, the bone shattered from Elora’s ice spike, and her pale skin was covered in severe third-degree burns and deep lacerations.
Some of her organs were even showing too.
She slowly opened her purple eyes, looking up at him through a mask of blood and soot.
"Silas..." Harper rasped with her voice barely a wet whisper.
She tried to shift her torn, ruined leather armor to cover her exposed, burned chest. "...I didn’t... I didn’t want you to see me like this. I have so many wounds... it isn’t lady-like at all."
Silas dropped to his knees beside her with the usual stoicness for her overridden by genuine shock.
Harper was dying.
Her breathing was shallow, her pulse was practically nonexistent, and her core had cracks in it.
It was an undeniable miracle that she hadn’t died by now from the blood loss alone.
She looked so completely gone.
Silas gritted his teeth with his jaw tightening as he looked at the ruin of the powerful lightning Lord.
"Why?" Silas asked, his voice rough with frustration. "Why did you go ahead and do all of that? Why did you hold the line against the entire group of Lords? You barely know me."
Harper bit her bleeding lip a bit, feeling her vision fade at the edges.
"Because..." Harper whispered with a smile touching her lips. "...I told you. I loved you, Silas-kun. This... this was nothing."
Silas didn’t say another word. He was a Lord, and he protected the people who bled for him.
Silas pressed his calloused right hand directly against her ruined chest, right over her failing heart.
Harper yelped weakly with her eyes fluttering shut.
"Hold still," Silas commanded her.
He didn’t use baseline healing magic as Silas tapped directly into his trump card.
The intricate glowing Genesis Rune tattooed across his knuckles violently flared to life.
FWOOSH!
A blinding surge of pure emerald-green healing energy completely covered her broken body.
Before Harper’s very eyes, the impossible happened.
The massive cauterized hole in her chest actively began knitting together. Muscle fibers reconnected, bone fused, and scorched skin was completely replaced by flawless pale flesh.
Her mangled left leg snapped back into perfect alignment.
Everything was healed completely shortly after.
Harper laid there on the cold stone, breathing deeply with her heart beating strongly in her chest.
She couldn’t help but blink, staring down at her perfectly restored body in absolute shock.
However, because her leather armor had been completely destroyed by the fire and the healing process, she was currently lying completely naked on the damp stone.
Silas immediately stood up. He unclasped his heavy dark trench coat and pulled it off, revealing the simple black tunic shirt he was wearing underneath.
He draped the heavy coat gently over her shivering form, placing it on her to preserve her dignity.
"Wear it," Silas told her softly.
He immediately turned the other way, facing down the dark corridor to give her privacy.
"Thank you," Harper whispered with her voice trembling.
She sat up, pulling the warm fabric of his trench coat around her shoulders and slipping her arms into the oversized sleeves.
And then, sitting there in the dark, wearing the coat of the man who had just pulled her back from the brink of oblivion... Harper cried.
She didn’t cry for manipulation.
She cried genuine silent tears.
She had been so incredibly close to death, and the suffocating terror of the void had truly scared her.
As she wore his trench coat, breathing in the scent of rain and steel woven into the fabric, she looked at his broad back.
"Silas..." Harper sniffled, wiping her eyes. "Thank you."
"Don’t worry about it," Silas replied without turning around with his focus returning. "Can you walk? We need to move. I want to regroup with the rest of my group before someone else finds the Core."
Harper sniffled, placing her hands on the stone wall. She tried to stand up but her newly fused leg muscles were still incredibly weak and completely uncoordinated from the trauma.
Her knees buckled instantly, and she fell back against the wall with a soft groan.
Silas heard her fall. He turned back around, taking in her exhausted trembling posture.
Without a word, Silas walked over. He turned around, giving her his broad back, and knelt slightly.
"Climb on," Silas told her. "I will carry you."
Harper knelt there on the stone, looking at his back in complete astonishment.
She slowly leaned forward.
Harper climbed onto his back, wrapping her arms securely around his neck.
"Sorry..."
Silas reached back, placing his strong hands firmly and respectfully directly on her lower thighs, right under her ass to secure her weight as she wrapped her pale legs around his waist.
Once she was securely positioned, Silas stood up effortlessly, adjusting her weight, and they began moving down the dark labyrinthine corridor.
Resting her chin on his broad shoulder, smelling the clean scent of his black shirt, Harper’s mind was spinning.
’Is this...?’ Harper thought, her purple eyes wide as she looked at the side of his sharp jawline. ’Is this how he treats the people he actually trusts...?’
At this exact point in time, Harper didn’t even think about the political mission for a single second.
She completely forgot the mission her father had assigned her.
Harper simply closed her eyes, resting her cheek against his neck, only enjoying the warmth of the man who had just saved her life.
Drip! Drip!
The rhythmic echoing sound of water falling from the high vaulted stone ceiling and striking the damp floor was the only noise accompanying them in the suffocating darkness.
Silas walked with heavy steps down the winding, cavernous corridor of the Treasury Dungeon.
His heavy combat boots sloshed slightly through shallow puddles of stagnant water, the sound reverberating off the slick moss-covered walls.
The air down here was incredibly thick, smelling pungently of dust, wet earth, and the tang of ozone radiating from the woman currently strapped to his back.
Harper was clinging to him like a terrified limpet.
Her pale arms were wrapped securely around his neck, her fingers tightly fisted into the dark fabric of his shirt.
Her bare legs were locked firmly around his waist, her face buried deeply into the crook of his neck.
She was squeezing him with a crushing intensity with her breathing becoming rapid and shallow against his skin.
Silas let out a long, deeply exhausted sigh, adjusting his grip on her lower thighs to hoist her weight a fraction higher.
"You don’t have to cling so tight, Harper," Silas told her. "I’m not going to drop you. You’re going to choke me out before we even find the exit."
Harper didn’t listen.
She merely let out a soft muffled whimper of protest, tightening her grip around his neck even further, completely refusing to let go of the anchor keeping her tethered to reality.
Silas just sighed again, shaking his head in the gloom.
His head, which was usually cool, was struggling to fully process the absurdity of the situation.
’So many strange things have happened throughout this raid...’
This woman had literally just thrown herself into a meat grinder against a dozen elites.
She had been pierced, electrocuted, frozen, and finally impaled through the chest by a white-hot flaming spear, beaten to the undeniable point of death.
And she had done it all for him... All for a man she barely knew, just to protect his retreat.
’She’s so stupid.’
It was too surreal.
Silas narrowed his golden-ringed eyes, staring into the impenetrable darkness ahead.
Who actually did that for some random, psychotic crush?
In the slums, people sold their own mothers for a loaf of moldy bread. Out here, high-tier Lords were throwing their lives away just to buy him five minutes of running time?
The emotional arithmetic simply didn’t compute in his head.
Before Silas could dwell on her sanity any further, the atmosphere in the corridor violently shifted.
"Attention, surviving vermin!"

’First he called us Sweet little Lords, now surviving vermin? What are you, on your period?’ Silas thought as the dead god’s voice boomed suddenly from the very stone walls themselves, the volume vibrating the puddles beneath Silas’s boots.
Ititus sounded incredibly cheerful, thoroughly enjoying the chaotic aftermath of his collapsing Spire.

"I see some of you have finally picked yourselves up off the floor!" the god laughed, the audio crackling with magical static. "Welcome to the true test of the Treasury Dungeon! Consider this a formal warning! This labyrinth is not a safe zone! There are incredibly hungry monsters roaming these very halls!"
Silas stopped walking, his jaw tightening as he listened.

"Furthermore," Ititus continued, his voice dropping and becoming even more sinister. "Let us establish the ground rules for this final phase! High-tier spatial abilities, such as Teleportation, Rift-Walking, and all the rest of that other extra, cheating fluff, are completely dampened down here! You will walk on your own two feet like the mortals you are!"
Harper groaned softly against Silas’s neck, her grip tightening.

"Also," the god announced gleefully, "there will be strict curfews enforced! Given that today marks the official Third Day of the Secret Realm drop, the timer is ticking! If a surviving Lord or group does not locate the central Dungeon Core by the end of the Sixth Day... the Secret Realm will automatically detonate! It will be completely destroyed, atomizing everything inside while throwing you all out and you will not have any chance to claim the rewards!"
Three days left... The clock was ticking down to zero gradually.
"To help you track the time in the dark," Ititus explained, "look up at the ceiling! I have provided an atmospheric indicator!"
Silas tilted his head back, looking up at the vaulted stone above.
There was a faint luminescent gold light softly radiating from the cracks in the masonry, casting a dim twilight glow over the wet stone.

"That faint gold light is the proper light of Daytime," the god clarified. "However, when the light shifts and becomes completely blue... that means it is Night Time and once it is Night Time, you are not allowed to move through the corridors!"
The cheerful voice vanished, replaced by a dark promise.

"If you move through the halls during the blue light," Ititus whispered, "you will immediately trigger the aggro of one of my very own Lesser Generals. They will spawn directly onto your coordinates, and they will absolutely try to brutally kill you. Therefore, I highly suggest you set camp and stay perfectly still the moment you notice that the light is turning blue! Good luck, little mice! And good monster killing!"
The broadcast clicked off, plunging the damp corridor back into a heavy oppressive silence.
Harper muttered a curse directly into Silas’s ear.
"I hate him," Harper whispered fervently, her breath warm against his skin. "I hate this dead, sadistic god so much."

"Agreed," Silas muttered, adjusting her weight again and resuming his heavy stride down the tunnel. "For all of this theatrical life-threatening bullshit, there better be a shit ton of high-tier treasures waiting for us at the end of this maze."
They walked in silence for a few minutes, the faint golden light from the ceiling guiding their path through the gloom.
"Well," Silas remarked casually, his eyes scanning the branching intersections. "The god talked a big game, but I haven’t seen any monsters ye—"
A low vibrating growl echoed from the absolute darkness of the corridor directly up ahead, instantly cutting him off.
Silas stopped dead in his tracks.
From the shadows, six pairs of glowing malevolent crimson eyes snapped open.
Stepping out into the dim golden light, completely blocking their path forward, was a pack of real Dire Wolves.
They were absolutely massive, their muscular shoulders standing higher than Silas’s waist.
Their fur was a matted, oily black, and thick acidic drool dripped from their elongated, razor-sharp fangs, sizzling as it hit the damp stone floor.
The pack fanned out, their heads lowered, recognizing the scent of fresh wounded blood radiating from the two humans.
They stared at each other for a tense breathless bit.
Harper’s entire body went rigid against Silas’s back.
Her Lord core was still completely depleted with her mana pathways down from her previous battle. She was functionally a baseline mortal right now.
"Silas," Harper whispered with her voice trembling. "Silas, put me down. I can get off. I can try to channel a spark to distract them so you can draw your sword—"

Silas just sighed again, shaking his head in the gloom.
His head, which was usually cool, was struggling to fully process the absurdity of the situation.
’So many strange things have happened throughout this raid...’
This woman had literally just thrown herself into a meat grinder against a dozen elites.
She had been pierced, electrocuted, frozen, and finally impaled through the chest by a white-hot flaming spear, beaten to the undeniable point of death.
And she had done it all for him...
All for a man she barely knew, just to protect his retreat.
’She’s so stupid.’
It was too surreal.
Silas narrowed his golden-ringed eyes, staring into the impenetrable darkness ahead.
Who actually did that for some random, psychotic crush?
In the slums, people sold their own mothers for a loaf of moldy bread.
Out here, high-tier Lords were throwing their lives away just to buy him five minutes of running time?
The emotional arithmetic simply didn’t compute in his head.
Before Silas could dwell on her sanity any further, the atmosphere in the corridor violently shifted.
"Attention, surviving vermin!"
’First he called us Sweet little Lords, now surviving vermin?
What are you, on your period?’ Silas thought as the dead god’s voice boomed suddenly from the very stone walls themselves, the volume vibrating the puddles beneath Silas’s boots.
Ititus sounded incredibly cheerful, thoroughly enjoying the chaotic aftermath of his collapsing Spire.
"I see some of you have finally picked yourselves up off the floor!" the god laughed, the audio crackling with magical static.
"Welcome to the true test of the Treasury Dungeon!
Consider this a formal warning!
This labyrinth is not a safe zone!
There are incredibly hungry monsters roaming these very halls!"
Silas stopped walking, his jaw tightening as he listened.
"Furthermore," Ititus continued, his voice dropping and becoming even more sinister.
"Let us establish the ground rules for this final phase!
High-tier spatial abilities, such as Teleportation, Rift-Walking, and all the rest of that other extra, cheating fluff, are completely dampened down here!
You will walk on your own two feet like the mortals you are!"
Harper groaned softly against Silas’s neck, her grip tightening.
"Also," the god announced gleefully, "there will be strict curfews enforced!
Given that today marks the official Third Day of the Secret Realm drop, the timer is ticking!
If a surviving Lord or group does not locate the central Dungeon Core by the end of the Sixth Day... the Secret Realm will automatically detonate!
It will be completely destroyed, atomizing everything inside while throwing you all out and you will not have any chance to claim the rewards!"
Three days left...
The clock was ticking down to zero gradually.
"To help you track the time in the dark," Ititus explained, "look up at the ceiling!
I have provided an atmospheric indicator!"
Silas tilted his head back, looking up at the vaulted stone above.
There was a faint luminescent gold light softly radiating from the cracks in the masonry, casting a dim twilight glow over the wet stone.
"That faint gold light is the proper light of Daytime," the god clarified.
"However, when the light shifts and becomes completely blue... that means it is Night Time and once it is Night Time, you are not allowed to move through the corridors!"
The cheerful voice vanished, replaced by a dark promise.
"If you move through the halls during the blue light," Ititus whispered, "you will immediately trigger the aggro of one of my very own Lesser Generals.
They will spawn directly onto your coordinates, and they will absolutely try to brutally kill you.
Therefore, I highly suggest you set camp and stay perfectly still the moment you notice that the light is turning blue!
Good luck, little mice!
And good monster killing!"
The broadcast clicked off, plunging the damp corridor back into a heavy oppressive silence.
Harper muttered a curse directly into Silas’s ear.
"I hate him," Harper whispered fervently, her breath warm against his skin.
"I hate this dead, sadistic god so much."
"Agreed," Silas muttered, adjusting her weight again and resuming his heavy stride down the tunnel.
"For all of this theatrical life-threatening bullshit, there better be a shit ton of high-tier treasures waiting for us at the end of this maze."
They walked in silence for a few minutes, the faint golden light from the ceiling guiding their path through the gloom.
"Well," Silas remarked casually, his eyes scanning the branching intersections.
"The god talked a big game, but I haven’t seen any monsters ye—"
A low vibrating growl echoed from the absolute darkness of the corridor directly up ahead, instantly cutting him off.
Silas stopped dead in his tracks.
From the shadows, six pairs of glowing malevolent crimson eyes snapped open.
Stepping out into the dim golden light, completely blocking their path forward, was a pack of real Dire Wolves.
They were absolutely massive, their muscular shoulders standing higher than Silas’s waist.
Their fur was a matted, oily black, and thick acidic drool dripped from their elongated, razor-sharp fangs, sizzling as it hit the damp stone floor.
The pack fanned out, their heads lowered, recognizing the scent of fresh wounded blood radiating from the two humans.
They stared at each other for a tense breathless bit.
Harper’s entire body went rigid against Silas’s back.
Her Lord core was still completely depleted with her mana pathways down from her previous battle.
She was functionally a baseline mortal right now.
"Silas," Harper whispered with her voice trembling.
"Silas, put me down.
I can get off.
I can try to channel a spark to distract them so you can draw your sword—"

chapters.title: Chapter 194: Under The Spire [III]
paragraphs: "Harper," Silas interrupted. "Calm down. Stay exactly where you are."

He didn’t reach for his mythril longsword as he couldn’t effectively wield a heavy two-handed blade in a narrow corridor while actively carrying a woman piggyback since the rotational force would throw off his balance.
Instead, Silas simply widened his stance.
The Alpha Dire Wolf lunged first. It propelled its massive six-hundred-pound body through the air with its jaws unhinging to tear Silas’s throat out.
FWOOSH!

Silas didn’t flinch. He planted his left boot firmly into the stone, pivoting his entire torso with devastating precision as he channeled the astronomical physical power of his Gold Core directly into his right leg.
He executed a flawless fast roundhouse kick directly into the side of the leaping Alpha’s head.
KRA-CRUNCH!
The sound of the wolf’s skull completely shattering echoed like a cannon shot down the corridor.
The overwhelming physical strength packed into Silas’s kick was so monstrous that the massive Dire Wolf’s neck snapped instantly.
The beast’s trajectory was violently redirected, launching it sideways through the air to smash heavily into the stone wall as it crumpled to the floor, instantly dead.
Clinging to his back, Harper gasped with her purple eyes widening in absolute, unadulterated shock.
She had known Silas was a Blue Core which was probably purple or gold if her suspicions about the Lord of the Blessed Land having gold was true.
Harper had seen his elemental magic but she had never, ever witnessed brutal physical brawling like this.
He wasn’t even using spells... He was treating dungeon beasts like training dummies.
Two more wolves charged simultaneously from the left and right flanks.
Silas dropped his center of gravity, smoothly carrying Harper’s weight as he ducked under the snapping jaws of the left wolf.
He drove a devastating upward knee strike directly into the beast’s exposed ribcage.
THUD-CRACK!
The wolf’s ribs caved in instantly, piercing its internal organs.
As the beast collapsed, Silas spun on his heel. The right wolf lunged for his leg.
Silas violently stomped his heavy combat boot directly downward onto the back of the creature’s neck, pinning it to the stone floor and snapping its spine in a single, brutal motion.
The remaining three wolves hesitated with their primal instincts screaming at them to flee from the Apex predator standing before them.
Silas didn’t give them the chance.
"Where do you think you’re going?"
He exploded forward, closing the distance in a blur of motion.

He launched himself into the air, executing a devastating flying front kick that caved in the chest of the fourth wolf, before immediately pivoting upon landing to deliver a sweeping leg sweep that shattered the forelegs of the fifth.

The final wolf turned to run with its tail tucked however Silas grabbed a loose piece of jagged stone debris from the floor and hurled it with the speed of a bullet, striking the fleeing beast in the back of the skull and dropping it instantly.
The entire fight lasted less than ten seconds.
Silas stood in the center of the corridor, slowly lowering his leg and rolling his shoulders to loosen his muscles.
He hadn’t even broken a sweat as six massive Dire Wolves lay completely dead on the damp stone.
On his back, Harper was completely speechless.
Her heart was hammering against his spine with her cheeks flushed a violent crimson.

Her upbringing had taught her that magic was supreme and that physical brawling was for peasants but watching Silas dismantle a wolf pack with his bare legs was the most incredibly attractive thing she had ever witnessed.
"Are you alright back there?" Silas asked, casually adjusting his grip on her thighs.
"Y-yes," Harper stammered with her voice breathless.

She looked down at the massive, meaty carcasses of the wolves as her survival instincts slowly booted back up. "Silas... we should keep the Dire wolves to cook later. We don’t know how long we will be stuck in this labyrinth, and monster meat holds high nutritional mana."
Silas looked at the bodies, nodding pragmatically. "Sound logic but I have to ask... how exactly do you propose we cook it?"
He let out a heavy, tired sigh, shaking his head.
"Neither of us has fire magic. I use water, and you use lightning. If Seraphina were here, she could have roasted it in two seconds." Silas muttered.
’I genuinely would have learned some basic baseline ignition spells if you hadn’t come to our camp and dragged me into this mess.’
Harper leaned over his shoulder, looking at the side of his face as if he was completely stupid.
"Silas," Harper said. "I can use my Lightning magic to roast them."
Silas blinked, genuinely pausing. He turned his head slightly to look at her.
"You can do that? I thought your lightning just electrocutes and explodes things."
Harper laughed.

"You are such a cute dummy sometimes," Harper teased him, her purple eyes sparkling. "Lightning generates extreme thermal resistance. If I carefully dial down the voltage and sustain a continuous low-amperage current through the meat, it acts exactly like an internal roasting oven. It cooks it perfectly from the inside out."
Silas stared at her for a second, deeply impressed by the scientific application of magic.
"Fair enough. Bag them."
Harper reached out her pale hand.
A pulse of spatial blue light washed over the corridor. The six massive Dire Wolf carcasses instantly vanished, smoothly stored into the endless spatial container of her Lord Inventory.
With the path clear, Harper tightened her arms around his neck, playfully kicking her bare heels gently against his hips.
"Move, Horsy," Harper commanded playfully, giggling into his ear.
Silas let out a long suffering sigh, resuming his heavy stride down the damp corridor. "You are getting quite comfortable up there, aren’t you?"
Harper smiled, pressing her cheek firmly against his neck, inhaling his scent.
"It’s because I’m with the man I love," Harper whispered softly.
Silas sighed again, pointedly ignoring the confession, and kept running at a more comfortable ground-eating pace.
He didn’t exactly know where he was going.
The subterranean labyrinth was a chaotic web of identical, moss-covered tunnels.
However, his thoughts dictated that the Vault and the ultimate exit would have to be located on a higher elevation relative to the sprawling basement level.
He constantly kept his eyes peeled for any architectural inclines.
As he ran, Silas closed his eyes for brief intervals, actively expanding his senses.

He tried to push his Gold Core perception outward, desperately looking for the familiar starlight signature of Aeliana, the water hum of Mia, or even the arrogant wind aura of Valerius but all he could feel was absolute nothingness.
The dark stone walls of the Treasury Dungeon were lined with high-density suppression runes.
This place completely dampened even his Gold Core senses, restricting his spatial awareness to a mere twenty-foot radius.
It felt like a heavy wet blanket had been thrown over his mind.
Silas gritted his teeth, hating the dead god Ititus even more.
Suddenly, as he rounded a wide, sweeping corner where the cavern aggressively diverged, his boots skidded to a halt.
Directly up front, carved into the solid bedrock, was a massive sweeping staircase leading upwards into the gloom but they were not alone at the base of the stairs.
Standing in the center of the intersection, panting and leaning against the stone wall, was a blond-haired Lord.
Both Harper and Silas turned to see the man clearly.
It was Julian.
The arrogant Valoria noble was holding a chipped, blood-stained sword in his right hand. He was running, looking completely exhausted.
Thick, black soot covered his usually immaculate face, his expensive noble armor was scorched and dented, and he looked like he had barely survived a warzone.
Silas and Julian stopped dead, staring at each other from thirty feet away. Clinging to Silas’s back, Harper’s purple eyes widened in shock.
"What?" Harper blurted out, her voice echoing in the quiet cavern. "Didn’t I kill you? I literally put a Thunder Lance directly through your forehead on the surface! I watched you turn into ash!"
Julian flinched at the sound of her voice, his eyes snapping to the woman on Silas’s back.
He recognized her instantly.
A cruel arrogant grin slowly spread across Julian’s soot-covered face as he straightened his posture, leaning his sword against his shoulder.
"Oh, the lightning bitch," Julian sneered. "You actually thought you managed to execute a Lord of the Valoria elite that easily? You didn’t kill me... You actually killed my summoned Hero."

Julian laughed darkly, wiping soot from his brow. "My Hero possessed the rare passive ability to flawlessly morph her physical appearance and magical signature into an exact duplicate of my own. I swapped places with her the moment you charged the Lords."
Julian spat on the stone floor, his face twisting into an ugly mask of disdain as he casually insulted the very Hero who had died to save him.

"She was only a weak pathetic shapeshifter," Julian mocked, waving his hand dismissively. "She had zero combat utility. With a completely useless class like that, she was destined to be cannon fodder anyway. She served her purpose and died so I could live. That is the natural order."
Silas stood perfectly still.
A dark cold sneer slowly etched itself across Silas’s face. His golden-ringed eyes locked onto Julian, his pupils dilating with pure murderous intent.
"Harper," Silas said quietly. "Climb down."
Harper felt the sudden shift in the temperature of his body and she didn’t argue.
She carefully unwrapped her legs from his waist, her bare feet hitting the damp stone floor.

Her legs were still visibly shaking from the residual trauma of her near-death experience, forcing her to lean heavily against the cavern wall for support, clutching his trench coat tightly around her shoulders.
Julian watched the exchange, raising an arrogant eyebrow. He twirled his chipped sword, stepping away from the wall.

"What are you doing, rat?" Julian asked, his tone mocking as he looked at Silas. "What do you want to do about it? Are you... going to tell me how to properly treat my own subordinates as a Lord? Are you going to give me a moral lecture down here in the dark?"
Silas let out a long slow sigh.
His eyes began to physically glow with brilliant liquid gold light.
Silas raised his right hand.
He didn’t draw his mythril blade from its scabbard.
He forcefully pulled the ambient condensation and stagnant water from the damp cavern walls, gathering it into a swirling hyper-pressurized sphere over his palm.
"Ice Transformation." Silas whispered.
KRKKKKKK!
The swirling water violently flash-froze, aggressively elongating and condensing until Silas was holding a flawless four-foot-long longsword forged from solid blue ice.
Cold vapor poured off the crystalline blade, chilling the immediate air.

"I couldn’t care less about how you treat your people," Silas told Julian as he took a slow step forward. "Right now, I just want to brutally kill you and I am glad that you haven’t died yet, so I can do it myself."
Julian’s arrogant grin faltered for a fraction of a second as the suffocating pressure of Silas’s presence slammed into him but his noble pride refused to back down.
Julian took a formal combat stance, raising his sword.
"Did I do something specific to you, peasant?" Julian sneered, trying to mask his rising anxiety with bravado. "Like steal your girl back in the city? Why the vendetta?"
Silas continued walking forward, his icy blade trailing vapor.
"No," Silas replied coldly. "My name is Silas Graves. Do you remember me now?"
Julian squinted, his mind racing through the thousands of faces he had dismissed over the years.
Suddenly, a spark of recognition hit him.
He remembered the filthy boy from Sector 4, the slums which had attended Valoria academy with his sister.
Julian threw his head back and burst out laughing.
"Ah!" Julian laughed, pointing his sword at Silas. "You’re that miserable little fucker from the slum—"
Julian didn’t get to finish his sentence.
Silas closed the thirty-foot distance in a single imperceptible second.
He broke the sound barrier with the stone floor shattering beneath his boots as he executed a flawless blitz.
Before Julian could even twitch his sword arm, Silas’s left hand shot out like a striking viper.
He drove his stiffened index and middle fingers directly into Julian’s left eye socket!
SQUELCH!
The horrific wet sound of the eyeball physically puncturing and violently bursting echoed through the cavern.

chapters.title: Chapter 195: Under The Spire [IV]
paragraphs: "AGGGGGGGGH!" Julian shrieked in soul-tearing agony, dropping his sword and staggering violently backward as blood sprayed from the ruined socket.
But the punishment wasn’t over.
Silas channeled mana directly through his fingertips into the wound.
The hot blood violently gushing from Julian’s ruined eye instantly froze over, expanding into ice crystals that tore through his optical nerve and locked his agonizing scream into a frozen gasp.
Silas stood before the staggering noble with his ice sword resting casually at his side.
He sneered and it looked like a demonic expression that promised violence.
"Fight for your life," Silas commanded.
Julian, blinded in one eye with his face half-covered in bloody ice shrieked in feral desperation.
"YOU FUCKERRRRRR!"
He blindly scooped his sword off the floor. His Lord core ignited, bursting into a roaring aura of red fire magic.
"I will burn you to ash!" Julian screamed, launching himself forward.
Julian executed the Verinda Sword Art... the elite high-tier combat style of the City Lord’s inner circle.
He unleashed a flurry of rapid incredibly complex thrusts and slashes, his steel blade completely wreathed in roaring fire and aiming to dismember Silas with a hundred burning cuts.
However...
CLANG! CLANG! SHWK!
Silas didn’t even step back.

He stood his ground, moving with terrifying perfection as he parried every single fiery thrust with his ice sword, the cold temperature of his blade instantly extinguishing Julian’s flames upon contact.
"FUCKER!"
Julian swung a burning horizontal arc aimed for Silas’s neck.
Silas ducked smoothly under the blade.
He stepped entirely inside Julian’s guard, entirely bypassing the technique as Silas swung his ice sword in a short brutal upward arc.
SHWK!
"AAAGH!" Julian screamed again.
Silas cleanly chopped off the three middle fingers of Julian’s right hand.
The severed digits flew through the air, completely frozen solid before they hit the ground.
Julian dropped his sword, clutching his bleeding, frozen stump in sheer terror.
"Is that the Verinda art?" Silas mocked coldly, kicking the dropped sword away. "It’s quite pathetic."
Julian scrambled backward, his fire aura wildly sputtering. He threw his left hand forward, desperately trying to cast a point-blank fireball to create distance but Silas didn’t dodge the spell.
He stepped forward and swung his ice sword horizontally with devastating force.
KRA-SLASH!
The razor-sharp ice blade cleanly severed Julian’s left hand entirely at the wrist.
"AGGGHHH!"
The noble collapsed to his knees, his mind completely breaking as he stared at his two ruined, bleeding stumps.
The agony was unimaginable with his noble reality completely shattered by the brutal violence of the slums.
"Please!" Julian begged, sobbing hysterically as tears and blood streamed down his face. "Please! Graves! I have money! I have influence! My family will give you anything!"
Silas walked slowly around the kneeling man. He didn’t speak as he raised his ice sword and brought it down in two rapid fast downward chops.
SHWK! SHWK!
"NOOOOOOOOO!" Julian wailed, his voice tearing his vocal cords.
Silas completely cut off both of Julian’s legs at the kneecaps.
The noble collapsed onto his back in the growing pool of his own freezing blood, completely dismembered, writhing like a dying insect on the damp stone.
Silas stepped over him. He placed his heavy combat boot directly onto Julian’s chest, pinning the thrashing Lord to the floor.
With terrifying precision, Silas rested the tip of his absolute-zero ice sword against the center of Julian’s ornate breastplate.
He pushed down, channeling dense pressure as the ice blade pierced the armor, slicing cleanly through the sternum, cutting Julian’s chest cavity wide open.
SHHHHHKKKKKK!
The cut was so deep and brutal, that the bleeding palpitating human heart was visibly exposed, furiously beating amidst the ruined flesh and shattered bone.
Julian stared up at Silas with his one remaining eye.
The terror and the realization of his impending death, was fully cemented in his gaze.
He couldn’t fight back... He couldn’t run... He was nothing.
"Graves... please..." Julian gurgled, blood bubbling violently from his lips. "Mercy..."
Silas leaned down with his face inches from the dying aristocrat as the light of the cavern reflected in his cold golden eyes.
"I might have spared you," Silas whispered, his voice a dark, lethal promise that echoed with years of buried hatred. "But you insulted my sister."
Silas raised his ice sword high above his head with both hands.
"Die."
SHWK-KRA-THOOM!
Silas brought the blade down with the maximal force that he could manage.
He slashed Julian completely in half, vertically bisecting the aristocrat from his collarbone straight down to his pelvis.

The force of the strike shattered the stone floor beneath the body as the two halves of Julian’s ruined corpse violently fell apart, spilling a massive steaming wave of blood and frozen viscera across the corridor.
The cavern fell completely silent, save for the rhythmic dripping of water.
Drip! Drip! Drip!
Silas stood up slowly.
"Haaah..."
He let out a long sigh with the deep burning tension in his chest finally releasing after years of holding it in.
He flicked his wrist, dispelling the ice sword back into harmless ambient water vapor.
He turned around slowly, looking back at Harper.
She was still leaning against the stone wall, clutching his trench coat tightly around her shoulders.
She had watched the entire brutal execution from start to finish.
Harper had watched him torture, dismember, and bisect a Valoria Lord without a single ounce of mercy but she didn’t look any bit disgusted by what she had seen.
In fact, her purple eyes were wide, her breathing was shallow, and a dark flush had spread across her pale cheeks.
Silas wiped a speck of frozen blood from his cheek as he looked at the massive stone staircase leading upward into the dark.
"So," Silas asked her calmly, his voice completely level. "Want to go up?"
"Y-yeah..."
The eerie light filtering down from the high, vaulted stone ceiling of the subterranean labyrinth had completely changed.
The golden hue of safety had bled away, entirely replaced by a cold and deeply ominous shade of luminescent blue.
Inside the flawlessly constructed, thick-walled ice house that Mia had erected in their isolated section of the dungeon, the atmosphere was thick.
Aeliana sat cross-legged on the smooth, frozen floor with her pristine white spider-silk robes pooling around her.
She was currently holding the ancient Grandmaster water mage in a tight protective embrace.
Mia was resting comfortably in her lap, looking entirely unbothered by the mortal peril surrounding them.
They were currently chewing on the dry rations that Valerius Sterling had begrudgingly shared from his spatial inventory.
To Aeliana, the preserved meat tasted like ash compared to what Kaelia could cook.
She stopped chewing, her glowing green eyes staring blankly at the solid blue ice wall of the shelter.
"Aunt Mia..." Aeliana whispered softly, her voice trembling with a rare uncharacteristic vulnerability.

She squeezed her Grand Aunt a fraction tighter. "Will he be alright? I haven’t seen Lord Sy for almost an entire day now. The labyrinth shifted violently when the Spire collapsed and he is alone out there in the dark."
Mia swallowed her bite of dried jerky, reaching up with a tiny hand to lazily pat Aeliana’s pale cheek.

"Calm your heart, little bird," Mia assured her, her voice raspy but carrying absolute, ancient confidence. "That boy is a Lord if I have ever seen one... He has a lot of mana, a ridiculously durable physical body, and the survival instincts of a starving wolf. A little collapsing architecture and a few monsters are not going to put him in the ground. He will be alright."
Sitting across the small, freezing enclosure, Valerius leaned his back against his mythril shield, chewing loudly on a piece of hardtack.

"Mia is right, Elf," Valerius chimed in, wiping crumbs from his golden armor. "Silas Graves is a tough nut to crack. If anyone is going to survive the separation, it’s him. You should be worrying about us."
Aeliana let out a long, shuddering sigh, burying her face into Mia’s soft white hair.
"I know that," Aeliana murmured with her pointed ears drooping slightly. "I know he is strong. But... he is out there."
She paused, her silver eyes narrowing slightly as a dark paranoid and jealous thought suddenly invaded her elven mind.
She remembered the purple-haired lightning mage who had forcefully kissed Silas’s cheek right in front of her.

"Lord Sterling," Aeliana asked, her voice dropping into a cold, deadly serious register. "What is the possibility that he is currently trapped in the dark with that scheming lightning-attuned harlot from the group? The one who kissed him."
Valerius choked on his hardtack. He pounded his armored chest, coughing violently before looking at Aeliana with a smirk.

"Harper?" Valerius coughed, shaking his head. "Given how aggressively she was stalking him, and the fact that she was literally standing not too far from the Spire entrance when the sand avalanche hit... I would say the possibility of her clinging to his leg right now is extremely high."
Aeliana’s flawless face instantly darkened.
She gritted her teeth so hard they audibly ground together as her silver starlight aura violently flared in the confined space, causing the temperature of the ice house to drop another ten degrees.
"That treacherous shameless harlot," Aeliana cursed under her breath with her fingers digging into the fabric of her robes. ’If she tries to lay a single finger on my Man...’
In her innermost thoughts, Aeliana viciously cursed the dead god Ititus for separating them, praying to Eluned that Silas was keeping his discipline intact.
In an entirely different sector of the sprawling Treasury Dungeon, Silas Graves let out a long exhausted sigh.
He stood near the center of a wide, cavernous intersection.
He looked around with his eyes analyzing the architecture.
The difference between the cavern corridors located below the grand staircase and the cavern corridors located above the staircase was that there was absolutely no difference.
It was exactly the same damp, moss-covered and oppressive black stone stretching infinitely into the gloom.
Right now, the luminescent light radiating from the cracks in the high ceiling was a vibrant eerie blue.
Directly beneath their boots, radiating from an unseen magical source in the stone floor, a perfectly geometric glowing blue ring had spread wide around them.
The circle was roughly thirty feet in diameter.
That was the Safe Zone and they were currently standing dead in the center of it.
When the dead god had cheerfully mandated "not moving" during the night cycle, he meant not stepping a single millimeter beyond the glowing perimeter of the blue Safe Zone ring.
As long as Silas and Harper remained within this specific magical boundary, they wouldn’t get targeted and instantly attacked by the roaming Lesser General.
AGGGGGGGH!
Just then, a horrifying blood-curdling scream echoed through the damp caverns, violently bouncing off the stone walls from a long distance away.
The scream was abruptly followed by a deafening sound of tearing flesh and crushing bone, before the labyrinth fell completely silent once more.
Silas sighed some more, slowly shaking his head.
"Fools," Silas muttered coldly.
Those were the actual sounds of rival Lords being brutally slaughtered in the dark for stepping outside their Safe Zones.
Silas couldn’t fathom the stupidity of these people.
The god had explicitly given them the rules of survival. He couldn’t understand why people didn’t just stay exactly where they needed to be and preserve their stamina for the daylight hours?
Silas turned his head, looking down at Harper.
The purple-haired Lord was sitting cross-legged on the damp stone floor near the center of the blue ring.

She had his black trench coat draped over her shoulders, covering her bare skin and she was currently deep in meditation with her eyes closed, desperately trying to manually gather electrical mana from the stagnant air to fill her core and properly activate her magical pathways.
Suddenly, the absolute silence of their Safe Zone was broken by a loud rumble.
Gurgle...
Harper’s eyes snapped open.
She immediately stopped meditating with an embarrassed flush of crimson spreading across her pale cheeks as she reached down, rubbing her bare stomach hungrily.
She looked up at Silas, biting her lower lip.
"Are you hungry?"
Before Silas could even attempt to deny it or brush off the necessity for sustenance, his own stomach betrayed him.
RUMBLE!
A deep hollow growl echoed from Silas’s muscled abdomen.
