chapters.title: Chapter 196: Under The Spire [V]
paragraphs: Harper burst out laughing, it was a melodious sound that momentarily chased away the crushing gloom of the dungeon.
’What’s so funny?’ Silas sighed as he crossed his arms with his face remaining perfectly stoic, though a faint hint of annoyance touched his golden-ringed eyes.
He honestly wasn’t sure if he had eaten a single real meal since he had first stepped foot into the Secret Realm days ago.
Lords with higher possessed incredibly dense bodies that didn’t strictly need normal food for long periods, sustaining their cellular function purely on mana.
But Silas wasn’t even past the first Core Refinement stage yet; his Gold Core burned astronomical amounts of calories to maintain his Body’s physical output.
"We need protein," Silas admitted. "I feel my body getting sluggish."

"We should cook the Dire Wolf meat now," Harper suggested eagerly, shifting her position on the stone floor. "Even if we only ate the meat without proper grains, the high nutritional content will repair our muscles and help us prepare for whatever we have to fight tomorrow."
As she spoke, Harper deliberately reached up to the collar of Silas’s trench coat.
She slowly unzipped the top of the heavy coat a bit further down her chest, intentionally letting the cool cavern breeze touch her bare skin.
The movement caused the heavy fabric to ride up her legs, fully exposing her long flawless and perfectly smooth pale thighs in the dim blue light.
She leaned back on her hands, looking up at him through her dark purple eyelashes with a dangerous smile.

"You know, Silas-kun..." Harper purred, her voice dropping into a thick whisper. "When we are done eating, and our stamina is recovered... you could take me right here. The blue light lasts for hours so we have nothing but time."
Silas stared at her exposed thighs, then looked up at her flushed face.
He rolled his eyes so hard it physically hurt.
"I am not interested, Harper," Silas told her, his voice echoing with uncompromising rejection.
Harper pouted, her shoulders slumping. "Why not? Am I not attractive enough for you?"

"It has nothing to do with your face," Silas lectured her. "Even if I was interested in compromising my awareness to sleep with you, look around us. The sand and stone floor in this cavern is covered in ancient moss, stagnant water, and probably ten thousand years of microscopic flesh-eating infections. What kind of absolute idiot has sex on a bare filthy dungeon floor?"
Harper blinked, looking down at the grimy stone beneath her. She hadn’t actually thought about the hygiene aspect.
’But still... if a girl keeps throwing herself at me like this, who am I to say no?’ Silas thought and though he didn’t tell her out loud, he was also actively calculating the moisture levels.
He was going to try and manually compress the water vapor to make a small Ice House... exactly like what Mia usually did for them to stay inside safely before he even considered resting properly.
"Get the wolf carcasses out," Silas commanded, walking toward the center of the ring. "Let’s eat."
Harper sighed, resigning herself to the culinary task. She waved her pale hand with her Lord inventory interface glowing blue.
THUD! THUD!
Two massive, headless carcasses of the subterranean Dire Wolves materialized directly onto the stone floor with their thick black fur matted with frozen blood.
Silas didn’t have a conventional hunting knife so he raised his right hand, forcefully drawing a sphere of dense moisture from the damp air.
"Ice Transformation," Silas muttered.
The water violently flash-froze, condensing into a perfectly balanced razor-sharp hunting knife made of solid blue ice.
The blade trailed freezing vapor as Silas knelt beside the first massive wolf carcass.
He possessed a deep awareness of how to butcher and process monster meat like this, having closely observed the huntresses in his territory handle massive boars and wolves back at the Blessed Land.
"Come on..."
With precision, Silas drove the ice knife under the wolf’s thick hide.
SHWK!
He drew the blade in a long flawless line down the beast’s abdomen, effortlessly parting the tough skin from the dense red muscle beneath without piercing the internal organs.
RIPPP!
He gripped the fur with his calloused left hand and forcefully tore the hide away with a sickening sound, exposing the rich mana-infused meat.
"Ummmm..."
Harper shuffled over on her knees to join him.
She wanted to help and to prove her worth beyond just her lightning magic so she grabbed a chunk of the heavy hide, pulling it back to expose the flank.
However, Harper was far less experienced in butchery.

Her hands slipped on the frozen blood, and as she struggled, the heavy trench coat actively rode up higher, completely exposing her bare hips and the smooth curve of her perfect thighs to the freezing air.
Silas ignored the distraction with his golden-ringed eyes locked entirely on the meat.
He rapidly carved out the cuts... the heavy tenderloins from the spine and the thick flank steaks from the hindquarters.
He tossed the massive, ten-pound slabs of raw red meat onto a clean slab of ice he generated on the floor and then he washed them after cutting up the other one.
"We can’t eat it raw," Silas noted, tossing the ice knife aside. "It’s too tough."
He reached into his own spatial ring.
Before the dungeon raid had commenced, Martha, his diligent maid back home, had forcefully packed his inventory with basic culinary supplies, refusing to let her Lord starve in the wilderness.
’Unfortunately I forgot to take the lunch she had made...’
Silas pulled out a small glass vial of refined olive oil and a leather pouch filled with crushed sea salt, dried rosemary, and crushed red pepper.
He poured the oil over the raw slabs of wolf meat, vigorously rubbing the thick liquid into the muscle fibers with his bare hands.
He generously coated the steaks in the spices, the savory aroma of the herbs instantly cutting through the pungent stench of the dungeon.
"Alright," Silas said, wiping his hands on a rag. "Roast it and don’t turn it to ash."
Harper smiled, her purple eyes glowing with excitement.
She loved showing off her magical control.
"Okay my love~"
She held both of her pale hands over the massive slabs of seasoned meat however she didn’t summon a catastrophic blast.
Harper closed her eyes, dialing down the raw voltage of her core to an incredibly precise microscopic fraction of its true power.
BZZZZZT.
A web of thin, incredibly precise purple electrical currents arched from her fingertips, sinking directly into the raw meat.
The high-frequency electrical resistance instantly generated extreme internal heat.
The water molecules inside the wolf steaks began to violently boil.
The fat rendered perfectly as the spices sizzled and popped against the searing meat, filling the damp cavern with a mouth-watering, intoxicating aroma of roasted garlic, pepper, and searing steak.
Within two minutes, the outside of the meat was perfectly seared with a dark caramelized crust, while the muscle was roasted to a flawless medium-rare.
"Done," Harper declared proudly, cutting the current.
Silas utilized his water magic again, rapidly condensing moisture from the air to create two wide fflat plates made of smooth, polished ice.
Harper carefully used a pair of ice tongs to transfer the steaming massive cuts of roasted meat onto the plates.
They sat side by side on the cold stone floor with their backs leaning against the cavern wall, exactly in the center of the blue Safe Zone ring.
"Bon’appetit Silas-kun."
They tore into the food with their bare hands.
The wolf meat was incredibly chewy and bursting with a rich, savory flavor that instantly flooded their exhausted bodies with a rush of nutritional mana.
"Mm~ We outdid ourselves, Silas-kun." Harper said and Silas sighed.
"You’re right..."
Silas ate like a starving beast, stripping the meat down to the bone.
As they ate, the crushing isolation of the dungeon seemed to fade. The romantic tension Harper had been desperately trying to force earlier organically softened into genuine intimacy.
’I think I can take a break from this mission for now...’ Harper thought, it didn’t matter if Silas was the Lord of Blessed Land or not.
The purple haired woman couldn’t bring herself to even think about hurting him.
’I might have to tell Papa I quit... and instead I’ll just marry Silas-kun for real.’
Harper finished her portion, sighing in contentment as the warm food settled in her stomach.
She shifted her body closer to Silas.
Without asking permission, she casually lifted her right leg, placing her smooth bare thigh directly over his lap.
She leaned her weight against his side, resting the side of her head comfortably against his broad chest.
Silas stopped chewing for a second. He looked down at the beautiful lightning Lord currently using him as a heated mattress.
He let out a long, long sigh but he didn’t push her away. He simply let her rest, staring out into the dark corridors beyond their blue ring.
"My stamina is regenerating," Silas broke the silence. "Once I rest a bit, I’m going to step out of the Safe Zone... I am going to find the Lesser General, kill it, and take its treasure."
Or at least Silas thought it had treasure, he really didn’t know.
Harper tilted her head up with her purple eyes widening in alarm.
"Can I fight it with you?" Harper asked immediately, her hand gripping the fabric of his shirt. "My core is recovering and I can provide support."
"No," Silas shut her down instantly, his voice brokering zero debate.
Harper frowned. "Why not? I am a—"

"Because you have risked your life too much already," Silas told her, his golden-ringed eyes meeting hers. "You nearly died trying to protect me on the surface. You were impaled and your body is still traumatized. You will stay in the Safe Zone and cover my retreat if things go bad."
Harper’s breath hitched.
She stared into his eyes with her heart fluttering wildly in her chest.
’Why does he make my heart beat so much...?’ What is wrong with me?!’
He wasn’t rejecting her out of disdain... He was trying to protect her.
Her heart thumped wildly, why was he so amazing?
They rested in silence for a bit and the blue light above them was slowly beginning to brighten.
"I think the night is at it’s peak..." Silas noted.
He stood up, gently shifting her leg off his lap. Harper sat up, pulling the trench coat tighter around herself.
"Good luck, Silas," Harper wished him softly, her purple eyes tracking his every movement.
"Thanks..."
He walked toward the glowing blue line of the Safe Zone perimeter.
’I need to be careful.’He reached down to his hip, drawing his heavy mythril longsword from its scabbard.
SHING!
The sound echoed sharply in the quiet cavern.
The moment the tip of Silas’s heavy boot crossed the blue threshold, stepping into the unprotected dark stone.
"HAHAHAHAHA!"
The dead god’s voice instantly boomed from the walls, vibrating with overwhelming joy.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The next second, the stone floor directly beneath the stairs violently exploded upward.
A massive condensed pillar of solid black sand erupted from the ground like a geyser.
The attack had come completely out of nowhere, bypassing Silas’s perception.
The force of the sand pillar slammed directly into Silas’s chest before he could even raise his sword to block.
"Silas!" Harper screamed out his name in absolute terror, scrambling to the edge of the Safe Zone ring.
Silas was violently launched backward through the air. He soared down the massive winding stone staircase with his body crashing against the stone steps but he didn’t panic.
He hit the stairs rolling, his Gold Core instantly flooding his muscles to absorb the blunt force trauma.
SHWK! SHWK! SHWK!
Massive razor-sharp spikes of hardened black sand violently shot out of the stairs, attempting to skewer him as he tumbled.
Silas violently twisted his torso mid-roll, dodging the lethal spikes by mere millimeters.
He forced himself onto his feet, his boots sliding against the dusty stone. He thrust his left hand forward.
"Abyssal Sever!" Silas roared.
He blasted three highly pressurized crescent-shaped blades of water down the staircase.
The water spells sliced through the pursuing sand spikes, completely obliterating them into wet mud.
Silas leaped backward, soaring over the remaining stairs and landing heavily on the smooth stone floor of the lower cavern in a perfect three-point combat stance.
He raised his mythril sword with his golden-ringed eyes narrowing.
At the base of the stairs, the wet mud and the swirling black sand violently coalesced.
The sand rapidly gathered together, compressing and solidifying into a massive, eight-foot-tall humanoid figure.
The creature wore intricate ancient armor forged entirely from hardened desert glass.
It didn’t have a face, only a smooth, featureless mask of swirling grit, and in its right hand, it wielded a massive, curved broadsword made of jagged obsidian.
"Intruder," the sand figure spoke. Its voice was not a roar, but a calm deep harmonic that resonated from the walls.
The General slowly raised its obsidian blade, pointing it directly at Silas’s chest.

"I am Xerxes," the figure introduced himself. "Lesser General of the Eternal Sands... Though I hold a lower rank within his divine army, do not mistake my power. I once stood by my Lord’s side, and I actively participated in the slaying of a Lesser God during the Ascension War."

sentences.text: Harper burst out laughing, it was a melodious sound that momentarily chased away the crushing gloom of the dungeon.
’What’s so funny?’ Silas sighed as he crossed his arms with his face remaining perfectly stoic, though a faint hint of annoyance touched his golden-ringed eyes.
He honestly wasn’t sure if he had eaten a single real meal since he had first stepped foot into the Secret Realm days ago.
Lords with higher possessed incredibly dense bodies that didn’t strictly need normal food for long periods, sustaining their cellular function purely on mana.
But Silas wasn’t even past the first Core Refinement stage yet; his Gold Core burned astronomical amounts of calories to maintain his Body’s physical output.
"We need protein," Silas admitted.
"I feel my body getting sluggish."
"We should cook the Dire Wolf meat now," Harper suggested eagerly, shifting her position on the stone floor.
"Even if we only ate the meat without proper grains, the high nutritional content will repair our muscles and help us prepare for whatever we have to fight tomorrow."
As she spoke, Harper deliberately reached up to the collar of Silas’s trench coat.
She slowly unzipped the top of the heavy coat a bit further down her chest, intentionally letting the cool cavern breeze touch her bare skin.
The movement caused the heavy fabric to ride up her legs, fully exposing her long flawless and perfectly smooth pale thighs in the dim blue light.
She leaned back on her hands, looking up at him through her dark purple eyelashes with a dangerous smile.
"You know, Silas-kun..." Harper purred, her voice dropping into a thick whisper.
"When we are done eating, and our stamina is recovered... you could take me right here.
The blue light lasts for hours so we have nothing but time."
Silas stared at her exposed thighs, then looked up at her flushed face.
He rolled his eyes so hard it physically hurt.
"I am not interested, Harper," Silas told her, his voice echoing with uncompromising rejection.
Harper pouted, her shoulders slumping.
"Why not?
Am I not attractive enough for you?"
"It has nothing to do with your face," Silas lectured her.
"Even if I was interested in compromising my awareness to sleep with you, look around us.
The sand and stone floor in this cavern is covered in ancient moss, stagnant water, and probably ten thousand years of microscopic flesh-eating infections.
What kind of absolute idiot has sex on a bare filthy dungeon floor?"
Harper blinked, looking down at the grimy stone beneath her.
She hadn’t actually thought about the hygiene aspect.
’But still... if a girl keeps throwing herself at me like this, who am I to say no?’ Silas thought and though he didn’t tell her out loud, he was also actively calculating the moisture levels.
He was going to try and manually compress the water vapor to make a small Ice House... exactly like what Mia usually did for them to stay inside safely before he even considered resting properly.
"Get the wolf carcasses out," Silas commanded, walking toward the center of the ring.
"Let’s eat."
Harper sighed, resigning herself to the culinary task.
She waved her pale hand with her Lord inventory interface glowing blue.
THUD!
THUD!
Two massive, headless carcasses of the subterranean Dire Wolves materialized directly onto the stone floor with their thick black fur matted with frozen blood.
Silas didn’t have a conventional hunting knife so he raised his right hand, forcefully drawing a sphere of dense moisture from the damp air.
"Ice Transformation," Silas muttered.
The water violently flash-froze, condensing into a perfectly balanced razor-sharp hunting knife made of solid blue ice.
The blade trailed freezing vapor as Silas knelt beside the first massive wolf carcass.
He possessed a deep awareness of how to butcher and process monster meat like this, having closely observed the huntresses in his territory handle massive boars and wolves back at the Blessed Land.
"Come on..."
With precision, Silas drove the ice knife under the wolf’s thick hide.
SHWK!
He drew the blade in a long flawless line down the beast’s abdomen, effortlessly parting the tough skin from the dense red muscle beneath without piercing the internal organs.
RIPPP!
He gripped the fur with his calloused left hand and forcefully tore the hide away with a sickening sound, exposing the rich mana-infused meat.
"Ummmm..."
Harper shuffled over on her knees to join him.
She wanted to help and to prove her worth beyond just her lightning magic so she grabbed a chunk of the heavy hide, pulling it back to expose the flank.
However, Harper was far less experienced in butchery.

Her hands slipped on the frozen blood, and as she struggled, the heavy trench coat actively rode up higher, completely exposing her bare hips and the smooth curve of her perfect thighs to the freezing air.
Silas ignored the distraction with his golden-ringed eyes locked entirely on the meat.
He rapidly carved out the cuts... the heavy tenderloins from the spine and the thick flank steaks from the hindquarters.
He tossed the massive, ten-pound slabs of raw red meat onto a clean slab of ice he generated on the floor and then he washed them after cutting up the other one.
"We can’t eat it raw," Silas noted, tossing the ice knife aside.
"It’s too tough."
He reached into his own spatial ring.
Before the dungeon raid had commenced, Martha, his diligent maid back home, had forcefully packed his inventory with basic culinary supplies, refusing to let her Lord starve in the wilderness.
’Unfortunately I forgot to take the lunch she had made...’
Silas pulled out a small glass vial of refined olive oil and a leather pouch filled with crushed sea salt, dried rosemary, and crushed red pepper.
He poured the oil over the raw slabs of wolf meat, vigorously rubbing the thick liquid into the muscle fibers with his bare hands.
He generously coated the steaks in the spices, the savory aroma of the herbs instantly cutting through the pungent stench of the dungeon.
"Alright," Silas said, wiping his hands on a rag.
"Roast it and don’t turn it to ash."
Harper smiled, her purple eyes glowing with excitement.
She loved showing off her magical control.
"Okay my love~"
She held both of her pale hands over the massive slabs of seasoned meat however she didn’t summon a catastrophic blast.
Harper closed her eyes, dialing down the raw voltage of her core to an incredibly precise microscopic fraction of its true power.
BZZZZZT.
A web of thin, incredibly precise purple electrical currents arched from her fingertips, sinking directly into the raw meat.
The high-frequency electrical resistance instantly generated extreme internal heat.
The water molecules inside the wolf steaks began to violently boil.
The fat rendered perfectly as the spices sizzled and popped against the searing meat, filling the damp cavern with a mouth-watering, intoxicating aroma of roasted garlic, pepper, and searing steak.
Within two minutes, the outside of the meat was perfectly seared with a dark caramelized crust, while the muscle was roasted to a flawless medium-rare.
"Done," Harper declared proudly, cutting the current.
Silas utilized his water magic again, rapidly condensing moisture from the air to create two wide fflat plates made of smooth, polished ice.
Harper carefully used a pair of ice tongs to transfer the steaming massive cuts of roasted meat onto the plates.
They sat side by side on the cold stone floor with their backs leaning against the cavern wall, exactly in the center of the blue Safe Zone ring.
"Bon’appetit Silas-kun."
They tore into the food with their bare hands.
The wolf meat was incredibly chewy and bursting with a rich, savory flavor that instantly flooded their exhausted bodies with a rush of nutritional mana.
"Mm~ We outdid ourselves, Silas-kun." Harper said and Silas sighed.
"You’re right..."
Silas ate like a starving beast, stripping the meat down to the bone.
As they ate, the crushing isolation of the dungeon seemed to fade.
The romantic tension Harper had been desperately trying to force earlier organically softened into genuine intimacy.
’I think I can take a break from this mission for now...’ Harper thought, it didn’t matter if Silas was the Lord of Blessed Land or not.
The purple haired woman couldn’t bring herself to even think about hurting him.
’I might have to tell Papa I quit... and instead I’ll just marry Silas-kun for real.’
Harper finished her portion, sighing in contentment as the warm food settled in her stomach.
She shifted her body closer to Silas.
Without asking permission, she casually lifted her right leg, placing her smooth bare thigh directly over his lap.
She leaned her weight against his side, resting the side of her head comfortably against his broad chest.
Silas stopped chewing for a second.
He looked down at the beautiful lightning Lord currently using him as a heated mattress.
He let out a long, long sigh but he didn’t push her away.
He simply let her rest, staring out into the dark corridors beyond their blue ring.
"My stamina is regenerating," Silas broke the silence.
"Once I rest a bit, I’m going to step out of the Safe Zone...
I am going to find the Lesser General, kill it, and take its treasure."
Or at least Silas thought it had treasure, he really didn’t know.
Harper tilted her head up with her purple eyes widening in alarm.
"Can I fight it with you?" Harper asked immediately, her hand gripping the fabric of his shirt.
"My core is recovering and I can provide support."
"No," Silas shut her down instantly, his voice brokering zero debate.
Harper frowned.
"Why not?
I am a—"
"Because you have risked your life too much already," Silas told her, his golden-ringed eyes meeting hers.
"You nearly died trying to protect me on the surface.
You were impaled and your body is still traumatized.
You will stay in the Safe Zone and cover my retreat if things go bad."

SHING!

SHWK!
SHWK!

Silas violently twisted his torso mid-roll, dodging the lethal spikes by mere millimeters.

He thrust his left hand forward.
"Abyssal Sever!" Silas roared.
He blasted three highly pressurized crescent-shaped blades of water down the staircase.
The water spells sliced through the pursuing sand spikes, completely obliterating them into wet mud.

The creature wore intricate ancient armor forged entirely from hardened desert glass.
It didn’t have a face, only a smooth, featureless mask of swirling grit, and in its right hand, it wielded a massive, curved broadsword made of jagged obsidian.
"Intruder," the sand figure spoke.
Its voice was not a roar, but a calm deep harmonic that resonated from the walls.

"I am Xerxes," the figure introduced himself.
"Lesser General of the Eternal Sands...
Though I hold a lower rank within his divine army, do not mistake my power.
I once stood by my Lord’s side, and I actively participated in the slaying of a Lesser God during the Ascension War."

chapters.title: Chapter 197: Under The Spire [VI]
paragraphs: Silas’s eyes widened slightly in genuine surprise.
He took a slow step backward as right now, The Lord wasn’t fighting a mindless beast.
He was fighting a veteran commander who had literally helped execute a divine entity ten thousand years ago.
"You have stepped beyond your bounds, mortal," Xerxes stated calmly.
The sand on the floor began to violently vibrate.
SHHHH-SWISH!
Instantly, the sand completely separated.

In a fraction of a microsecond, the single Lesser General split into four perfectly identical, eight-foot-tall copies of himself. All four towering sand figures raised their obsidian blades in perfect unison.
"There will be no running," all four copies of Xerxes spoke simultaneously with their voices overlapping in a terrifying unified chord.
Silas stopped stepping backward.
He firmly planted his heavy boots into the stone floor, gripping his mythril longsword with both hands.
His fear completely evaporated, replaced by a cold thrill of high-tier combat.
A dark, incredibly dangerous smile slowly spread across Silas’s face.
"I’m not running," Silas told them, however he could sense that Harper was watching or he would have already summoned his gold aura. "Come at me."
BOOOOOOM!
All four copies of Xerxes charged Silas simultaneously, their heavy glass boots shattering the stone floor.
They didn’t attack wildly as they moved with flawless military synchronization.
The first clone swung a massive overhead chop aimed to cleave Silas in half.
SWISH!
Silas deflected the blow, angling his mythril sword to slide the obsidian blade off his guard with a shower of sparks.
The second clone lunged, thrusting for his ribs.
Silas violently twisted his torso, entirely evading the thrust.
He dropped his left hand, forcefully drawing a massive volume of moisture from the air.
"Tidal Impact!" Silas roared.
He blasted a condensed sphere of heavy water directly into the chest of the second clone at point-blank range.
The hydraulic shockwave was massive, blowing a gaping, wet hole straight through the sand figure’s torso.
However, the third and fourth clones instantly capitalized on the opening, their swords swinging in a deadly intersecting pincer attack.
Silas parried the right sword, but the physical weight of the strike forced him to his knees.
The left sword descended toward his neck.
Silas didn’t try to block it.
He utilized the environment to his advantage.
The massive volume of water he had just blasted into the second clone had aggressively soaked the surrounding stone floor, completely saturating the bodies of all four sand figures.
Silas slammed his palm flat against the wet stone.
"Ice Transformation!" Silas commanded.
KRKKKKKKKKKK!
The temperature in the lower cavern violently plummeted to absolute zero.

The heavy water thoroughly soaking the sand figures instantly flash-froze and all four copies of Xerxes were abruptly halted mid-swing, their massive eight-foot-tall bodies completely solidified into jagged unbreakable statues of freezing, hardened brown ice.
Silas didn’t waste a second as he exploded off his knees, his mythril sword glowing with mana.
KRA-CRUNCH!
He swung his heavy blade horizontally with devastating kinetic force, cleanly decapitating the first frozen clone.
The frozen sand head flew through the air, violently shattering against the cavern wall into thousands of harmless, icy fragments.
"One down," Silas smirked, preparing to completely shatter the rest.
But as he raised his sword to execute the second clone, the ice violently shuddered.
CRACK! SNAP!
A massive surge of pressurized earth mana erupted from within the frozen statues.
The three remaining figures completely shattered their icy prisons from the inside out, blowing the frozen fragments across the cavern like a frag grenade.
"Do not mistake me for a baseline elemental," the three copies of Xerxes spoke in unison.
The sand constituting their bodies immediately violently shifted.
"We are all Xerxes," the clones declared.
They began moving and Silas’s perception tracked the shifting silhouettes perfectly through the freezing mist and he noticed they didn’t bother reforming their obsidian broadswords.
The Lord watched in real-time as the ancient general completely altered its body.
The right arm of the clone on his left rapidly expanded, the black sand aggressively compressing layer upon layer until it formed a massive boulder-sized war hammer.
Simultaneously, the clone on his right extended its arm outward, the sand hyper-heating itself through intense friction to flash-melt into a twenty-foot-long razor-sharp whip of flexible black glass.
CRACK!
The glass whip brought forth a shockwave with the boom echoing like a cannon shot in the confined corridor.
It snapped violently toward Silas’s throat, moving with imperceptible speed but Silas didn’t duck.
A smirk crossed his face instead.
He channeled his dense mana into his left hand, instantly coating his forearm in a thick unbreakable gauntlet of absolute-zero blue ice. He threw his arm up.
CLANG-SHATTER!
Silas completely intercepted the glass whip.

The razor-sharp tip violently shattered against his ice gauntlet. Before the sand clone could retract the weapon, Silas closed his fist, gripping the remaining length of the glass whip with monstrous physical strength.
"Get over here," Silas commanded.
He violently yanked the glass whip backward.
The force of his pull completely uprooted the eight-foot-tall sand clone from the floor, ripping the massive beast through the air directly toward him.
Silas rotated his hips, gripping his mythril longsword tightly with his right hand.
As the flying clone entered his striking range, he swung his blade in a devastating horizontal arc.
KRA-SLASH!
The mythril steel cleaved cleanly through the clone’s neck and torso, violently bisecting the sand entity in mid-air.
The top half of the monster crashed into the stone wall, dissolving into useless dirt.
"Two," Silas counted with his eyes flashing.
WHOOSH!
The third clone launched itself into the air, bringing the massive compressed sand hammer down with all of its multi-ton physical might, aiming to crush Silas into the bedrock.
Silas didn’t even look up.
He pointed his left palm directly down at the wet stone floor beneath the descending beast as he utilized the precise spell Mia had drilled into his head just hours ago.
"Currents deep, pressure rise..." Silas chanted rapidly, cutting the chant in half too. "Abyssal Geyser!"
KRA-THOOM!
A hyper-pressurized geyser of pure, freezing water violently erupted from the damp stone floor directly beneath the hammer-wielding clone.
The hydraulic force was astronomical.
The geyser slammed into the clone’s chest with the impact of a breaching whale, completely reversing its downward momentum and launching the massive sand monster fifty feet straight up into the air!
The clone smashed brutally into the vaulted stone ceiling, completely disintegrating into a shower of wet, harmless mud that rained down across the corridor.
"Three..." Silas smirked, stepping forward through the falling mud.
The fourth and final clone, wielding a jagged obsidian blade, charged forward. Silas met it head-on.
Silas deflected the heavy obsidian thrust with a casual flick of his wrist, stepped cleanly inside the clone’s guard, and unleashed a blistering flurry of sword strikes.
SHWK! SHWK! SHWK!
In three seconds, Silas severed the clone’s sword arm, chopped off its left leg, and drove his mythril blade straight through its featureless face.
He ripped the blade free, kicking the crumbling sand construct backward onto the floor.
Silas stood perfectly still while lowering his sword. He wasn’t even breathing heavily.
"Is that really all a ’God-Slayer’ has?" Silas mocked the crumbling dirt. "I fought tougher rats in the slums."
But the Lesser General was ten thousand years old, and infinitely more adaptable.
Xerxes realized instantly that engaging this human in close-quarters martial combat was absolute suicide.
The severed sand limbs and the wet mud didn’t stay dead.
The second the debris touched the bedrock, it immediately dissolved into the damp stone floor like acid melting through wax.
SQUELCH!

The solid stone directly beneath Silas’s heavy boots instantly liquefied as the bedrock actively turned into a suffocating spinning maelstrom of black quicksand, attempting to drag him down into the earth.
Silas just rolled his eyes.
"Ice Transformation," Silas stated boredly.
KRKKKKK!
He violently stripped the heat from the quicksand.
The trap solidified instantly into jagged brown ice.
Before his boots could even be caught, Silas effortlessly stepped out of the freezing perimeter, shattering the edges of the trap with a casual stomp.
"You’re going to have to try harder than that..." Silas taunted.
The dungeon responded.
The sand on the floor began to violently vibrate, emitting a terrifying, low-frequency hum.
The three destroyed clones rapidly pulled themselves back together, their forms bubbling up from the stone but they didn’t take humanoid shapes this time.
The three clones completely dissolved into a massive, swirling cloud of fine, abrasive black grit.
FWOOSH!
The cloud violently expanded, completely filling the narrow corridor and generating a massive, high-velocity sandstorm.
Silas narrowed his eyes, raising his arm to shield his face.
The abrasive dust completely blinded his vision, plunging the battlefield into suffocating darkness.
The fine, razor-sharp particles of glass and sand aggressively whipped against his skin, tearing at his shirt and slicing dozens of microscopic cuts across his cheeks.
Xerxes had changed the rules of the engagement. It was no longer a sword fight as it was an environmental execution.
From within the blinding storm, the attacks began coming from every conceivable angle.
SHWK!
A massive spike of hardened sand erupted horizontally from the left wall. Silas violently twisted his torso, the spike grazing his ribs.
CRACK!
A glass whip materialized from the ceiling, snapping down toward his skull. Silas parried it blind with his sword ringing out in the dark.
THUD!
A heavy sand fist formed directly from the floor, slamming into his thigh and forcing him to stumble.
’I can’t even hate on this...’ Silas thought as he gritted his teeth with his smirk vanishing.
The sand was utilizing its physical form with creativity.
The attacks were relentless, overlapping, and perfectly synchronized.
He slashed and parried, weaving through the storm with monstrous physical agility, but he couldn’t hit a target that was literally the air he was breathing.
SHING! SHING!
Obsidian blades manifested from the storm, slashing at his back and Silas forcefully drew moisture from the bone-dry air.
"That will be enough!" Silas roared.
A pressurized invisible ring of spinning water violently erupted around him, expanding outward like a buzzsaw and completely obliterating the incoming sand constructs.
But the constant magical expenditure was rapidly depleting his water reserves.
The Lord couldn’t generate an ocean in a dry cavern.
’Plus if I had a sea of mana like this, that might confirm things... Sigh...’ Silas thought, he wasn’t in danger though.
The sand storm intensified, sensing his stamina draining.
The three clones began to rapidly materialize and dematerialize within the swirling grit.
A clone would form, swing a massive hammer, and instantly dissolve back into dust before Silas’s sword could even make contact.
"Weight of the ocean!" Silas chanted, aiming his palm at a forming clone. "Hydraulic Press!"
BOOOOOOM!
A crushing weight of atmospheric pressure slammed the sand clone into the floor, completely flattening it into a pancake of dirt.
But a microsecond later, the dirt just swirled back into the storm, entirely unharmed.
Silas parried a thrust from the dark, but the force was staggering. The mass of the sand entity was finally gaining the upper tactical advantage.
CRASH! BOOM! SHWK!
A synchronized triple-layered attack converged on him. A glass whip wrapped around his left ankle, pulling his balance off.

A sand hammer slammed into his mythril sword, forcing his guard completely wide open and a massive, solid wall of jagged sand spikes violently materialized in front of him, pushing forward like a bulldozer.
Silas dug his boots into the stone with his muscles bulging as he tried to hold his ground, but the weight of the pushing wall forced him backward.
His boots dragged across the stone.
THUD!
Silas’s back slammed heavily against the cold damp bedrock of a dead-end alcove as he was completely cornered.
The sandstorm parted slightly, revealing the massive shifting wall of spikes preparing to violently crush him into paste.
Up at the top of the stairs, standing safely within the glowing perimeter of the blue Safe Zone ring, Harper watched the battle unfold.

SNAP!
A massive surge of pressurized earth mana erupted from within the frozen statues.
The three remaining figures completely shattered their icy prisons from the inside out, blowing the frozen fragments across the cavern like a frag grenade.
"Do not mistake me for a baseline elemental," the three copies of Xerxes spoke in unison.
The sand constituting their bodies immediately violently shifted.
"We are all Xerxes," the clones declared.
They began moving and Silas’s perception tracked the shifting silhouettes perfectly through the freezing mist and he noticed they didn’t bother reforming their obsidian broadswords.
The Lord watched in real-time as the ancient general completely altered its body.
The right arm of the clone on his left rapidly expanded, the black sand aggressively compressing layer upon layer until it formed a massive boulder-sized war hammer.
Simultaneously, the clone on his right extended its arm outward, the sand hyper-heating itself through intense friction to flash-melt into a twenty-foot-long razor-sharp whip of flexible black glass.
CRACK!
The glass whip brought forth a shockwave with the boom echoing like a cannon shot in the confined corridor.
It snapped violently toward Silas’s throat, moving with imperceptible speed but Silas didn’t duck.
A smirk crossed his face instead.
He channeled his dense mana into his left hand, instantly coating his forearm in a thick unbreakable gauntlet of absolute-zero blue ice.
He threw his arm up.
CLANG-SHATTER!
Silas completely intercepted the glass whip.
The razor-sharp tip violently shattered against his ice gauntlet.
Before the sand clone could retract the weapon, Silas closed his fist, gripping the remaining length of the glass whip with monstrous physical strength.
"Get over here," Silas commanded.
He violently yanked the glass whip backward.
The force of his pull completely uprooted the eight-foot-tall sand clone from the floor, ripping the massive beast through the air directly toward him.
Silas rotated his hips, gripping his mythril longsword tightly with his right hand.
As the flying clone entered his striking range, he swung his blade in a devastating horizontal arc.
KRA-SLASH!
The mythril steel cleaved cleanly through the clone’s neck and torso, violently bisecting the sand entity in mid-air.
The top half of the monster crashed into the stone wall, dissolving into useless dirt.
"Two," Silas counted with his eyes flashing.
WHOOSH!
The third clone launched itself into the air, bringing the massive compressed sand hammer down with all of its multi-ton physical might, aiming to crush Silas into the bedrock.
Silas didn’t even look up.
He pointed his left palm directly down at the wet stone floor beneath the descending beast as he utilized the precise spell Mia had drilled into his head just hours ago.
"Currents deep, pressure rise..." Silas chanted rapidly, cutting the chant in half too.
"Abyssal Geyser!"
KRA-THOOM!
A hyper-pressurized geyser of pure, freezing water violently erupted from the damp stone floor directly beneath the hammer-wielding clone.
The hydraulic force was astronomical.
The geyser slammed into the clone’s chest with the impact of a breaching whale, completely reversing its downward momentum and launching the massive sand monster fifty feet straight up into the air!
The clone smashed brutally into the vaulted stone ceiling, completely disintegrating into a shower of wet, harmless mud that rained down across the corridor.
"Three..." Silas smirked, stepping forward through the falling mud.
The fourth and final clone, wielding a jagged obsidian blade, charged forward.
Silas met it head-on.
Silas deflected the heavy obsidian thrust with a casual flick of his wrist, stepped cleanly inside the clone’s guard, and unleashed a blistering flurry of sword strikes.
SHWK!
SHWK!
SHWK!
In three seconds, Silas severed the clone’s sword arm, chopped off its left leg, and drove his mythril blade straight through its featureless face.
He ripped the blade free, kicking the crumbling sand construct backward onto the floor.
Silas stood perfectly still while lowering his sword.
He wasn’t even breathing heavily.
"Is that really all a ’God-Slayer’ has?" Silas mocked the crumbling dirt.
"I fought tougher rats in the slums."
But the Lesser General was ten thousand years old, and infinitely more adaptable.
Xerxes realized instantly that engaging this human in close-quarters martial combat was absolute suicide.
The severed sand limbs and the wet mud didn’t stay dead.
The second the debris touched the bedrock, it immediately dissolved into the damp stone floor like acid melting through wax.
SQUELCH!

The solid stone directly beneath Silas’s heavy boots instantly liquefied as the bedrock actively turned into a suffocating spinning maelstrom of black quicksand, attempting to drag him down into the earth.
Silas just rolled his eyes.
"Ice Transformation," Silas stated boredly.
KRKKKKK!
He violently stripped the heat from the quicksand.
The trap solidified instantly into jagged brown ice.
Before his boots could even be caught, Silas effortlessly stepped out of the freezing perimeter, shattering the edges of the trap with a casual stomp.
"You’re going to have to try harder than that..." Silas taunted.
The dungeon responded.
The sand on the floor began to violently vibrate, emitting a terrifying, low-frequency hum.
The three destroyed clones rapidly pulled themselves back together, their forms bubbling up from the stone but they didn’t take humanoid shapes this time.
The three clones completely dissolved into a massive, swirling cloud of fine, abrasive black grit.
FWOOSH!
The cloud violently expanded, completely filling the narrow corridor and generating a massive, high-velocity sandstorm.
Silas narrowed his eyes, raising his arm to shield his face.
The abrasive dust completely blinded his vision, plunging the battlefield into suffocating darkness.
The fine, razor-sharp particles of glass and sand aggressively whipped against his skin, tearing at his shirt and slicing dozens of microscopic cuts across his cheeks.
Xerxes had changed the rules of the engagement.
It was no longer a sword fight as it was an environmental execution.
From within the blinding storm, the attacks began coming from every conceivable angle.
SHWK!
A massive spike of hardened sand erupted horizontally from the left wall.
Silas violently twisted his torso, the spike grazing his ribs.
CRACK!
A glass whip materialized from the ceiling, snapping down toward his skull.
Silas parried it blind with his sword ringing out in the dark.
THUD!
A heavy sand fist formed directly from the floor, slamming into his thigh and forcing him to stumble.
’I can’t even hate on this...’ Silas thought as he gritted his teeth with his smirk vanishing.
The sand was utilizing its physical form with creativity.
The attacks were relentless, overlapping, and perfectly synchronized.
He slashed and parried, weaving through the storm with monstrous physical agility, but he couldn’t hit a target that was literally the air he was breathing.
SHING!
SHING!
Obsidian blades manifested from the storm, slashing at his back and Silas forcefully drew moisture from the bone-dry air.
"That will be enough!" Silas roared.
A pressurized invisible ring of spinning water violently erupted around him, expanding outward like a buzzsaw and completely obliterating the incoming sand constructs.
But the constant magical expenditure was rapidly depleting his water reserves.
The Lord couldn’t generate an ocean in a dry cavern.
’Plus if I had a sea of mana like this, that might confirm things...
Sigh...’ Silas thought, he wasn’t in danger though.
The sand storm intensified, sensing his stamina draining.
The three clones began to rapidly materialize and dematerialize within the swirling grit.
A clone would form, swing a massive hammer, and instantly dissolve back into dust before Silas’s sword could even make contact.
"Weight of the ocean!" Silas chanted, aiming his palm at a forming clone.
"Hydraulic Press!"
BOOOOOOM!
A crushing weight of atmospheric pressure slammed the sand clone into the floor, completely flattening it into a pancake of dirt.
But a microsecond later, the dirt just swirled back into the storm, entirely unharmed.
Silas parried a thrust from the dark, but the force was staggering.
The mass of the sand entity was finally gaining the upper tactical advantage.
CRASH!
BOOM!
SHWK!
A synchronized triple-layered attack converged on him.
A glass whip wrapped around his left ankle, pulling his balance off.

A sand hammer slammed into his mythril sword, forcing his guard completely wide open and a massive, solid wall of jagged sand spikes violently materialized in front of him, pushing forward like a bulldozer.
Silas dug his boots into the stone with his muscles bulging as he tried to hold his ground, but the weight of the pushing wall forced him backward.
His boots dragged across the stone.
THUD!
Silas’s back slammed heavily against the cold damp bedrock of a dead-end alcove as he was completely cornered.
The sandstorm parted slightly, revealing the massive shifting wall of spikes preparing to violently crush him into paste.
Up at the top of the stairs, standing safely within the glowing perimeter of the blue Safe Zone ring, Harper watched the battle unfold.

chapters.title: Chapter 198: Under The Spire [VII / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Her purple eyes darted frantically, tracking Silas’s retreating silhouette through the dust.
Her heart hammered violently against her ribs.
Harper saw Silas get pushed back, his back hitting the stone wall. She saw the massive wall of sand spikes actively rearing back to impale him.
"Fuck!" Harper screamed.
She didn’t think about her depleted core and she didn’t think about the explicit orders to stay put and cover the retreat.
Harper ran completely out of the Safe Zone, her bare feet slapping against the cold stone as she sprinted toward the top of the stairs and the heavy trench coat billowing behind her.
The very instant her body crossed the glowing blue threshold into the unprotected corridor, the labyrinth reacted.
FWOOSH!
The damp stone floor directly in front of her violently exploded.
A massive towering wave of black sand erupted from the ground, aggressively morphing into a jagged wall of spikes designed to impale her instantly for breaking the curfew.
Harper didn’t flinch. Her purple eyes flashed with electrical power.
"Get out of my way!" Harper roared.
She thrust both of her pale hands forward, unleashing a catastrophic torrent of superheated purple lightning directly into the incoming wave of sand.
The raw heat of the lightning was absolute.
The massive wall of black sand didn’t just stop... the intense electrical voltage instantly superheated the silicon dioxide to over three thousand degrees!
The towering sand spikes completely melted, instantly turning into a beautiful and harmless sculpture of smooth, branching violet glass!
Harper slid to a halt on the stone, breathing heavily as she lowered her sparking hands.
She stared through the translucent glass sculpture with her eyes narrowing as she looked down at the swirling storm cornering Silas.
Her education regarding elemental constructs and summoned entities rapidly clicked into place.

"Wait," Harper whispered to herself, wiping sweat from her brow as she analyzed the way the clones shared a single, perfectly distributed mana signature. "If they are all identical copies... where the hell is the main body?"
The howling abrasive tornado of black grit and razor-sharp glass shards violently whipped against the damp bedrock walls of the alcove, completely trapping Silas in a meat grinder.
SHWK! SHWK!
Two jagged spears of condensed sand materialized from the spinning vortex, shooting forward with enough velocity to pierce solid iron but once again, Silas didn’t flinch.
He planted his right combat boot into the stone floor, pivoting his torso with devastating precision as his mythril longsword blurred in a protective arc.
CLANG! SHATTER!
The steel blade intercepted both spears simultaneously, shattering the hardened sand into a useless shower of harmless brown dirt.
But before Silas could even reset his posture, the stone floor directly beneath his boots violently liquefied into a spinning gravitational sinkhole of black quicksand.
"You’re getting quite repetitive," Silas spat coldly.
He didn’t bother stepping back.
He forcefully slammed his left palm flat against the damp cavern wall, violently stripping the heat from the immediate atmosphere.
"Ice Transformation!" Silas commanded.
KRKKKKKKKKKK!

A catastrophic wave of absolute-zero frost aggressively raced across the floor, flash-freezing the spinning quicksand into a solid unbreakable platform of jagged brown ice before his boots could sink an inch.

Without wasting a second, Silas channeled an explosive surge of his mana directly into his calves and launched himself forward, completely abandoning defense to execute a brutal blitz directly into the heart of the sandstorm.
He knew exactly how to overwhelm an elemental hive-mind... You don’t fight the individual limbs; you violently overload their shared processing capacity.
FWOOSH!
Silas swept his left hand through the air, drawing upon every single remaining drop of condensation hanging in the surroundings down here.
’I should be able to do this...’ Silas thought.

He didn’t form blades or shields this time as instead he unleashed a high-pressure deluge of pure aqua mana, aggressively blanketing the entire thirty-foot intersection in a torrential downpour of dense water.
The heavy water slammed into the swirling sandstorm like a collapsing dam.
The microscopic grains of silicon dioxide, suddenly saturated by hundreds of gallons of pressurized aqua mana, instantly lost their aerodynamic lift and structural cohesion.
The roaring tornado of abrasive grit violently choked, sputtered, and collapsed into the floor, completely unable to sustain its high-velocity rotation while weighed down by the water.
"Let’s see you fly now," Silas sneered.
Forced out of its sandstorm state by the weight of the water, the ancient Lesser General had no choice but to reassemble its physical form.

The saturated muddy sand violently coalesced in the center of the corridor, rapidly compressing layer upon layer until it assumed the towering, eight-foot humanoid silhouette of Xerxes, wielding a massive jagged broadsword forged from wet obsidian.
The General raised its blade to strike, but Silas was already there.
BOOOOOOM!
Silas closed the distance with a concussive boom, his combat boot driving directly into the center of Xerxes’s chest with monstrous uncompromising physical strength.
The impact caved the wet sand inward, sending the eight-foot giant skidding violently backward across the slick stone floor.
Before the General could recover its footing, Silas unleashed a relentless combination of brutality.
CLANG! KRA-SLASH! SHWK!
He swung his mythril blade in a devastating sequence of overhead chops, horizontal cleaves, and thrusting lunges.
He moved so fast that the steel blade left a trailing, luminous afterimage in the dim blue light.

Xerxes desperately tried to fight back, swinging its heavy obsidian broadsword in wide, sweeping arcs designed to decapitate the mortal, but Silas merely tilted his head or shifted his shoulders, effortlessly dodging every single counterattack by mere millimeters.
Yet, as Silas drove his blade deep into the sand giant’s shoulder, ripping a massive chunk of wet mud away, his instincts spiked.

’Something is very wrong...’ Silas thought with his golden-ringed eyes narrowing as he ducked under a desperate obsidian swipe. ’I feel like this fucker isn’t the real thing and not only that but he’s trying to trap me too.’
As if confirming his suspicion, the damp bedrock on either side of the corridor violently bulged outward.
SQUELCH! SQUELCH!

Two additional fully formed clones of Xerxes aggressively erupted from the walls, raising their arms to manifest twenty-foot-long whips of compressed glass designed to catch Silas in a lethal pincer movement.
Silas didn’t even turn his head to look at the flanking reinforcements.
He simply dropped his left hand toward the puddles of heavy water he had just flooded the arena with.
"Ice Transformation!" Silas roared.
KRKKKKKKKKKKKKKKK!
The entire thirty-foot intersection flash-froze in a fraction of a microsecond.
The standing water on the stone floor violently erupted upward, transforming into a dense inescapable forest of razor-sharp five-foot-tall spikes of solid blue ice!
KRA-CRUNCH!

The erupting ice spikes cleanly skewered the two emerging sand clones from below, tearing through their midsections and instantly freezing their saturated mud bodies into fragile, immobilized statues.

Silas spun on his heel, bringing his mythril sword around in a sweeping horizontal execution that shattered both frozen clones into thousands of harmless, glittering ice fragments across the corridor.
Up at the top of the sweeping stone staircase, Harper was leaning heavily against the masonry, her breath catching in her throat as she watched the violence below.

She had just watched Silas effortlessly dismantle a sandstorm, freeze the entire arena, and shatter these clones in less than five seconds but as she tracked the glittering ice shrapnel falling across the cavern, her perception noticed an anomaly.
The ambient magical density in the room hadn’t dropped at all.
Harper’s purple eyes darted away from the slaughtered clones, rapidly scanning the dark, vaulted stone architecture of the cavern.
She checked the walls, the stairs, and finally... she looked directly up at the high, eighty-foot ceiling.
Her heart violently seized in her chest.
Clinging silently to the damp, moss-covered masonry directly above the center of the intersection, camouflaged within the deep shadows of the ceiling, was a massive mass of swirling black grit.
It was the real Sand General.
The towering, eight-foot figure Silas was currently engaging on the floor was nothing more than a dense intricate puppet designed to hold his attention.

The real Xerxes had completely condensed its primary core and physical mass onto the ceiling, holding a massive, four-foot-long execution spear forged from hyper-compressed, obsidian-tipped desert glass.
The ancient entity’s glowing, malevolent red eyes were locked entirely on the back of Silas’s neck, waiting for the exact microsecond his swing finished to execute a top-down assassination.
"Silas!" Harper screamed at the absolute top of her lungs, her voice tearing through the cavern’s acoustics to alert him. "Above you! The ceiling!"
However, before the final syllable of her warning even left her lips, the monster jumped off.
WHOOSH!
Xerxes detached from the high stone ceiling, plummeting directly down toward Silas’s exposed back like a falling meteor, its razor-sharp obsidian spear pointed dead center for the Warlord’s spine.
For Harper, standing forty yards away at the top of the stairs, it felt as though time had suddenly slowed to an agonizing suffocating crawl.
CRACK! KRA-THOOM!

Harper’s purple eyes flared with electrical power as she thrust both of her pale hands forward, instantly letting off three consecutive condensed bolts of white-hot purple lightning directed straight at the descending sand giant’s trajectory.
The lightning bolts screamed across the cavern, illuminating the damp stone in blinding violet flashes but Xerxes was a veteran commander who had survived the Ascension War.
Mid-air, without any physical leverage to push off from, the Lesser General fluidly shifted the internal density of its sand body.
The entity actively dissolved the center of its torso into an empty, hollow ring of loose grit a fraction of a microsecond before the lightning arrived.
ZZZZZT!
All three bolts of Harper’s lightning passed harmlessly through the gaping hole in Xerxes’s torso, scorching the stone floor below without dealing a single drop of damage.
The General instantly re-condensed its chest, continuing its terrifying high-velocity descent directly toward Silas without losing an ounce of momentum.
"No you don’t!" Harper shrieked.
She violently bitten her lower lip, tasting iron, and instantly activated her signature blood technique.
FWOOSH!
The residual iron in her boiling blood violently converted into a liquid electrical medium.
Her pale skin literally began to emit static sparks, her purple eyes glowing like twin supernovas as she violently launched herself off the top of the staircase.
She blasted forward through the air like a human lightning bolt, desperately trying to physically intercept the falling spear before it impaled Silas.
Sensing the incoming electrical projectile from its flank, Xerxes didn’t even turn its head.
While still plummeting toward the floor, the General casually extended its left hand toward the lunging woman.
SHHHH-BOOM!
A twister of abrasive black sand violently erupted from Xerxes’s palm, blasting directly across the cavern and slamming point-blank into Harper’s face!
"AGGGH!" Harper cried out as the spinning vortex of grit completely engulfed her head, violently stripping her momentum in mid-air and plunging her vision into suffocating darkness.
The razor-sharp grains of sand aggressively scored her skin, attempting to shred her corneas and blind her completely but Harper refused to be taken out of the fight.
While suspended mid-air inside the blinding twister, she violently dumped a massive surge of raw voltage directly from her palms into the swirling grit around her face.
BZZZZZZZZZT!
The electrical resistance instantly superheated the spinning black sand to over three thousand degrees.
In less than a heartbeat, the blinding twister of grit flash-melted into a solid, hollow cylinder of fragile violet glass wrapped around her head!
KRA-SHATTER!
Harper violently headbutted the glass, completely shattering the cylinder into thousands of glittering fragments.
She cleared her vision instantly, thrusting her hands forward to unleash a devastating, close-range electrical blast directly at the General’s torso.
However, at that exact point in time, it was already too late.
Xerxes had already crossed the remaining vertical distance.

The eight-foot sand monster was hovering directly above Silas’s shoulders, its massive obsidian spear thrusting downward with multi-ton force, mere inches away from impaling the Lord straight through the heart.
Harper’s purple eyes widened in horror as her scream caught in her throat.

While suspended mid-air inside the blinding twister, she violently dumped a massive surge of raw voltage directly from her palms into the swirling grit around her face.
BZZZZZZZZZT!
The electrical resistance instantly superheated the spinning black sand to over three thousand degrees.
In less than a heartbeat, the blinding twister of grit flash-melted into a solid, hollow cylinder of fragile violet glass wrapped around her head!
KRA-SHATTER!
Harper violently headbutted the glass, completely shattering the cylinder into thousands of glittering fragments.
She cleared her vision instantly, thrusting her hands forward to unleash a devastating, close-range electrical blast directly at the General’s torso.
However, at that exact point in time, it was already too late.
Xerxes had already crossed the remaining vertical distance.

The eight-foot sand monster was hovering directly above Silas’s shoulders, its massive obsidian spear thrusting downward with multi-ton force, mere inches away from impaling the Lord straight through the heart.
Harper’s purple eyes widened in horror as her scream caught in her throat.

chapters.title: Chapter 199: Under The Spire [VIII / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Then, Silas moved.
He didn’t panic and he didn’t stumble. In fact, his face was set in a cold smile.
Silas had, of course, easily sensed the fucker preparing to ambush him from the ceiling after taking time to think about it...

That was precisely why he had flooded the floor with water, executed the decoy clones, and purposefully turned his back toward the center of the room... he had deliberately put himself in an easy inviting position to bait the main body into committing to an irreversible aerial drop.
The very microsecond the obsidian spear tip descended within six inches of his neck, Silas violently pivoted on his right heel, spinning his entire torso around with superhuman speed.
He didn’t try to dodge out of the way. He brought his heavy mythril longsword up in a vicious two-handed vertical thrust.
SHWK-CRUNCH!

Silas parried the descending obsidian spear with the crossguard of his weapon, violently deflecting the lethal point past his shoulder, before driving the razor-sharp tip of his mythril longsword straight upward directly through the dead center of Xerxes’s falling chest!

The four-foot steel blade punched completely through the General’s condensed sand core, erupting out the back of the entity’s masonry armor with a sickening grinding sound of shattering glass and tearing earth.
Time abruptly bled back to normal speed.
THUD!
Harper landed heavily on the damp stone floor ten yards away with her boots skidding across the ice as she watched the unbelievable spectacle before her.
Impaled mid-air on the length of Silas’s sword, the Sand General let out a deep echoing groan of ancient disbelief.

Recognizing that its primary physical core had been severely compromised, Xerxes immediately attempted to phase out... desperately trying to dissolve its dense sand body back into a harmless intangible cloud of floating dust to escape the blade and reform elsewhere.

"You’re not going anywhere," Silas stated and before the grains of sand could even begin to separate and disperse into the air, Silas violently clamped his left hand directly onto the General’s armored wrist.

He tapped into his deepest reserves of elemental control, aggressively pumping a continuous pressurized torrent of raw water mana straight up through the blade of his sword and directly into the interior of Xerxes’s sand body!
SQUELCH! GURGLE!

"For somebody that was supposedly part of a legendary group that killed a Lesser God..." Silas told the struggling entity, his golden-ringed eyes glowing with cold disdain as he pumped gallons of pressurized aqua mana directly into its core. "...you sure are a coward."
The effect of the internal water injection was immediate and catastrophic.

The hyper-condensed black sand constituting Xerxes’s body, suddenly flooded from the inside out by high-pressure aqua mana, was completely unable to phase into dust or maintain its structural integrity.
The dry grains absorbed the water like a sponge, violently expanding and bloating at an exponential rate.

Within two seconds, the eight-foot, terrifyingly sleek elemental General was forcibly expanded in the center of the corridor, rapidly transforming into a massive waterlogged and incredibly fat sphere of wet mud.
"No..." Xerxes gurgled, its deep voice heavily muffled and bubbling as its muddy limbs helplessly flailed outward from its rapidly bloating torso. "The glory... of the Sands..."
Silas twisted his mythril sword inside the bloated mud sphere, channeling a final, lethal spike of ice magic directly into the center of the mass.
"Pop." Silas said simply.
KA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The massive fat sphere of mud violently detonated from the inside out!

The explosion sent a massive tidal shockwave of wet harmless brown dirt and shattered obsidian shrapnel blasting across the entire thirty-foot intersection, plastering the damp stone walls and ceiling in thick layers of sludge.
Yet another one of the ancient Sand God’s legendary commanders had formally passed away, completely eviscerated by a Lord from the land of the living.
Silas stood calmly in the center of the settling mud shower, slowly lowering his mythril longsword.
He flicked his wrist, smoothly cleaning the wet sludge off the shining steel blade before sliding the weapon securely back into its heavy leather scabbard with a sharp sound.
CLANG!
He didn’t waste a second celebrating.

He immediately knelt down in the mud with his eyes scanning the remains of the General’s core, actively looking around for some kind of high-tier treasure, glowing skill tome, or divine jewel that could naturally be gotten from the corpse of a veteran boss monster.
As his hands sifted through the wet dirt, the dead god’s voice boomed directly from the vaulted stone ceiling above, dripping with sarcastic mockery.

"HAHAHAHA!" Ititus laughed hysterically over the broadcast. "Are you seriously digging through the mud like a starving swine, mortal?! You actually thought there was going to be some magnificent, divine jewel hidden inside the corpse of a low-ranking Lesser General like that?!"
The audio crackled with sadistic amusement as the dead god continued his taunts.

"Xerxes was mere fodder during the Ascension War!" Ititus mocked loudly. "The fact that you actually had to exert yourself and struggled like that against such a minor bottom-tier subordinate is quite pitiful! You are miles away from worthy of my true treasures!"
Silas didn’t even bother looking up at the ceiling, nor did he waste his breath talking back to the pathological lying god.
He completely ignored the theatrical broadcast, his calloused hands systematically sifting through the dense center of the mud blast where the entity’s core had detonated.
A second later, his fingers brushed against something solid, warm, and softly vibrating within the sludge.
Silas pulled his hand back, revealing a small intricately woven pouch made of indestructible golden dragon-leather.
The moment his fingers closed around the item, a translucent blue system tab immediately projected itself directly in front of his eyes.
[Tier 4 Boss Monster ’Xerxes, Lesser General of the Eternal Sands’ has been slain!]
[You have gained 300 UP!]
[Loot Acquired: Shifting Sand]
[Tier: 2]

[Description: A sealed pouch containing three pounds of primordial, highly conductive desert grains harvested from the Ascension Era. When integrated into the mana pathways of an individual possessing the Earth, Sand, or Glass affinity, this catalyst exponentially increases construct versatility, shape-shifting speed, and structural density. Can be manipulated to assume weaponized or defensive states without standard incantations.]
Silas read the system interface with a look of deep disappointment crossing his sharp face.
He smoothly took the pouch of Shifting Sand and stored it directly into his endless Lord Inventory interface with a wave of his hand.
He let out a long deeply exhausted sigh, shaking his head at the ceiling.

"Unbelievable," Silas muttered bitterly to himself, stepping out of the mud. "Usually, when a Lord risks his neck and steps foot into an ancient Secret Realm drop, they expect to see Tier 4 artifacts lying around, and sometimes even Tier 5 sovereign treasures if they kill a named boss. But a Tier 2 catalyst for a multi-stage Secret Realm? This dead god is too cheap... It’s almost as if he’s completely broke and just throwing scraps at us to hide his empty treasury..."
Hearing his blatant financial insult, the magical broadcast on the ceiling abruptly clicked off with an angry static hiss, plunging the corridor back into silence.
Silas turned around, looking across the thirty-foot intersection toward the base of the staircase.
Harper was standing there on the damp stone with her bare legs trembling slightly as she leaned against the masonry.
She was still covered in a thin layer of soot and glittering glass dust from her mid-air twister escape, and his oversized black trench coat was hanging loosely from her shoulders.
Her chest was heaving and her purple eyes were wide as she stared at him with complete awe.
Silas walked over to her, his expression softening just a fraction from his usual cold demeanor.

"You shouldn’t have worried about me," Silas told her quietly, stopping two paces away. "And you definitely shouldn’t have broken cover and jumped out of the Safe Zone with a depleted core just to intercept an aerial drop. I had the angle covered from the start."
Harper stood there for a second, absorbing his gentle reprimand.
Then, her flawless face flushed a brilliant shade of pink.
She aggressively puffed out her pale cheeks in an adorable uncharacteristic display of childish frustration, instantly canceling the lingering electrical static of her spell.

"You could have warned me you were baiting him!" Harper complained, crossing her arms tightly over his trench coat and sticking her chin in the air. "I literally thought you were about to get impaled! I turned my own blood into lightning just to save your stubborn neck, you ungrateful brute!"
Silas actually let out a small genuine chuckle at her pouting expression. He didn’t argue with her logic.
He simply reached out, casually placing his hand on her shoulder to steady her trembling frame.
"Let’s go back," Silas instructed her quietly. "Your stamina is bottomed out."
Harper nodded, her defensive posture instantly melting under his touch.
She stood up properly, leaning a fraction of her weight against his side as they slowly walked side-by-side back up the sweeping stone staircase toward the upper corridor.
As they ascended, the landscape of the subterranean labyrinth had changed.
There were no more distant blood-curdling screams echoing through the dark tunnels, there were no more sounds of tearing flesh or crushing stone.
The initial chaotic slaughter of the night cycle’s curfew enforcement had concluded.
Whatever rival Lords had been stupid enough to wander the corridors during the blue light had either decided to stay at their Safe Zone or been permanently eliminated by the roaming Lesser Generals.
Once they reached the top of the stairs and stepped safely back inside the thirty-foot glowing blue ring of their Safe Zone, Silas decided to run a practical experiment.
"I just need to check..."
He turned around, facing the dark stairs.

With deliberate slowness, Silas lifted his right combat boot and purposefully stepped backward... placing his foot completely outside the glowing blue boundary line of the Safe Zone, standing in the unprotected blue light of the corridor.
He stood there for five solid seconds with his hand resting casually on his sword hilt, waiting for the dungeon to react.
Nothing happened.
There were no sand pillars erupted from the floor and no massive obsidian blades materialized from the shadows.
In short, nobody came after him.
A moment later, Ititus’s voice sighed directly from the ceiling masonry above his head, sounding deeply bored and disappointed.

"You are of absolutely no fun, Silas Graves," the dead god complained over the audio link. "You already slayed the general and you can stand out there all night if you want, I am not wasting another one of my Generals on a brute who inflates my commanders with water until they explode... Go to sleep."
Silas smirked, stepping his boot safely back inside the blue ring. "Good to know."

He walked toward the center of the Safe Zone, where Harper had already sat down heavily on the damp stone floor, hugging her knees to her chest while wrapping his trench coat tightly around herself to ward off the chill.

"I will take the first watch," Harper offered immediately, looking up at him with tired, serious purple eyes. "You fought the General, butchered the wolves, and carried me through the tunnels. Your physical stamina has to be lagging so let me guard the perimeter while you rest."
Silas rolled his shoulders, letting out a heavy sigh as he stood over her.
"No. I will do so instead. Your core is still actively repairing its pathways. If an enemy Lord stumbles into this intersection, you won’t have the raw output to repel them. Lay down and sleep."
"I am not a helpless damsel, Silas!" Harper argued, glaring at him stubbornly. "I am a Valoria City elite! I can hold a watch for four hours without collapsing!"
They stood there in the center of the glowing blue ring, fiercely arguing back and forth for several minutes over the military logistics of the watch schedule.
Silas completely refused to yield his responsibility for security, while Harper stubbornly refused to feel like a useless burden.
Finally, Harper threw her hands up in defeat, offering a practical compromise.

"Fine!" Harper huffed, crossing her arms. "If neither of us is going to sleep while the other watches, then we should just stay awake together! Or better yet... I can manually project an automated defensive barrier around our perimeter. That way, the magic holds the watch, and we can both actually relax without staring into the dark!"
